title: The 2024 Seahawks did indeed have one specific Michigan influence
summary: The story of the day on Tuesday featured the unexpected disclosure of a behind-the-scenes beef between the Seahawks and Broncos.
full_text: ' The story of the day on Tuesday featured the unexpected disclosure of a behind-the-scenes beef between the Seahawks and Broncos. And while the whole thing was eye opening (and likely not intended for air), one specific line caught my eye. Regarding Broncos coach Sean Payton's assertion that the Seahawks had obtained training-camp footage through improper means, Macdonald said, "He thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant." That's a reference to the 2023 Connor Stalions scandal in Ann Arbor, where Stalions developed a mechanism (in violation of NCAA rules) to scout future opponents with the goal of figuring out their sideline signals. In this specific context, Payton presumably suggested that the Seahawks sent someone to Broncos training camp to record their plays. Beyond the fact that Macdonald's journey included a year on Jim Harbaugh's Michigan staff (2021, as defensive coordinator), the 2024 Seahawks employed former Michigan assistant Matt Weiss as an outside contractor . And while Weiss's coaching career has imploded due to criminal allegations of widespread hacking, it's fair to point out that the 2024 Seahawks had a distinct Michigan component. That's not to say Payton's allegations had any merit. Faced with a threat that the Seahawks would sue the Broncos if Payton went public with his suspicions of shenanigans, the issue died. And it would have remained unknown if Macdonald had spoken about it into a hot mic. It will be interesting to hear what Macdonald and Payton have to say about it today, when they meet with reporters for their usual Wednesday press conferences. Regardless of their likely efforts to downplay the situation and move on, the Seahawks have self-applied the kind of scarlet letter that will give the coaches of the teams they beat the same kind of excuse that plagued the Patriots during their run of dominance. Pressed by owners as to why the Seahawks keep beating their teams, coaches can resort to the notion that the Seahawks cheat. Even without a shred of evidence to support that claim. If/when that happens, it will trace to the fact that Macdonald got way too comfortable — and said way too much about a topic that otherwise would have never come to light. Meanwhile, the Broncos host the Seahawks in 22 days, for a Thursday night game. Which will create a motivation for multiple media outles to fully explore the rabbit hole that, as of Tuesday morning, no one even knew existed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys stressing discipline, communication ahead of matchup with Lamar Jackson
summary: The Cowboys defense has had a hard time keeping quarterbacks from making plays with their legs through the first two weeks of the season and they'll face another player capable of hurting them in that area this week.
full_text: The Cowboys defense has had a hard time keeping quarterbacks from making plays with their legs through the first two weeks of the season and they'll face another player capable of hurting them in that area this week. Lamar Jackson will be on the other side of the line when the Cowboys take on the Ravens in Brazil this Sunday and the Ravens are surely aware that the Cowboys have allowed an average of 6.6 yards every time a quarterback has run with the ball this season. Finding a way to keep Jackson from having the same kind of success is central to the Cowboys' preparation this week and defensive tackle Kenny Clark identified the key facets to the team's approach. "Just being disciplined ," Clark said, via the team's website. "Communication, just understanding our rush lanes, playing with extension, powering offensive linemen and just restricting those gaps so you can't get through. But the main thing is just staying disciplined and communicating." The Cowboys' job will be made more difficult by the presence of Derrick Henry in the Ravens' backfield, so defensive coordinator Christian Parker will have his work cut out for him when it comes to improving on the team's underwhelming defensive performance so far this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers place RB Jonathon Brooks on IR, sign Isaiah Simmons to 53-man roster
summary: The Panthers have made a couple of roster moves official.
full_text: The Panthers have made a couple of roster moves official. With news emerging that Jonathon Brooks will undergo core muscle surgery, Carolina has placed the running back on injured reserve. He will reportedly miss at least six weeks. As a corresponding move, the Panthers have signed safety Isaiah Simmons to the 53-man roster from the club’s practice squad. Carolina had elevated Simmons to the gameday roster for each of the first two games. He has played 80 percent of the club’s special teams snaps. The Panthers will be on the road to face the Browns in Week 3.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike Macdonald recounts "Cold War" with Sean Payton over cheating suspicions during the 2024 season
summary: The Week 6 game between the Broncos and Seahawks has gained a new subplot.
full_text: The Week 6 game between the Broncos and Seahawks has gained a new subplot. During an appearance on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald recounted a story involving Broncos head coach Sean Payton from his first season in Seattle. The Seahawks played the Broncos in Week 1 that year and Macdonald said that the team's staff collected fan videos posted to social media from Broncos practices as part of their preparation because they were "public knowledge." The Seahawks won 26-20 and Macdonald said Payton "got wind of" how they used the videos in the middle of the season. Payton called Seahawks General Manager John Schneider and, per Macdonald, "lost it." "He basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriot Spygate type of thing," Macdonald said. "I'm sitting there like, 'Oh my god. We didn't cheat.' They thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant and the whole thing. So we had to counter with him and say, 'If you come out with this, we're going to sue you because it's not true.'" Macdonald said that Payton eventually dropped the issue, but that it felt like the two teams were involved in something more geopolitical than football until that happened. "It was like the Cold War," Macdonald said. "He's like, 'I'm going to hit the button. I'm going to hit the button.' 'Well, we're going to hit the button.' None of us hit the button." Macdonald said he and Payton subsequently crossed paths at the Scouting Combine, but the issue didn't come up. Payton will likely be asked about his version of events at some point before the Week 6 meeting between the teams.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks needs surgery, out at least six weeks
summary: The groin injury suffered by Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks on Sunday was worse than initially believed.
full_text: The groin injury suffered by Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks on Sunday was worse than initially believed. Although Brooks was initially described as week-to-week, he will actually miss at least six weeks, according to Ian Rapoport. Brooks is scheduled for core muscle surgery today. The Panthers will put him on injured reserve. At this point, it's more newsworthy when Brooks is healthy than when he's injured. The Panthers made him the first running back selected in the 2024 NFL draft while he was still recovering from a torn ACL in college, he tore the same ACL as a rookie, and he didn't play at all in 2025. Brooks has just 52 yards on 18 carries in his career. He still has never so much as gained a single rushing first down.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tyson Bagent placed in concussion protocol, putting Case Keenum in line to start Week 3
summary: Chicago is dealing with multiple injuries at quarterback. The club will play Philadelphia on Monday night.
full_text: As it turns out, Chicago's backup quarterback is also dealing with an injury. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Tyson Bagent has been diagnosed with a concussion and is now in the protocol. With starter Caleb Williams week-to-week with a hamstring injury, Case Keenum is now in line to start against the Eagles next Monday night. Bagent entered Sunday’s 9-3 loss to the Vikings midway through the fourth quarter after Williams exited with his hamstring injury. He played the rest of Chicago’s 10 offensive snaps to conclude the contest, going 5-of-9 passing for 54 yards. Keenum, 38, has not appeared in a game since he started two for Houston back in 2023. He was 34-of-53 in those two contests for 291 yards with a touchdown and three interceptions. Keenum has appeared in 80 games with 66 starts in his career, dating back to 2013. The Bears also have rookie Miller Moss at quarterback on their practice squad. Playing Monday night, Chicago’s first injury report of Week 3 is due out on Thursday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Klint Kubiak: I enjoy that our team's 2-0, but no one's made the playoffs going 2-0
summary: There might be a little something brewing with the Raiders.
full_text: There might be a little something brewing with the Raiders. The club has started 2-0 for the first time since 2021. Klint Kubiak is the first head coach to begin his tenure with the franchise 2-0 since Bill Callahan back in 2002. But Kubiak isn't putting too much stock in the team's hot start. “I enjoy that our team is 2-0, our organization is 2-0,” Kubiak said in his Monday press conference, via transcript from the team. “No one's made the playoffs going 2-0.” Still, when beginning a head coaching tenure, a hot start is particularly valuable. “I think it just reinforces the messages that we've been sending,” Kubiak said. "Our guys have been very coachable, and our guys want to win. Winning is important to this team, it’s important to this coaching staff. We also have very short memories and know that you can only win one at a time. “And so, we're turning the page, and now we get to prepare to play a really good Saints team.” After a game at home and a game in Los Angeles with a favorable crowd, the Raiders will travel to New Orleans to take on the Saints for what could be a sneaky good game in Week 3.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike Macdonald's comments about Sean Payton weren't intended for public consumption
summary: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald launched his career as a head coach with a win over Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos.
full_text: ' Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald launched his career as a head coach with a win over Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos. The game from September 2024 moved back to the front burner on Tuesday, thanks to footage from Macdonald's recent interview with Graham Bensinger. The excerpt , which wasn't released when the first clips and quotes began to be circulated, relates to a squabble that emerged regarding the use by the Seahawks of fan-generated video from Broncos training-camp practices. It got ugly , as Macdonald told the story to Bensinger. It could get ugly between the Seahawks and Bensinger's camp. As we understand it, the conversation was not intended by Macdonald for public consumption. The Seahawks, we're told, didn't even know that portion of the "more off than on" the record discussion had been recorded until Tuesday morning. The situation is another reminder that everything is potentially on the record, absent a clear agreement between the parties that it's not. And while Bensinger's people didn't breach any journalistic rules by using it, the fact that it was posted could make future subjects more leery about agreeing to be interviewed. On or off the record, others are befuddled by Macdonald's decision to air gripes from two years ago. And there's a question as to whether the various things Macdonald said to Bensinger (regarding Payton and others) are the product of arrogance or naiveté. "What's the point?" said one source connected to neither the Seahawks nor the Broncos. "It was reckless." The Broncos declined comment on the situation. Undoubtedly, Payton will be asked about it when he conducts his usual Wednesday press conference. Either way, the kerfuffle adds a little extra sizzle to a spicy Week 6 Thursday night game between the two teams.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Jaxson Dart's injury could be season-ending
summary: MRI brings bad news for the Giants.
full_text: ' One day after an apparently serious injury to Bears starting quarterback Caleb Williams ended up being not nearly as bad as it seemed, an injury to Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart has turned out to be far worse than believed. Via NFL Network, an MRI showed that Dart's knee injury is worse than expected. He's now expected to be out an extended period of time, and possibly for the rest of the season. It's very bad news for a team that showed great promise in Week 1, and it moves Jameis Winston into the starting job. He struggled in relief of Dart on Monday night, completing 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception. The Giants have no other quarterbacks on the 53-man roster; Jake Haener is on the practice squad. Which means that the Giants will likely be scouring all available options for another player at the position — from free agency to a potential trade with a team that has a surplus at the position. Originally, it was believed that Dart had an MCL sprain. Coach John Harbaugh told reporters on Monday night that the injury was in that "neighborhood." Clearly, it wasn't.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Harbaugh gets another chance to consider Colin Kaepernick
summary: When Colin Kaepernick was being ignored by the NFL teams, he didn't have much to say.
full_text: ' When Colin Kaepernick was being ignored by the NFL teams, he didn't have much to say. Now that he's selling a book, interviews with Kaepernick are popping up everywhere. We haven't paid much attention to his various sit-downs and sound bites because, frankly, it's an old story. The NFL has long since moved on from Kaepernick, freezing him out long enough to make it unrealistic that the now-38-year-old quarterback would have a plausible path to a roster, a practice squad, or even a tryout. Still, one news item caught our eye in recent weeks. With Kaepernick's book tour putting him back in the vicinity of the front burner, Giants coach John Harbaugh told Ian O'Connor of The Athletic that Harbaugh wanted to add Kaepernick to the Ravens in 2017 . Through it all, Kaepernick got one workout, five years ago with the Raiders. With the Giants now desperate for quarterback help (and with Jake Haener and Brandon Allen as the most viable options behind new starter Jameis Winston), why not bring Kaepernick in for a look? Kaepernick continues to say that he's staying in shape, and that he wants to play. It should be immediately obvious whether he still has the abilities that made Harbaugh interested in him nine years ago. Harbaugh's New York staff includes Greg Roman, who was the offensive coordinator during Kaepernick's first four years in San Francisco. It would be easy, in theory, to configure the offense to fit Kaepernick. If Kaepernick still has the skills he had when he last played. It starts with a workout (and quite possibly ends with one). There's no reason not to give it a whirl. The anthem controversy has subsided. (Harbaugh and the Giants surely would want assurances that Kaepernick wouldn't dust it off, if he ended up on the sideline before games.) The threshold question is how does Kaepernick look? And there's only one way to find out. The Giants, who now face not having Jaxson Dart for up to the rest of the season, have plenty of reasons to give Kaepernick a chance to show them what he can do. It would be different if John Harbaugh hadn't recently spoken in such glowing terms about Kaepernick. With not many viable options available in free agency — and with Harbaugh having considerable power in New York — let's see if Harbaugh puts his recent words into current action.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Harbaugh on Jaxson Dart: Evaluations ongoing, no final decisions yet
summary: A report on Tuesday indicated Dart may miss the rest of the season with a knee injury.
full_text: Giants head coach John Harbaugh isn't ready to make any announcements about the extent of quarterback Jaxson Dart's knee injury. A report on Tuesday indicated that an MRI showed more damage than doctors initially believed Dart sustained early in Monday night's loss to the Rams and that he could be out for the rest of the season. Harbaugh spoke to reporters on a videoconference shortly after that report and said that the team is still working to determine next steps with their starter. "I’m not sure exactly what news or how anything’s been stated," Harbaugh said, via SNY. "Right now, evaluations are ongoing. We haven't got any final decisions yet, we've learned a lot more. I wouldn't want to share too much until decisions get made and that takes more than one person." Harbaugh said that the team has confidence in Jameis Winston, but Harbaugh said it's " pretty self-evident " that losing a starting quarterback is a big blow to what the team would like to achieve this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Giants could re-sign Brandon Allen as their third QB
summary: With Jaxson Dart's injury worse than expected, Jameis Winston will become the Giants' starting quarterback.
full_text: ' With Jaxson Dart's injury worse than expected , Jameis Winston will become the Giants' starting quarterback. The team, though, is in the market for a third quarterback. Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that the Giants could re-sign Brandon Allen. They have Jake Haener on the practice squad. Allen, 34, has spent five of the past six seasons with Giants quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan. He backed up Cam Ward with the Titans last season. Allen, though, struggled in three preseason games, going 26-of-38 for 224 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions. He has played 19 games with 10 starts in his career, completing 56.7 percent of his passes for 1,882 yards with 11 touchdowns and nine interceptions. He has made at least one start for the Broncos, Bengals and 49ers.
author: Charean Williams

title: Through two weeks, four starting quarterbacks have been injured
summary: The 2023 season featured more than a few serious quarterback injuries.
full_text: The 2023 season featured more than a few serious quarterback injuries. The 2026 season has started with four of 32 starters suffering injuries during the first two weeks of action. In Week 1, the Seahawks lost quarterback Sam Darnold for at least one game with a glute injury. (He could be back in Week 3.) In Week 2, Bears quarterback Caleb Williams pulled a hamstring and is week-to-week. In the late-afternoon window, Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow, again. On Monday night, Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart sustained what is believed to be an MCL sprain. More recently, the next man up in Chicago (Tyson Bagent) has landed in the concussion protocol . The situation highlights an ever-present risk when it comes to playing football. Quarterbacks get hit, in all sorts of ways — after weeks of practice in which they're insulated from contact. As Mike Tomlin said in Week 1, the inability to hit quarterbacks in practice put defenses at a disadvantage. The quarterbacks are at a disadvantage, too; they've gone from bubble wrap to fair game. On Monday's Let's Go! , North Carolina coach Bill Belichick (who is far chattier than he is during games ) suggested that limited padded practices make it harder for the blockers and, in turn, the quarterbacks. “The offensive line has really gotten shortchanged because they're not in pads very often," Belichick said. "Basically 20 times a year, 10 in training camp, 10 during the regular season. And I think 20 practices is just not really enough for those guys to develop their skills. And the defensive players are ahead of them and offensive lineman gets beaten and you know who's getting hit. And so I think one thing that would really help the situation would be some type of developmental program for offensive linemen who don't play. Not saying guys that have played 16 games, but talking about guys that don't play, that need that development coming into the NFL and type athletes they face and pass protection and blitz pick[up] and all that. It's so involved and so difficult that I think that would help the quarterback’s longevity as much as anything." Even with a highly competent offensive line, a quarterback is always one play away from taking a big hit, and possibly from being injured. And nothing can change a team's fortunes faster than losing their starting quarterback. UPDATE 9:10 p.m. ET : Actually, the number is five. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a concussion on the third drive of the Week 1 win over the Packers. Carson Wentz replaced Murray, who has been cleared for Week 3.
author: Mike Florio

title: Tua Tagovailoa returns to full participation at Falcons practice
summary: Tua Tagovailoa won't be starting for the Falcons on Thursday night, but he could suit up for the first time this season.
full_text: Tua Tagovailoa won't be starting for the Falcons on Thursday night, but he could suit up for the first time this season. The Falcons listed Tagovailoa as a full participant in practice on Tuesday for the first time since he suffered an oblique injury during a practice ahead of Week 1. The Falcons already announced that Michael Penix will make his 2026 debut as their starter against the Packers this week and Tagovailoa could be their backup ahead of Cooper Rush and Jack Strand. Rush started the first two games and Strand replaced him in the second half of Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Panthers. Defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring) was the only player listed as out of practice Tuesday. The Falcons also put cornerback A.J. Terrell (groin) on injured reserve earlier in the day. Cornerback Billy Bowman (Achilles), tight end Nick Muse (shoulder), right tackle Jawaan Taylor (rib), defensive end Brandon Dorlus (thumb), running back Brian Robinson (ankle), and defensive lineman LaCale London (hip) were listed as full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: UFL puts Houston and Birmingham teams in Rhode Island and Colorado
summary: Houston and Birmingham are out.
full_text: Houston and Birmingham are out. Pawtucket and Colorado Springs are in. The UFL announced on Wednesday that the teams moved from existing markets will be relocated to Rhode Island and Colorado for 2027. The spring league reiterated the plan to expand to 10 teams in 2028, with Utah and Oklahoma joining the operation. “2026 was an incredible year for the UFL, and seeing the response from our fans, players, and partners has made what comes next even more exciting,” UFL co-owner Mike Repole said in a press release. “There is a real energy around this league right now, and we’re thrilled to bring that energy to four new markets. We said in July that our next step was finding the right markets, venues, and fan bases where we can work with local leaders to build the strongest franchises for today and for the future, and we believe Colorado, Rhode Island, Oklahoma, and Utah represent those qualities. We’re thankful to the local leaders and partners who believed in this vision and have helped us get here. We can’t wait to see these markets come to life and the best part is that this is just the beginning.” Colorado will host its first game on Sunday, April 11st Weidner Field in Colorado Springs. Rhode Island gets its home slate rolling on Friday, April 2, at Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket. The nicknames, colors, and logos for the relocated teams will be revealed next month. Which means they won't keep the existing names that date back to the original USFL — the Gamblers and the Stallions.
author: Mike Florio

title: Reports: Austin Ekeler to work out for Panthers
summary: The Panthers will be without Jonathon Brooks for an extended period of time and they're set to kick the tires on a veteran running back as they work to fill out their backfield in Brooks's absence.
full_text: The Panthers will be without Jonathon Brooks for an extended period of time and they're set to kick the tires on a veteran running back as they work to fill out their backfield in Brooks's absence. Austin Ekeler will try out for the club on Wednesday, per a report from Aaron Wilson that has been confirmed by multiple other outlets. Ekeler has not played since tearing his Achilles while with the Commanders last September. Ekeler was in his second season with Washington after spending his first seven years in the league with the Chargers. He was a dual threat throughout his time with the Chargers, and peaked with 3,195 yards from scrimmage and 38 touchdowns across the 2021 and 2022 seasons. Brooks is expected to miss more than a month after having core muscle surgery. Chuba Hubbard and AJ Dillon are the other backs on the 53-man roster for Carolina.
author: Josh Alper

title: Michael Penix: Being healthy was my target, I feel I'm where I want to be
summary: Michael Penix is set to make his first start for the Falcons since last November when the team faces the Packers on Thursday night and the quarterback shared his excitement about that return during a press conference on Tuesday.
full_text: Michael Penix is set to make his first start for the Falcons since last November when the team faces the Packers on Thursday night and the quarterback shared his excitement about that return during a press conference on Tuesday. Penix had said in recent weeks that he felt close to getting back in the lineup, but not all the way back to where he needed to be to feel confident in playing. He said that changed late last week as lingering soreness went away and he was convinced it was time to get back on the field after "pushing it to the limit" in a workout and finding that the knee "responded good." Penix said that the timing of his return had nothing to do with having extended rest heading into Week 4 or because of how poorly the first two weeks have gone for the team. “Being healthy is what I was targeting . I was never no week-to-week thing," Penix said at a press conference. "It was being healthy. Whenever I felt like I can go out there, like I said, get out of all that soreness and get stronger each and every day, that’s what it was always about. Once I felt healthy, it felt like I was ready to go. . . . I’m never gonna sit out if I’m healthy. I knew I wasn’t where I needed to be the first two weeks and now I feel like I’m where I want to be, so that’s why you’ll see me up this week." Penix called it "very exciting when you make the final decision" and, given the way the offense has floundered through two games, he's likely not the only Falcons player excited about the change in plans for this week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Derrick Henry says Ravens weren't good enough, but not complaining about lack of carries
summary: The Ravens barely used Henry in the second half of their loss to the Saints.
full_text: The Ravens gave the ball to Derrick Henry nine times in the first quarter on Sunday against the Saints, and the last of those touches was a touchdown run that gave Baltimore a 7-0 lead. But as the game went on, Henry disappeared. Even though the Ravens were leading for most of the game, Henry was hardly getting the ball. In the fourth quarter, when the Ravens went from a 17-9 lead to a 24-17 loss, Henry only got the ball once. Overall, Henry finished the game with 16 carries for 68 yards and three catches for 19 yards. Henry wasn't complaining after the game about his lack of carries, but he did say the whole team needed to be better. “ We just weren’t good enough in the second half to win this game,” Henry said, via the Baltimore Sun . “We were put in a position to win this game. We just have to be better. We just weren’t good enough — at all.” Asked if Henry wasn't getting the ball because he was injured, head coach Jesse Minter said nothing was wrong with Henry. "Derrick was definitely himself," Minter said. Minter acknowledged the Ravens are going to need to get better at playing with a lead. “This team is going to have a lead [again],” Minter said. “We are going to continue to chase and learn from what happened in those situations. We will get better and put our guys in the best position to be successful given the circumstances.”
author: Michael David Smith

title: Alleged victim of Daejon Love says she reported him to 49ers in December 2025
summary: The 49ers have said, via information previously provided by an unnamed team source to Kalyn Kahler of ESPN, that they did not know about Daejon Love, who allegedly posed as a player on the team as part of an elaborate scheme, until the FBI contacted the 49ers in August 2026.
full_text: The 49ers have said, via information previously provided by an unnamed team source to Kalyn Kahler of ESPN, that they did not know about Daejon Love, who allegedly posed as a player on the team as part of an elaborate scheme, until the FBI contacted the 49ers in August 2026. One of Daejon Love's alleged victims says otherwise. Via Kahler, Gwen Herndon says she completed a “complaint/concern” form through the team's website on December 20, 2025. In the message, Herndon said "there is a federal investigation surrounding a man pretending to be a 49ers player," and she named Love. She also said he stole money from women and that "he is severely damaging the reputation of your team." "I wanted you to be aware of the situation and hopefully proactive in denouncing his involvement on your team," Herndon wrote to the 49ers. She said she received a response from Levis Stadium guest services one week later. "We take reports of individuals misrepresenting themselves as members of the San Francisco 49ers very seriously," the response said. "For safety and legal reasons, the team cannot comment on ongoing investigations or specific individuals. However, we appreciate you bringing this to our attention and encouraging proactive measures to protect the integrity of the organization. "If you have information that could assist law enforcement or legal authorities, we encourage you to contact the appropriate agencies directly. Our internal team will also monitor any instances of impersonation and take action as appropriate to protect fans and the team's reputation. Thank you again for your vigilance and concern for the Niners community." The 49ers declined to confirm to Kahler the existence of the exchange or to otherwise comment. Love and his alleged partner, Taylor Chan, were arrested on August 24. Authorities contend they defrauded more than two dozen women out of approximately $1.3 million. Last week, Kahler reported that the actual number of victims may exceed 60. Obviously, if the 49ers knew about Love, took no action, and the fraud continued until the arrests in August, that would be a problem for the team. While it may not create civil liability to anyone who was defrauded after December 20, 2025, it's a P.R. issue that would reflect very poorly on the organization.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones pushes back on idea of an expansion team in Europe
summary: In recent weeks, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has commented on multiple occasions regarding his "no doubt" belief that the NFL will have multiple teams in other countries — with Europe being the most likely destination.
full_text: In recent weeks, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has commented on multiple occasions regarding his " no doubt " belief that the NFL will have multiple teams in other countries — with Europe being the most likely destination . Cowboys owner Jerry Jones doesn't see that happening through expansion of the league. “ I don’t know about an expansion ," Jones said on 105.3 the Fan in Dallas, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing . "I see the games continuing like they are. And I see the ethos, if you will, of the game, the story of the game really expanding all over the world. But fundamentally, to have an expansion team, probably is pretty far. If it’s here, it’s in the future.” It's unclear whether Jones was expressing pessimism about an international presence generally, or specifically through expansion. Absent adding new teams, the only way to put teams in Europe or elsewhere would be to relocate existing franchises. (Good luck identifying teams that would be viable candidates to move.) Regardless, Goodell currently has more power than any one owner. And if Goodell sees an international team coming, it makes sense to take him seriously. For years, the NFL has dangled the possibility of a team in London as part of the effort to build interest there. More recently, the talk feels like something more than pandering to Europe. If it happens, it surely won't happen soon. At some point, however, the only way to truly export the passion that American fans feel for the sport will be to give fans in other countries a local team around which they can rally. London continues to be the most logical starting point, with one team playing home games at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and the other playing at Wembley Stadium. Since the merger in 1970, the NFL hasn't had a dramatic uptick in teams at one time. Two were added in 1976 (Buccaneers and Seahawks). Two more were added in 1995 (Jaguars and Panthers). The Browns returned in 1999, after the Browns became the Ravens, and the Texans rounded out the league at 32 in 2002. Twenty-four years later, the NFL is in the longest stretch in league history without the addition of a new team. At some point, it will grow. When it does, two new teams in London make the most sense.
author: Mike Florio

title: Brock Bowers is expected to make his season debut Sunday
summary: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers has not played since Dec. 21, 2025.
full_text: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers has not played since Dec. 21, 2025. He has played in a win since Sept. 7, 2025, in the season opener. The Raiders are 2-0 without one of their biggest stars. Bowers, though, is expected to make his 2026 debut against the Saints on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports. He had a meniscus trim procedure earlier this month after injuring his left knee in training camp. It's the same knee that sidelined him with a PCL sprain and bone bruise during the 2025 season. Bowers missed five games last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jonathan Owens, Simone Biles had their Porsche stolen in Chicago by "three men in masks"
summary: In March, linebacker Jonathan Owens left the Bears in free agency for the Colts.
full_text: '' In March, linebacker Jonathan Owens left the Bears in free agency for the Colts. Before Owens and his wife, gymnast Simone Biles, left Chicago, they found themselves the victims of a robbery. In a video posted Tuesday on social media, Biles said that " three men in masks came to our house and stole my Porsche" before they moved out of Chicago. The car was recovered. It's not clear when the theft occurred. And while some have interpreted Biles's quotes to mean that their home was invaded, that's not entirely clear from her video. Either way, it makes Owens the latest known NFL victim of a theft at his home. Owens, 31, has played for the Cardinals, Texans, Packers, Bears, and Colts. He has appeared in 84 regular-season games with 35 starts.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders-Cowboys delivers 27.3 million in late Sunday window
summary: A whole lot of people heard Tom Brady say "oh shit" and "piss missile" on Sunday afternoon.
full_text: A whole lot of people heard Tom Brady say " oh shit " and " piss missile " on Sunday afternoon. (Hey, if smoking weed on the air is fair game, anything goes.) title: Colts-Chiefs generated 24.3 million viewers, on average
summary: Based on the way the respective teams played in Week 1, many expected Sunday night's game between the Colts and Chiefs to be a snoozer.
full_text: Based on the way the respective teams played in Week 1, many expected Sunday night's game between the Colts and Chiefs to be a snoozer. Instead, it was an overtime thriller. The game attracted 24.3 million viewers on average for NBC and Peacock. The audience, which peaked at 27.4 million between 9:15 and 9:30 p.m. ET, made it the most-watched Week 2 Sunday night game since 2015. It was also the fourth highest figure for an overtime game in 21 seasons of Sunday Night Football on NBC. In that span, 22 Sunday night games have gone to overtime. author: Mike Florio

title: Adam Vinatieri sets Guinness World Record for the highest FG
summary: Adam Vinatieri isn't in the NFL record book for the longest field goal, but he now is the Guinness World Record-holder for the highest field goal.
full_text: '' Adam Vinatieri isn't in the NFL record book for the longest field goal, but he now is the Guinness World Record-holder for the highest field goal. The Hall of Fame kicker made a field goal from an altitude of 11,332 feet (3,434 meters) above sea level in the Swiss Alps on Tuesday. Vinatieri's record-setting kick took place at Jungfraujoch, known as the “Top of Europe,” on snow-covered ground with swirling winds. A Guinness World Records adjudicator was on hand to certify the achievement. “Snow is simply part of my time with the Patriots,” Vinatieri said, via a team news release. “But kicking a field goal at 3,454 meters is something completely different from anything I've ever done. You feel the altitude with every breath you take. Your heart rate is different. Your rhythm is different. And no one can really tell you beforehand how it will affect the kick, because no one has done this before. The fact that we were able to set the record under these conditions makes me very proud.” The event kicked off the Patriots’ countdown to their Nov. 15 game in Munich and celebrated Vinatieri’s legendary career. He last kicked in the NFL in 2019, retiring as the NFL’s all-time leader with 599 field goals.
author: Charean Williams

title: WR Brandin Cooks to sign with 49ers practice squad
summary: The 49ers are adding a veteran wide receiver to their practice squad.
full_text: The 49ers are adding a veteran wide receiver to their practice squad. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that they will sign Brandin Cooks. Cooks recently worked out for the Ravens, but he'll join a 49ers receiving corps that's been riddled with injuries. Demarcus Robinson sprained his ankle in Week 2 and Mike Evans suffered a hip injury in the win over the Dolphins. The 49ers were already without Ricky Pearsall, who is out for the season, and De'Zhaun Stribling, who will miss a couple of months after having ankle surgery. Cooks played for the Saints and Bills last season, and he was the intended target on the interception that helped the Broncos eliminate Buffalo in the playoffs. He's also played for the Cowboys, Texans, Rams and Patriots since entering the league as a Saints first-rounder in 2014. Cooks has 734 catches for 9,811 yards and 60 touchdowns over the course of his career.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Jets TE Mason Taylor week-to-week with thumb injury
summary: The Jets placed three players on injured reserve Tuesday and they may be missing another member of their offense for their Week 3 game in Detroit.
full_text: The Jets placed three players on injured reserve Tuesday and they may be missing another member of their offense for their Week 3 game in Detroit. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that tight end Mason Taylor is considered week-to-week due to a thumb injury. The Jets will release their first injury report of the week on Wednesday. Taylor started each of the Jets' first two games. He did not catch a pass in Sunday's loss to the Packers and his two catches in Week 1's win over the Titans resulted in a loss of two yards. First-round pick Kenyon Sadiq, Jeremy Ruckert, and Jelani Woods are the other tight ends on their 53-man roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jayden Reed back in Green Bay, "too early" to tell if he'll play again this season
summary: Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed has returned to Green Bay.
full_text: Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed has returned to Green Bay. Reed remained in a New Jersey hospital after suffering a neck injury in Sunday's overtime win over the Jets. Head coach Matt LaFleur said that Reed is still undergoing tests on the injury and that conversations about whether he'll play again this season will have to wait. “It’s way too early for that right now. . . . He’s got a lot going on," LaFleur said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com. Reed missed 10 games with injuries last season and signed a three-year contract extension this offseason. Reed was injured on the Packers' second offensive play of the game and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele was carted off on the next play. Bako-Bewele said on Tuesday that he will miss the rest of the year with a torn patellar tendon.
author: Josh Alper

title: Vikings add P Johnny Hekker, RB Jaret Patterson to practice squad
summary: With punter Brett Thorson set to miss some time with a hamstring injury, the Vikings have added a veteran punter to their practice squad.
full_text: With punter Brett Thorson set to miss some time with a hamstring injury, the Vikings have added a veteran punter to their practice squad. Minnesota announced the team has signed Johnny Hekker to the unit. Hekker, 35, spent the offseason program and training camp with Minnesota. He spent the 2025 season with Tennessee, averaging 46.8 yards per punt with a 40.3-yard net average. A four-time AP first-team All-Pro, Hekker has appeared in 229 career games for the Rams, Panthers, and Titans. A fake punt specialist, Hekker has also completed 15-of-26 career passes for 193 yards with a touchdown. The Vikings also signed running back Jaret Patterson to their practice squad and released receiver Trayvon Rudolph and cornerback Bryce Phillips from their practice squad.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Panic meter for every 0-2 team: Texans have been here before, Commanders on downward spiral
summary: Washington's nightmare start and Jayden Daniels' elbow injury send the Commanders to the top of our panic rankings
full_text:
You heard the same general concept from almost every coach of an 0-2 team after their loss this past weekend.
From Chargers coach John Harbaugh: "I'm not deterred. No one in that locker room is deterred."
From Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski: "We've got great resolve, we've got great resilience in that locker room."
From Titans coach Robert Saleh: "I've got a lot of faith in the group we have."
What else are they going to say? They don't believe in themselves or their teams?
Unfortunately, teams are what their records say they are, and beneath the belief that things will get better, there are some major, major concerns bubbling under the surface. It can start to get late early for some teams and, in turn, some coaches.
The popular stat is that from 2020 to 2025, only 16% of teams that started 0-2 made the playoffs, but what about the ones facing down the misery of not just an awful season but also larger developments? The seasons that set franchises back multiple seasons.
After Bryan DeArdo ranked every 0-2 team's chances of making the playoffs , today we detail the panic meter for every 0-2 team, ranking them from least panicked to most panicked, taking the big picture into account.
Miami knew this was going to be a rough season. There was a wholesale destruction transitioning into this season. Eight of the Dolphins ' nine largest cap hits this year are from players not on the team. We expected the Dolphins to have the least talented roster in the NFL and be among its worst teams -- at best. So far, they are living up to that.
Miami is 32nd in offensive success rate and 27th in defensive success rate. And yet much of this is by design. It's unfortunate, hard-to-watch design, yes, but this is what it was supposed to look like.
If anything, the Dolphins can be encouraged by several players from their 13-player draft class, which is far, far more important than any result. Caleb Douglas had 94 receiving yards in his NFL debut. Jacob Rodriguez leads the team in tackles, and Michael Taaffe is second. First-round cornerback Chris Johnson has a pair of pass breakups.
The Dolphins are in for a long, slow build. The word "panic" shouldn't enter their lexicon, even as the losses accumulate.
Like the Dolphins, the Falcons are in their first year under a new head coach. Unlike the Dolphins, there's a decent amount of talent on the team, talent that is frustratingly going to waste again. With Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr . out for the first two weeks, Cooper Rush looked unplayable, capping everything on offense.
But Penix will start Thursday, giving him yet another chance to prove he should be the answer as starter (even if the returns so far have been uninspiring). Atlanta has had a different Week 1 starter each of the last six seasons. And even if Penix isn't the answer, and Tagovailoa isn't either, there's not a lot of reason for panic. This was always going to be a gap year of sorts, given the quarterback situation. Yes, the Jalon Walker injury stinks, and James Pearce Jr . is suspended eight games, but there's no real panic. Bijan Robinson and Drake London are still here for the long haul.
If this were a "frustration meter" or even a "misery meter," the Falcons would be ranked higher. It seems like the same story every year in Atlanta. But panic? There's no panic here.
After Week 1, the Titans would have been much higher on this list. They looked downright awful in a 23-3 loss to the Jets , a performance that had Jordan Dajani saying, "In fact, it's fair to question if this is as bad as it has ever been."
It was much better -- though still not a win -- in Week 2, a 24-20 loss to the Eagles . Unlike Week 1, both the offense and defense looked competent, and they did so against a playoff hopeful with a talented roster. Most importantly, Cam Ward had some nice moments. Wow, isn't it nice when everything around a quarterback doesn't look completely broken?
There are no moral victories, but there is improvement, and the Titans showed the latter. It's a week-to-week league, of course, and another Week 1-esque performance would sound alarm bells. But for now, we can lay off Tennessee as a complete disaster zone.
This is a tough one. The case for the Texans panicking is ...
The case for the Texans not panicking is ...
The injuries are worrisome; they show how paper-thin the depth is at wide receiver, and guard Ed Ingram's absence was also noticeable in Sunday's 20-6 loss to the Bengals . The offensive line is worrisome, but it has been for a bit. At least this unit should have higher floor and ceiling heights. The Texans shouldn't be panicking whatsoever, but a divisional showdown against the Colts has quickly become nearly a must-win. Speaking of the Colts ...
On one hand, the Colts looked much, much better against the Chiefs in Week 2. On the other hand, they still lost, the defense still looks completely lost, and Alec Pierce suffered another injury.
Rather, the bigger cause for concern is that Shane Steichen was already perceived as a hot-seat coach , and Chris Ballard absolutely is (and has been) a hot-seat manager. Carlie Irsay-Gordon's comments at the end of last year made that clear as day. I'm of the opinion that Ballard is far more at fault than Steichen, especially given that the side of the ball he doesn't coach is arguably the worst in the NFL.
The Colts can't be any higher than this because Jonathan Taylor and the offensive line are excellent and should keep things at least somewhat on track. But potential rumblings about Steichen's and/or Ballard's jobs could throw things completely off course.
The Buccaneers' six-point loss to the Bengals was a missed opportunity, but not exactly an upset. The Buccaneers' loss to the Browns , though? It was a stunner. And even worse in terms of panic meter, Baker Mayfield -- extended at the 11th hour this preseason -- looks awful. Only Cooper Rush has more turnovers this season. He's running around and trying to make plays like he's still the Heisman winner at Oklahoma. The problem? It's 10 years and many, many injuries later, and Mayfield should know (and probably does know) he can't play like this:
SCOOP AND SCORE FOR THE BENGALS 🐅 📺FOX pic.twitter.com/gH62K5EdtZ
BRYAN COOKED. #TBvsCIN at 1:00 PM on Fox pic.twitter.com/J0ZyIeZs05
Meanwhile, the defense -- the side hot-seat coach Todd Bowles controls -- was really disappointing against the Deshaun Watson-led Browns. Watson had 238 passing yards, two touchdowns and zero turnovers one week after looking like an absolute disaster in the opener. First-round pick Rueben Bain Jr . has two pressures in two games, unfortunately casting a shadow over second-round pick Josiah Trotter , who looks awesome.
We don't even need to talk about how brutal the schedule gets for the Chargers -- and it gets really brutal -- if they can't beat the Cardinals or the Raiders . The offense is a train wreck. The defense is getting exposed now that former ace coordinator Jesse Minter is gone. It's all bad, and I wrote about it here:
For the offseason hype to go to in-season dread so quickly is so disappointing and, frankly, so Chargers. Justin Herbert has shown high-level stuff, and Mike McDaniel has shown high-level stuff. But the stylistic meld between the two just isn't happening, the procedural issues are all over the place, there are clear issues with the interior offensive line, Omarion Hampton keeps fumbling, and the entire offense falls apart without Ladd McConkey . Other than that ... it's going great!
In Week 1, the Commanders ' offense started slow, but the defense allowed them to hang around with the Eagles. It wasn't a win -- in fact, it was a major missed opportunity -- but it was a respectable showing.
Week 2 was a disaster. A panic-meter-shattering disaster. Jayden Daniels looked outstanding until suffering a dislocated left elbow , the same injury he suffered last year. Then the Cowboys sliced and diced the Washington defense en route to a 37-20 win, exposing the…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Ranking MVP candidates after Week 2: Josh Allen takes early lead, but a RB not too far behind
summary: Evaluating 10 players who have made a case for early MVP consideration
full_text:
It's only two weeks, but several players have made an early impression in the season-long race to win the NFL's MVP award.
The league's most prestigious individual award, the NFL MVP was first given out in 1957, with Browns ' legendary running back Jim Brown winning the title. It didn't take long for quarterbacks to monopolize the award, however, starting with Johnny Unitas, who in 1959 became the first QB to win the honor.
Quarterbacks have now come to define the award. A quarterback has won the award every year since Adrian Peterson won it in 2012 after nearly breaking Eric Dickerson's single-season rushing record. Only twice has a defensive player won the honor (Alan Page in 1971 and Lawrence Taylor in 1986). A receiver has never won league MVP, although Jerry Rice should have in 1987 when he caught 22 touchdown passes (an NFL record at the time) in 12 games.
Who will win league MVP in 2026? To find out, we're doing a week-by-week ranking of the candidates most likely to win the honor.
If the MVP vote happened today, Allen would be the winner . The 2024 league MVP, Allen is the first player in NFL history with five or more touchdown passes and three or more touchdown runs through the first two games. Allen has five touchdown passes and a league-high four touchdown runs while leading the Bills to impressive wins over the Texans and Lions .
Allen, who has yet to throw an interception this season, leads the NFL in adjusted yards gained per pass attempt (11.4). He enters Week 3 with a gaudy 125.8 passer rating.
If there was an award for the league's best free agency signing, Walker would be the front-runner. The reigning Super Bowl MVP has made an immediate impact on the Chiefs , who are off to a 2-0 start.
Walker rumbled for 173 yards and a score in Kansas City's Week 1 win over the Broncos . This past Monday night, Walker outrushed his counterpart, Jonathan Taylor (117 yards to 92 yards), while helping the Chiefs defeat the Colts in overtime.
In addition to his success on the ground, Walker has also been an asset for Patrick Mahomes as a receiver. He caught a touchdown pass in Week 1 and pulled down six passes for 61 yards against the Colts.
The league's reigning Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is once again making a case to become the first receiver to win league MVP.
Mired in a defensive duel in Week 1, Smith-Njigba was the difference in Seattle's Super Bowl rematch with New England. He caught eight of 11 targets for 122 yards and a score while leading the Seahawks to a 13-10 win.
Against the Cardinals in Week 2, Smith-Njigba found the end zone three times and tallied 155 yards on nine catches. His success so far is more impressive when you consider that he has been catching passes from Drew Lock after Sam Darnold sustained an injury early during Seattle's first offensive series of the season.
In helping lead the 49ers to a 2-0 start, Purdy has completed a league-high 80% of his passes. He's also thrown five touchdowns (against one interception) and leads the NFL in passing success rate (67.9).
Purdy has continued to play at a high level despite missing some of his top receivers due to injury. To help Purdy, the 49ers signed veteran wideout Brandin Cooks , one of just two players in NFL history (the other being Brandon Marshall ) to post 1,000-yard receiving seasons with four different franchises.
As long as he's healthy, Burrow — one of just two players in league history to win Comeback Player of the Year multiple times — should be in the MVP conversation all season. While he doesn't have the gaudiest numbers through two weeks, Burrow has led the Bengals to a 2-0 start, which is the most important stat.
In Week 1, Burrow completed 71.4 percent of his passes while outplaying his counterpart, Baker Mayfield . This past Sunday, Burrow overcame five sacks to throw a pair of touchdown passes in Cincinnati's 20-6 win over the Texans in Houston.
While it's been 40 years since a defensive player has won league MVP, Lloyd nonetheless deserves early consideration. The league's best defensive player through two weeks, Lloyd had 13 tackles in Week 1 and had a game for the ages this past Sunday against the Falcons .
In leading Carolina to a 34-3 win, Lloyd filled the stat sheet with two interceptions, an interception return for a touchdown, nine tackles, three pass breakups and a sack. He should be considered the early favorite for Defensive Player of the Year.
Cousins and the 2-0 Raiders are the NFL's biggest surprise story through two games. The 38-year-old Cousins threw three touchdowns in each of the Raiders' first two games and is tied for the league lead in touchdown passes. He leads the NFL in percentage of touchdown passes thrown when attempting to pass (10.2).
Shough has emphatically put last year's pre-draft concerns about him to rest. The 27-year-old, second-year quarterback is flourishing in Kellen Moore's offense. He leads the NFL in passing yards after nearly leading the Saints to a come-from-behind win in Week 1 and leading New Orleans to an upset win in Baltimore in Week 2.
Prescott's 2026 season is off to a hot start. The 33-year-old is completing a whopping 73.8% of his passes and is tied for the league lead in touchdown passes. During Sunday's win over the Commanders , Prescott passed Tony Romo as the Cowboys ' career leader in touchdown passes.
While Week 2 wasn't his best game, Henry still managed to rush for his fourth touchdown of the season, tied for the league lead. In Week 1, Henry chewed up the Colts' defense for 144 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries.
Henry edged out Amon-Ra St. Brown for the final spot on this list. Through two games, the Lions' prolific receiver is tied for the league lead in touchdown catches. He caught nine passes for 142 yards and two scores in last Thursday's loss to the Bills.

title: NFL Week 3 picks, odds: Josh Allen furthers Chargers free fall, Saints stay hot in home opener
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every agme on the Week 3 schedule, plus five locks against the spread
full_text:
If you have anyone in Chicago, D.C., or New York, check in on them. Hug them. Buy them a coffee (or maybe something stronger). They need a pick-me-up. Why? Because their quarterbacks all went down in Week 2.
Of course, there are varying degrees of severity when it comes to these injuries, with Caleb Williams ' hamstring seemingly the least severe, while Jayden Daniels (elbow) will miss time, and Jaxson Dart (knee) could miss the entire season. Some may be back sooner than later, but all of them will likely be sidelined for Week 3, which is our central focus here.
Those injuries (among others) have sent the odds ping-ponging in different directions, which adds a layer of difficulty to pinpointing our bets for the upcoming slate. Nevertheless, we'll plow through.
It's been a solid start to the season for us, owning a 16-16 ATS record overall and a 24-8 record straight-up. Last week, I went 7-9 ATS and 11-5 straight-up. When it comes to my five Locks of the Week, I rebounded with a 3-2 ATS mark in Week 2, which brings us to an even 5-5 ATS record through two weeks. Now, we try to move above .500 ATS, and that'll start with my five Locks of the Week for Week 3.
The Chargers feel like they're lost at the moment. They've dropped back-to-back games they should've won if we were looking at it solely from a talent standpoint. In fact, they are the first team ever to start 0-2, with both losses coming against teams that lost 14 or more games the previous season. And we're supposed to expect them to march into Buffalo and take down Josh Allen and the Bills ? Jim Harbaugh and the defense just let Kirk Cousins throw for 253 yards through the air and three touchdowns. Allen is on an MVP trajectory over his first two games, totaling nine touchdowns. He's a freight train, and it feels like the Chargers will be his next victim. Meanwhile, Justin Herbert hasn't shown much through the first two games. The offense is averaging 14 points per game, and Herbert is being pressured at the second-highest rate (46%) in the NFL this season, despite being blitzed at the fifth-lowest rate (23%). He's struggled mightily on throws that have traveled 10-plus air yards, throwing just one touchdown and three interceptions on such throws. This feels like it could get ugly.
Projected score : Bills 31, Chargers 20 The pick : Bills -7
I feel like Fredo Corleone by turning my back on the Jets like this. We backed them over the last two weeks (straight up in Week 1 and then ATS in Week 2), and they cashed both times. But like Paulie said in Goodfellas : "Now I gotta turn my back on you."
With this line sitting below a touchdown, we'll pounce on it in favor of Detroit. This is an offense that has put up at least 30 points in each of the last two games, and both contests turned into a track meet. While New York has been frisky this season (and I expect them to continue to be an ATS darling for the bulk of the year), I'm not sure Geno Smith and company keep up in this spot. Sure, this defense has allowed just 65.5 rushing yards per game over the first two weeks (second-lowest in the NFL), but that's come against backfields led by Tony Pollard and MarShawn Lloyd . Jahmyr Gibbs is a totally different animal, and I don't see that level of containment on the ground to continue.
The Lions ' shaky defense admittedly gives me some pause. They are giving up 35.5 points per game and 457.5 total yards per game through the first two weeks, which rank 31st in the NFL. But as I said, if this turns into a shootout, I like Detroit's chances with the slew of weapons they have, especially given the added rest after playing on Thursday. They are also 11-1 straight up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 home games following a loss.
Projected score : Lions 33, Jets 21 The pick : Lions -6.5
History will be made Sunday at Hard Rock Stadium. Since 1970, the Chiefs have not covered a single game in which they are a double-digit favorite on the road. In those prior 11 instances, they are 0-10-1 ATS. That changes in Week 3.
While Kenneth Walker III stole the show in Week 1, Patrick Mahomes is the one who really grabbed my attention. After a modest return in the season opener, where he still didn't look quite comfortable throwing the football, Mahomes was BACK against the Colts , completing 32-of-47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns. If Mahomes is getting closer to his old self, throwing the ball, and Walker provides a much-needed burst out of the backfield, it's hard to imagine the Dolphins having any chance of keeping this close.
Miami was nearly a two-touchdown (-13.5) underdog on the road last week against the Niners and couldn't cover, losing 35-13. Brock Purdy sliced up the Dolphins' secondary, missing just two of his 22 pass attempts on the day. Most of his production went to George Kittle (four catches for 80 yards and a touchdown), so you best believe Andy Reid will look to attack that same weakness with his star QB-TE duo of Mahomes and Travis Kelce .
Projected score : Chiefs 33, Dolphins 16 The pick : Chiefs -10.5
It's a bummer to see so many quarterbacks go down, especially Daniels. When he's been healthy, he's lifted the ceiling for a Commanders organization that desperately needed a shot in the arm. However, injuries have been an unfortunately large part of his story, and it rears its head again with this latest elbow dislocation. With Daniels sidelined, Marcus Mariota (who has lost six of his last seven starts) gets the nod, and I just have a hard time fathoming how the veteran can consistently put up points against this stellar Seattle defense.
The Seahawks come into this Week 3 matchup after allowing just 17 total points over the first two weeks, which is the lowest through two games by any team since 2013. They are also lights out on the road, winning 15 of their last 16 games away from Lumen Field. While Sam Darnold is planning to practice this week, I'm confident backing Seattle if it remains Drew Lock . He has filled Darnold's shoes admirably, including a three-touchdown showing in Week 3 (all of which went to Jaxon Smith-Njigba ).
Projected score : Seahawks 27, Commanders 17 The pick : Seahawks -7
Both the Raiders and Saints have been pleasant surprises to begin the season. Las Vegas is 2-0, which puts them multiple games above .500 for the first time since 2021. Meanwhile, the Saints have been one of the most potent offenses in the league through two weeks and just pulled off a notable upset over the Ravens in Week 2. Specifically, I think Tyler Shough is legit. The Saints quarterback was dynamite in the fourth-quarter comeback over Baltimore, completing 12-of-14 for 119 yards and a touchdown. He'll present the toughest challenge of the season so far for the Raiders, who beat up against a lackluster Dolphins team and a Chargers club that, as I mentioned above, is lost. There is real buzz for New Orleans to win the NFC South this season, and I expect that buzz to be palpable when the Saints open up Caesars Superdome for the first time after beginning the year with back-to-back road games.

title: Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks headed to IR, Austin Ekeler scheduled for workout
summary: Brooks has played in just five games over the last three seasons and will miss another six weeks with core muscle surgery
full_text:
Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks will undergo core muscle surgery and miss at least six weeks, the latest blow for the oft-injured former second-round pick, ESPN reports . Carolina will place him on injured reserve.
Brooks left the Panthers' 34-3 Week 2 win over the Falcons with what was deemed a groin injury, and after the game, he was seen walking with a heavy limp, according to ESPN .
Brooks suffered a torn right ACL in 2023, his final season at Texas. Still, he was the first running back drafted in 2024 (46th overall). He missed the bulk of his rookie year recovering from the injury, making his debut in Week 12. But just two weeks later, he re-tore his right ACL, which caused him to miss all of last season as well.
Brooks, 23, was expected to form a solid 1-2 punch in the Carolina backfield alongside Chuba Hubbard , though so far this season, Hubbard has been the clear top running back. He has 27 touches to Brooks' 11 and has played 68% of Carolina's offensive snaps to Brooks' 25%. One could make the case that the Panthers were hoping to bring Brooks along slowly after two consecutive devastating knee injuries, but now they will have to begin that build-up process again later this season.
The Panthers have already begun looking for outside help, with Austin Ekeler set to work out for them on Wednesday, according to KPRC2's Aaron Wilson . Ekeler, 31, is coming off his own devastating injury -- a torn Achilles early last year, when he was with the Commanders -- but he had a solid 2024 in Washington and is a proven pass catcher out of the backfield.
After Hubbard, the only other running back on the active roster is AJ Dillon . The Panthers also have Anthony Tyus III and Ahmani Marshall on the practice squad.

title: Predicting full 14-team NFL playoff bracket entering Week 3, including history-making Super Bowl
summary: The early postseason forecast includes several surprises, from two winless AFC South teams getting in to Carolina winning its division with a losing record
full_text:
The best part about making NFL playoff predictions early in the season is that everyone is still very much alive for the playoffs. For instance, just because a team is 0-2 doesn't automatically mean their season is over . As a matter of fact, of the eight 0-2 teams in the NFL right now, we project TWO of them to make the postseason.
That projection comes from our resident analytics expert, Stephen Oh, who simulated the rest of the 2026 NFL season to see how things will play out. For those of you who are not familiar with Oh's work, he's what you get when you put AI in a human brain.
With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.
With Patrick Mahomes coming off an ACL injury, our projection model wasn't quite sure what to make of the Chiefs going into the season, but after watching Kansas City jump out to a 2-0 start, the computer is sold on them. The Chiefs are now projected to get the No. 1 overall seed in the AFC. The more things change, the more they stay the same.
1. Chiefs (2-0) -- AFC West champion 2. Bills (2-0) -- AFC East champion 3. Ravens (1-1) -- AFC North champion 4. Texans (0-2) -- AFC South champion 5. Colts (0-2) 6. Broncos (1-1) 7. Bengals (2-0)
The biggest surprise in this week's projections is probably the fact that two 0-2 teams from the AFC South are projected to get in, but the Jaguars aren't. The Jags were in a virtual tie with the Bengals for the final wild-card spot, so the AFC South almost got THREE teams in.
In the NFC, the computer has the Rams finishing with the second-best record in the conference, but since Seattle is projected to finish with the best record, that means L.A. will be stuck playing in the wild-card round for the second straight year, according to our projection.
1. Seahawks (2-0) -- NFC West champion 2. Lions (1-1) -- NFC North champion 3. Eagles (1-1) -- NFC East champion 4. Panthers (1-1) -- NFC South champion 5. Rams (1-1) 6. Vikings (2-0) 7. 49ers (2-0)
The biggest change from last week is that the Panthers are now projected to win the NFC South. The computer views them as a slight favorite over the Saints , and the best part of this projection might be the fact that we have the Panthers winning the division with a record of just 7-10. Only two seven-win teams have ever made the postseason, and coincidentally, the last one was the Panthers in 2014, when they finished 7-8-1.
Also, the Bears are now projected to miss the playoffs following their Week 2 loss to Minnesota. It doesn't help that Caleb Williams could end up missing a game or two after injuring his hamstring in that game.
Now that we know who's in the playoffs, let's see who's going to make it to Super Bowl LXI.
And now, we're down to our final eight teams.
If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: Two teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Bills and Lions), the team that won the Super Bowl last year (Seahawks), and the team that has won two of the past four Super Bowls (Chiefs).
This is the second straight week the Seahawks have been projected to win it all, so the computer definitely likes what it's seeing from Seattle, even without Sam Darnold .
author: John Breech

title: Super Bowl stock report for Week 3: Bengals are total package, Chargers' season over before it started
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 2 and identify four upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
Overreactions to Week 1 often regress back toward preseason expectations in Week 2. The NFL has a way of leveling itself out. But for a few teams, it is quickly becoming hard to ignore early-season results, for better or worse. The Cincinnati Bengals are off to an ideal start, for instance, while the Los Angeles Chargers look far worse than anyone could have imagined. Their second games of the year only confirmed what they put on display in their respective season openers.
Both teams had reasons to believe at the start of the season that they could make dark-horse pushes toward the Super Bowl . The Bengals are two steps closer to that goal. The Chargers took two giant leaps in the wrong direction.
Elsewhere across the league, a litany of quarterback injuries reshaped the early-season pecking order.
Here is a snapshot of the Super Bowl race heading into Week 3.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
For too much of the Joe Burrow era in Cincinnati, the story has been that a leaky defense caps the ceiling of a high-octane offense. The first two weeks of 2026 squashed that narrative. The Bengals are now a complete team, and they look like a top-tier squad as a result .
The additions of Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen , Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook all paid dividends in the 2-0 start. Following a season opener in which the defense forced four turnovers, the unit held the Houston Texans out of the end zone and limited them to just 60 rushing yards. The Bengals proved in their first two games that they can win in different ways, first with a high-scoring effort against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and later with a grind-it-out 20-6 win over a Super Bowl hopeful.
None of this is at the expense of the offense, either. Ja'Marr Chase grabbed two touchdown catches against the Texans and hauled in an early contender for catch of the year. Joe Burrow is healthy and effective as usual, and the running game is in a good place with Chase Brown leading the charge.
This is the second consecutive year in which Cincinnati won its first two games, and things went off the rails in 2025. But there is reason to believe that this season will be different. If Burrow stays healthy, this team finally has all the pieces. The defensive personnel changes are difference makers -- ones that can help the Bengals get back to the Super Bowl.
The Chargers' stock was down considerably after Week 1 . Now it is in the basement. Their Super Bowl odds are more than twice as long heading into Week 3 as they were after the season-opening loss to the Arizona Cardinals .
The Chargers could have made the excuse that the Cardinals' defeat was one of those fluky results that always seem to pop up somewhere in the first week of the season. But since they followed it up with a loss to the Las Vegas Raiders , the underperformance can no longer be categorized as a one-off.
Losing twice by the exact score of 26-14 to two bottom-dwelling teams is bad enough in a vacuum. To do so in advance of a brutal seven-game stretch amplifies the desperation Jim Harbaugh ought to already be feeling. Every team the Chargers will meet between now and the middle of November has Super Bowl aspirations and, at the very least, should reach the playoffs. How can Los Angeles be trusted to win any of those games after dropping two contests by double digits to the potential last-place teams in the NFC West and AFC West?
This is a nightmare scenario for a team that was supposed to finally reach the next level. The pairing of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert has been a disaster. The defense regressed in its first two games without Jesse Minter at the helm. And in order to salvage the first month of the campaign, the Chargers have to right their wrongs on the road against the Buffalo Bills and Seattle Seahawks. That feels unachievable.
Through the first 36 minutes of the season, the New Orleans Saints had zero points and appeared destined for a Week 1 blowout loss. They did end up losing that opener to the Detroit Lions, but from the third quarter of that game through the end of the Week 2 win over the Baltimore Ravens, this squad outscored its opponents by a combined margin of 54-27.
The Saints are a two-point conversion away from being 2-0 with road wins over the Lions and Ravens. That is as impressive a two-game résumé as any in the wide-open NFC South. It continues to seem like the hot streak the Saints rode in the second half of last season was legitimate, and that with Tyler Shough under center, this team has its franchise quarterback .
Shough is the NFL's passing leader through two games with 662 yards, and that comes with a 68.9% completion rate, four touchdowns and another score on the ground. He just lost his left tackle to a severe high ankle sprain, but the rest of the supporting cast commands a ton of respect. When Jordyn Tyson gets healthy and makes his NFL debut, the Saints might even boast one of the league's best collections of skill position talent.
The schedule ahead is favorable, and if the Saints take advantage, the division should be theirs to lose.
Sunday, 8:15 p.m., NBC, stream on fubo
Both teams opened the year with clunkers but responded in Week 2. Now, one of them will fall below .500 for the second time this season. That is not where either was expected to be at the end of September, considering they are coming off playoff runs and hope to advance even further into the postseason this time around.
Sunday, 4:25 p.m., CBS, stream on Paramount+
Hopefully, the field conditions at Maracanã Stadium do not impact this game, because the matchup deserves better. Two electric offenses have a chance to put on a show in front of an international audience. It might come down to which defense can spring the most stops, and while neither is off to a perfect start to the year, the Baltimore Ravens' unit is the more promising unit. The loser will fall into a 1-2 hole and open the season in early danger of missing the playoffs again.
Sunday, 1 p.m., CBS, stream on Paramount+
The New England Patriots ' defense is off to a roaring start with just 16 points allowed in two games. The offense is still waiting for Drake Maye to wake up, though, and there is no guarantee that will happen until A.J. Brown returns from injured reserve. The Jacksonville Jaguars have lost consecutive games just once since 2024 and could put up a number New England cannot match in this contest between 1-1 squads.
Monday, 8:15 p.m., ESPN, ABC, stream on fubo
The Chicago Bears ' quarterback situation is bleak heading into "Monday Night Football." Caleb Williams is likely out with a hamstring issue , and with Tyson Bagent in concussion protocol , the Bears might have to turn to Case Keenum for a primetime showdown with the Philadelphia Eagles. That is an unenviable matchup for a third-string quarterback and a prime spot for the Eagles to improve to 3-0.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Prisco's Week 3 NFL picks: Browns upset Panthers, Giants rally behind Jameis Winston
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 3 picks, including Jaguars over Patriots and Bucs over Vikings
full_text:
The joys of a good Week 1 picking games turned into misery in Week 2.
So much for stacking good weeks.
I went 9-7 straight up, but a miserable 5-10 against the spread. Let's just hope that's the last bad week for a while.
My straight-up record for the season is now 21-11 and my ATS season mark is 15-17.
This week's slate has some big games, but also some where I think an upset will happen and I probably differ on the pick in those games than most.
I have Tampa Bay beating Minnesota and Cleveland beating Carolina. Those two games might be key to me getting back on track. One bad week is all I can take.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
This will be Michael Penix back in at quarterback for the Falcons , who badly need it. The Packers rallied to beat the Jets last week, thanks to the defense. That defense will play well here as well. Jordan Love gets it going if the banged-up line can hold up. I think they will.
Pick: Packers 27, Falcons 17
The Chargers are a disaster at 0-2 and playing bad football. Buffalo has played well in its 2-0 start. Can the Chargers contain Josh Allen ? I don't think they can, and Justin Herbert won't keep up in the Chargers' first road game. Bills take it.
Pick: Bills 32, Chargers 23
The Panthers are out on the road for the second straight week after blowing out the Falcons, while the Browns are playing their first home game. Bryce Young is rolling for the Panthers, but I think the Browns defense will play well again here as they did in Tampa last week. The Browns take it in an upset.
Pick: Browns 23, Panthers 20
The Lions will have extra rest here as they welcome in their former defensive coordinator, Jets coach Aaron Glenn. The Jets are playing better on defense, but this is a big challenge against the Lions' offense. The Detroit defense hasn't been good, but they will play better here with the lead to win it. But it's close.
These two both come in 0-2 and are in need of a victory. They can't afford to go to 0-3. The Colts ' defense has been bad, and the Texans ' defense hasn't lived up to the hype. But they will here. The Texans get their first victory as the offense comes to life against the Colts.
The Chiefs are 2-0, but this is their first road game. It won't matter. Miami is playing a lot of young players and building for the future. They won't win many games, and they won't win their first here. Look for a big day by the Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes .
Pick: Chiefs 28, Dolphins 10
The Titans are 0-2 and playing on the road for the first time this season. The Giants will be without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart , which means it's Jameis Winston time. He wasn't good in relief Monday night in the loss to the Rams , but he will be better here. Look for the Giants to rally around him in Dart's absence.
Pick: Giants 23, Titans 14
The Bengals are playing a second-straight road game after beating the Texans last week. The defense had a big day, and that will be the case here. The Steelers have been limited on offense so far, so look for the Bengals to play well again on that side of the ball as they go to 3-0. Joe Burrow and the offense should be better as well.
Pick: Bengals 23, Steelers 13
