author: Matt Severance

title: Sean McVay rips himself for Rams' Week 1 Australia travel plans: 'Sometimes you have a dumbass coach'
summary: McVay's team bounced back in a big way on Monday night
full_text:
Rams coach Sean McVay has emphatically -- and humorously -- taken accountability for his team's lackluster performance during its season-opening loss in Australia.
McVay's travel plans for that game -- arriving in Australia just 28 hours prior to kickoff -- backfired as Los Angeles was thoroughly outplayed by the 49ers , who rolled to a 27-7 win. McVay called himself out for that decision following Monday night's win over the Giants .
"Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn and sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that puts you in bad spot," he said.
"Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn and sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that puts you in bad spot." Sean McVay on the difference with the Rams between Week 1 and Week 2. pic.twitter.com/RjfnnGLuJn
During Monday night's game, ESPN broadcasters shared that McVay told them that he and his team simply had no energy during the loss to the 49ers, which was likely the byproduct of the travel schedule. In the immediate aftermath of the loss, however, McVay was hesitant to put too much blame on the travel while crediting the 49ers for their performance.
"I don't believe that's why we didn't play well enough," he said . "I really don't. I'm more than comfortable with that. I'll always make decisions that I think are best for the football team. It's easy in hindsight to be able to say it was a miss. But those are responsibilities that I'll take and then you try to be able to look at it. I'll always look at myself inside out and figure out where I can improve."
Regardless of why, McVay has obviously had a change of heart as it relates to the reasons behind his team's struggles in Week 1. On Monday night, however, the Rams looked much more like the team that was a popular preseason pick to win the Super Bowl .
The 28-6 win was highlighted by Matthew Stafford's four-touchdown performance, Davante Adams torching the Giants' defense to the tune of 195 yards and two touchdowns on eight receptions, and a defense that welcomed back the return of Aaron Donald , who made three tackles (including a tackle for loss) in his first game in nearly three years.
"Obviously we're happy about it," Adams said afterward . "We're thrilled to win, and any win in this league is one to celebrate. But when you look back, it's you're trying to be great and be a be a Super Bowl caliber team. You got to hold yourself to a high standard, and I think we can do a little bit better than we did."
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: NFL Week 3 picks and score predictions: Two undefeated teams go down, Broncos edge Rams in thriller
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks
full_text:
I don't usually want to write any team off after watching it play just two games, but guys, I'll be honest, I don't think the Dolphins are going to make the playoffs this year, and now that I'm looking at their schedule, I'm not sure they're even going to win a game.
I know we're only two weeks through the season, but I'm starting the 0-17 watch now.
If you're wondering how bad the Dolphins have been this year, just consider this: They're the only team that has yet to hold a lead in a game. Forget winning, they haven't even HELD A LEAD. We are heading into Week 3 and they have not been in the lead for even a single second this season. If you can't hold a lead, you can't win. That's how you end up 0-17.
That's a rough stat for Dolphins fans, but if you're a fan of the Falcons or Chargers fan, you can't laugh, because your team might be worse.
The Falcons haven't run a single play in the red zone this year. I don't know if they're doing red zone work in practice, but if they are, they can just skip over that this week and work on something else. It's almost impossible to go the first two weeks of the season without getting into the red zone a single time. As a matter of fact, the Falcons are the first team in 18 years to make it through the first two weeks without running a red zone play.
And then there's the Chargers.
The Chargers are the second team in NFL history to lose back-to-back games by double digits with both coming at home against teams that had a sub-.200 win pct the previous season. The other was the 1926 Racine Tornadoes (Oct. 10-17), who played just one more game before folding.
The Chargers have literally set football back 100 years. My takeaway from that stat is that the Chargers are essentially one game away from folding their franchise, and to be honest, that might be for the best.
So did I pick against the Chargers, Falcons and Dolphins this week? Let's get to the Week 3 picks and find out.
Actually, before we get to the picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . I get 1.7 cents every time someone clicks through on that link, so make sure to click early and often. But I also get docked 1.7 cents every time I get a pick wrong, so it all evens out.
Let's see how much I'm going to lose this week.
Somehow, a game between two WINLESS teams might be my favorite game on the schedule this week. Actually, now that I'm looking at the entire Week 3 schedule, this is probably closer to my fourth favorite game, but that's still pretty high for a matchup involving two 0-2 teams.
There's a good chance that the Colts and Texans are both actually good, but we just don't know it yet, because the NFL scheduling department threw them under a bus to start the season.
Out of these two teams, I'm probably more worried about the Colts. This team hasn't won a game since Nov. 9. They lost Alec Pierce to an injury in Week 2 and he won't be able to play this week, so that means the Colts' passing game will be taking a hit. This feels like a week where Jonathan Taylor is going to be getting a lot of work, but I'm not sure that's a good thing with the Colts about to face one of the best defenses in the NFL.
Not only does Houston have what should end up being a top defense, but this year, the Texans have the offense to go with it. I know, that seems like a crazy thing to say with the Texans coming off a game where they scored just SIX POINTS, but they shot themselves in the foot against the Bengals . They had a missed field goal, a separate botched field goal snap and a failed fourth-and-inches in Bengals territory. If one or all of those things go their way, it's a different game.
Although they struggled to score, they did just fine in Week 1 by putting up 31 points against the Bills . I'm starting to think C.J. Stroud found a time machine and went back and kidnapped the 2023 version of himself, because that's what he's looked like this year. He's thrown for 627 yards through two weeks, which is the third-highest number in the NFL, and a big reason that's happened is because he's been playing smart football. The Texans likely won't have Nico Collins this week, but Stroud didn't have him in Week 2 and he still managed to throw for 353 yards.
This is the third time in the past four seasons that the Texans have started 0-2 and on the previous two occasions (2023, 2025), they made the playoffs. I'm starting to think they're starting 0-2 on purpose.
PICK: Texans 27-24 over Colts
My favorite game to play every week is to try and guess who the Vikings ' starting quarterback is going to be.
The NFL is a quarterback-driven league, except in Minnesota. If the Vikings have proven one thing over the past 12 months, it's that they can win games no matter who's under center. As a matter of fact, with their win over the Bears in Week 2, they became the first team in NFL HISTORY to win four straight games with four different starting quarterbacks.
2025 -- Week 17 starting QB: Max Brosmer 2025 -- Week 18: J.J. McCarthy 2026 -- Week 1: Kyler Murray 2026 -- Week 2: Carson Wentz
At this point, they should just start someone new every week. I think Jimmy Garoppolo is available in free agency. Call him.
Actually, the Vikings don't need to call anyone and that's because Kyler Murray will be returning to the field on Sunday after playing just three possessions in Week 1.
Whether it's Murray, Wentz or anyone else, it almost doesn't matter who the Vikings have at QB because their defense is so dominant. This is a team that will happily win games 9-3, just like it did on Sunday.
The Vikings' defense is one of the best in the NFL: The unit is fun to watch and I'm not just saying that because one of their players celebrated a turnover in Week 2 by doing the "Hot Dog" dance.
I thought I recognized this dance 😂😂 @rodgers_isaiah | @Vikings pic.twitter.com/VOlNzijGV1
If you have a kid under five, the Vikings are now their favorite team just because of that celebration.
I trust the Vikings' defense more than almost any other defense in the NFL right now, but I think their offense is going to struggle in Tampa Bay. At 0-2, the Buccaneers ' season is essentially on the line: Over the past 30 years, no NFC team has started 0-3 and rebounded to make the playoffs. It's put up or shut up time in Tampa and if the Bucs don't win this game, they might start looking to see if there's any fine print in Baker Mayfield's contract to see if they can get a refund on his extension. I don't think NFL contracts work like that, but it doesn't hurt to check.
I think the desperate Bucs somehow find a way to pull off the upset here.
PICK: Buccaneers 19-16 over Vikings
For the first time ever, the NFL is playing a game in Rio De Janeiro and the best part about that is the fact that I now get to remind you about the time I played an extra in a movie that took place in Rio De Janeiro. I was a train passenger in "Fast Five" and my train in the movie was headed to Rio, but I'm not actually sure if it made it, because the train got blown up by Paul Walker and Vin Diesel.
I've seen every Fast and the Furious movie and as someone who played a key role in Fast Five, I can personally attest to the fact that it's the best one in the series https://t.co/4lQNomUGjL pic.twitter.com/BBopsqGeO1

title: NFL head coach hot seat rankings: Jim Harbaugh on thin ice in Week 3 after Chargers' 0-2 start
summary: The Buccaneers' Todd Bowles claims the top spot, while Aaron Glenn and Dan Quinn also face questions after uneven starts
full_text:
We're merely two weeks into the 2026 regular season, but the stumbling out of the gate is rampant for some teams. Things have gone so sideways for a few coaches that the temperature under their seats is rising. Of course, every coach entered the season with varying degrees of job security, and some (like Bengals coach Zac Taylor) have been able to cool things down with a solid start. Others have not been as fortunate, and those are the unlucky bunch that we'll be highlighting here.
Have things reached a fever pitch to the point that a change could be imminent? No. We probably have a few weeks before anything definitive happens, as organizations typically let the first month play out before making any decisions about staff. For instance, Matt Rhule was fired by the Carolina Panthers after Week 5 of the 2022 season. Robert Saleh was also fired by the Jets after Week 5 of the 2024 season.
However, that's not to say that things aren't uneasy around the halls of various facilities. So, with that in mind, let's roll out and rank the seven coaches who have the hottest seats in the league after Week 2.
LaFleur may have found himself higher on this list had it not been for his Packers rallying late to beat the Jets in Week 2. Even in the winning effort, they weren't that impressive. In fact, Green Bay became the first team in the Super Bowl era to win a game with under 200 total yards, 10-plus penalties, and zero turnovers (teams were previously 0-38). This lackluster showing (albeit in a win) also comes off the heels of blowing a 22-10 second-half lead to the Vikings in Week 1, where they were outscored 22-0 in the fourth quarter. It just hasn't looked right.
Part of that can be attributed to not having two key pieces of their roster: pass rusher Micah Parsons (on injured reserve) and running back Josh Jacobs (commissioner's exempt list). Parsons could be back by mid-October as he continues to recover from his ACL tear last season. Meanwhile, it's unclear what Jacobs' status will be. Even accounting for their absences, it still looks clunky. They play the Falcons on Thursday to begin Week 3, which should be an opportunity to put together a second straight win as they open up Lambeau Field. Their Week 4 matchup is also favorable against the Bucs (road), so they could conceivably come out of the first month 3-1. That would alleviate a lot of pressure for LaFleur (who signed an extension this offseason), especially with reinforcements possibly on the horizon.
Houston finds itself at 0-2 to begin the season, but that's become a relatively familiar place under Ryans. This is the third 0-2 start in Ryan's four-year tenure as Texans coach. Despite those shaky starts, they've ended up making the playoffs in every season with him at the helm, so maybe this is just what they do. That said, there are some red flags surrounding the organization. Namely, the offense got next to nothing from the rushing attack in their Week 2 loss to Cincinnati. They rushed just 18 times for 60 yards. While the backfield did score three total touchdowns in Week 1, it still wasn't an efficient day.
The biggest concern, however, is the defense (Ryans specialty) not delivering the same lockdown performances we saw from them in 2025. The unit surrendered 36 points to Buffalo in Week 1 and then 20 to the Bengals on Sunday. Houston let both Josh Allen and Joe Burrow throw for at least two touchdowns and zero interceptions. That matched its total from all of last season. If the defense under Ryans regresses, overcoming the early-season losses may not happen this time around. And if they miss the playoffs, that could open the door for change.
Carlie Irsay-Gordon was quite clear in her end-of-season press conference at the conclusion of the 2025 campaign that if this current group didn't start putting together wins, they'd be gone. Well, we're two weeks into the 2026 season, and the Colts have yet to put a notch in the win column. Indy's defense has been sliced and diced throughout the first couple of weeks. First, the Ravens dropped 41in the season opener, with Derrick Henry accounting for three rushing touchdowns. Then, on Sunday night, Patrick Mahomes carved them up to the tune of a 33-30 overtime win. Through two games, the Colts' defense has given up 1,029 total yards and is allowing 37 points per game. That's not going to cut it.
Beyond the poor numbers defensively, there have also been some in-game coaching lapses. Against the Chiefs in Week 2, after Laquon Treadwell caught a 48-yard pass to put the Colts at the K.C. 17-yard line, Shan Steichen and the offense balked. They ran it with Jonathan Taylor on back-to-back plays that traveled -3 yards. Then, on third-and-13, Daniel Jones scrambled for a 5-yard gain. They then opted for a 38-yard field goal to simply tie the game. If I'm Irsay-Gordon, I'd want them to be more aggressive in that spot. They didn't make one throw to the end zone and, given how the defense had been playing, should've tried to win the game right then and there with a touchdown.
The Colts have a divisional matchup with the Texans in Week 3 before heading to London to face the Commanders . If they head back to the United States still without a win by that point, everything could be on the table.
Quinn may get the benefit of the doubt because of Jayden Daniels ' elbow injury, but the start of the 2026 season has been pretty rough for the head coach. The franchise is 0-2 for the first time since 2019 and is now just 2-12 over their last 14 games played. To make matters worse, this 0-2 start has come against NFC East teams, digging them into an early hole in the division race.
Quinn is a defensive-minded coach, and the unit has shown little improvement in the first couple of weeks this season. The 30.5 points allowed per game are the fourth-highest in the league. Meanwhile, opposing quarterbacks have averaged a league-high 137.1 passer rating against this Washington secondary. The Commanders are one of just three teams that have yet to generate a turnover. Again, this is supposed to be Quinn's specialty, so seeing deficiencies here is jarring.
Then, there are some befuddling coaching decisions. For instance, Quinn should have probably taken the points against Dallas right before the half and opted for a field goal. That would've cut it to a 17-13 Cowboys lead at the break, with Washington getting the ball to start the third with the chance to take the lead. Instead, he kept the offense on the field for the third-and-goal attempt from the Dallas 1-yard line and couldn't convert. To add insult to injury, that was the play on which Daniels suffered the elbow injury.
Coming into the season, the Chargers were the sexy pick to win the AFC West and even to come out of the AFC. The theory was that they were getting their star offensive tackles back and that new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel would supercharge Justin Herbert . Through two games, it's been an unmitigated disaster. Los Angeles has dropped to 0-2 and has lost to what was thought to be inferior competition. The Chargers lost the opener to the Arizona Cardinals in the biggest Week 1 upset, then fell to the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. The McDaniel-led offense has been stagnant, averaging just 14 points per game, while Herbert has thrown three interceptions and has an off-target rate of 13%.
The Chargers are the first team ever to start 0-2, with both losses coming against 14-plus loss teams from the previous season. Going back to last year (including playoffs), L.A. has now lost five straight games. That's the first five-game losing streak of Jim Harbaugh's coaching career ( NFL or NCAA). The Chargers are averaging just 10 points per game over those contests.
It won't get any easier for Harbaugh either. Over the next seven games, the Chargers will play five teams that won a playoff game last season ( Bills , Seahawks , Broncos , Rams and Texans). The only two who did not win a playoff game that they'll see over…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: How Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss can buck the trend of short starting QBs in NFL
summary: The Ole Miss star is lighting up college football at just under 6 feet, but changing NFL defensive schemes means his path to pro success will look different than those before him
full_text:
The 2018 quarterback draft class will go down as a historic one for a number of reasons. It produced multiple MVPs, a Super Bowl champion, and a PFWA Rookie of the Year, none of whom were the same person. It was also the start of an interesting trend that's swept through the NFL ever since - the shorter quarterback. From the AFL-NFL merger announced in 1966 up until the 2018 draft, only one quarterback shorter than 6-foot-3 went No. 1 overall. That quarterback was Michael Vick in 2001, and it's safe to say it wasn't his work as a passer that got him drafted there.
Then came the 6-foot-tall Baker Mayfield . Fresh off a Heisman campaign at Oklahoma, the Browns made Mayfield the No. 1 overall pick in 2018 over the likes of 6-3 Sam Darnold (No. 3 overall), 6-5 Josh Allen (No. 7), 6-4 Josh Rosen (No. 10), and 6-2 Lamar Jackson (No. 32). While not a bad athlete by any means, Mayfield was being coveted purely because of his passing ability in a frame that had never been coveted that highly before. The early returns were gangbusters as he broke the rookie passing touchdown record with 27.
Mayfield's overnight success greenlit the Cardinals to draft his even shorter former Sooners teammate, Kyler Murray , No. 1 overall the very next year, and the floodgates were opened at the position. Then came 6-0 Tua Tagovailoa in 2020, 5-10 Bryce Young in 2023, and 6-1 Caleb Williams in 2024 - the stigma around using premium picks on shorter quarterbacks was gone.
But should it be? That conversation is coming back into the mainstream because the best quarterback in college football through three weeks is the 5-11 ⅞" Ole Miss signal caller, Trinidad Chambliss. This is nothing new, as Chambliss showed out in relief of Austin Simmons all last season and through the playoffs - only losing to Miami in the semifinal after putting up the most points anyone had scored vs. the Hurricanes all season (27).
If Chambliss were 6-foot-4, this wouldn't even be a conversation. It would have been a serious debate for the Raiders on whether to pick Chambliss or Fernando Mendoza last spring - that's how good his tape was against top competition. But he's not. Chambliss would be the fourth-shortest quarterback in the NFL if he hadn't gotten clearance for a 6th-season last winter:
Kyler Murray and Bryce Young
Brock Purdy , Sam Howell and Baker Mayfield
Unfortunately, that's not great company to keep at the position, as that list has not been known for its consistent success in the NFL. In fact, the one common denominator amongst the group seems to be their inconsistency - especially over the past few seasons. I don't think that's a coincidence, but rather part of a larger league-wide trend.
You see, when Mayfield and Murray entered the NFL, it was the age of the spread offense. 11 personnel was the norm as offenses tried to air it out at all costs. The NFL is cyclical, though, and defenses steadily found answers for themselves. That ushered in the era of 2-high shells, nickel base defenses, and amoebus blitzing front-sevens. It's that last trend that I believe has given shorter quarterbacks the most problems. The sightlines for a 6-foot quarterback when facing only four down linemen with four split wide receivers are a heck of a lot different than having to face seven standup rushers posted along the line of scrimmage. Just look at Kyler Murray's immediate post-snap picture on his interception Week 1 (and then how ugly the throw looked).
Keisean Nixon intercepts the first pass of the game GBvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rV7m8xe3TQ
That is a throw from someone who did not see a darn thing behind the line of scrimmage.
How this relates to Chambliss's prospects is difficult to say for several reasons. The first is that it only takes one team to fall in love with a player to take him highly. The second is that Mayfield, Tagovailoa, Murray, Purdy, and Young are all objectively among the top 32 quarterbacks in the NFL. Sure-fire starters, but not top-10 starters.
Finally, and most importantly, Chambliss is his own quarterback coming into the league at a different time. Not only are his strengths and weaknesses different from all the other short quarterbacks above, but he's also faced a different college football landscape than those quarterbacks did as well. The transfer portal and NIL era have raised the level of play at the upper echelons of college football. Those same defensive trends that are occurring in the NFL are also happening across the SEC. Chambliss is not only more experienced than all those guys at 24 years old, but his weekly tests are preparing him far more than those of the guys who came before him.
So how can Chambliss buck the trend? By staying the same fearless quarterback he is now. The biggest thing that separates Chambliss from the other short quarterbacks is his tools and confidence in the pocket. Chambliss has comparable arm talent to Baker Mayfield, with much more horsepower as a runner. Physically, he's more similar to prime Russell Wilson than any of the short quarterbacks today.
Trinidad Chambliss arm talent reel Spins it so consistently. We can argue about his ceiling at his height, but this is a starter in the NFL pic.twitter.com/Y2KdX7pguD
Like Wilson, he has elite escapability and playmaking outside the pocket. Unlike end-of-career Wilson, though, Chambliss is more than willing to hang in when his pockets get tight and deliver downfield. That's a skill that's been missing for quarterbacks like Bryce Young and Kyler Murray, but kept someone like Brock Purdy afloat as a starter. Chambliss has a lofty 11.7-yard average depth of target this season under pressure and has taken only three sacks on 29 pressured dropbacks. Being willing to attack downfield while not taking sacks under pressure is a great combination to have at the position.
So, how high should the NFL draft Trinidad Chambliss? If we didn't see another snap from every quarterback in this draft class, the No. 1 overall pick wouldn't be too high. That's more an indication of his floor than his ceiling, but you can't watch what he's done to top-notch defenses the past season and not think he can at least join the likes of Mayfield and Purdy in the NFL. The good news is we'll have nine more regular-season games, and likely more after that, to reach a conclusion on Chambliss. If he keeps passing test after test, chances are NFL evaluators will look the other way when the measuring stick comes out at the Combine in Indy.
author: Mike Renner

title: Ranking 0-2 teams by playoff chances: Why Texans are best positioned to recover
summary: Only 12% of teams to start 0-2 since 2002 have reached the playoffs
full_text:
Each 0-2 NFL team faces an uphill battle. Only 12% of teams to begin 0-2 since 2002 have made the playoffs, according to USA Today . Only three teams in NFL history won the Super Bowl after starting 0-2: the 1993 Cowboys , 2001 Patriots and 2007 Giants . The 1996 Patriots also went to the Super Bowl after starting 0-2.
The '93 Cowboys won it all after Emmitt Smith (that year's league and Super Bowl MVP) returned from a two-game absence amid a contract issue. The '01 Patriots started the franchise's two-decade-long dynasty after Tom Brady replaced an injured Drew Bledsoe. The '07 Giants made history by denying the Patriots the chance to become the NFL's first 19-0 team.
Will any of this year's 0-2 teams follow suit? Below is a ranking of the winless teams entering Week 3 from least to most likely to reach the postseason.
Let's be honest, the odds of Miami making the playoffs this season are as likely as in their 2019 "Tank for Tua" campaign. If there is a sliver of hope, it's the fact that six of the Dolphins ' next seven games are against teams that did not make the playoffs in 2025.
For Miami, this season is about building the foundation under new coach Jeff Hafley and new GM Jon-Eric Sullivan. When looking at the rest of their schedule, the Dolphins have potential winnable games against the Jets , Lions (who gave up 71 points in their first two games) and the Chargers . It's possible that the Dolphins could give the Vikings a scare in Week 4 if Kyler Murray struggles in his initial games back as Minnesota's starting quarterback.
While it was a loss, Sunday's game against the Eagles is evidence that the Titans are starting to turn a corner under Robert Saleh. Tennessee matched the Eagles score for score and took the lead with under two minutes left before Jalen Hurts delivered the game-winning touchdown pass with 14 seconds left.
Following an underwhelming loss to the Jets in Week 1, the Titans were a vastly improved team in Week 2. Cam Ward had an efficient game and was complemented by a running game that tallied 122 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries. Defensively, the Titans recorded three sacks and forced two turnovers that included a 92-yard interception return by Amani Hooker that set the first of Ward's two short touchdown runs.
Jayden Daniels ' latest injury -- and the uncertainty surrounding his possible return -- has compounded Washington's 0-2 start. One positive from Daniels' injury, however, is that it does not appear to be season-ending.
Another positive for the Commanders is that they have a solid backup quarterback in Marcus Mariota , a fellow former No. 2 overall pick whose career includes a playoff win as the Titans' starting quarterback. During his time with Washington (which dates to 2024), Mariota -- the 2014 Heisman Trophy winner -- has thrown 15 touchdowns against seven interceptions and has completed 64.1% of his passes.
Atlanta's hopes for a playoff push were bolstered by Monday's news that Michael Penix Jr . will make his season debut in Week 3 (Thursday night against the Packers ). The Falcons ' offense struggled during its first two games and are the only unit that has yet to enter the red zone.
If Penix can provide a spark to the Falcons' offense, it's possible that Atlanta can claw out of its current predicament. The Falcons have the NFL's top-ranked run defense and arguably the NFL's best running back in Bijan Robinson . They also play in the NFL's most winnable division in the NFC South.
Like the Titans, the Colts' performance (albeit in a losing effort) in Week 2 is reason for optimism. After a listless performance in Week 1 (a 41-23 loss to the Ravens ), the Colts took the Chiefs to overtime on Sunday night on the strength of an offense that put 30 points on the board.
The Colts lost Alec Pierce during the game with a heel injury, but in his absence, Josh Downs stepped up with 72 yards on seven catches. Indianapolis still has one of the league's best running backs in Jonathan Taylor , who ran for 92 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday night. The Colts also play in a winnable division in the AFC South.
The Colts' defense, however, will need to play better moving forward if they want to make a playoff run. Indianapolis surrendered 506 and 523 yards in its first two games, respectively.
The Chargers' first two games were ugly, and their upcoming schedule is daunting. That being said, Chargers fans still have reasons for optimism, starting with the fact that Jim Harbaugh guided Los Angeles to the playoffs in each of his first two seasons.
Los Angeles also still has one of the NFL's best quarterbacks in Justin Herbert , an emerging player in running back Omarion Hampton (who ran for 94 yards and a score in Sunday's loss to the Raiders ) and a defense that -- like its offense -- is currently top 10 in the NFL in red zone efficiency.
The Chargers' playoff hopes may depend on how quickly new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel can find a rhythm with Herbert and Co.
There's no sugarcoating it. The Buccaneers ' first two games were bad. Tampa Bay beat itself in Cincinnati in Week 1 by committing four turnovers, and lost on Sunday at home to a team (the Browns ) and a quarterback ( Deshaun Watson ) that have had virtually no success in recent years.
It is worth noting that Tampa Bay lost both games by a combined 10 points and could have won either. The Buccaneers' offense took better care of the ball in Week 2 and is ninth in the league on third down. Tampa Bay's defense is seventh in the red zone through two games.
Let's start with the fact that the Texans were in this exact spot last year. In fact, Houston started 0-3 last year before winning 12 of its final 14 regular-season games. Houston then recorded a win in the AFC wild card round for the third straight year.
Houston is once again 0-2, but Texans fans can take solace in the fact that their team just played two very formidable opponents in the Bills and Bengals . Four of Houston's next five games are against 2025 non-playoff teams.
While Week 1 wasn't their best outing, the Texans still boast one of the NFL's best defenses. They also reside in the mediocre AFC South, which they won during C.J. Stroud's first two seasons.
Speaking of Stroud, he played well in Week 1 but wasn't as good on Sunday without Nico Collins , who is expected to miss this Sunday's game against the also-winless Colts.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Prisco's NFL Week 3 Power Rankings: Bengals catching fire behind revamped defense, Bills just behind Seahawks
summary: Pete Prisco shares his latest Power Rankings of the 2026 NFL season, and let the debate begin
full_text:
The same refrain has been heard a lot since Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow started lighting up NFL opponents:
If he only had a defense. He does now.
The Bengals are 2-0 after beating the Houston Texans on the road Sunday, but that game wasn't about the flashy passing game, although Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase made some special plays, but rather about a revamped defense.
They limited the Texans offense all day in the 20-6 victory, doing so with a dominant defensive front that had four sacks and spent the day in the Texans backfield. It was just the third time that the Bengals have kept a team without a touchdown since coach Zac Taylor took over.
That front also had a key fourth-down stop when defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence stopped running back David Montgomery on a fourth-and-1 at the Cincinnati 18 in the second quarter. The Bengals traded a first-round pick for Lawrence this year, and so far, that move is paying off in a big way.
They also added defensive tackle Jonathan Allen and pass rusher Boye Mafe to help that front. Young players like Shemar Stewart , Cedric Johnson — two sacks Sunday — and rookie Cashius Howell give them some real edge pop to go with those veterans. If the Bengals can be a top-15 defense, they have a real chance to be a Super Bowl contender. This defense is giving up 16.5 points per game, which ranks tied for eighth right now, and they are tied for first in sacks with eight.
The Bengals are up to fourth in my Power Rankings this week as they prepare for a division game at Pittsburgh against the Steelers . The Bengals are the only team in the AFC North that is still undefeated.
The Seattle Seahawks stay in the top spot after beating Arizona, with backup quarterback Drew Lock playing well. But the Buffalo Bills are right behind them with Josh Allen off to an MVP start.
The biggest shock after two weeks is where some supposed contenders are in these rankings. The Texans, Chargers and Bucs are all 0-2 and looking up at a lot of teams ahead of them. None of those teams can afford to fall to 0-3 this week, or they might be done.
As for the bottom, the Miami Dolphins stay there after getting beaten up on the road by the San Francisco 49ers . The good news is they play their home opener this week. The bad news is they play the unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs .

title: Arizona Cardinals fall in new 2026 power rankings
summary: For one week, we all thought the Arizona Cardinals were going to prove a lot of people wrong. Then week two of the 2026 NFL season happened and a humbling loss to the defending Super Bowl champions that saw the Arizona Cardinals offense produce 127 yards with the starters in 58.5 minutes of game time […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Mike LaFleur of the Arizona Cardinals looks on from the sidelines during a game against the Seattle Seahawks at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images For one week, we all thought the Arizona Cardinals were going to prove a lot of people wrong. Then week two of the 2026 NFL season happened and a humbling loss to the defending Super Bowl champions that saw the Arizona Cardinals offense produce 127 yards with the starters in 58.5 minutes of game time made us wonder… maybe they are better, but only slightly? Well, the reality might be that they are better but not anywhere close to being ready for the big time, at least the big time in the NFC West. We will hopefully know more at the end of this week, but we pulled power rankings from five different sites to see what they are saying after two weeks of Arizona Cardinals football. ESPN: 26 The first two weeks have already been a roller coaster for Brissett, who threw for 277 yards in Week 1 but only 95 on Sunday against the defending Super Bowl champions. His body of work since he became Arizona’s starter in Week 6 last season is solid. He ranks No. 1 in completions and attempts, No. 2 in passing yards, No. 4 in completion percentage over expected and No. 5 in passing touchdowns. His performance Sunday was vastly different than the last time he played Seattle, when he threw for 258 yards and two touchdowns in a blowout loss in Week 10 last season. B/R: 27 Any belief that Arizona could be a surprise playoff contender likely dissipated after Sunday’s crushing loss against the rival Seattle Seahawks. Arizona’s defense managed to keep the game close early, but it fell apart in the second half, while the Cardinals’ offense struggled throughout the contest. CBS Sports: 26 Reality hit them in the mouth in the loss to the Seahawks after the upset of the Chargers. Their offense has to be better throwing the football. Pro Football Talk: 24 They may find out the hard way that the Chargers are just really bad. The Athletic: 26 The first-round running back is only playing about 40 percent of the offensive snaps. That could be due to his preseason ankle injury, but it won’t take Cardinals fans long to get restless if that number doesn’t increase. Love has 20 carries for 70 yards and five catches for 25 yards through two weeks. The rankings are all pretty consistent. Not among the three worst teams, but in that next pack of five teams. Let’s hope a strong showing against the Niners changes some thoughts.

Falcons injury report Full • CB Billy Bowman Jr. (Achilles) • QB Michael Penix Jr. (knee) • TE Nick Muse (shoulder) • QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) • DE Brandon Dorlus (thumb) • OL Jawaan Taylor (rib) • RB Brian Robinson (ankle) • DL LaCale London (hip) Limited • N/A Did Not Practice • DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring) Packers injury report Full • CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) • WR Bo Melton (neck) Limited • CB Brandon Cisse (teeth) • OL Anthony Belton (elbow) • DT Anthony Campbell (ankle) • LB Edgerrin Cooper (shoulder) • DT Javon Hargrave (knee, concussion) • OL Donovan Jennings (hand) Did Not Practice • OL Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) • OL Aaron Banks (knee, toe) • DT Warren Brinson (calf) • WR Jayden Reed (neck) As mentioned above, we had quite a few updates for the Falcons following Tuesday’s practice. full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Robert Longerbeam (37) looks on after the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Atlanta already lost Tyler Goodson to the NFC East this season after the Cowboys swiped him off their practice squad. Now the Falcons are returning the favor, sort of, by poaching a practice squad player from another NFC East team. With A.J. Terrell on injured reserve , Atlanta’s taking Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Robert Longerbeam from Philly’s practice squad and adding him to the 53 man roster. We’ll see what the corresponding move is sometime in the next 12-24 hours. Longerbeam is unlikely to play much in Week 3, but gives Atlanta a developmental option with some real upside. The former Rutgers cornerback was a playmaker in college who flashed real coverage skills and boasts quality physicality, but isn’t the biggest corner and missed all of the 2025 season with an injury after the Ravens drafted him in the sixth round in the 2025 NFL Draft. Baltimore risked waiving him after a quality summer and lost him to the Eagles, and now the Falcons will get a closer look at him. The hope is that he’ll be able to contribute as a reserve sooner than later for Atlanta, which for now will roll on with a top three of C.J. Henderson, Mike Hughes, and Avieon Terrell, with Billy Bowman Jr. set to debut soon as well. It’s a very worthwhile gamble for this football team.

The Falcons are now 0-2 and dealing with some injuries, so we will take a look at the first injury report of the week. Falcons injury report Full • CB Billy Bowman Jr. (Achilles) • QB Michael Penix Jr. (knee) Limited • OL Jawaan Taylor (knee) • DE Brandon Dorlus (thumb) • TE Nick Muse (shoulder) • RB Brian Robinson (ankle) • QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) Did Not Practice • DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring) • CB A.J. Terrell, which kept him out of practice even though he was eventually able to play on Sunday. This week, Terrell is now dealing with a groin injury which caused him to leave the Falcons’ Week 2 game agains the Carolina Panthers. We will be monitoring this closely as groin issues are known to linger, and with the team having a short week, I wouldn’t be too optimistic with Terrell playing on Thursday. We will see though. Some positive news, Michael Penix Jr. has officially been announced as the starting quarterback for the Falcons. He has been able to practice fully in practice and was cleared to play a few weeks ago. The Packers also held no practice on Monday, so their injury report is a team estimation. The most notable injury of theirs is receiver Jayden Reed who is a longshot to play this week. Although the report says he has an injured neck, ESPN’s Adam Schefter is reporting that it’s actually a back injury for Reed. Regardless, the way they are talking about the injury, I would expect him to miss the game on a short week.

summary: The Panthers and Saints grab their first wins of the season, while the Falcons and Buccaneers quest for a W continues. full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 20: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is sacked by Mason Graham #94 of the Cleveland Browns during the second quarter of the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Panthers and Saints grab their first wins of the season, while the Falcons and Buccaneers quest for a W continues. The division’s young quarterbacks are making a case that their time is now. Are the Buccaneers already feeling buyer’s remorse, and will the Falcons ever reach the red zone? Here’s the Week 2 NFC South Review. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-2) Week 2 Result: Buccaneers 19 – Browns 23 Week 3 Opponent: Minnesota Vikings The Buccaneers are a volatile product, as they’ve always been during the Bowles-Mayfield era, but things feel different this year. Mayfield has only thrown for one touchdown across two games, and Tampa Bay is 0-2 for the first time since 2024. Bowles’ defense couldn’t hold off a second-half surge from the Browns, and unlike most seasons, Tampa Bay isn’t dealing with a laundry list of injuries. If this team can’t get a win soon, Todd Bowles could find himself unemployed before the season ends. The Buccaneers will host the 2-0 Vikings, who will have Kyler Murray under center after he cleared concussion protocol Monday. New Orleans Saints (1-1) Week 2 Result: Saints 24 – Ravens 17 Week 3 Opponent: Las Vegas Raiders "And the @Saints turn out the lights on the Ravens here in Baltimore!" – Spero Dedes on the Lamar Jackson INT pic.twitter.com/x6R3QjITJG — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) September 20, 2026 The Saints scored 15 unanswered points in the 4th quarter, delivering an upset on the road in Baltimore. Tyler Shough is looking like the quarterback he was hyped up to be all offseason. The offense has shown its potential in the first two weeks, but the defense deserves credit for keeping the Ravens offense in check in the second half. Chase Young has been off to an impressive start, and if this defense can keep playing complementary football, this team will be a force in the division. The Saints return home to host the red-hot Raiders, who are 2-0. Carolina Panthers (1-1) Week 2 Result: Panthers 34 – Falcons 3 Week 3 Opponent: Detroit Lions Bryce Young continues to torment the Dirty Birds. He delivered another cerebral performance, escaping pressure with ease and consistently finding the open man. After building a quick lead, the Panthers defense stuffed the Falcons in a locker. Devin Lloyd was all over the field, racking up a sack, two TFLs, two interceptions, and a touchdown. There is a Cooper Rush/Jack Strand tax applied here, but credit to the Panthers for taking care of a weaker opponent the way a good team should. They’ll host the Lions in Charlotte, who are desperate to turn their 0-2 start around. Just a few plays from Devin Lloyd on Sunday. Genuinely, this was one of the best linebacker performances I've seen. The way he mirrors and funnels to the RB in the first clip is great. Good patience to read and attack the angle route from Bijan as the hook-curl defender, and he… pic.twitter.com/bHs6Jlogpw — Jared Feinberg (@Jared_NFLDraft) September 21, 2026 Atlanta Falcons (0-2) Week 2 Result: Falcons 3 – Panthers 34 Week 3 Opponent: Green Bay Packers The Falcons lost by 30 and were shut out in their first 2025 matchup against the Panthers. This Sunday they lost by 31, but hey, they got on the board this time. This offense is a disaster, and this defense already looks stretched thin after two games. Tommy Rees is struggling, and his offense has more than personnel problems; it’s schematically inept. Special teams hasn’t looked sharp, and fans have a right to worry that their 41 year old kicker has lost his touch. It’s a short week for the Falcons, who travel to Green Bay Thursday for their first of three consecutive primetime games. Pray for America. Two weeks isn’t enough time to make concrete proclamations, which is good news for the Falcons and Buccaneers. There’s still plenty of time to recover, but if things don’t get back on track for the 0-2 teams, the Saints and Panthers could make this a two-team race by mid-season.

title: Ravens news: Lamar Jackson among NFL’s most-pressured quarterbacks
summary: Welcome to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of all of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover Lamar Jackson’s way-too-high pressure rate through two games, a few mitigating factors for the team’s offensive collapse vs. the Saints, and Let’s dive in! Lamar Jackson begins 2026 season among NFL’s […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - SEPTEMBER 20: New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young (99) holds onto Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) for a sack during a NFL football game between New Orleans Saints and Baltimore Ravens September 20, 2026 at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, MD (Photo by Charles Brock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of all of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover Lamar Jackson’s way-too-high pressure rate through two games, a few mitigating factors for the team’s offensive collapse vs. the Saints, and Let’s dive in! Lamar Jackson begins 2026 season among NFL’s most-pressured QBs Pass protection has been the undoing of the Ravens offense for multiple years, and the first two weeks of the 2026 season prove that old habits die hard. The unit has been excellent in the run game, ranking first in ESPN’s win rate and second in PFF’s grading , but they fall to 30th and 32nd in each service’s respective pass-blocking metrics. Plenty of other teams have disparities of their own, but none are nearly as severe as Baltimore’s. As a result, Lamar Jackson has been feeling the heat to start the season. He has faced pressure on 41.2% of his dropbacks ( via Next Gen Stats ), the sixth-highest rate in the league. And despite different collection methodology, Pro Football Focus also ranks the two-time MVP as the sixth-most-pressured quarterback in the league: NFL quarterbacks facing the highest pressure rates through Week 2 – Mark Chichester (Pro Football Focus) 6. Lamar Jackson, Baltimore Ravens 42.6% pressure rate | 47.1 PFF grade under pressure | -0.280 EPA per play under pressure Jackson has faced pressure on 42.6% of his dropbacks, the sixth-highest rate among qualifying quarterbacks. His results in those situations have been mixed: His 8.6 yards per attempt under pressure ranks sixth among 32 qualifiers, but he has taken five sacks and produced two turnover-worthy plays. Jackson’s 6.5% turnover-worthy play rate ranks 10th-highest at the position, helping drag his production down to -0.280 EPA per play despite his ability to generate yardage when pressured. Next Gen Stats has Jackson producing -0.31 EPA/play under pressure, again aligning with PFF’s numbers and indicating a major drop-off in his performance in such situations. He struggled last year due to his injuries, but in 2023 and 2024, he ranked among the league’s best passers against pressure – and that is without accounting for his scrambling ability. There are schematic elements at play here. The Saints countered the Ravens’ under-center offense with linebacker blitzes that closed the distance to Jackson while his back was turned and disrupted Baltimore’s rhythm. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle and offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford can be better-prepared for similar strategies in the future, while Jackson and his blockers will have to sharpen up their pre-snap adjustments at the line of scrimmage. If center Jovaughn Gwyn continues to struggle in pass protection, the Ravens may consider inserting veteran Ethan Pocic into the starting lineup to stabilize the middle of the unit. What is your biggest concern coming out of the Ravens' Week 2 loss to the Saints? | Baltimore Beatdown Derrick Henry won’t solve all of the Ravens’ late-game problems Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 3 – Ben Solak (ESPN) The Ravens never entered salt-the-clock mode against the Saints because they never got to that game state. They weren’t up by two scores in the fourth quarter. They lost Zay Flowers (and Ja’Kobi Lane ) at wide receiver, and left tackle Ronnie Stanley left the game in the third quarter (toe) after struggling against Chase Young . The Saints were also run-blitzing in the second half in an effort to take Henry out of the game plan, and coordinator Declan Doyle had some good calls to beat those looks, but pass protection failed across the board… …Could the Ravens have funneled more runs to Henry? Sure. The larger issue is that they never put the Saints to bed in the bulk of the game; the Ravens were too lacking in talent on offense, and defensively, their dam burst as the Saints made second-half adjustments. I still like the Ravens from a season-long perspective, but this is a growing team. The Ravens get an unbelievable soft stretch of defenses over the next three weeks (Cowboys, Titans and Falcons) with a potential return of Flowers. This is good soil from which to grow confidence and cohesion on offense. Are you confident the Ravens are headed in the right direction? | Baltimore Beatdown Rio field conditions still under question NFL intends to proceed with Ravens-Cowboys in Brazil, but field will look bad on TV – Mike Florio (Pro Football Talk) On Sunday, the Ravens will face the Cowboys at Maracaña Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Despite concerns regarding the quality of the field, the NFL does intend to proceed. It’s our current understanding that the game is “likely” to happen as scheduled. If/when it does, expect the field to not look great on TV. Also, it will be very important for the teams to get early access to the field so that the players will be able to make the right decisions about footwear for the game.

title: Ravens Reacts Survey: biggest concern heading into Week 2
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country. After a complete victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1, the Baltimore Ravens looked disarrayed in all phases of their Week 2 to the New […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens runs and hurdles with the ball against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country. After a complete victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1, the Baltimore Ravens looked disarrayed in all phases of their Week 2 to the New Orleans Saints. It’s no surprise that a new head coach and a first-time offensive play-caller are facing some early-season bumps. What matter is their response. Past Ravens squads faced similar issues and stayed stuck in neutral for some, if not all of the season. Sunday’s defeat in Baltimore exposed a number of flaws. In this week’s Ravens Reacts survey, we want to know which one is the biggest concern for the Ravens moving forward. Here’s the case for each: OL pass protection: The Ravens’ new-look offensive line has yet to find their footing in front of Lamar Jackson, who has been one of the league’s most-blitzed and -pressured quarterbacks through two weeks. Baltimore also owns the NFL’s worst team pass-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus . This has been the downfall of the offense for multiple years; Doyle and offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford to get the unit settled in as quickly as possible. 3rd down defense: Minter’s defense held the Colts to a 4-for-11 mark on third and fourth downs in Week 1, but the Saints went 10-for-16 on Sunday. Part of the issue came on first and second down, when quick completions by Tyler Shough would keep New Orleans ahead of the sticks. Baltimore had numerous opportunities to stop the bleeding and get off the field in the second half, but they could not dig their heels in for a stop. After Trey Hendrickson and Mike Green wiped out a third-quarter drive with a pair of sacks, the pass rush did not get home for the rest of the game. That is not quite “being the best when the best is needed.” Special teams: Anthony Levine’s units took care of business in Week 1 with a number of chunk returns, solid coverage, and perfect days from kicker Tyler Loop and punter Ryan Eckley. But in Week 2, Loop had a 49-yard field goal blocked, Eckley averaged just 41.3 yards per punt with zero inside the 20-yard line, and the Ravens lost the field position battle on returns and coverage. Beatdown’s Zach Canter noted a potential nine-point swing as a result of special teams miscues that should simply not happen with this roster’s talent and coaching. Injuries: The Ravens’ depth is already being tested by early-season injuries. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley played through his toe injury for more than half of Sunday’s game, but he eventually gave way to backup Carson Vinson. The 2025 fifth-round pick had his hands full with Chase Young, who was instrumental in helping the Saints defense close out the game. Wide receiver Zay Flowers missed the entire matchup with a hamstring injury; there were certainly times in the second half he would have made a difference. Now, it’s your turn! title: Ravens vs Saints: the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
summary: In what was supposed to be the welcome party for a new era of football in Baltimore, Ravens fans were instead treated to an all-too-familiar sight of a fourth-quarter collapse in their home opener. There was still some good, definitely some bad, and a lot of ugly, so let’s get into it: The Good Rashod […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints is knocked out of bounds by Malaki Starks #24 and Tavius Robinson #95 of the Baltimore Ravens in the fourth quarter of a game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what was supposed to be the welcome party for a new era of football in Baltimore, Ravens fans were instead treated to an all-too-familiar sight of a fourth-quarter collapse in their home opener. There was still some good, definitely some bad, and a lot of ugly, so let’s get into it: The Good Rashod Bateman: People will focus on the last play of the game, but I’m not going to blame Rashod Bateman for the game-sealing interception. Lamar Jackson clarified that Bateman ran the correct route, which the veteran receiver confirmed himself. Instead, I’m going to focus on what was good. The Ravens needed at least one receiver to step up with Zay Flowers and Ja’Kobi Lane down, and after a quiet Week 1, Bateman produced like the top target. With seven catches for 88 yards and a touchdown, Bateman showed exactly what made him a first-round pick so long ago: top-tier elite route running and the ability to create space. His career hasn’t gone how anybody would have wished, especially after his massive foot injury, but he can still get open at will in the NFL. He was wide open on the 3rd and 1 questionable deep shot to Chris Moore as well. Rashod Bateman 7 receptions for 88 yards Stemming off at the top of his routes, head fakes and selling his cuts. Finding soft spots in zones and sitting down. Got friendly to the qb. pic.twitter.com/xY3f0LDtqc — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) September 22, 2026 Mark Andrews: Mark Andrews also stepped up on a day when the Ravens needed pass catchers too with a solid six catches for 49 yards. His peak explosiveness is behind him, but he is still a favorite safety valve for Lamar Jackson and seems to be exactly where he needs to be when needed most of the time. Trenton Simpson: Simpson was by far the most eye-popping defender against the Saints. While he didn’t blow up the stat sheet – only six total tackles and one tackle for loss – he was everywhere on the field and seemingly involved on every single play. Whether he made the tackle or not, it felt like Simpson was wherever the ball was and laying big hits on blockers and ball carriers all day. I can’t wait to see how Minter turns him into a chess piece hunter when Teddye Buchanan comes back, and Simpson’s athleticism can be freed up even more. Who is turning pass rush wins into pressures (PFF). Had to bump up the snap minimum because Trent Simpson broke the chart (second image) https://t.co/YJNG4mIjmW pic.twitter.com/noFRzRbCXK — Shaun Newkirk (@Shauncore) September 21, 2026 Edge rushers: Though Baltimore’s defense largely struggled on Sunday, the team’s stable of edge rushers did flash during the game. All three of the sacks came from each of the top guys in the room. Trey Hendrickson pressured Tyler Shough all day despite his club-covered broken finge and rnotched his first sack as a Raven. Tavius Robinson got his second sack of the season to go along with a tackle for loss, continuing his hot start to a contract year. Mike Green also got involved after a quiet game last week, hunting down Shough for his first sack of the season along with two tackles for loss and two quarterback hits. Green’s sack came two plays after Hendrickson’s to force a three-and-out in the third quarter, flashing the game-altering ceiling of this group. After an uneventful rookie season, Mike Green finally had some flashes of the guy we saw at Marshall on Sunday pic.twitter.com/1mQWNzc4Rf — Mike Renner (@mikerenner_) September 21, 2026 Devontez Walker: It was only one play, but it was exactly what we know and expect from Tez Walker at this point. With the Ravens backed up at their own 11-yard line, Lamar Jackson launched a bomb for Walker down the field for a 49-yard gain. Walker was inexplicably not targeted the rest of the game afterwards, something I’m sure the coaching staff is probably regretting at this point. Hopefully we see him more involved in the future. Now that Bateman is being used and Walker is healthy, this could be a well-rounded top three wide receiver group once Zay Flowers returns. The Bad Pass protection: It was an issue last week, it was an issue this week, and it will probably continue to be an issue going forward as the offensive line grows and gels together. After being one of the better rookies in the league last week, Vega Ioane struggled next to center Jovaughn Gwyn against the Saints. While the total pressure rate was less than last week, it felt like New Orleans consistently converted those pressures into negative plays for the offense. Defensive coordinator Brandon Staley countered the Ravens’ shift to a more under0center offense by blitzing up the middle a ton into the A-gap, which is hard for a quarterback to handle when he turns his back for play-action. It’s something the offensive line should expect to see a ton going forward from other teams, especially until they prove they can consistently handle it. Luckily, to my eyes, it seemed like the pressures and losses on the line were more from miscommunications and not correctly filling their assignments rather than just a lack of talent and losing hand fights. These kinds of errors are to be somewhat expected when you have two guys who are starting in the NFL for the first time and should improve. According to PFFs preliminary charting, Lamar Jackson was pressured on 36.8% of his drop backs. Which is actually less than last weeks 46.7% of dropbacks. The blitz rate was roughly the same around 45% of dropbacks. Vega Ioane led the team with 4 pressures allowed. Gwyn allowed… — Cole Jackson (@ColeJacksonFB) September 21, 2026 Penalties : The one thing that I won’t give grace on for the offensive line is the penalties. Through two games, the Ravens offense has been flagged 12 times, but even more frustratingly, half of them are pre-snap penalties, and another two are simple errors you can avoid. Four false starts, two illegal shifts, an ineligible man downfield, and a chop block. They have got to get it fixed. Referees: I won’t do this often because every team deals with it, but similar to the first Pittsburgh game last year, this one was filled with weirdness from the referees. The entire sequence at the goal line during New Orleans last drive was down right bad. It was fairly obvious to most viewers that Tyler Shough made it into the end zone on his first push attempt that was called short. Then on his second attempt, the refs both missed a facemask and then called Shough in when every angle of the camera showed that he wasn’t in. It almost felt like the refs kept the touchdown on the board because they saw they missed the facemask despite Shough’s body being short of the line. There were also two massive phantom holding calls called on the Ravens. Chris Moore had one that was iffy that eliminated a 12-yard scramble for a first by Jackson. The more egregious one was a non-existent holding call on Jaylin Hawkins during a failed two-point attempt that gave the Saints another try that certainly altered the game. The refs were bad. But, again, this is not unique to the Ravens, and they shouldn’t have put themselves in this situation to begin with. The Ugly Fourth quarter: I don’t know what it is. But the players on the Baltimore Ravens have some sort of mental hurdle they need to clear when the fourth quarter starts. The defense allowed 15 points in the fourth quarter alone, and the offense only scored three points in the entire second half, none in the fourth quarter. They’ve been statistically the worst defense in the NFL since 2018 during the fourth quarter in one-score games. They have no idea how to consistently kill an opponent on either side of the ball. They’ve done it occasionally over the years – like…

The Ravens open Week 3 as three-point favorites over […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 22: Quarterback Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys hugs quarterback Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens after agame at AT&T Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images High expectations for the Baltimore Ravens’ home opener gave way to a disappointing 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints. Next up, the team is heading to Brazil to take on the Dallas Cowboys, who are fresh of a dominant 34-17 victory over the Washington Commanders. The Ravens open Week 3 as three-point favorites over the Cowboys ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ). Dallas is technically the home team in this matchup, and their internationally-recognized brand could give them more supporters in the stands of Maracaña Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. But will that be enough to constitute a home-field advantage when both teams are traveling to another continent and playing in an entirely foreign stadium? The matchup is further complicated by reports of poor field conditions from Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio and A to Z Sports’ Mauricio Rodriguez . The NFL has downplayed those concerns, but both teams could wait until they assess the field in person before making decisions on players dealing with injuries, especially those affecting lower body parts. The Ravens did not have wide receiver Zay Flowers (hamstring) on the field on Sunday, and left tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe) left the game and did not return. Returning to the field after months away on an international trip with a questionable playing surface could also be a tough ask for defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) and Teddye Buchanan (knee). The Cowboys entered the season relatively healthy outside of a thumb injury to left guard Tyler Smith that landed him on injured reserve. But in their first two games, they have already lost three defensive backs: cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and safeties Malik Hooker (arm) and P.J. Locke (foot). Those absences could quickly place Dallas’ secondary under the microscope against a Baltimore passing game that ranks third with 8.3 yards per play and ninth with +0.16 EPA/dropback. title: Ravens news: NFL downplays concerns about Brazil field conditions
summary: Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of all of the latest news and analysis regarding the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover recent concerns about field conditions for the team’s upcoming trip to Brazil, early-season concerns after Sunday’s loss to the Saints, and the officiating pool report on Tyler Shough’s controversial game-winning […]
full_text: This general view shows players on the pitch during the Copa Libertadores quarter-final second leg football match between Brazil's Flamengo and Ecuador's Independiente del Valle at the Maracana stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on September 17, 2026. (Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of all of the latest news and analysis regarding the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover recent concerns about field conditions for the team’s upcoming trip to Brazil, early-season concerns after Sunday’s loss to the Saints, and the officiating pool report on Tyler Shough’s controversial game-winning touchdown. Ravens’ Week 3 trip to Brazil to proceed as planned Multiple reports over the weekend raised concerns about the field conditions at Maracaña Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, where the Ravens are scheduled to take on the Cowboys next Sunday. Members of CR Flamengo, the home soccer team, have criticized the playing surface, but NFL field director Nick Pappas said on Monday that there are “no concerns right now.” NFL: ‘No concerns’ over field conditions in Rio for Cowboys-Ravens – Jamison Hensley (ESPN) ‘Look, there’s the realities of managing any playing surface and then there’s also the realities of managing a grass playing surface that’s being used midseason,” Pappas told ESPN on Monday. “So it’s all about monitoring it. It’s all about having a plan in place and then being able to react to anything that maybe comes our way.’ Pappas added, ‘So what we’ve seen in Rio is a significant amount of rainfall, a record kind of rainfall over the last six weeks. And that obviously poses challenges just from a management perspective, but nothing that we’re not capable of managing or prepared to take.’ Ravens-Cowboys in Brazil ‘full speed ahead’ despite field concerns, Stephen Jones says – Jeff Howe, Mike Jones and Dan Pompei (The Athletic) ‘I don’t have concerns only because the league has said full speed ahead. … I think if there was a real concern, there would have already been contingent plans being made,’ [Cowboys co-owner Stephen] Jones said. ‘I know how the league works, about where we play the game if it weren’t there, and there’s none of that. So, I think we’re full speed ahead.‘ ‘Whatever work needs to be done on the field to make sure that it’s safe and great for our players, no one understands that more than the league, that we’ve got to have great surfaces and great playing fields that are very safe for our players. As far as I’m concerned, we’re full speed ahead and we’re ready to go to Rio.’ Let’s be realistic here. The NFL has invested heavily in expanding football’s international appeal. It would take something extreme for the league to change their plans for a game featuring one of the most recognizable teams in the world and one of the sport’s biggest stars. The Ravens and the Cowboys will simply have to prepare and adjust. For Baltimore, that could mean a conservative approach with players dealing with lower-body injuries like Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ronnie Stanley (toe). Teddye Buchanan (knee) and Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) could also have to wait another week to make their 2026 debuts after months away from the field. Ravens expected to rebound from Week 2 loss to Saints NFL Week 2 panic meter: Caleb Williams’ injury, another Chargers no-show shake up early season – Jeff Howe, Mike Jones and Dan Pompei (The Athletic) Which version of the Baltimore Ravens is closer to reality? The team that blew out the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1 or the group that blew a second-half lead and lost 24-17 to the New Orleans Saints on Sunday? Pompei: The Ravens’ collapse was rough with self-inflicted wounds, and head coach Jesse Minter’s leadership will be tested early. Their performance was sloppy — not unusual for many teams early in the season. The Ravens have committed 17 penalties in two weeks. That cannot continue if the Ravens are going to be contenders. But this is a talented team that’s capable of high-end football, as they showed in Week 1 against the Colts. It will be a surprise if the Ravens don’t rebound and remain one of the better teams in the AFC. They just need to get in a groove. Jones: The Ravens are somewhere in the middle, but a smidge closer to the Week 1 product. Many elements of Sunday’s performance resemble the Ravens of last season (penalties and ill-timed turnovers, a couple of head-scratcher offensive play calls, late-game defensive collapse). But the roster and energy within the organization improved. It’s important to remember that Baltimore has a 30-year-old rookie offensive coordinator in Declan Doyle, and that the unit wasn’t at full force with two of Lamar Jackson’s top wide receivers injured. There were some drops (even one by the reliable Mark Andrews) that, if caught, could have extended drives, and extended drives lead to heavier emphasis on the run. And had Doyle displayed more discipline/patience by giving Derrick Henry the ball on third-and-1 late rather than calling a deep shot downfield, perhaps the Ravens would have kept moving the ball and eventually scored. The Ravens hurt themselves on Sunday, but they’re still one of the better teams in the AFC. Howe: The Ravens’ inconsistent start is reminiscent of issues with blown leads under the previous regime, ceding control of a winnable game while falling out of sorts in the second half. Jackson and the offense went three-and-out on back-to-back drives while the Saints orchestrated consecutive touchdowns. The Ravens should be in the playoff conversation throughout the season, but I’m curious to see if this team can distinguish itself from past incarnations. NFL explains officiating call on Tyler Shough’s controversial game-winning touchdown Pool report with NFL Vice President of Instant Replay Mark Butterworth – Jamison Hensley (ESPN) Question : Was there clear evidence that Tyler Shough crossed the goal line on the fourth down quarterback sneak (1:32 remaining, New Orleans 4th and 1, Baltimore 1 yard-line)? Mark Butterworth : “The key here is the ruling on the field is a touchdown. So, we need clear and obvious video evidence that he didn’t score in order to reverse the on-field ruling. We stopped the game, it’s a high-leverage play, we wanted to make sure to either find clear and obvious video evidence that he didn’t score or to confirm the call on the field. We exhausted all available angles and could not prove clear and obvious that he did not break the plane of the goal line.” Question : During any of the replays, did it show that Tyler Shough lost control of the ball at any point while trying to get the ball across the goal line? Butterworth : “No. If he did lose control of the ball, we would need to find, after he regained possession, if the ball broke the plane of the goal line. In that mass of players, we weren’t able to find clear and obvious video evidence that the ball did not break the plane of the goal line. Therefore, the ruling on the field stands.” Ravens get ‘C’ grade for Week 2 showing NFL Week 2 grades for all 32 teams: Rams earn an ‘A’ for steamrolling Giants on Monday night – John Breech (CBS Sports) The Ravens’ new offense looked unstoppable in Week 1, but it came crashing back to earth on Sunday. The Ravens had multiple chances to put this game away, but the offense was only able to muster a total of 32 yards on Baltimore’s final three possessions of the game combined. The Ravens also seemed to forget that Derrick Henry existed. Their star running back had just five carries in the second half, including just one in the fourth quarter. With the Ravens leading 14-3 at halftime, it’s surprising that they didn’t lean on Henry more in the second half. One reason the Ravens got rid of John Harbaugh is because of the blown leads in the second half. Well, in his second game on the job, Jesse Minter now has a blown fourth-quarter lead on his resume.

title: Bills news: Assessing Buffalo’s 2-0 start
summary: The Buffalo Bills are off to a 2-0 start for the sixth time in the last eight seasons, and Josh Allen and the offense are off to a dynamic start, averaging 38.5 points per game in wins over the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions. Despite the fast start, the Bills are not without their issues, […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are off to a 2-0 start for the sixth time in the last eight seasons, and Josh Allen and the offense are off to a dynamic start, averaging 38.5 points per game in wins over the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions. Despite the fast start, the Bills are not without their issues, especially on defense, where Buffalo became just the third team in league history to begin a season 2-0 while allowing at least 30 points per game (along with the 1991 Bills and 2000 St. Louis Rams). After two weeks, today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by assessing what has gone right and where the Bills can still improve following their 2-0 start. Check out the assessments below and then let us know your thoughts in the comments section. Bills offense has been explosive, defense has work to do Among the reasons for optimism among Bills fans: the red-hot starts from quarterback Josh Allen, defensive tackle Deone Walker, running back James Cook, pass rusher Greg Rousseau, and tight end Dalton Kincaid; how well Buffalo’s offensive and defensive lines have played through two games; how efficient Allen has been directing a dynamic offense; and how vastly improved Buffalo’s third-down defense has been so far. Among the causes for concern: Buffalo’s secondary has been picked apart in the first two games of the season; the depth along the defensive line beyond Rousseau, Walker, Ed Oliver and Bradley Chubb has been inconsistent at best; and the defense has allowed opponents to convert on 53 percent of their late-down chances when a stop would clinch a victory.
