title: Bengals Film Room: Cashius Howell isn’t playing like a rookie
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals selected edge Cashius Howell during the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The Bengals only played Howell during one preseason game this year, which was a testament to how highly they valued what he did throughout training camp. In that lone preseason game, Howell showed exactly why he shouldn’t have even […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals selected edge Cashius Howell during the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The Bengals only played Howell during one preseason game this year, which was a testament to how highly they valued what he did throughout training camp. In that lone preseason game, Howell showed exactly why he shouldn’t have even lasted to the second round in the draft. Howell combined with Kris Jenkins Jr. for a sack against Detroit. The former Texas A&M standout went to his patented spin move that is giving offensive tackles fits already this year. Kris Jenkins and Cashius Howell meeting at the quarterback. pic.twitter.com/1N10STEb2E — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 14, 2026 During the Bengals ‘ season-opening victory against Tampa Bay, Howell was credited with just one pressure during the game. However, he drew a holding penalty and should have been credited with at least .5 of a sack, combining once again with Jenkins. The Buccaneers tried to slow him down with a tight end; that was not a good idea. Howell continuously showed off his explosiveness to generate quick pressure. Cashius Howell was such a good draft pick for the Bengals in the second round. pic.twitter.com/HIGK5NT6WT — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 14, 2026 The performance on Sunday against the Houston Texans was the most impressive game to date for the young rookie edge rusher. Howell was credited with six pressures during the game. He caused havoc from both sides of the line and played as many snaps as starter Myles Murphy. One thing that stands out besides his pure explosiveness is just how deep his arsenal of pass rush moves are. He is able to keep offensive tackles guessing on what he is going to do next, and he goes from move to move so smoothly, even in the same rep at times. Cashius Howell vs. Houston Texans pic.twitter.com/Vh3rzaZrVH — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 21, 2026 While Howell has not been credited with a sack yet, his impact has been undeniable. It won’t be a bit surprising when he has a two- or three-sack game soon for Cincinnati. Early returns on this draft pick are showing a home-run selection for the Bengals. Howell should garner consideration for Defensive Rookie of the Year honors if he continues playing at such a high level.

title: Bengals vs. Texans: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly from Week 2
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-0. And perhaps more importantly, they just showed they can win a football game without needing Joe Burrow to throw for 300-plus yards or the offense to put up 30 points. The Bengals traveled to Houston on Sunday and walked out with a convincing 20-6 victory over the Texans. Cincinnati never […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-0. And perhaps more importantly, they just showed they can win a football game without needing Joe Burrow to throw for 300-plus yards or the offense to put up 30 points. The Bengals traveled to Houston on Sunday and walked out with a convincing 20-6 victory over the Texans. Cincinnati never trailed, scored in three of the game’s four quarters, and held Houston out of the end zone all afternoon. It wasn’t a perfect performance. In fact, Houston outgained Cincinnati 374-267 and ran 78 offensive plays to the Bengals’ 59. But when the Bengals needed to make plays, they did. Here’s the Good, the Bad and the Ugly from Cincinnati’s Week 2 win. The Good Ja’Marr Chase is still Ja’Marr Chase After being held to just two receptions in Week 1, Chase wasted little time reminding everyone why he’s one of the most dangerous players in football. He finished with seven receptions for 75 yards and two touchdowns on nine targets. And both touchdowns were spectacular. The first was a 32-yard touchdown in the second quarter that required Chase to make an incredible sideline grab. The second came on an 18-yard connection with Burrow in the third quarter. Those two plays accounted for all of Cincinnati’s touchdowns. More importantly, Chase was involved from the beginning. After a quiet opening week, getting the ball to No. 1 early and often was clearly a priority. The Bengals are at their most dangerous when Burrow can lean on Chase. Houston got a reminder of that Sunday. Tee Higgins quietly had a huge game Chase got the touchdowns, but Higgins actually led the Bengals in receiving yards. He caught five passes for 95 yards, averaging an impressive 19 yards per reception. His longest reception went for 23 yards. That’s an important development. Defenses simply can’t dedicate all of their attention to Chase when Higgins is capable of producing like this on the other side. Higgins also came up with one of the game’s prettier receptions, hauling in a 23-yard sideline catch. Burrow doesn’t need to force the ball to Chase on every important down. Having Higgins available as a legitimate second option makes this passing game much harder to defend. The defense looked completely different This was the biggest positive of the afternoon. Houston scored 31 points against Buffalo in Week 1. Against Cincinnati, the Texans scored six. That’s not a typo. C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards, so this wasn’t some dominant statistical shutdown. Houston moved the football. The Texans finished with 22 first downs and 374 total yards. But Cincinnati consistently prevented Houston from finishing drives. The Texans went 5-for-17 on third down and 0-for-4 on fourth down. They never reached the end zone. That’s winning defense. Dexter Lawrence is already making an impact The biggest addition to Cincinnati’s defensive front made one of the biggest plays of the game. In the second quarter, Houston faced fourth-and-inches from the Bengals’ 18-yard line. Dexter Lawrence exploded through the line and tackled David Montgomery for a one-yard loss. Turnover on downs. Instead of Houston potentially taking the game’s first lead, Cincinnati got the football back. Lawrence finished with three tackles, a tackle for loss and a quarterback hit, but his impact went beyond the box score. The Bengals’ defensive front consistently made life difficult for Houston’s offense. That’s exactly what Cincinnati envisioned when it acquired Lawrence. The run defense was excellent The Bengals’ run defense was a major question entering this season. It didn’t look like one Sunday. Houston finished with just 60 rushing yards on 18 attempts, good for 3.3 yards per carry. Montgomery and the Texans’ rushing attack simply couldn’t establish much of anything. Considering how important it was for Cincinnati to improve in this area, this was one of the most encouraging parts of the victory. Evan McPherson was automatic from distance McPherson didn’t get many opportunities, but he made both of them count. He connected on field goals of 51 and 57 yards. That’s 108 yards of field-goal distance on two attempts. When an offense struggles to finish drives, having a kicker who can turn possessions into points from deep is extremely valuable. McPherson did exactly that. The Bad The Bengals’ offense wasn’t exactly humming Twenty points is enough when your defense holds the opponent to six. But Cincinnati’s offense wasn’t particularly efficient. The Bengals managed just 267 total yards and 12 first downs. They averaged 4.5 yards per play and converted only five of 15 third-down attempts. Those numbers aren’t going to scare many defenses. Burrow completed 20/31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns without throwing an interception. That’s a solid stat line, especially considering the pressure he faced. But the offense still had too many possessions that went nowhere. The Bengals don’t need to score 30 every week. They do need to be capable of doing it when their defense inevitably has an off day. Houston controlled the yardage battle This is the strangest part of the game. The Bengals won 20-6, yet Houston gained 107 more yards. The Texans ran 78 plays compared with Cincinnati’s 59. Houston also had 22 first downs to Cincinnati’s 12. So how did the Bengals win by 14? They finished drives better, protected the football, and repeatedly stopped Houston when the Texans needed to convert. It’s a good reminder that yardage totals don’t always tell the story of a game. But Cincinnati can’t make a habit of giving opponents that kind of offensive volume. Eventually, one of those teams is going to finish those drives. Burrow took too much punishment This is the biggest offensive concern coming out of Houston. Burrow was sacked five times for 25 yards. He also spent a good portion of the afternoon dealing with pressure. The Bengals’ quarterback has proven over and over that he’s capable of creating plays when things break down. That doesn’t mean Cincinnati should make broken plays part of the offensive game plan. Keeping Burrow upright has to be priority No. 1. The Ugly Five sacks allowed There’s really no way around it. Five sacks is ugly. Burrow threw only 31 passes, and Houston managed to bring him down five times. That’s a sack on roughly 16% of his dropbacks. Against a better offense, the Bengals might not get away with absorbing that kind of punishment. The offensive line deserves credit for some good moments, but protection needs to improve. Burrow is too important to this team to consistently take this kind of beating. The Bengals couldn’t get Chase Brown going through the air Brown was effective on the ground, rushing for 80 yards on 20 carries, an average of 4.0 yards per attempt. But his receiving production was essentially nonexistent. He caught three passes for just two yards. That’s not necessarily a problem by itself, but Cincinnati’s offense needs to find ways to get its running backs involved in space. The Bengals finished with only 85 rushing yards as a team, so there wasn’t much offensive explosion on the ground. Again, the defense made that irrelevant Sunday. It won’t always be irrelevant. The offense needs to turn more yards into points This might be the most important lesson from the game. Cincinnati scored 20 points despite gaining only 267 yards. That’s a credit to the defense and special teams, but it also means there is plenty of room for improvement. The Bengals had eight punts. Eight. They also had three possessions that ended in three-and-outs. That’s a lot of wasted opportunities for an offense with Burrow, Chase, and Higgins. The good news? The Bengals still won by two touchdowns. If this offense gets rolling while the defense continues playing at this level, Cincinnati becomes a much more difficult team to deal with. The Bottom Line This wasn’t a pretty offensive performance. It didn’t need to be. The Bengals went on the road, held a talented Texans offense to six points, stopped Houston on all four…

title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: Defense saves the day
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-0 to start the 2026 season. They’re alone atop the AFC North, with the Steelers, Ravens and Browns all sitting at 1-1. All good news! It’s hard not to be excited about what we saw from the Bengals in Week 2. Winning on the road in the NFL is difficult, especially […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II (97) drives into Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) as he throws in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 2 game between the Houston Texans and the Cincinnati Bengals at Reliant Stadium in Houston on Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. The Bengals improved to 2-0 on the season with a 20-6 win on the road. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-0 to start the 2026 season. They’re alone atop the AFC North, with the Steelers, Ravens and Browns all sitting at 1-1. All good news! It’s hard not to be excited about what we saw from the Bengals in Week 2 . Winning on the road in the NFL is difficult, especially against a good team—and the Texans are a good team, regardless of their 0-2 start. What should be most exciting, though, is how the Bengals won. The offense sputtered, especially in the first half. At this point, I guess that’s just something we should expect from Joe Burrow and the offense early in the season. Had the 2025 Bengals defense played this game, Cincinnati probably loses 30-20. But this isn’t the 2025 defense. Dexter Lawrence showed everyone why he was worth the No. 10 overall selection, and the rebuilt defense kept the Texans out of the end zone for the entire game—in their own stadium. Houston’s only points came on field goals from 37 and 45 yards. When the Texans managed to move the ball into Bengals territory, the defense either forced a turnover on downs or Houston shot itself in the foot. Here are some observations from the game: Lawrence was incredible against the Texans. In the second quarter, Houston opted to go for it on fourth-and-inches in the red zone. The game was still scoreless, and the Texans passed up the easy points in hopes of picking up a fresh set of downs, getting the crowd into the game and building some momentum before halftime. Lawrence wasn’t having it. He split a double team and tracked down David Montgomery in the backfield, forcing a turnover on downs and giving the ball back to Cincinnati. On the following drive, Burrow found Ja’Marr Chase in the end zone to give the Bengals a 7-0 lead. Behold: Wake up babe a new angle of the Dexter Lawrence 4th down run stop just dropped pic.twitter.com/jeLg0IXhwB — mike (@bengals_sans) September 21, 2026 And that touchdown catch Chase made? Not only did Burrow place the ball where no one other than Chase could make a play on it, but Chase somehow contorted his body, made the catch and kept his feet in bounds. It should absolutely be in the conversation for catch of the year when the season comes to an end. Behold again: Unbelievable touchdown catch by Ja’Marr Chase. The Bengals have a 7-0 lead after this. Chase somehow kept both feet in bounds. Unreal. pic.twitter.com/hMKwrkAfEZ — James Rapien (@JamesRapien) September 20, 2026 Orlando Brown Jr. was outmatched on Sunday. He struggled badly protecting Burrow’s blind side, allowing three sacks and committing two penalties. A big reason the offense got off to such a slow start was because Burrow was constantly under pressure, often from behind. Again, the Bengals made a point of putting Burrow under center. The running game looked great when Burrow took the snap directly from Ted Karras with Chase Brown in the backfield. Brown averaged four yards per carry, and as a result, the offense looks much more balanced in 2026 than it did in 2025. While the Bengals’ running game worked when called upon—for the most part—the Texans were absolutely stuffed all day. Running backs David Montgomery and Woody Marks combined for just 18 yards on 14 carries. Making any offense one-dimensional is huge, and the Bengals did exactly that. If the Bengals defense had a weakness on Sunday, it was covering the tight end. Dalton Schultz caught 12 passes for 140 yards. The Bengals’ offensive line was also flagged several times. That’s something they’ll need to clean up. In 2025, the Bengals defense sacked the quarterback three times over the first two weeks of the season. In 2026, they have nine sacks through two games. That puts them on pace for 76 sacks over a 17-game season. Once again, there were waves of pass rushers, and everybody got in on the action. Cedric Johnson had two sacks, while Shemar Stewart and Jonathan Allen each had one. Lawrence didn’t record a sack, but he led the team with an 83.9 pass-rushing grade, per PFF, while adding four hurries. Boye Mafe had eight hurries, and Cashius Howell added five. This isn’t one guy carrying the pass rush. It’s coming from everywhere. Goosebumps… This Jonathan Allen speech was so cold😭 pic.twitter.com/JAS90Y7fe0 — Drake Burton (@bengalsdrake) September 20, 2026 The Bengals hit the road again in Week 3 as they open AFC North play against the Steelers in Pittsburgh. The Steelers are 1-1 and coming off a loss to the Patriots in Foxborough after defeating the Falcons 20-13 in Week 1. Pittsburgh, led by Aaron Rodgers, has struggled offensively so far. The Steelers rank 30th in the league in both total offensive yards and points scored. But, in typical Steelers fashion, their defense has been solid. They’ve allowed the 10th-fewest yards and are tied for the eighth-fewest points allowed. So, we could be looking at a battle of defenses in Week 3. At the same time, if I have to choose which offense I trust in a defensive slugfest, I’ll almost always choose the one led by Burrow and Chase. The Bengals opened as 3.5-point favorites in Pittsburgh, and with a win, they would become the 10th team in franchise history to start a season 3-0. The last time it happened was way back in 2015, when we were chanting “MVP” for Andy Dalton before his season was derailed by a broken thumb. As always, it’s one week at a time, but it’s hard not to be excited about what we’re seeing. For years, we’ve said things like, “If they could just get off to a hot start, they wouldn’t have to spend the second half of the season trying to dig themselves out of a hole.” Or, “If they could just have a mediocre defense, this offense could take them all the way.” Well, they’ve gotten off to the hot start. And they don’t have a mediocre defense. They have a good one. Once the offense really gets firing—and we all know it will—watch out. Now they just need to stay healthy. Who Dey! title: Browns Todd Monken gets his first win as NFL head coach: 2 takeaways on CLE’s new HC
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ 23-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers gave Todd Monken his first win as an NFL head coach. While the game was far from perfect, this win was important for the overall team morale. There was also plenty to learn about Monken from a coaching standpoint following the win, including how he […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns’ 23-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers gave Todd Monken his first win as an NFL head coach. While the game was far from perfect, this win was important for the overall team morale. There was also plenty to learn about Monken from a coaching standpoint following the win, including how he will navigate the media throughout the season. Monken has a much more fiery personality than prior head coach Kevin Stefanski . Stefanski was known for his more monotone way of speaking and reserved interactions with the media. After just two weeks, it is already clear that Monken speaks with much more emotion and is not afraid to call people out. He even referenced negative comments from former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin and used his postgame media availability to clap back at them. It is clear Monken has a chip on his shoulder and is ready to come out swinging when needed. On the field, the offense had to rely heavily on the passing game this week. After struggles in the passing game in week one, it is important to see that Monken did not panic and completely change up what he wants this team to do on offense. He continued to trust in those individuals and find opportunities to move the ball. While there were few explosive plays, the team put together enough drives to secure the win over the Buccaneers. Confidence in the offense will be important as the season continues. Let me know what you think in the comments – Todd Monken gets his first win. What did we learn about him as a coach?

full_text: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 16: Carolina linebacker Krys Barnes (40) warms up prior to the start of the NFL game between the Carolina Panthers and the Atlanta Falcons on November 16th, 2025 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns announced that they have placed LB Nathaniel Watson on the practice squad/injured list with a knee injury. A sixth-round pick in 2024, Watson was on injured reserve all of last season. Although he did not make the team this year, he was on the practice squad and had been elevated to the gameday roster for the first two games. The practice squad/injured list is similar to the short-term IR list, in the sense that it’s a temporary removal until he is ready to play again. Taking Watson’s spot is LB Krys Barnes , who is in his seventh season in the NFL. He has spent most of his career with the Green Bay Packers, but last year, he was a member of the Carolina Panthers, who just so happen to be the Browns’ opponents this Sunday. Last year with the Panthers, Barnes made 3 starts and had 25 tackles with a 1/2 sack. We’ll see if Barnes ends up being a gameday elevation this Sunday, or if the Browns decide to call up someone else. Barnes was with the Washington Commanders briefly this training camp, but did not make their team.

title: Week 3 Browns NFL Power Rankings: All it took was a win to, and now look at Cleveland
summary: It is Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are officially back in the category of respectability. full_text: It is Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are officially back in the category of respectability. Some rankings had them rise just a few spots, but a couple of sites had them make a significant jump, with one of them even putting the Browns ahead of the Steelers. Overall, the Browns went up by 5.4 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 26.0 . Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 28 (up 3 spots) Deshaun Watson actually looked good in beating the Bucs. The defense also took a step forward. ESPN – No. 29 (up 3 spots) One thing we know about the QB1: Deshaun Watson found a risk-averse winning formula. In Week 2, Watson earned his first win since September 2024 with the lowest average depth of target (3.7) of his career. At times, it has seemed like the Browns’ passing game has been played in a phone booth: Watson’s 6.7 air yards per attempt would tie a career low. However, the play style has limited turnover potential and allowed the Browns’ young playmakers to get the ball in their hands. Cleveland ranks third in yards after the catch (260) through two games. NFL.com – No. 23 (up 9 spots) In the second half against the Buccaneers, the Browns enjoyed adequate quarterback play, experienced the thrill of a long, game-tying touchdown pass and capped off a methodical scoring drive with a go-ahead TD on a well-designed and properly executed play. The defense showed up, too, after getting torched in Week 1. I know it must have seemed rather foreign to Browns fans, but on Sunday in Tampa, Cleveland was the better team. We’ll see if this lasts for more than a week. Sporting News – No. 28 (up 4 spots) Todd Monken is getting a lot of heat for starting Deshaun Watson, but the bottom line is that Watson gives the Browns a much better chance to win than Shedeur Sanders. He has done well to lift some young pieces early and inspire the whole team. Yahoo Sports – No. 24 (up 6 spots) If that seemed like Deshaun Watson’s greatest moment with the Browns, it was, statistically speaking. It was his top EPA per dropback in any game for Cleveland. Watson had a good second half with the Browns’ running game doing nothing. Removing Watson’s 22 yards on seven rushes, the Browns rushed for 22 yards on 16 carries. Watson and the Browns’ defense were the drivers of this win. Watson clearly did enough to keep his job for another week, and the reaction to him from Browns fans at the home opener will be interesting. At least it’s coming off a win and a good performance. Bleacher Report – No. 28 (up 4 spots) Deshaun Watson stayed the executioner’s hand for one more week. If anything, growing confidence may have germinated in Cleveland’s QB1 with Sunday’s performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. During a contest expected and billed as Baker Mayfield’s revenge game, Watson outplayed the former Browns quarterback and helped lead his team to its first victory this season. In fact, Watson completed 80 percent of his passes and threw a pair of touchdowns. The next step is stacking competent outings. Otherwise, the Browns fan base will not allow any leeway after the previous four seasons of disappointment. Shedeur Sanders is waiting in the wings to take over as soon as Cleveland has had enough of Watson. USA Today – No. 22 (up 9 spots) An impressive Week 2 win amid disadvantageous circumstances in Tampa. But all due respect to Coach Monken, betting the “Browns are gonna Browns” when they roll out QB Deshaun Watson to start the team’s home opener this weekend. Not only have we seen huge injuries, but teams who looked one way in Week 1 turned a different leaf in Week 2 , including the Cleveland Browns . A lot of the outcomes in the NFL come down to quarterback play, a quality head coach, and injury luck. For Cleveland’s Week 15 opponent, the New York Giants, the roller coaster of the season has already hit a big high (Week 1’s victory), a low (Week 2’s loss), and now an off-the-rails experience with QB Jaxson Dart’s injury being worse than expected: #Giants QB Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury last night that was worse than anticipated, sources told me and @MikeGarafolo after the MRI. title: Browns O-line is much better in one area than the other; still learning to dance
summary: The exciting win in Week 2 versus the Tampa Bay Buccaneers did not come without some concerns for the Cleveland Browns. The run game continues to struggle two weeks in, and the defense was bailed out by quite a few overthrows by QB Baker Mayfield. That doesn’t mean there isn’t a lot to celebrate, including […]
full_text: The exciting win in Week 2 versus the Tampa Bay Buccaneers did not come without some concerns for the Cleveland Browns. The run game continues to struggle two weeks in, and the defense was bailed out by quite a few overthrows by QB Baker Mayfield . That doesn’t mean there isn’t a lot to celebrate, including the way-too-early look at the AFC playoff picture after the first two games of the season. QB Deshaun Watson had one of his best games , WR Denzel Boston joined history , and the defense was able to get pressure when they needed it . The revamped offensive line is one of the pieces causing issues in the rushing attack , but is much better at protecting Watson in the passing game: Through two games, the Browns’ offensive line is much farther ahead as a pass-blocking unit than a run-blocking unit. Cleveland now ranks second in ESPN’s pass block win rate metric but 21st in run block win rate. The Browns rank 31st in rushing yards per game (65.5) and 29th… — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) September 22, 2026 The issue in run blocking, as well as for the running back behind it, is the nuanced dance that requires everyone to be on beat, in rhythm, and with the right timing. One step too quick and someone’s toes are getting stepped on. There is no guarantee that time will heal all the issues for Cleveland’s offensive line. The good news is that the passing blocking, which is less of a dance and more of a skill issue, has been good. Now, the line needs to stay healthy and get their dance in lockstep so RB Quinshon Judkins, Raheim Sanders, and Jaleel McLaughlin can waltz their way into the defensive secondary and end zone. title: The Parker Report: Cowboys defense shows incremental improvement
summary: After coming away with a win in week two, let’s take a look at how Christian Parker’s defense performed against the Washington Commanders. Team stats allowed This week, Dallas won 37-20 against the Commanders. Their defense allowed 389 total yards and a 57.1% third-down conversion rate. They also gave up a 99.1 passer rating to […]
full_text: Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After coming away with a win in week two, let’s take a look at how Christian Parker’s defense performed against the Washington Commanders. Team stats allowed This week, Dallas won 37-20 against the Commanders. Their defense allowed 389 total yards and a 57.1% third-down conversion rate. They also gave up a 99.1 passer rating to Daniels and a 109.1 rating to Mariota. The Cowboys continue to struggle against mobile quarterbacks, surrendering 69 yards on the ground to Jayden Daniels in the first half before his injury. The defense did a much better job this week in points allowed (20) and time of possession, although Washington still held the ball longer than Dallas. Some of that is due to the offense’s big-play capability, shortening the field in a hurry paired with their inability to run the ball. But the defense still needs to do a better job at preventing long, clock-chewing drives moving forward. That starts with stopping the run. Individual stat leaders Caleb Downs was once again flying all over the field on Sunday. He tied linebacker Dee Winters with a team leading nine tackles, six of which were solo. Jaishawn Barham and Caleb Downs each forced one fumble on the day. Dee Winters recovered the one forced by Barham on defense, the other was recovered by the Commanders on special teams. Advanced analytics Dallas took a massive step forward in the EPA per play department. According to SumerSports, the defense moved up from the 30th ranked defense last week to 21st this week. Using the same grading system, their pass defense was good enough to finish 14th in EPA per play, but the run defense still struggled with Dallas finishing 28th in that department. The Cowboys are getting a decent amount of pressure on opposing QBs with a four-man rush, but they just can’t seal the deal. This week, SumerSports has Dallas ranked 18th in pressure rate and just 31st in blitz percentage. But even with that pressure, Dallas was one of four teams in the league to finish without a sack. How’d the rookies look? Caleb Downs is as advertised. The rookie seemingly teleports from sideline to sideline, is rock solid in coverage, and has limited his rookie mistakes as well as one could hope for. He recorded a pass breakup on a huge hit and he also quietly forced another fumble this week, this time on special teams. Downs is currently PFF’s highest rated first-round rookie . His ability to do anything that’s asked of him makes him the ultimate chess piece for Christian Parker. Malachi Lawrence is quietly putting together some nice film. He’s currently leads all rookie edges in pass rush win rate by a wide margin. He hasn’t been able to consistently make contact with the opposing team’s quarterback, but he’s been close. At some point this season, expect to see Lawrence begin to put it all together and finish the season with a respectable stat line for a rookie edge. Pass rush win rate among rookie edge rushers this season: 26.9% – Malachi Lawrence 17.0% – Cashius Howell 15.8% – Akheem Mesidor 10.5% – R Mason Thomas 7.4% – Dani Dennis-Sutton 7.1% – Gabe Jacas 6.3% – David Bailey 2.9% – Romello Height 2.6% – Rueben Bain Jr. pic.twitter.com/eYvse5ekCJ — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) September 21, 2026 Jaishawn Barham is a shape-shifting freak of nature. He’s able to bend and contort his body to get around blockers in the run game. He’s instinctive and physical at the point of attack. This week in a one-score game, he had a huge moment with the forced fumble in the third quarter. And with the rookie wearing the green dot, this defense didn’t appear to have many communication issues. Definitely a positive step forward for the rookie. LT Overton finished with 15 snaps. There wasn’t enough volume to properly evaluate the rookie. Final grade: D+ The Cowboys only gave up 20 points. If they were to do that every week, this team might not lose another game. But the point total lies. After the first drive ended in a three-and-out, the Commanders had their way with this defense for the remainder of the first half. Dallas couldn’t contain the mobile quarterback. They couldn’t get off the field on third down, resulting in a first half 66.7% conversion rate. Without the injury to Daniels, it’s possible that Dallas could have seen a repeat of last week’s second half fiasco where the Cowboys offense rarely saw the field. The Commanders also had multiple “unlucky” plays as noted in this week’s post game article . They had two touchdowns that were mere centimeters away that could have turned the tide in this game. Such is the way of the sport, however, and close never put a ‘W’ in the win/loss column. Now in all fairness to Christian Parker and his defense, there were more positives this week than last. Blink your eyes and you’ll miss Caleb Downs flash across the field making a play. Barham had a really solid game, forcing that game-changing fumble in the third quarter. Revel made an appearance with a pass break up. Malachi Lawrence and Donovan Ezeiruaku were around the quarterback all day, but just couldn’t finish with sacks. That’s something you would expect to click at some point this season. The defense is trending in the right direction, but the question will be just how long will it take to really come together? The offense won’t score 37 points every week. And the defense won’t survive on just turnovers alone. They need to improve against the run game. They need to convert pressures into sacks. And until they do that, every week is going to be a struggle. This week’s grade was a ‘D’ with the plus added for Barham’s forced fumble at a key moment in the game. Can this defense continue to improve and post the year’s first ‘C’ or better grade against the Baltimore Ravens? It will certainly be a tall task in Brazil against Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry. We’ll see if Christian Parker and crew can answer the call.

title: Washington’s nightmare end to first half changed the Cowboys game
summary: Football is all about momentum. Sometimes those shifts happen quickly and unexpectedly. The Washington Commanders were a yard away from potentially drawing level with the Dallas Cowboys right before halftime. Jayden Daniels was giving the Cowboys defense problems while the Commanders were threatening another touchdown, and Dallas’ early control of the game was slipping. Then […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) reacts as he leaves the game with an apparent injury to his left arm during the second half against the Washington Commanders at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Football is all about momentum. Sometimes those shifts happen quickly and unexpectedly. The Washington Commanders were a yard away from potentially drawing level with the Dallas Cowboys right before halftime. Jayden Daniels was giving the Cowboys defense problems while the Commanders were threatening another touchdown, and Dallas’ early control of the game was slipping. Then everything changed. Washington’s final possession before halftime ended without points and with Daniels suffering a gruesome left elbow injury that ended his afternoon. What followed was a different challenge for the Dallas defense, while Dak Prescott and the offense helped turn a narrow advantage into a 37-20 victory. The Commanders had reached the Dallas 1-yard line with 12 seconds remaining in the half, trailing 17-10. Dallas held firm, leaving Washington with a decision as the clock dwindled. With three seconds left, the Commanders took another shot at the end zone rather than attempting a short field goal. That final opportunity ended disastrously. Daniels lost his footing after contact with offensive lineman Chris Paul and planted his left arm as he fell. His elbow buckled awkwardly beneath him. Washington came away empty-handed, and Marcus Mariota had to take over after the break. Daniels had already produced 69 rushing yards alongside 96 passing yards and a touchdown. Instead of kicking a field goal at the end of the half the commanders went for it with three seconds left and Jayden Daniels got hurt. Great call. pic.twitter.com/PiQOg17aWR — Chad Fisher DNP (@ChadFisher) September 20, 2026 Jayden Daniels is being carted off after a devastating left arm injury pic.twitter.com/KqgUqdz9WH — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) September 20, 2026 Those rushing yards explain why his departure mattered so much. Dallas was struggling to finish plays against him. Even when the initial coverage held up, Daniels could escape, find space and turn a broken play into another gain. Defenders had to account for both the receivers downfield and the quarterback threatening to run. That creates difficult decisions. Step forward too early and a receiver can become available behind you. Stay back too long and Daniels can take the open grass. His ability to improvise was keeping Washington dangerous even when Dallas disrupted the original play. Losing him changed that equation. Mariota can move, too, but Washington had lost the player whose scrambling had been causing Dallas its biggest headaches. The Cowboys still needed to execute, but the threat they had spent the first half struggling to contain was gone. Washington initially steadied itself with a field goal after halftime. Dallas answered with a drive that put Brandon Aubrey in position to connect from 44 yards, restoring a seven-point cushion. Then the defense delivered the play that helped turn the momentum shift into clear separation. Jaishawn Barham forced the ball loose, and Dee Winters recovered. Given that extra possession, Prescott found Jake Ferguson for a 12-yard touchdown, his second score of the afternoon. Washington later missed a field goal, and Aubrey punished that missed opportunity by drilling a 60-yarder. Dallas had scored 13 unanswered points to move ahead 30-13. TD No. 2 for Jake Ferguson 🤠 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/NKpsobgh9v — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 20, 2026 Jaishawn Barham force fumble 🚨 pic.twitter.com/OssbCglCXA — SleeperCowboys (@SleeperCowboys) September 20, 2026 Brandon Aubrey from 60 YARDS OUT 🦵 The Cowboys kicker drills the long FG to give Dallas a 30-13 lead over the Commanders! pic.twitter.com/nbJ56YzvEr — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) September 20, 2026 That stretch showed how the Cowboys needed to respond. The defense supplied a takeaway, the offense converted it into a touchdown, and Aubrey extended the lead when another possession stalled. Washington’s chances to regain control kept disappearing while Dallas continued adding points. The injury was an awful moment for Daniels, and its impact on the contest was significant. It also should not erase the work Dallas did afterward. The Cowboys still had to recover the fumble, finish the touchdown opportunity and make the kicks. Washington entered the closing seconds of the first half with a chance to tie the game and a quarterback Dallas was struggling to contain. It left without points and without Daniels. The Cowboys’ response made sure Washington never recovered control.
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys vs. Commanders historical notes: CeeDee Lamb, Dak Prescott impressed
summary: Last week was highly impressive for the Dallas Cowboys offense. They scored 37 points and ultimately did so on just eight possessions. That is some truly elite work. You don’t have to be a football historian to understand that, clearly. Everyone can tell that the Cowboys offense is moving and grooving and that the defense […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last week was highly impressive for the Dallas Cowboys offense. They scored 37 points and ultimately did so on just eight possessions. That is some truly elite work. You don’t have to be a football historian to understand that, clearly. Everyone can tell that the Cowboys offense is moving and grooving and that the defense certain still needs to figure things out a bit. Regarding both sides of the spectrum, something we like to do around here is put what happened up against the prism of franchise history. The folks at Stathead and Pro Football Referenc e make this possible with their tools, and all work comes from there. Here are this week’s historical notes. CeeDee Lamb did indeed have a day During the game against the Washington Commanders, CeeDee Lamb recorded over 150 receiving yards and had multiple touchdowns. It was his third career game where this was the case. With three career games of this variety Lamb is now tied with several people for second in franchise history. He has to double his total to match Bob Hayes, though. Dak was dominant AND clean Much was made about how Dak Prescott passed Tony Romo as the franchise’s all-time leader in passing touchdowns during the game. That makes sense given how stout of a record that is, although it was obviously inflated for both players given the eras they played in as opposed to other quarterbacks in franchise history. Prescott also tied Romo for the most games with multiple passing touchdowns thrown which only requires two to be the case. Prescott threw four touchdowns on the day, but impressively he did so without any interceptions. This was Prescott’s 11th career game with four or more touchdowns and zero interceptions on his day. You can see that he has a significant lead on the field in franchise history. In fact, there are 23 games in all of franchise history where this has happened so Dak has almost matched everyone else’s total combined. Jake Ferguson got in on the action, too Back to receiving touchdowns, Lamb was not the only player to haul in a pair. Jake Ferguson found the endzone twice as well. If we isolate games with multiple receiving touchdowns to tight ends specifically we can see that Ferguson has now had four across his career. With his next one he would obviously tie the trio ahead of him. Interestingly, of the four games total, three have come in the last year for Ferguson. This happened at the New York Jets last season and in both home games against Washington last and this year (obviously). Brandon Aubrey was good from downtown again There were so many points scored throughout this game that it was easy to miss Brandon Aubrey going a perfect three for three as far as his field goal attempts. It appears that any concern born out of Week 1 and his miss there has fully dissipated. One of Aubrey’s field goals was his specialty though as it came from beyond the arc, as in from at least 60 yards out. This was Aubrey’s seventh career field goal from this range and just the 11th overall in franchise history. All of them have occurred between Aubrey and Brett Maher, amazingly all since 2018. All told these are some pretty neat and interesting marks from a handful of Cowboys players. Here’s to hoping they continue to reach these types of places as the season goes on.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Dak Prescott stands alone atop Cowboys history in this area
summary: For the better part of 66 years, the Dallas Cowboys and their quarterback have been the NFL equivalent of asking who is playing shortstop for the Yankees. It’s a position steeped in history, success and prestige. Many have taken snaps but few have reached heights like Roger Staubach, Troy Aikman, or statistical dominance like Tony […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) jogs off the field after a game against the Washington Commanders at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For the better part of 66 years, the Dallas Cowboys and their quarterback have been the NFL equivalent of asking who is playing shortstop for the Yankees. It’s a position steeped in history, success and prestige. Many have taken snaps but few have reached heights like Roger Staubach, Troy Aikman, or statistical dominance like Tony Romo. Now Dak Prescott has become the quarterback whose name sits atop one of the most important records in Cowboys history. And he did it while putting together one of his best individual games in recent memory. Tony Romo previously sat atop the Cowboys’ record books in this one particular area. His last touchdown pass came in 2016. It took Romo 10 years to amass 248 passing touchdowns. Then came Prescott. On Sunday, nearly 10 years after Prescott unexpectedly became the Cowboys’ starting quarterback, he passed Romo. Prescott’s 24-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb in the fourth quarter of Dallas’ 37-20 victory over Washington gave him 249 career touchdown passes, moving him into first place in franchise history. It was a fitting way for Prescott to break the record. Playing like a quarterback at the top of his game, zipping a pass to his receiver, who had coverage draped all over him, in the end zone. Prescott finished 26-of-31 for 279 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions, good for a 143.8 passer rating. The efficiency was particularly impressive. Jake Ferguson caught two touchdown passes. Lamb caught two more, including the one that put Prescott alone atop the Cowboys’ record book. George Pickens made several important catches of his own, including some tough grabs in traffic. It was the kind of performance Dallas needed from its quarterback after an ugly opening week. More importantly, it looked like the offense Dallas expected to have when the season began. That said, records can be funny. A quarterback can accumulate statistics simply because he plays for a long time. That’s part of the equation. Prescott has now played 141 regular-season games for Dallas, compared with the 156 Romo played. Prescott’s 249 touchdown passes have come in fewer games. The crazy thing is longevity doesn’t happen by accident. What’s that old saying? Prescott has survived many different versions of the Cowboys. He’s played under multiple head coaches and offensive coordinators. He’s played through injuries. He’s gone from a fourth-round rookie who unexpectedly took over for Romo to the unquestioned leader and face of the franchise. And now his name sits above Romo’s in the Cowboys’ record book. That’s worth appreciating without pretending it settles every argument about Prescott’s career. Because it doesn’t, but we don’t have to argue about the playoffs today. The Cowboys have had plenty of quarterbacks who have thrown important passes. Only one has thrown more touchdown passes than anyone else in franchise history. Dak Prescott is that quarterback now. . @Dak was having fun out there in the @DallasCowboys home opening win 🔊 @insidethenfl Week 2 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/DtnW37Dlvn — NFL (@NFL) September 21, 2026

title: 2026 NFL Week 3 Power Rankings: Cowboys rise after Commanders win
summary: Just like that the first two weeks of the NFL season are in the books. It flies by fast. Thankfully the Dallas Cowboys are on the board with a win, and that makes everything feel better. The team has things to clean up, but that is so much easier to process coming off of a […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just like that the first two weeks of the NFL season are in the books. It flies by fast. Thankfully the Dallas Cowboys are on the board with a win, and that makes everything feel better. The team has things to clean up, but that is so much easier to process coming off of a victory. There are still teams who have yet to put one in the win column this season and 0-2 starts make everything feel heavy. Most of those teams fall at the bottom of our weekly power rankings. As we always do, we have ranked every team across the NFL and we have also curated where outlets across the internet have the Cowboys ranked. 1 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 2) It is their world right now. They looked great last Thursday night. Like with the Cowboys though, it is time to put it all together in January. 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 3) Unfortunately it appears that they are very much back. 3 – Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 6) So are they! 4 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 7) The Seahawks are so admirable. They simply show up, dominate, and get out. They are arguably a perfect organization in that sense. 5 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 8) The Titans were so close to pulling off the upset. Credit to the Eagles and Jalen Hurts for delivering when it mattered most, though. 6 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 9) The Bengals have been threats in the past despite 0-2 starts. Well, now they are 2-0 and looking like anything is possible. 7 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 14) It is fair to point out, like with the Cowboys, that they cruised against a team that lost their starting quarterback. But the Rams have proven that they deserve benefit of the doubt. 8 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 5) They stumbled last week and will be ready to answer back against the Cowboys in Brazil. 9 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 4) I was someone who did not think much of the Jaguars before the season, and then I picked them to beat Denver and looked silly. There is a ton of potential here and they will likely bounce back themselves. 10 – New England Patriots (LW: 17) Perhaps last week was the sign of a return to form. 11 – Chicago Bears (LW: 1) Thankfully Caleb Williams is alright. We will see if he plays next Monday night or if the Eagles catch a break. 12 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 12) They have essentially gone 2-0 without their desired starter at quarterback… and against division rivals in the process. Pretty impressive stuff. 13 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 19) This offense is so much fun. The NFC South is totally theirs. 14 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 21) Unless these guys have something to say about that. 15 – Denver Broncos (LW: 27) I was also not much of a believer in the Broncos, but wow this past week was something. 16 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 23) The offense is clearly one of the best in the NFL. Now it is time for the defense to rise to the occassion. 17 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 18) They are 2-0! Seriously! Good for the Raiders. 18 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 20) They came so very close to starting the season off 0-2. A win is a win, but this smells like a team that is going to play with fire a lot. 19 – Detroit Lions (LW: 11) It was impressive how they fought back. I’m not sure that I am fully ready to write them off, but they are hardly the Lions of the last few years. 20 – Houston Texans (LW: 13) Now this is a very tough scene. They are 0-2 which obviously stings, but they have lost both of those games to teams who they will (theoretically at least) be contending with for playoff seeding. No bueno. 21 – New York Giants (LW: 10) Hopefully Jaxson Dart is alright. Until he’s back under center… this is a group that is hard to really evaluate. 22 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 15) Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers are not exactly in perfect harmony right now. 23 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 22) It is legitimately shocking that they fell to 0-2. 24 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 32) They had a huge hand in that! 25 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 24) Maybe the internet will stop crowning them now. 26 – New York Jets (LW: 26) They are hardly the pushover that they have been in the past, but they still stink. 27 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 28) Why would you give the ball to Patrick Mahomes in a must-win situation??? 28 – Washington Commanders (LW: 25) All the best to Jayden Daniels. It feels like that really takes some wind out of their sails. 29 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 16) It is shocking how unreliable Marvin Harrison Jr. is right now. 30 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 31) They gave Philly a fight, but they still lost. 31 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 29) Gross. 32 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 30) Mega gross. And they have three straight games in primetime starting this week! ESPN : 16 (LW: 16) Here we go. Week 2 result: Beat the Commanders 37-20 Week 2 ranking: 16 One thing we know about the QB1: The Cowboys will go as far as Dak Prescott can take them. There have been — and will be — growing pains with the defense, so a lot will be on Prescott’s plate. The run game has not been what the Cowboys have wanted so far, either. Through two games, Prescott is completing 73.8% of his passes, and he has been able to escape harm with his legs, too. He has six touchdown passes and one interception, but the one giveaway shows the Cowboys’ thin margin for error. The Giants turned that into a touchdown to shift the momentum in Dallas’ Week 1 loss. — Todd Archer NFL.com : 12 (LW: 17) A nice bump up. After a frustrating open to the season, Dallas rediscovered its offensive form against Washington on Sunday. Dak Prescott displayed the same pinpoint passing and fantastic rapport with CeeDee Lamb that helped propel the Cowboys to a No. 2 finish in yards per game last season. There are still concerns about the defense, but for now, the ‘Boys will enjoy their first win of 2026. USA Today : 12 (LW: 15) Same story here. You knew QB Dak Prescott was now the franchise’s all-time leader in TD passes (249). But did you know he’s one win from defeating NFC East rivals 21 times in a row at home, which would break Tom Brady’s post-merger NFL record against a divisional foes? However Prescott will have to wait until the Eagles visit on Thanksgiving to take aim at that TB12 standard. Yahoo : 17 (LW: 16) The Cowboys dropped here. Hmm. That’s more of what we expected from the Cowboys. Dak Prescott threw four touchdowns, breaking Tony Romo’s franchise record for career TD passes. The offense came alive but the defense is still a question after giving up 389 yards despite Jayden Daniels missing half of the game due to an elbow injury. The Cowboys didn’t have a sack. They have two sacks in two games, and the only player with more than a half-sack is safety Caleb Downs. Things will be fine if the Cowboys’ offense is putting up 37 points like Dallas did Sunday, but it’s hard to win that way in the NFL. It’s easier to attack those issues after a win, and team owner Jerry Jones is optimistic. “We’re better than we’ve been in the last two years on defense,” Jones said, according to the team’s site. “And offensively, we saw some really impressive things tonight.” CBS Sports : 17 (LW: 17) No movement. The offense impressed in the blowout of the Commanders. But the best news is the defense made strides after a bad opener. The Athletic : 16 (LW: 20) Another bump up. Rookie spotlight : Jaishawn Barham Sure, first-round safety Caleb Downs is starting and filling up the stat sheet — he has 17 tackles, a sack and two forced fumbles — but have you seen what the less heralded Barham is up to? The third-round defensive end from Michigan has 13 tackles, including two for loss. He had seven tackles and a forced fumble against Washington. ProFootballTalk : 20 (LW: 22) The lowest ranking of the bunch. The defense is still a work in progress. Week To Week Movement Full Power Rankings Roundup

title: Broncos vs Rams preview: Denver aims to stack wins
summary: Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos got that winning feeling. Now the Broncos will hope for a better showing in prime time than they did in their season opener on Monday Night Football. Up next is Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. As with Denver, the Rams got their first […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on during the third quarter of the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos got that winning feeling. Now the Broncos will hope for a better showing in prime time than they did in their season opener on Monday Night Football. Up next is Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. As with Denver, the Rams got their first win of the season. In a Week 3 matchup of two of the better teams in the NFL, this could be a fun game. The Broncos currently sit as +2.5-point underdogs to LA at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 45.5 points. Offensive Rankings LA Rams : Sixth in total offense (385.5 yards per game), sixth in rushing offense (142.5 YPG), 10th in passing offense (243 YPG), 22nd in scoring offense (17.5 points per game). Denver : Twenty-fifth in total offense (284 yards per game), 27th in rushing offense (82.5 YPG), 20th in passing offense (201.5 YPG), tied for 26th in scoring offense (15 points per game). Defensive Rankings LA Rams : Seventh in total defense (280.5 yards per game), 19th in rushing defense (113 YPG), seventh in passing defense (167.5 YPG), tied for eighth in scoring defense (16.5 points per game). Denver : Seventeenth in total defense (330 yards per game), 29th in rushing defense (157.5 YPG), eighth in passing defense (172.5 YPG), 13th in scoring defense (22 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Sunday night’s game. Start fast offensively Nix and the Broncos offense finally clicked in the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars. There was great balance with the run and pass game; Nix was throwing to the middle of the field, and Davis Webb got into a rhythm with his playcalls. Now do that from the first drive of the game and stay consistent throughout. Denver’s offense has the potential to do it; now, just make it happen. Given how dangerous and explosive Stafford and the LA offense are, the Broncos must start fast. — Ian St. Clair Get pressure on Stafford We just watched the Rams passing attack without Puca Nacua, and it was pretty scary. The best way to help keep Davante Adams in check (and Nacua if he’s healthy) is to make Matthew Stafford uncomfortable. — Adam Malnati Score more points than the Rams Stats and analytics don’t lie. Unlike in Week 1, the Broncos outscored their opponent and remained undefeated. My key to the game is just that. Score more points than the Rams, and they will walk away with a victory. — Scotty Payne Contain the short, quick passing game I feel like the Rams feast on the short-pass game, and that is an area the Broncos defense struggled with at times last year. For me, the pass rush will be a critical component of success in this matchup, and they have to show up and put Matthew Stafford on skates. — Tim Lynch Establish the run The Broncos gained over 100 yards on the ground against the Jaguars. To limit the impact of Matthew Stafford and the Rams’ offense, Denver needs to be committed to the run on Sunday Night Football and control the pace of the game. I was impressed with Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb’s halftime adjustments. The Broncos ran the ball efficiently under center. In turn, that also helped Bo Nix play better. Achieving this will help them sustain long drives and keep Stafford and his top-tier playmakers on the sidelines. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday night’s game?

title: Broncos vs. Jaguars stats analysis from Week 2
summary: The Denver Broncos bounced back from from that humiliating loss to the Kansas City Chiefs to win a come-from-behind game against a very strong Jaguars team. The Jacksonville Jaguars had won nine straight regular season games coming into Sunday’s matchup with the Broncos, although they did lose to the Buffalo Bills in the playoffs last […]
full_text: The Denver Broncos bounced back from from that humiliating loss to the Kansas City Chiefs to win a come-from-behind game against a very strong Jaguars team. The Jacksonville Jaguars had won nine straight regular season games coming into Sunday’s matchup with the Broncos, although they did lose to the Buffalo Bills in the playoffs last season. The Bronco defense which was atrocious against the Chiefs in missing 24 tackles, missed only 3 tackles against the Jaguars. Both Alex Singleton and DJ Jones were tagged with four missed tackles in the loss to the Chiefs. Neither player had a missed tackle against the Jaguars. While the Bronco defense is still “leading” the NFL in missed tackles with 27, the Colts are close with 22. After missing 24 tackles in week 1, the Bronco defense missed only 3 in week 2. pic.twitter.com/ksg7lDUOtX — Joe Mahoney (@ndjomo76) September 22, 2026 What concerns me more than the missed tackles is the lack of pressure. The Broncos are only getting pressure on 20.3 percent of dropbacks. That is currently 23rd. Two defenses are getting pressure on more than 40% of opponent dropbacks, The Raiders and the Vikings. In terms of allowing pressure, the Bronco offense is currently 15th according to PFR – allowing pressure on 21.9 percent of dropbacks. The best pass blocking team right now (by pressure allowed) is the 49ers (9.38 percent). The worst pass blocking team right now is the Panthers allowing pressure on an astounding 41.5 percent of dropbacks. By most accounts the Broncos allowed a great deal of pressure on Bo Nix in game one and they were much better in game two. NFL.com shows that the Broncos allowed seven QB pressures in game 1 and only three in game two . The Jaguars got 10 pressures on the Browns the week before . The Bronco run game was mostly silent in week one partly because of the lack of run plays. Denver had 14 actual runs (kneeldowns count as runs in the NFL STILL, for some stupid reason) for 62 yards (4.43 YPC). That’s respectable, but the run game was not employed very often. The Broncos had 25 actual runs for 107 yards on Sunday against the Jaguars (4.28 YPC). The Broncos have been about average in terms of avoiding wasted run plays. Denver has five runs that gained 11 or more yards – one by Pat Bryant, two by JK Dobbins and two by Jonah Coleman – that’s 12.8 percent. So far the average NFL team gets 16.7% stuffed, 24.3 % gaining 1-2 yards, 31% gaining 3-5 yards, 18.8% gaining 6-10 yards, and 9.2% gaining 11 or more yards. Every team in the NFL has as least one long run with the exception of the Browns. The Texans have been the worst at getting 28 percent of their runs stuffed (no gain or loss). The Broncos had 48 runs in 2025 that gained 11 or more yards with JK Dobbins getting 19, Bo Nix 13, RJ Harvey 8, Jaleel McLaughlin 4, Marvin Mims 2, and Troy Franklin and Adam Prentice both had one. The run game looked much better against the Jaguars than it did against the Chiefs. The Broncos have 11 total runs that gained 6 or more yards, with eight of those coming against Jacksonville and only three coming against Kansas City. The defense did a much better job of stopping the run against the Jaguars. After giving up 223 rushing yards on 35 actual runs (6.37 YPC) the week before, the Broncos allowed 95 yards on 24 carries on Sunday (3.96 YPC). The Denver defense is still 30th in the NFL in YPC allowed, but they were 31st after week one. Not missing tackles is good for stopping the run.

title: The Broncos offense is unlocked with Jaylen Waddle
summary: Thinking back to last week’s win, I think that may have been the first time that the Broncos under Sean Payton have used the same player over and over again throughout the game offensively to dominate the opponent. Jaylen Waddle popped off with 8 catches for 138 yards. I think that is notable because this […]
full_text: Thinking back to last week’s win, I think that may have been the first time that the Broncos under Sean Payton have used the same player over and over again throughout the game offensively to dominate the opponent. Jaylen Waddle popped off with 8 catches for 138 yards. I think that is notable because this is not what the Sean Payton offense does. His offense is never that simple. Payton beats teams by scheming players into plus situations and creating plays from any player at any depth on the roster. Heck, Nate Adkins popped off from the tight end room last week (which doesn’t surprise me…he’s probably the best 2-way tight end on the team). But what’s worth noting is that Waddle showed the capability to create his own separation over and over. Bo Nix showed that he trusts and understands where to lead Waddle with that blazing speed. We’ll see more of this as the season wears on, but one thing to watch is not what Waddle does in the next few weeks. No, look out for who else gets big plays off the pressure Waddle is now going to create as teams start doubling him and running coverage games to remove his deep crossers. We’ll likely see some big games from Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, and RJ Harvey in the near future that you will be able to point to Waddle’s clearing route opening up holes in the defense that Payton and protegee Davis Webb are going to attack. The Broncos needed a talent infusion on offense just for this reason. The offense is going to be able to really start humming as you give one of the league’s best offensive minds more ways to scheme guys open. title: Broncos vs. Jaguars: The No Bull Review
summary: It feels good to see our team hit the reset button, lock in, and get the W for the fans on their home field. They looked much more like the team we saw last season and far less like whatever it was we witnessed last Monday night. Given last year’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos catches a pass during the fourth quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images It feels good to see our team hit the reset button, lock in, and get the W for the fans on their home field. They looked much more like the team we saw last season and far less like whatever it was we witnessed last Monday night. Given last year’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, I was pretty worried about this matchup. The Jags are a well-coached team that has playmakers on both sides of the ball. But the Denver Broncos came out looking to take a big step forward in 2026. The defense played actual tackle football this week. The offense finally took off the kiddie gloves and got to work. Offense Davis Webb is taking strides just like the offense. The first half was mostly a head-scratcher offensively. By the end of the game, I felt much better about the play calling from Davis Webb. Last week and in the first half of this game, the play calls all seemed to be 5 yards deep at most, with way too many screens being called early and often. Screens are a part of the Sean Payton offense and have always been so. I just wasn’t a fan of how much they were used against the zone defense of the Jags with only one blocker to help vs 3 defenders. Honestly, if the Broncos would just start off throwing more of their intermediate passes, it would back up the defense, which would open up more for them in the running game and running-adjacent screen plays. The other thing offensively that needs work is the number of penalties. We are getting false starts and illegal formation penalties consistently, and it is a sign of either poor coaching or a lack of focus from the players (or both). Finally, the offense absolutely needs to spend some quality time with their goal-line offense. If you are going to enforce your will in the running game, then get your bigs, run out your fullback, and smash some fools 3 downs in a row to get your score. If you want to play patty-cake instead, then spread them out with either 12 or 11 and pass the ball. Toss plays on 3rd and 1 in single back against a superb run-defending team is a waste of a play. Quarterbacks Bo Nix finally got online after 6 quarters of play. I guess we may want to consider playing him more in the preseason so we can hit the ground running in the future. But let’s talk more about that next offseason. His interception at the goal line was inexcusable. It was just a play where he went off design and yolo’d the ball to the corner instead of reading the defenders post-snap. He could have gotten a touchdown by passing to Waddle, and it would have been a much safer play even if it didn’t work. On a positive note, I know there are those here at MHR that have bought into some nonsense that Bo sucks against zone defense. Go watch the tape from this game. The Jags ran zone the majority of the time, and Bo carved it up like a Thanksgiving turkey. If he wasn’t able to have success against teams playing zone, he would have washed out 2 years ago. I love seeing Bo hitting the plays downfield. He obviously was fire on the crossers with Waddle, but he hit Franklin at the left sideline, Engram down the seam, and Waddle on a filthy double move on the right sideline. When you have a quarterback hitting all levels of the field, good things are going to happen offensively. Line The pass blocking held up much better this week (still had a pressure on McGlinchey this week), but there’s work to be done in the run blocking game. Too many defenders are able to shed blockers and stop runs. I’d like to see more grit in our blocking game to enable our runners a little more room to rumble. We did see some runs by both Dobbins and Coleman that went for explosive gains, but too many of their runs were stopped for less than 3 yards. Running Backs Jonah Coleman got quite a few good snaps in this game due to Dobbins having a pulled hamstring. I loved seeing him run with vision behind some excellent blocking up front for his touchdown. Neither he nor Dobbins ran at an amazing rate (3.9 ypc and 3.6 ypc, respectively), but they ran well enough. I did like seeing Coleman show his receiving chops with 3 catches for 19 yards. Tyler Badie also got some extra work. He mainly helped with his one catch of 27 yards and some excellent pass blocking. Receivers Welcome to Denver, Jaylen Waddle! Man, does this cat have a gear that other players do not have. His speed was on display, opening up some really simple routes because the defenders just do not have the ability to stay with him. The crossing routes vs. man or match were just constantly there all game long. I damn near fell out of my seat laughing when he pulled a split-second double move and shook his defender straight out of his ankles. Speed kills in the NFL, and my boy Waddle has it in spades. Let’s give some love to Troy Franklin, who made a one-handed catch down the left sideline off a dime pass from Nix for 27 yards. He may be the most talented #5 WR in the NFL. Also, welcome back, Nate Adkins. We missed you last season! Adkins balled out from the tight end position for the Broncos in this game with 3 catches for 32 yards, including a touchdown on a play-action bootleg inside the 10. Also, let’s give Evan Engram some love for that great catch on a crosser where he had to dig the pass out off a low throw from Nix. Defense Rumor has it that Vance Joseph opened up practice this past week with tackle drills. His team responded with a much more sound job this week tackling with proper form and angles. The defense was smothering, honestly. That’s a very talented offense in Jacksonville. Holding them to 13 points through 4 quarters is pretty darn impressive. Luckily for the defense, the Jags felt strongly about letting Lawrence air it out. This game may have gone differently if they had run Bhayshul Tuten more. Front 7 Malcolm Roach had a monster game this week with 1 sack, 2 TFLs, and 2 quarterback hits. Both he and Zach Allen were disruptive forces, shooting gaps and creating pressure. Que Robinson had a great sack off the edge with help from Zach Allen. He also got a TFL and quarterback hit in the game. I have been a bit bummed with what we’ve seen so far from Jonah Elliss. He did put big pressure off a stunt to the inside and tipped a pass away, but outside of that, his work on the edge has been somewhat lackluster from a pass-rushing perspective. Alex Singleton, for the second week in a row, gave up an unnecessary roughness penalty in the red zone with the helmet-to-helmet hit. To his credit, he had an excellent pass defense at the goal line, hitting the receiver and forcing the ball out on 3rd down. Secondary Riley Moss gets my game ball this week. He was an absolute baller in this game from start to finish. I do think his illegal contact penalty early was nonsense. He let the guy run after 5 yards, just like he is supposed to. It was a very ticky-tack call to bail the Jags out of a turnover. He played inside leverage perfectly to get an interception on a horrendous throw by Lawrence (it was as bad as Bo’s last week). He almost had another interception late that had a chance to score and ended the game with 3 passes defended and one interception. Patrick Surtain saved a touchdown with a shoestring tackle on Washington. He also defended a pass late by being in his receiver’s hip pocket while being completely oblivious as to where the ball was, which doinked off his helmet. It worked, though…he didn’t interfere with the route and broke up the play. Special Teams Wil Lutz put in another excellently boring game for a kicker. He was perfect on extra points and field goals (2 of each). Tyler Badie had a very nice return in the 2nd quarter for 38 yards. It almost made me not miss Marvin Mims…almost. Final Thoughts The…

title: NFL Power Rankings for Week 3: Denver Broncos solidly in the Top 10
summary: Predictably, I ghosted this post last week because I didn’t want to look at the kneejerk reactions or blog about them. I’m not proud of it, but I’m not apologizing for it either. NFL Power Rankings for Week 3: Denver Broncos solidly in the Top 10The bounce-back must have been incredibly because the Denver Broncos […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Alex Singleton #49 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during the third quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Predictably, I ghosted this post last week because I didn’t want to look at the kneejerk reactions or blog about them. I’m not proud of it, but I’m not apologizing for it either. NFL Power Rankings for Week 3: Denver Broncos solidly in the Top 10The bounce-back must have been incredibly because the Denver Broncos are mostly all solidly within the Top 10 and only one major outlet knocking them out of it. If I’m being honest, I think 6th is rather fair given the 1-1 start and one of those games being U-G-L-Y. If they take care of business at home against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football , then we should see a big recovery back into the upper echelon of NFL power rankings. NFL.com – 6th Denver’s Jekyll-and-Hyde offense is back, but that’s better than what Sean Payton’s team produced in Week 1 . The Broncos withstood early challenges presented by the Jaguars , came together defensively to stay within striking range — their third quarter goal-line stand swung the momentum in their favor — and woke up offensively with enough time to complete the comeback. Much like last season, I’d like to see that type of output happen earlier in a game, but at least Denver was able to get Jaylen Waddle going. CBS Sports – 9th Rallying from 10 down in the fourth quarter was impressive in beating the Jaguars. The defense really showed up in the second half. NBC Sports – 6th Jaylen Waddle arrives, a few days later than they’d hoped. ESPN – 8th Whether it’s an issue with his mechanics or rushing into plays, Nix is caught up in the Broncos’ propensity for slow starts under coach Sean Payton. In his first two seasons, Nix has thrown eight of his 23 interceptions in September — including three games with at least two picks. And in the season-opening loss to the Chiefs, Nix had his first career three-fumble game and was sacked four times, tying a career high. The Broncos escaped with a win in Week 2 after Nix and the offense got things cranked up in the second half. But he did throw his second interception of the season. New York Times – 11th The second-round running back might have earned a starting job Sunday. He led the Broncos with 39 yards on 10 carries and scored his first touchdown, celebrating with the Mile High Salute made famous by Terrell Davis. “You gotta pay respect to the guys that come before you,” Coleman said after the game. He’s the only player from Denver’s seven-man class making much of an impact. What do you think of these power rankings? Share in the comments section below!

If Nacua is unable to go, the Broncos would face a Rams team down Myles Garrett AND Puka Nacua. Puka Nacua’s status is TBD for next Sunday in Denver, per Sean McVay. A better approach with a star after learning a lesson with Myles Garrett in Melbourne. — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) September 22, 2026 Nacua was added to the injury report last week with a hip injury due to what Sean McVay described as groin soreness. His status for Monday Night’s game vs. the Giants was up in the air, but he was eventually ruled out. However, the Rams offense did not miss a beat without him, mostly due to the performance of veteran wide receiver Davante Adams. The veteran wide receiver had a vintage performance against a Giants secondary that had no answer for him and totaled 8 catches for a whopping 195 yards and 2 touchdowns. So, if Nacua does indeed miss Sunday Night’s game, the Broncos secondary still faces a tough test in Adams. With that said, the Broncos do have plenty of history with Davante Adams due to his time with the Raiders. In that time period, the veteran wide receiver did get the best of star corner Pat Surtain II a few times, so it should be fun watching those two go at it one more time. We will have to pay attention to Nacua’s status as the week progresses, but regardless, the Rams’ passing offense will be a tough test for the Denver Broncos’ secondary. Quarterback Matthew Stafford is the reigning NFL MVP and is led by head coach/play caller Sean McVay, who is one of the best in the business. Coming from the Shanahan tree, McVay loves to run the ball and often does it well, so the Broncos’ run defense will be tested again. Also, they love to utilize their tight ends, so we need to hope Vance Joseph’s history of tight end struggles doesn’t pop up on Sunday Night. This will be a big game for both teams that sit at 1-1 and are considered Super Bowl favorites. Neither team wants to fall to 1-2, so it should be a fun battle.
