title: Jonah Coleman explains why he pays homage to Hall of Fame RB Terrell Davis with the Mile High Salute
summary: Denver Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman had a bit of a breakout performance during Sunday’s comeback victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars. With injuries to JK Dobbins and RJ Harvey, Coleman was thrust into the starting role late in the 4th quarter in a close game between two of the better teams in the AFC, […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 20: Running back Jonah Coleman (20) of the Denver Broncos gives a Mile High Salute after a touchdown run during the second half a 20-13 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colo. (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Denver Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman had a bit of a breakout performance during Sunday’s comeback victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars. With injuries to JK Dobbins and RJ Harvey, Coleman was thrust into the starting role late in the 4th quarter in a close game between two of the better teams in the AFC, and he did not disappoint. Not only did he ice the game late with some key runs, but he also scored his first career touchdown and hit the Mile High Salute afterwards, paying homage to Hall of Fame running back Terrell Davis. Jonah Coleman with his first of many Mile High salutes pic.twitter.com/rhMehYVGjF — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 After the game, Coleman was asked about paying homage to the ‘Mile High Salute’ as his touchdown celebration, and he told reporters, “You just have to pay respect to the guys that came before you”. “You just have to pay respect to the guys that came before you. [Pro Football Hall of Fame RB] Terrell [Davis], him and I have the same marketing rep, so we talked before, talked a couple of times. He’s one of the best to ever to do it. I just felt like I could pay my dues and pay my respects because, at the end of the day, you are playing for something bigger than yourself.” Coleman just gets it. He’s a talented runner; he showcased his high-level football IQ by sliding in-bounds after picking up the first down, and is showing his appreciation to the legends before him. He is going to quickly become a fan favorite in Broncos Country, if he isn’t already. The legend of Jonah Coleman could continue to grow this weekend. Both JK Dobbins and RJ Harvey are dealing with hamstring injuries, and those injuries specifically can linger for a bit. So, Coleman could see a larger role vs. the Rams on Sunday Night. On Monday, Broncos head coach Sean Payton said he believes all three of the running backs can be bell cow backs and handle a majority of the carries. He also added, “I think there’s a lot ahead of us this week relative to who our runners are going to be.” “So yesterday, [RB] RJ [Harvey] was out, and then [RB] J.K. [Dobbins] got nicked up and wasn’t able to finish. None of that today on Monday is at a place where we’re—I think all three of those players we’re discussing can be bell cow, handle a majority of the carries. Yes, I think there’s a lot ahead of us this week relative to who our runners are going to be.” The Broncos running back room will become clearer as the week progresses. Second-year back RJ Harvey practiced on a limited basis twice last week and was deemed questionable before he was ruled out of Sunday’s game, so he seems fairly close to returning barring any setbacks. As for Dobbins, he left the game late, and reports came out yesterday that the veteran back is “good” , so we will have to see how he progresses throughout the week. Still, Coleman deserves more carries. I have said this multiple times this week already, and I am saying it again. It is only a matter of time before he takes over this backfield, and I think it should be sooner rather than later. Obviously, Dobbins and Harvey will still be involved, but Coleman cannot go back to the role had in Week 1 vs. the Chiefs.

title: Detroit Lions mailbag: What shakeups are coming on defense?
summary: Changes are coming for the Detroit Lions defense. After giving up the second-most points through two weeks and having an extended weekend to diagnose their problems, Lions coach Dan Campbell promised changes were coming. “We’re going to do a couple of things defensively. We’re going to move some guys around,” Campbell said Monday. “We’re going […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NY - SEPTEMBER 17: Christian Izien #5 of the Detroit Lions lines up before the snap during an NFL game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Changes are coming for the Detroit Lions defense. After giving up the second-most points through two weeks and having an extended weekend to diagnose their problems, Lions coach Dan Campbell promised changes were coming. “We’re going to do a couple of things defensively. We’re going to move some guys around,” Campbell said Monday. “We’re going to give some guys some more opportunities to play here and shake it up a little bit. And because they’ve earned that, we’ve got some guys in here that have earned some play time that they deserve a chance to do more for us.” On top of that, the Lions have to make some adjustments in the secondary after losing starting safety Avonte Maddox for the season to a foot injury. They started by signing Jalen Mills to the practice squad and poaching rookie safety Bishop Fitzgerald, but more mixing and matching is certainly on the way. On this week’s Midweek Mailbag podcast, Erik Schlitt and I offer ideas and depth chart shakeups the Lions may consider moving forward. Our discussion starts at safety, where the Lions have some choices to make. Will the Lions roll with Chuck Clark and Thomas Harper as starters, or will Christian Izien take over one of those roles? Schlitt suggests the Lions may have a three-person rotation at safety moving forward. But if the Lions pull Izien from the nickel position, how will that impact the cornerback room? Will Roger McCreary become the full-time starter, or will rookie Keith Abney see more opportunities? If it’s McCreary, then the domino effect continues at outside cornerback. Who is CB3? Is this where Ennis Rakestraw or Nick Whiteside get the call-up to the game-day roster? And is Rock Ya-Sin’s starting job in jeopardy? That conversation kicks off this week’s podcast, but there are plenty of topics we cover this week, including: Is it practical to simplify the defense right now? Why does the defense keep looking good in training camp, but fail to carry it over to the regular season? Are safeties more important than cornerbacks in this defense? Is Brad Holmes to blame for early extensions that have backfired because of injury (Kerby Joseph, Alim McNeill)? Does Kelvin Sheppard need a senior defensive assistant? What’s more likely: Campbell fires Sheppard midseason, the Lions hire a defensive assistant, or Detroit rides out the season and reassesses in 2027? Why does Dan Campbell have such a short leash on offensive coordinators, but leeway for Aaron Glenn and Sheppard? When, if ever, will the Lions get offensive weapon reserves (Jacob Saylors, Tay Martin, Tom Kennedy) involved in the offense? You can hear our answers to the questions by searching “Pride of Detroit” on any of your favorite podcasting platforms, or just use the Spotify embed below: If you’d like the watch the podcast, which has a ton of extra content in between segments that is not included on the audio version, you can catch replays over on our YouTube page and Twitch channel .

title: Free agent RB Jamaal Williams contacted Detroit Lions about a reunion
summary: Jamaal Williams was one of the most beloved players for the Detroit Lions during his two-year stint with the team from 2021-22. His energy was palpable, he showed leadership in times of strife, and he was also pretty dang good, rushing for 17 touchdowns in 2022—a franchise high at the time. He left Detroit after […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - JANUARY 01: Jamaal Williams #30 of the Detroit Lions reacts after the Lions defeated the Chicago Bears, 41-10, at Ford Field on January 01, 2023 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jamaal Williams was one of the most beloved players for the Detroit Lions during his two-year stint with the team from 2021-22. His energy was palpable, he showed leadership in times of strife, and he was also pretty dang good, rushing for 17 touchdowns in 2022—a franchise high at the time. He left Detroit after a free agency contract dispute, and his career fizzled away after two unsuccessful years with the New Orleans Saints. Williams has been out of football since the end of the 2024 season, but he wants back, and he’s been keeping in shape to do so. Apparently he is very much interested in a reunion in Detroit, despite a slightly messy divorce in 2023 . Williams told the Detroit Free Press this past weekend that he called Lions coach Dan Campbell about a possible return to Detroit. Campbell responded that they’d keep the door open, but his services were not needed at this time. “He reached out to Lions coach Dan Campbell last weekend to let Campbell know he was on the comeback trail,” Dave Birkett wrote. “And while Campbell said the Lions are holding tight at running back for now but would keep him in mind if things change, Williams is hopeful he’ll land a job soon and ready to contribute when he does.” As for the way things ended in Detroit, Williams doesn’t take it personally. “I didn’t want to go nowhere. I wanted to be there,” Williams told Birkett. “That’s where I wanted to be, but at the same time it’s just like, ‘We just got done having this crazy season, what am I doing that you don’t think I deserve?’ And they had their right, they have their things and it’s cool. And then at the time, it was just the Saints who offered what I wanted. They gave it to me and I ended up there. And that’s pretty much it. There’s no personal feelings, no hard feelings.” The Lions are down their RB2 with Isiah Pacheco sidelined indefinitely after going through back surgery recently . Reports suggest Pacheco won’t be back until December at the earliest, potentially leaving a power back role for someone like Williams. However, the Lions have increased the workload of Jahmyr Gibbs, which has severely lessened the role of backup running back in Detroit. Through two weeks, Gibbs’ is currently tied with Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker for the most touches in the NFL (56). Beyond that, the Lions have shown a lot of faith in 2024 fourth-round pick Sione Vaki to pick up the slack. Though he only has three rushes and two catches, Vaki has played 33 offensive snaps, providing Gibbs with some rest and the Lions offense with a decent pass protector. Detroit also has Jacob Saylors, a strong special teamer who proved he has some rushing skills when he led the NFL in rushing yards this preseason. As Campbell told Williams, their situation could certainly change. But, for now, it looks like any hope for a reunion between the Lions and Williams is not in the cards.

title: Detroit Lions scouting report: Jets are improved, but by how much?
summary: With an embarrassing performance on “Thursday Night Football,” the Detroit Lions turn the page and shift their attention to the New York Jets. Lions head coach Dan Campbell has faced his former offensive coordinator in Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson, winning both games, and now he’s facing off against former defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: The defensive team of the New York Jets celebrate after recovering a fumble during the fourth quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images With an embarrassing performance on “Thursday Night Football,” the Detroit Lions turn the page and shift their attention to the New York Jets. Lions head coach Dan Campbell has faced his former offensive coordinator in Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson, winning both games, and now he’s facing off against former defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn. Glenn’s looking to improve after an awful 2025 in his head-coaching debut season and keep his head above water. Detroit enters the contest 1-1, and after a tough loss on national television, they’ll be hungry to get back on the field and right the wrongs of last week. New York is also 1-1 and coming off an overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers at home. The Lions need this win badly to wash the bad taste out of their mouths early in the season. The Jets will want to bounce back from the win they fumbled and regain momentum. Let’s take a deep look at the Jets and how much they’ve changed ahead of Week 3. New York Jets 2025 season 3-14 record (4th in AFC East) 29th in points for, 31st in points allowed Overall DVOA: 32nd (30th on offense, 31st on defense) 2025 was not a fun introduction to being a head coach for Glenn. The defense was a laughing stock in the NFL, and the offense had a revolving door at quarterback. Injuries also didn’t help the team’s chances of putting something together. After having successful seasons in Detroit, Glenn got another taste of what it’s like to be at the bottom again. At quarterback, the Jets had Justin Fields, Tyrod Taylor, and Brady Cook all start last season. Together, the trio threw for 2,385 yards, 15 touchdowns, and 13 interceptions. Fields was the best of the three, throwing for seven touchdowns and only one interception, but he was benched by Glenn after starting 2-7. Taylor and Cook could manage only one win between them, and neither threw more touchdowns than interceptions. The Jets leaned on the ground game, with running back Breece Hall rushing for 1,065 yards, averaging 4.4 yards per carry, and tying with Fields for the most rushing touchdowns with four. While they didn’t find the end zone often, the unit was their most consistent. Star receiver Garrett Wilson only played in seven games and still finished as the team’s top receiver with 395 yards and four touchdowns on 36 catches. Rookie tight end Mason Taylor impressed with 44 catches, 369 yards, and a touchdown. The defense is where this team fell apart the most, as they had the fewest takeaways in the NFL with four, all fumbles. The Jets became the first team in NFL history to go a full season without recording a single interception. The best player on defense was EDGE Will McDonald IV, who led the team with eight sacks. With the defense struggling, the Jets traded both DT Quinnen Williams and CB Sauce Gardner to help kick-start a full rebuild. Overall, it was a disaster of a season for the Jets. The biggest problem was the defense, which allowed the second-most points in the league at 29.6. Glenn didn’t impress and fired multiple assistant coaches after the season, bringing an overhaul to the coaching staff. 2026 offseason Key additions: EDGE Joseph Ossai, LB Demario Davis, DL David Onyemata, EDGE Kingsley Enagbare, K Jason Sanders, DT T’Vondre Sweat (trade), S Minkah Fitzpatrick (trade), QB Geno Smith (trade) Key losses: G Alijah Vera-Tucker, G John Simpson, LB Quincy Williams, EDGE Michael Clemons, K Nick Folk, EDGE Jermaine Johnson II (trade) 2026 NFL Draft picks Round 1: EDGE David Bailey Round 1: TE Kenyon Sadiq Round 1: WR Omar Cooper Jr. Round 2: CB D’Angelo Ponds Round 4: DT Darrell Jackson Jr. Round 4: QB Cade Klubnik Round 6: G Anez Cooper Round 7: S VJ Payne Jets general manager Darren Mougey made some big moves via trade to give the team new life, trading for safety Minkah Fitzpatrick and defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat. That wasn’t the only move on defense: he signed more EDGE rushers in Joseph Ossai and Kingsley Enagbare, while also adding interior help with defensive lineman David Onyemata and linebacker Demario Davis. On offense, more people left than arrived, as the team traded for quarterback Geno Smith to be their starter but lost both starting guards, John Simpson and Alijah Vera-Tucker. The defense also lost EDGE Jermaine Johnson in the trade for Sweat, along with linebacker Quincy Williams and EDGE Michael Clemons in free agency. Even special teams saw kicker Nick Folk move on before getting replaced by Jason Sanders. Once the draft started, the Jets got help in multiple spots, first on defense, drafting EDGE David Bailey to add firepower to that defensive line. The offense got two good weapons in tight end Kenyon Sadiq and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., relieving pressure on Wilson to do all the heavy lifting. New York shifted focus back to defense, selecting cornerback D’Angelo Ponds in the second round and defensive tackle Darrell Jackson Jr. in the fourth. To round things out, they drafted project quarterback Cade Klubnik, who they hope could be their future starter, and added depth on the offensive line and in the secondary. In the end, this team went hard to address its defensive issues from 2025, revamping its entire defensive line, improving its linebacker room and secondary. The offense could use more attention, but with a coach like Glenn, he’ll believe the defense can do the heavy lifting. After what happened in 2025, if the defense can even be a fraction better, this team can win more games in 2026. 2026 season thus far (1-1) Week 1: Defeated Tennessee Titans 23-10 Week 2: Lost to Green Bay Packers 20-17 (OT) Stats: 20th in points scored, 6th in points allowed Overall DVOA: 8th (14th on offense, 3rd on defense, 26th on special teams) The Jets have had a tale of two games so far this season. The Week 1 win against the Tennessee Titans was a strong defensive showing, holding the Titans to 195 total yards, getting three sacks, and recovering a fumble. The offense was average, with the running game as the heavy hitter, and it scored twice. It was a step in the right direction for the team that only captured a victory three times in 2025. Week 2 against the Green Bay Packers was similar, but also vastly different in a way. First, the defense played well again, holding the Packers to 199 total yards, getting three sacks, and recovering a fumble. That part is familiar, but the offense and coaching took a step back. After rushing for over 150 yards against Tennessee, New York only mustered 67 yards and found the end zone once. The Jets defense again did all it could to win the game, but the offense could only give them a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter before it all went south. New York allowed Green Bay to come back in the fourth quarter and force overtime. The coaching issues came in the fourth quarter, toward the end of regulation. Green Bay completed a 5-yard pass to make it fourth-and-5 at the Jets’ 45, and instead of calling a timeout with about a minute left, Glenn allowed the Packers to drain essentially all of the clock, giving Green Bay an opportunity at a game-winning hail mary with no risk. Then, once overtime started, the Jets made the controversial decision to take the ball first. It immediately backfired when Smith was sacked twice in a quick three-and-out. The defense would allow Green Bay to move down the field and kick the game-winning field goal. It was a massive failure by the team and completely erased all the good they had from the previous week. So far this season, the defense has carried the team, and the offense can’t seem to get things going through the air with Smith. He’s been accurate with a 70.8 completion percentage, but he has only one touchdown…

Lions coach Dan Campbell telegraphed this move on Monday, noting that the team needed both a shakeup in the secondary and some help at safety after Avonte Maddox suffered a season-ending foot injury [Note: Maddox is now officially on IR]. Earlier in the week, the Lions signed veteran Jalen Mills to their practice squad . “We had a workout this morning just looking for a veteran guy. And then we’re looking for some of these safeties that are on other teams right now that are promising young players that we could potentially poach and bring in and let them compete,” Campbell said. Fitzgerald went undrafted this year after playing for NC State and USC in college. In 2025, he was named First-Team All-Big Ten after tallying 51 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss and five interceptions for the Trojans. BISHOP FITZGERALD DOES IT AGAIN! INTERCEPTION! 🦈 pic.twitter.com/iOSxnHyCTc — Trojan Football ✌️ ᶠᵃⁿ (@TrojanFBx) September 14, 2025 Fitzgerald initially signed with the Tennessee Titans after going undrafted, but he failed to make the team’s 53-man roster. Shortly after, he signed to the Pittsburgh Steelers practice squad, where he’s been for the last three weeks. Here’s what NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein had to say about Fitzgerald coming out of college : Compact, ballhawking safety prospect with alignment versatility. Fitzgerald’s consistency of execution is quite different in coverage versus run support. In coverage, he is assignment-oriented, displaying an adequate mix of route balance and response quickness. He’s clear-eyed to recognize takeaway opportunities and has the ball skills to flip the field. He can match underneath but might not have the speed to stay in-phase if the route travels deep. As a run defender, Fitzgerald plays with urgency but issues diagnosing the play and suspect pursuit angles have led to chunk runs, creating an imbalance that affects his draft grade. The Lions still have an open spot on their 53-man roster after cutting Bachie and putting Maddox on injured reserve. We’ll see if any other moves are coming before Sunday’s matchup against the New York Jets.

title: NFL Week 3 power rankings: National media still debating Lions potential
summary: Immediately following the Detroit Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Buffalo Bills, the narrative surrounding the Lions was grim. Their offense struggled to get going early, and their defensive performance was riddled with mental mistakes, leading them into a hole they couldn’t climb out of. While the final score suggests the game was competitive—they lost […]
full_text: Sep 17, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell looks on in the first half against the Buffalo Bills at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Immediately following the Detroit Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Buffalo Bills, the narrative surrounding the Lions was grim. Their offense struggled to get going early , and their defensive performance was riddled with mental mistakes , leading them into a hole they couldn’t climb out of. While the final score suggests the game was competitive—they lost 41-31—the Bills controlled it throughout. In the ensuing days, fans expressed their concerns, local media broke down what went wrong, and the national media hammered the Lions’ defense, questioning whether they could correct their errors moving forward. However, when the power rankings were released on Tuesday, cooler heads prevailed as analysts realized that September football can be ugly, with many teams facing a plethora of issues. The Lions certainly have their problems, and with those obstacles come doubters, but there were a surprising number of national media outlets that expressed confidence in the Lions’ ability to right the ship quickly, with two outlets ranking the Lions as a top-10 team—including one that moved the Lions up INTO the top 10—and seven of the eight ranking the Lions in the top 15. Let’s take a look at where the national media believe the Lions stand entering the 2026 season in this week’s power rankings. The Athletic: 8 (Previous rank: 8) From Chad Graff and Josh Kendall : Rookie spotlight : Blake Miller The first-round tackle started in Week 1 but wasn’t active in Week 2 due to an ankle injury — and the offensive line missed him. Fifth-round cornerback Keith Abney had a TFL in Week 1 but was not active in Week 2. (On an unrelated note, the Lions could be big risers here soon. They face the Jets, Panthers, Cardinals and Packers next.) USA Today: 10 (Previous rank: 12) From Nate Davis : Just what they needed, S Avonte Maddox, who’d been pressed into the starting lineup himself, is out for the season with a foot injury. GM Brad Holmes needs to consider making a move or two to augment what is, by far, the NFC’s worst pass defense through two weeks. Yahoo Sports: 13 (Previous rank: 9) From Frank Schwab : The Lions have given up 658 passing yards, which is second-most in the NFL, with only the Colts being worse. They are decimated due to injuries, which is why they were working out defensive backs like Jordan Fuller and Jalen Mills on Monday, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. Safety Avonte Maddox is the latest to go down; he’ll miss the rest of the season due to a foot injury. Since halftime of the season opener, the Lions have given up 71 points and 804 yards. Facing Josh Allen in Week 2 factors into the defensive problems, but it’s still alarming. “Defensively, we knew it was a tall task, but we gave up too much,” Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. “There were some things in there that we have to get cleaned up. You have to play your best ball to have a chance to reduce points against that team and that quarterback, and we did not do that. We had a hand in helping them out there a little bit, and it wasn’t good enough. It’s not good enough.” The good news is the Lions still have an easy schedule, and there are winnable games coming up against the Jets, Panthers and Cardinals. Detroit needs to win those games to quell some fears, especially about its defense. NFL.com: 13 (Previous rank: 13) From Nick Shook : Detroit’s offense is capable of hanging with most everyone. The opposite is true of the Lions’ defense, at least until the unit gets healthier in the back end. With a leaky secondary existing as a major liability, the Lions can’t realistically expect to beat the best, but their fight (and Jared Goff’s second-half performance) in Thursday night’s loss to Buffalo shows they’re still an above-average team with clear flaws. ESPN: 14 (Previous rank: 11) From ESPN Staff, excerpt from Eric Woodyard : One thing we know about the QB1: Jared Goff continues to build a case the greatest QB in franchise history. Despite facing heavy pressure behind a banged-up offensive line, Goff has continued his efficient play in Year 11. He has racked up 25 straight games with a passing touchdown, which is the longest active streak in NFL and the longest in Lions history, per ESPN Research. He also reached 40,000 career yards in Buffalo, tying Kirk Cousins and Dan Marino as the fourth-fastest to that mark in NFL history (153 games). Goff is currently in his sixth season in Detroit and continues to reach major milestones at 31 years old. Sporting News: 14 (Previous rank: 13) From Vinnie Iyer : The Lions knew they might have some bigger defensive problems away from their Aidan Hutchinson-led front. They are trying to compensate better with Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown and the rest of their offensive stars, but are they stuck trying to win high-scoring games every week. CBS Sports: 15 (Previous rank: 15) From Pete Prisco : The defense is awful right now. The injuries in the secondary have crippled that unit. Can the offense score enough to compensate on a weekly basis? Sports Illustrated: 18 ( Previous rank: 10) From Connor Orr : I’m trying to separate the issues of some disappointing teams into different buckets. Are these seemingly broken scheme issues, talent issues, or both? The Lions’ back end seems to be both, with Kelvin Sheppard facing an early do-or-die scenario with Detroit sitting at 1–1. Dan Campbell has had a quick-ish hook for underperforming assistant coaches in the past. Will Sheppard buck that trend?

title: Discussion: What defensive personnel changes should the Detroit Lions make?
summary: On Monday, while addressing the team’s defensive woes, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell intimated that they plan on making some changes to their lineup. “We’re going to do a couple of things defensively. We’re going to move some guys around,” Campbell said. “We’re going to give some guys some more opportunities to play here and […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 13: Wide receiver Barion Brown (19) of the New Orleans Saints carries the ball under the pressure of linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez (44) of the Detroit Lions and long snapper Hogan Hatten (49) of the Detroit Lions during the an NFL football game between the New Orleans Saints and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 13, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images On Monday, while addressing the team’s defensive woes, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell intimated that they plan on making some changes to their lineup. “We’re going to do a couple of things defensively. We’re going to move some guys around,” Campbell said. “We’re going to give some guys some more opportunities to play here and shake it up a little bit. And because they’ve earned that, we’ve got some guys in here that have earned some play time that they deserve a chance to do more for us.” Now, we can speculate all we want on the Lions adding players—be it a practice squad poaching from another squad, the addition of someone like nickelback Kenny Moore , or whatever trade you’re still dreaming of—but for the purposes of this article, I’m going to keep the discussion on internal personnel decisions. Today’s Question of the Day is: What internal personnel changes should the Lions make? My answer: I’ve got a few ideas, one for each level of the defense. On the defensive line, I don’t have too many complaints. I do just think the players need to play more disciplined, very much including Aidan Hutchinson. I understand that people want more Derrick Moore, but he also has to earn those snaps, and he’s still very much learning and growing. That said, DJ Wonnum is off to a slower start than expected, so maybe this is the time to get Moore ramped up. At the linebacker level, I’d like to see more Malcolm Rodriguez and less Devin White. While I like the explosiveness and pass rush that White brings, the biggest thing that is currently ailing this defense is mental mistakes. White is not only still learning the defense, but his aggressive playstyle often leads to overpursuit and misdiagnosis. Rodriguez, on the other hand, plays assignment-sound football and is good with his fundamentals. PFF grades aren’t everything, but they’re telling in this moment: Rodriguez (on 35 snaps): 82.2 PFF grade White (on 51 snaps): 44.4 PFF grade On the back end, a conversation needs to be had about Rock Ya-Sin. He’s struggled mightily through two weeks. The problem is there is no clear answer among Detroit’s depth chart. Do you kick Roger McCreary to the outside, and if you do, are you prepared to start rookie Keith Abney at nickel? Do you elevate Nick Whiteside from the practice squad and push him into the starting lineup? Is it time to see what Ennis Rakestraw can do? I’m not particularly hopeful in any of those plans, but Ya-Sin’s play certainly hasn’t been acceptable. Then, when it comes to the safety position, figuring out how to replace Avonte Maddox—who is out for the season with a foot injury—won’t be easy. Maybe it’s just as simple as moving Thomas Harper into a starting position, but the 25-year-old is still pretty green. Detroit could drop Christian Izien back to safety, but it’s hard to know how ready he’d be for a full-time role after playing in just 26 snaps through two weeks. title: Dan Campbell defends DC Kelvin Sheppard: ‘He’s an outstanding coach’
summary: Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has recently come under fire after the team’s poor defensive start. Through two weeks of the NFL season, the Lions rank 31st in points allowed, yards allowed, and EPA/play. They’ve allowed the most first downs, the second-most passing yards, and fifth-most rushing yards. And after Thursday night’s disaster—which featured […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard reacts to a play against Washington Commanders during the second half at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md. on Sunday, November 9, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has recently come under fire after the team’s poor defensive start. Through two weeks of the NFL season, the Lions rank 31st in points allowed, yards allowed, and EPA/play. They’ve allowed the most first downs, the second-most passing yards, and fifth-most rushing yards. And after Thursday night’s disaster—which featured missed assignments and mental mistakes at every level of the defense—some have understandably wondered if the coaching staff is doing their job properly. Lions coach Dan Campbell is typically the first to put the blame on himself and the rest of the coaching staff. And on Monday, he did the same. “The bottom line is when it looks like that, we are responsible as coaches,” Campbell said. “I’m responsible. And so, it’s up to us to make sure the guy—we put the right guys in positions to where they can be trusted to do what they do.” It’s one thing to take accountability for a team’s performance, it’s another to lose faith that the coaching staff is incapable of fixing the problems. Later in the press conference, it became clear that Campbell still believes he’s got the right coaches in place, particularly when it comes to Sheppard. “I believe he’s an outstanding coach,” Campbell said of Sheppard. “There is a bump in the road. I think the staff is outstanding, that defensive staff. I think it’s a veteran staff, and I think they’re versatile, and we have got to coach better—and they can coach better. I can coach better, but I believe they’re the right guys to get this thing done.” When asked why he has faith in Sheppard, he spoke to his intelligence and grasp of defenses. “He knows what he’s doing, man,” Campbell said. “I think that he understands and has a real good grasp of—look, there are so many things that we came into this year from last year that we wanted to do.” One of those things was be more aggressive and dictate how the offense needs to play. Campbell pointed to the team’s ability to get opponents in second-and-long, noting that they lead the league in second-and-7+’s faced on defense. That’s one box checked, but now they need to obviously improve second and third down performances. “So, now it’s alright, now once we get them there, now what do we need to change?” Campbell said. “What do we need to do? What kind of packages do we need to run? And tighten up some of the players here on a few things.” Ultimately, it’s clear he trusts Sheppard’s knowledge and teaching abilities to turn around six bad quarters of football. “I believe he’s got a real good grasp of what offenses are trying to do. I think he’s got a good grasp of his own personnel. I think he’s doing a lot of the way we want to play here,” Campbell said. “And you know what? It didn’t work the other night and we didn’t coach it up good enough. And then we’ll adjust a little bit. We’ll adjust and we’ll get this thing back to where we need to get it. And it’s not going to all happen overnight, but as long as we just tighten a few things up and play a little bit better and a little more sound, that’ll go a long way.”

title: Dan Campbell can’t reassure fans who think Kerby Joseph’s career is done
summary: On Monday, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell noted that safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph will remain sidelined on the Physically Unable to Perform list, despite them being eligible to return to practice this week. He noted that Branch is closer to returning than Joseph, and then gave some additional details on Joseph’s recovery from […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 28: Kerby Joseph #31 of the Detroit Lions walks off the field after the game against the Cleveland Browns at Ford Field on September 28, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Monday, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell noted that safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph will remain sidelined on the Physically Unable to Perform list, despite them being eligible to return to practice this week. He noted that Branch is closer to returning than Joseph, and then gave some additional details on Joseph’s recovery from a knee injury that has now lingered for over a full year. “We were strengthening the knee, and it wasn’t a setback, but there was a little time there where we weren’t able to do everything we needed to do. And so now we’re back at it,” Campbell said. “And until we can get the knee to a certain point to where it feels strong, as strong as we can possibly get it and he feels comfortable. We’re not going to put him out there until he’s ready.” Lions fans have been understandably skeptical about Joseph’s football future. The team has said there is no surgery or procedure that fixes this issue. It’s something Joseph will just have to manage. At times, it seems like the former All-Pro safety was nearing a return, only for Campbell to provide a dubious update. So some have started to question whether Joseph will ever play another down of football in his life. On Tuesday, 97.1 The Ticket radio host Jim Costa asked Campbell what he would say to Lions fans who think Joseph will never play again. Campbell’s response was not reassuring. “Well, I wish I could make you feel good. I can’t make you feel good,” Campbell said. “It’s going to come as it comes, and he’s not ready. We’re trying to get him there as fast as we can, and we’re trying to be as smart about it as we can. And if he’s ready, when he’s ready, of course we want to play him and get him on the field.” Costa followed it up with another question, and Campbell gave a puzzling response that did not sound particularly good: Costa: “What would have to change? Because we’re coming up on a year since that Chiefs game. If he’s unable to practice what would change for him to get out there?” Campbell: “I guess, nothing.“ At this point, it certainly seems like the Lions are operating under the assumption they are going to get very little—if anything—out of Joseph this season. And you have to wonder what that means for the rest of his football career with a $16.6 million option bonus due in March of 2027.

title: Week 3 matchup with Packers is a homecoming of sorts for Falcons’ Za’Darius Smith
summary: The 2019 offseason was a busy one for Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst. In his second offseason at the helm of the franchise’s personnel department, Gutekunst headed into the start of free agency with a plan: spend money to bolster a few position groups in desperate need of help, most significantly the edge […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Za'darius Smith #55 of the Atlanta Falcons waves to fans during an NFL football game against the Carolina Panthers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2019 offseason was a busy one for Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst. In his second offseason at the helm of the franchise’s personnel department, Gutekunst headed into the start of free agency with a plan: spend money to bolster a few position groups in desperate need of help, most significantly the edge defenders. Gutekunst did just that, first agreeing to a 4-year deal with former Washington Commander Preston Smith before landing one of the biggest fish in the pond: Za’Darius Smith, who had spent his first four NFL seasons with the Baltimore Ravens. The Smith Brothers proved to be a formidable tandem for the next two seasons. Za’Darius recorded back-to-back Pro Bowl campaigns in 2019 and 2020, as he posted 13.5 and 12.5 sacks in the two seasons, respectively. Preston also had a double-digit sack season in the players’ first year in Green Bay with 12, though he tapered back a bit with just four in 2020. The 2021 season brought an abrupt end to the experiment, however. A back injury and controversy about not being voted a team captain led to Za’Darius playing in just one game, the season opener, before being shut down on injured reserve. Green Bay released him in the offseason before the last year of his 4-year contract, and he signed with the Minnesota Vikings, where he posted another ten-sack Pro Bowl season. Since then, Smith has bounced around to various teams, spending time with the Browns, Lions, and Eagles before landing in Atlanta this offseason. With a limited workload through two games with the Falcons, Smith has flashed some of the power rushing ability that made him a Pro Bowler in Green Bay and elsewhere earlier in his career. He has 2.5 sacks in just 44 defensive snaps so far this season, making him the only player on the Falcons’ roster with more than a half-sack so far this season despite being third among the team’s defensive ends in snaps. Two of those sacks came against his old teammate Aaron Rodgers in Week 1; meanwhile, Pro Football Reference has him down for a total of six QB pressures, certainly a solid rate to start the season. Thursday night’s game will be Smith’s fourth time matching up with the Packers since his split with the team after the 2021 season, though only one of the previous three games took place at Lambeau Field. That came right away in 2022 with the Vikings, though Smith had little impact with just three tackles in a 41-17 Packers victory late in the season. Smith’s other two games also both came as a divisional opponent — the Vikings defeated the Packers in Minnesota in week 1 of that 2022 season, and Smith was a member of the Detroit Lions in 2024 when they beat Green Bay 34-31 at Ford Field on Thursday Night Football. Both of those two games saw Smith record a sack. With starting end Samson Ebukam limited on the Falcons’ injury report this week, Smith might well be in line for a heavier workload. His snap count increased from 16 against the Steelers in Week 1 to 28 last Sunday against the Panthers. If Ebukam is significantly limited or inactive on Thursday, Smith will almost certainly be on the field for more than 30 snaps, and the Packers will need to find a way to cobble together a pass rush plan to minimize his impact on the game.

title: Packers say it’s ‘too soon’ to know if Jayden Reed will be out for the year
summary: In his press conference on Tuesday, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed that receiver Jayden Reed, who was knocked out against the New York Jets and suffered an injury to his neck, stayed overnight on the East Coast to undergo tests, but that he has since returned to Green Bay. He also stated […]
full_text: (Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In his press conference on Tuesday, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed that receiver Jayden Reed, who was knocked out against the New York Jets and suffered an injury to his neck, stayed overnight on the East Coast to undergo tests, but that he has since returned to Green Bay. He also stated that while the Packers officially list Reed with a back injury, it’s a neck injury that he suffered. What LaFleur wouldn’t make a firm statement on, though, was when Reed will be back. According to LaFleur, it’s “too soon” to know whether Reed will miss the rest of the 2026 season. Previously, Reed had been the team’s starting slot receiver, a role that returner Skyy Moore filled on Sunday after Reed dropped out of action. Reed also recently received a three-year, $50.25 million contract extension with the team and was supposed to be a big part of what they did in the passing game moving forward. This all came after the news of Zach Bako-Bewele admitting that he had a full tear of his patellar tendon in his right knee, the same one that he partially tore at the end of last season. That is a potentially career-altering injury for Bako-Bewele , who received his first game check for his four-year, $88 million deal in Week 1 of this season. Reed’s extension years don’t kick in until 2027, though he was paid a $16.5 million signing bonus this offseason. In other injury news, LaFleur said that he will give left guard Aaron Banks until game time before they rule him out for his knee/toe injuries, but that he expects Bako-Bewele’s injury replacement, Anthony Belton, to play on Thursday, despite him popping up on the injury report today with a shoulder issue . If Banks can’t go, it will likely be Donovan Jennings, who himself is on the injury report with a hand injury, who would get the first opportunity at left guard and then Jager Burton if Jennings can’t play. If Belton can’t play right tackle, one of John Williams or Travis Glover, who were both healthy scratches last week against the Jets, would have to start at right tackle. After LaFleur’s press conference, offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich stated that a reason why Burton isn’t being pushed into the lineup more is that the team wants continuity up front, despite having played five offensive line variations over the first two weeks of the season, and because they aren’t sure yet if he isn’t going to be playing at left guard, considering the team’s health at the position — a sign that Banks and Jennings really might be on the active/inactive bubble against the Atlanta Falcons.

summary: With right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele out for the remainder of the 2026 season with a full tear of his patellar tendon, the Green Bay Packers will be leaning on Anthony Belton, their 2025 second-round pick, to fill the gap at the position in 2026 (and maybe longer). full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images With right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele out for the remainder of the 2026 season with a full tear of his patellar tendon , the Green Bay Packers will be leaning on Anthony Belton, their 2025 second-round pick, to fill the gap at the position in 2026 (and maybe longer). On Tuesday, the Packers announced their injury report after their walkthrough, and it included Belton, with a new injury to his shoulder. In total, here’s the status of all of the Packers’ offensive linemen: Left tackle: Jordan Morgan – healthy Left guard: Aaron Banks – non-participant (knee/toe) Center: Sean Rhyan – healthy Right guard: Jacob Monk – healthy Right tackle: Zach Bako-Bewele – out for the year (knee) Backup left guard: Donovan Jennings – limited participant (hand) Backup right tackle: Anthony Belton – limited participant (elbow) Backup: Jager Burton – healthy Backup John Williams – healthy Backup Travis Glover – healthy Four injuries to the top seven options on the line is less than good. The team has nearly an entire offensive line’s worth of injuries on the 53-man roster right now, and they’re only two days away from playing against the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday Night Football . The other changes in status today on the injury report, from Monday’s estimation (the Packers did not practice) were defensive lineman Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Jennings (hand) being elevated from non-participant estimations to limited participants in the team’s walkthrough. Other limited participants, besides Campbell and the offensive linemen, were: cornerback Brandon Cisse ( wisdom teeth ), linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (shoulder) and defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (knee/concussion). The non-participants in practice (besides the offensive linemen) were defensive lineman Warren Brinson (calf) and Jayden Reed (neck). The Falcons seem to be taking a much different approach to their TNF prep, as they had a walkthrough on Monday, when Green Bay decided not to hit the field at all, and had a full practice on Tuesday, when the Packers held just a walkthrough. The only 53-man roster player who was limited or a non-participant for Atlanta today was edge rusher Samson Ebukam (hamstring), as starting cornerback A.J. Terrell was placed on the injured reserve earlier today . Another offensive lineman popping up on the injury report…add Anthony Belton as limited with an elbow. Aaron Banks a DNP as well. title: Packers rookie Brandon Cisse had wisdom teeth removed
summary: When the Green Bay Packers published their first injury report of Week 3 on Monday, the team listed one of the strangest statuses imaginable for an NFL team. Ahead of the team’s Thursday Night Football game this week, rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse was estimated to be a limited participant had the team practiced on Monday […]
full_text: Feb 26, 2026; Indianapolis, IN, USA; South Carolina defensive back Brandon Cisse (DB04) speaks to members of the media during the NFL Combine at the Indiana Convention Center. Mandatory Credit: Jacob Musselman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When the Green Bay Packers published their first injury report of Week 3 on Monday, the team listed one of the strangest statuses imaginable for an NFL team. Ahead of the team’s Thursday Night Football game this week, rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse was estimated to be a limited participant had the team practiced on Monday (which they did not do because of the short week), but the injury was formally listed as “teeth.” Did Cisse crack a tooth in Sunday’s win over the New York Jets? Was he getting new veneers put on, like so many other NFL players have in recent years? No, as it turns out, Cisse had his wisdom teeth removed, as he told the media on Tuesday , and he expects to have no issues playing against the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday. If Cisse had them removed on Monday, which would appear to be the only time that he could have had the procedure performed, it would be an impressively quick turnaround to play on Thursday even if he has no complications. Typically, patients are kept on a diet of exclusively liquids or extremely soft foods for the first few days following the extraction as bleeding and swelling gradually resolve. Speaking from my own experience, the recovery from that procedure, particularly if the teeth are impacted and all four are removed at once, can take several days. In high school, I had mine removed on a Thursday morning and I was still taking pain medication the following Monday, four days later. Playing on a Thursday night after a Monday morning procedure, at least in my own experience, would have felt impossible. Admittedly, I neither am nor ever was cut out to be a professional athlete, so Cisse’s mileage will surely vary from my own. Still, his status will be worth monitoring over the next 48 hours, even if he currently believes that he’ll be able to suit up normally this week. Maybe he can consult with his fellow rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton on the procedure. Surely, someone with the initials DDS will have some opinions on dental surgery.

title: Packers’ Zach Bako-Bewele tore his patellar tendon vs. the Jets
summary: According to The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman, Green Bay Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele said he “fully tore” his patellar tendon on Sunday against the New York Jets. Bako-Bewele partially tore his patellar tendon last year, which ended up requiring surgery. The full tear occurred in the same knee as his previous partial tear. There’s no […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman , Green Bay Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele said he “fully tore” his patellar tendon on Sunday against the New York Jets. Bako-Bewele partially tore his patellar tendon last year, which ended up requiring surgery. The full tear occurred in the same knee as his previous partial tear. There’s no way around this one: This is a brutal injury. It’s not only a 9- to 12-month recovery, but a full tear of the patellar tendon is maybe the hardest injury to bounce back from in sports. According to a paper written by the National Library of Medicine , only 21.4 percent of athletes “returned to their prior performance level within two years.” There was also a notable drop-off in the number of games that players ended up suiting up for before and after the injury/recovery process, according to the study. 2026 is the first year of Bako-Bewele’s four-year, $88 million extension that he signed back in 2025, before he suffered his first patellar tendon issue. The tackle carries a cap charge of $11.8 million this year and $17.9 million next year, with a dead cap of $18 million in 2027 — meaning that the team can’t cut him for cap relief next offseason. There’s a chance that Bako-Bewele will get paid $49.41 million over 2025-2027 for just 12 games of healthy play in 2025, the final year of his rookie contract, as he clearly didn’t look like himself over the two games he saw action in for 2026. In 2028, the Packers will have the option to move on from Bako-Bewele to free up cap space, as they’ll save around $12 million on the cap (after taking on around $12 million in dead cap) with a direct release. In the meantime, the starting right tackle for the Packers moving forward will be 2025 second-round pick Anthony Belton, who received the majority of reps for Green Bay at the position in training camp as Bako-Bewele ramped up.

full_text: (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s not like the Atlanta Falcons were playing great over the first two weeks of the season already, but their defenders are going to have to pick up even more of the slack moving forward. On Tuesday, the Falcons announced that they were shutting down cornerback A.J. Terrell, a former All-Pro who has been the team’s top cornerback for more than a half-decade. Terrell is going on the injured reserve for a minimum of four weeks, meaning he won’t be playing on Thursday Night Football against the Green Bay Packers. Terrell was listed on the Falcons’ injury report with a groin injury yesterday. Without Terrell, the starting outside cornerbacks for Atlanta are likely to be Mike Hughes (preferred starter) and C.J. Henderson (replacement starter). Henderson did not look good against the Carolina Panthers last week, as he allowed two touchdowns once Terrell went down. Henderson is a former 2020 first-round pick who is already with his fifth NFL club in his career. He is currently playing on a two-year, $2.4 million contract. Hughes is on his fourth team, and the 29-year-old is being paid $6 million per year, in the ballpark of Packers cornerback #4 and special teams ace Benjamin St-Juste ($4.8 million per year). To say the least, it’s not like Atlanta will be rolling out two studs out there on Thursday.

title: Packers Film Room: Dashing for a dagger
summary: Last week, we talked about the Green Bay Packers’ use of Dash motion and how they used the Vikings defensive tendencies to hit a play behind it. Today, we’re looking at that same motion and a play the Packers hit off of it in Week 2 against the New York Jets. Before we get started, […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers passes the ball against the New York Jets during the first half of the game at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, we talked about the Green Bay Packers’ use of Dash motion and how they used the Vikings defensive tendencies to hit a play behind it. Today, we’re looking at that same motion and a play the Packers hit off of it in Week 2 against the New York Jets. Before we get started, let’s talk about the type of motion. “Dash” motion is something we’ve been seeing quite a bit of around the league this year. It’s a type of slow motion that arcs behind the line, then run towards the line at the snap for a block. Over the first two weeks of this season, the Packers have used this motion 10 times. They have run on 8 of those for an average gain of 6.5 yards, and they have run the same power concept on every one of those runs. The Dash motion man kicks out the EMOL (End Man on Line), the right guard pulls and works as a lead, the rest of the line blocks down. (I have the pullers in blue to make it easier to see.) Last week, the Packers hit a backside slant late, as the Vikings were blitzing the backside every time the Packers showed that motion. This week, they had the backside WR run a Bubble. That Bubble tag was on the backside of every one of these plays this week. Last week the only time we saw a route run on the backside of one of these plays was the slant to Matthew Golden that we covered last week . The Jets played this route a couple different ways. When they aligned a man tight to Golden, that defender aligned outside and shadowed the bubble. (Bottom of the screen on the next clip.) When the Jets were in off coverage, the safety over Golden would shadow the bubble motion. (Top of the screen on the next clip.) Now, to the last play. After stopping the Jets on their first possession of overtime, the Packers drove down the field. With 5:47 remaining in overtime, they were facing 1st & 10 at the Jets’ 22 yard line. With the Jets already having had a possession, a field goal would win it, but you want to drive a little closer. Trey Smack had been a perfect 3/3 on field goals and extra points up until that point (due in some part to a great snap-and-hold operation ), but you want to make this a little easier on him. The Packers come out in 12 personnel (1 RB, 2 TE, 2 WR) in a completely balanced set: one wide receiver split to each side, an in-line tight end to each side, and a single back behind the QB. Matthew Golden [0] is split wide to the left and Christian Watson [9] is wide to the right. The cornerback over Golden is shaded to the inside shoulder and the safety is playing on the hash. This is important. Before the snap, Mark Redman [86] starts his Dash motion, triggering the play. At the snap, Golden bubbles out. Instead of handing it off – or throwing to Golden on the Bubble – Love throws a lollipop up the field. The cornerback is blitzing off the edge to try to stop the run from the backside, so he’s in no position to make a play on this ball. The safety playing so far inside is also in no position to make a play on this. By throwing it over the top, Love avoids any opportunity for the defender to that side to make a play. A couple interesting things here. The Jets did not really blitz their cornerbacks in this game. They blitzed on 31.25% of their defensive snaps (per SumerSports ), but, unless I missed some, this was the only time they blitzed a cornerback in this game. More than anything, I think the alignment of the cornerback and safety is what informed the decision to throw this. If the cornerback was playing on Golden’s outside shoulder, I think Love hands the ball off. If the Jets are in off coverage and the safety is over the top, I think Love throws this to Golden on the bubble. With the cornerback playing the inside shoulder and the safety playing on the hash, Love makes the decision to throw to Golden, but throw further outside and up-field than simply throwing the Bubble (since the cornerback could have a chance to knock down a throw to the flat). And, since Golden is running a Bubble, Love puts enough air under this ball to allow Golden to adjust as the ball is in the air. The cornerback blitzing makes this more open than it would have been, but even if that cornerback simply played how he had been playing this – a soft mirror on the Bubble – he still would not have been in a great position to defend this. I love the call in this moment (it was the best run concept on the day for the Packers), but I love seeing the recognition from Love at the line and the adjustment from Golden to be able to make this catch and pick up yards afterwards. By the time the dust had settled, it was a 14 yard gain, setting up a 26 yard field goal, which Smack knocked through. FOR THE WIN! 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/6SaV3LwqmI — Green Bay Packers (@packers) September 20, 2026 Albums listened to: Nicole Atkins – Drama ; Beck – Ride Lonesome

Through two seasons, he’d produced just seven sacks and 16 quarterback hits. He was solid against the run, but you don’t pick an edge rusher 13th overall because he’s stout in the ground game. Year three was promising, but then the injuries came. Nagging issues limited Van Ness to just nine games in 2025, and for more than a few of those nine, he clearly wasn’t quite himself. And then the Packers picked up his fifth-year option this past offseason. I was a fan of the move, but I can understand anybody who was skeptical. Injuries and a lack of production are a recipe for some negativity, and Van Ness had plenty of both of those things. But through two weeks, Van Ness has paid off every bit of faith the Packers have had in him. Two weeks does not a season make (and the Packers are thanking the ghost of Lombardi for that), but the start for Van Ness is about as promising as things could be. title: The Day After the Day After: Reliving the Houston Texans’ 20-6 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals
summary: The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 2: Houston’s D-Line was Good; Cincinnati’s was Better: The Texans generated 5 sacks, held the Bengals […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 20: Safety Jordan Battle #27 of the Cincinnati Bengals runs down the field after breaking up a pass as defensive tackle Kris Jenkins Jr. #90 of the Cincinnati Bengals signals incomplete during the NFL football game between the Houston Texans and Cincinnati Bengals on September 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 2: Houston’s D-Line was Good; Cincinnati’s was Better: The Texans generated 5 sacks, held the Bengals to 80 yards total rushing and made the Bengals work for everything. Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter upped their play. Yet, it was the Bengals’ D-Line that ruled the game. They held Houston to only 60 total yards rushing, with RBs Marks and Montgomery only managing 18 combined. They obliterated the Houston interior, and it was all Stroud could do to keep out of their way until the 4th Quarter, when the Bengals sacked him four times. They surrendered over 350 yards in the air, but only 6 points. Dexter Lawrence took whatever Texans’ interior player he faced and made them into a glorified blocking dummy. How dominant was that Bengals’ interior? Houston only attempted four designed running plays in the 2nd half. 0-4: Box Scores aren’t the end-all/be-all for a game. They can’t always tell the full story. However, there are times when they can say everything. If you had not watched the game and just went to the box score to see how this game played out, you would find this for Houston: 4th Down Conversions: 0/4 Red Zone (Attempts/Makes): 0/4 Last season, a big reason why the team struggled to that 0-3 and 3-5 start was that the offense could not convert on 3rd/4th Down and they couldn’t convert in the Red Zone. Houston was 5 of 17 on 3rd Down, so they were already in pain there. Yet, to go 0 for 4 on a follow-up 4th Down…not good at all. This included the 4th and 4 at the CIN 16 when the muffed FG snap happened; a 4th and 1 at the CIN 16, resulting in a stuff by Dexter Lawrence; a 4th and 1 at the HOU 41 in the 4th Quarter resulting in an incomplete pass; a 4th and 17 sack at the CIN 19 that ended the game for Houston. Just a critical in those data points, three of the four 4th Down conversion failures happened in the CIN Red Zone. 4 total trips into the CIN Red Zone with ZERO points scored. For reference, the Bengals only got into the Red Zone once, but they made it count with a TD pass to Chase in the 3rd Quarter. Special Teams…Yikes!!!: This was a game to forget for that unit. Fairbairn went 2-for-3, including missing a 58-yarder, which he can normally make. P Kai Kroeger’ punting was solid for the most part, but his most notable play was a botched snap in the 2nd quarter, which deprived Houston of a key scoring opportunity. The coverage units for punts and kickoffs were not all that impressive, and a critical 15-yard penalty after a 15-yard punt return by the Bengals early in the 3rd quarter set up a Bengals’ scoring opportunity. The Kroeger muff was not helped by a less-than-ideal snap from Austin Brinkman. As a long-time Texans fan, one thing that is not a common occurrence is a bad kicking snap/hold. The Critical Plays: 2 nd Quarter (6:58): 4th and 1 at the CIN 16: David Montgomery -1 yard rush (Dexter Lawrence on the stop) 3 rd Quarter (5:56): 3rd and 7 at the HOU 49: Joe Burrow pass to Samaje Perine for 16 yards (HOU 33) There were two critical conversion plays in this game. Both went against Houston. The first one not only dented a Houston drive, but it seemed to alter the decision-making process of the Texans. The running game struggled even before that stuff, but it seemed to confirm to Houston that they were not going to get much of anything on the ground. You wouldn’t think that much could scare Ryans, but that play did. In the third quarter, Houston faced another potential 4th and 1, but at the CIN 40. After two failed plays before, and remembering what happened in the 2nd Quarter, Ryans settled for a 58-yard FG attempt. It failed, and it set up the next situation. The second play saw Houston only down 7 (10-3). After the missed FG, the Bengals got the ball in good field position, but faced 3rd and 7 at the HOU 49. If the defense gets the stop, the Bengals likely punt and Houston gets the ball back. The Houston D-line forced Burrow to move around in the pocket. However, the secondary coverage could not hold and Burrow found his Perine to catch and run for 16 yards to the HOU 33. That conversion kept the Bengals’ drive alive, culminating in a 18-yard TD pass to Ja’Maar Chase. At 17-3, and with the running game M.I.A., this made Houston one-dimensional, and against the Bengals’ D-Line on this day, that did not bode well. FUN WITH NUMBERS: 2-6 : Houston Texans’ record in regular season games under Ryans in the Summer: Perhaps Ryans and the Texans take it literally that the NFL is a fall sport and that the games don’t really start until after the Equinox. The one exception was 2024, when Houston actually went 2-0 in Summer games. 6: Total number of sacks surrendered by Houston in the 4th Quarter this season: Houston has given up 7 sacks this season. All but one happened in the 4th quarter. The two on the final three plays against Buffalo, and then in this game, when the Bengals had no reason to worry about the Texans’ run game and Stroud was forced to make all of the plays with his arm, all four of the Bengals’ sacks came at that time. 37.5%: Conversion percentage for Houston’s offense when facing 3 yards or less: Houston faced 8 total plays needing 3 yards or less to convert for a 1st down. They only converted on 3 of those. On plays where Houston only needed 1 yard to convert: 16.7%. GAME BALLS DE Will Anderson, Jr: He was back to his usual relentless self, abusing the Bengals with 8 total tackles (4 solo)/1.0 sack/3.0 TFLs/2 QB hits/1 PD. On his credited sack, he was effectively embraced by the tackle, but it made no difference. Anderson also set up another sack by Hall, as he bulled all the way to Burrow, grabbing his foot and allowing Hall to clean-up. TE Dalton Schultz: No Nico Collins hurt, especially in the Red Zone. However, Stroud had a dependable backup security blanket in Schultz. 12 receptions for 140 yards will do that. SHOULD BE FORCED TO EAT ONLY SKYLINE CHILI, WITH BEANS AND STALE SPAGHETTI, FOR THE REST OF THE FALL SEASON Texans’ Interior O-line players: The whole of the O-line could live here, especially in the 4th quarter, but the interior was completely overwhelmed by the Bengals’ D-Line. Houston could not stop Lawrence and many times Stroud had to roll out of the pocket or could not step into his throws as the center was collapsing too quickly. Officials’ UCLs : 21 total flags between both teams. For Cincinnati, their 12 penalties did a lot to keep Houston in this matchup. Not that Houston was playing that much cleaner, as they lost more yards in penalties (83 to CIN’s 78). Houston’s Sporting Teams: You know about the Texans, but they weren’t alone. It started Friday night when the Houston Cougars went up to rival Texas Tech and couldn’t hold a double-digit lead. The Astros entered the weekend with a one-game lead in the AL West. They left down one. The Houston Dynamo didn’t technically lose but blew a 2-goal second period lead to end up with a tie. At least the Dash won, but they live at the bottom part of the table. Houston, now 0-2, will go on the road to take on their division rival, and fellow 0-2 squad, Indianapolis in what is shaping up to be a near-must win for both. Kickoff is slated for noon CDT on CBS/Paramount+

title: How does Chris Ballard continue to keep his job?
summary: I don’t know how I continue to write these articles. We’re going on Year 4 of me calling for Chris Ballard’s firing, and somehow he continues to survive. If there is a nuclear war in my lifetime, I would love to live with Chris Ballard because I know I will survive. In 2022, I was […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - SEPTEMBER 13: Indianapolis Colts General Manager Chris Ballard walks the sideline prior to the start of a NFL game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Indianapolis Colts on September 13, 2026 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I don’t know how I continue to write these articles. We’re going on Year 4 of me calling for Chris Ballard’s firing, and somehow he continues to survive. If there is a nuclear war in my lifetime, I would love to live with Chris Ballard because I know I will survive. In 2022, I was saying his team building approach needed to change and in 2024 I was calling for his firing . I finished that 2024 article saying “I have to go with what I see and what I see is an incompetent front office and staff that are guiding this team to nowhere.” Unfortunately two years later, it is the same old crap. At some point, you run out of excuses. You can blame Andrew Luck’s retirement, injuries, coaching, bad luck, bad quarterback play or whatever else people have used over the years, but eventually the person responsible for building the roster has to answer for the results. Ballard is now in Year 10, and the Colts are still having the same conversations they were having five, six and seven years ago. Who is the long-term quarterback? Where is the pass rush coming from? Why is the roster always one injury away from scrambling for help? Why is this team constantly hovering around .500 without ever actually going anywhere? That is what makes this different from another article reacting to one bad loss or one bad season. This is about a decade of the same patterns repeating themselves. Ballard has made some good picks, found some good players and built a few teams that looked promising for stretches, and he deserves credit for those things. The problem is that none of it has translated into sustained success. The Colts are always close, always one move away, always one year away, and somehow still in the same place. After ten years, “close” is not progress anymore; it is the result. The definition of mediocre If there is one word that perfectly describes the Chris Ballard era, it is mediocre. Not terrible. Not historically bad. Not completely dysfunctional. Just mediocre enough to keep convincing people that something better might be around the corner. Before this season, Ballard’s record as Colts general manager was 70-78-1. In nine seasons, Indianapolis made the playoffs twice, won one playoff game and never won the AFC South. Since Philip Rivers retired after the 2020 season, the Colts have not made the playoffs at all. Their best record over that stretch was 9-8, which they accomplished twice. Nine wins has essentially become the ceiling. The zero division titles might be the craziest part of the entire résumé. The AFC South has not exactly been some impossible gauntlet over the last decade. Houston has torn itself down and rebuilt. Jacksonville has gone through multiple coaches, general managers and quarterbacks. Tennessee reached an AFC Championship Game, won the division twice and has already gone through another two resets since then. All three franchises have had seasons with more postseason success than anything the Colts have produced under Ballard, and all three have still been willing to start over when things stopped working. Indianapolis just keeps hovering in the middle. That is almost worse than being terrible. Bad teams eventually get premium draft picks, clear out the building and start again. The Colts have spent most of Ballard’s tenure picking somewhere in the middle because they are usually good enough to win seven, eight or nine games but rarely good enough to accomplish anything meaningful. They never fully bottom out, but they never take the next step either. The one recent season where they actually did bottom out gave them the fourth overall pick in 2023. They used it on Anthony Richardson. That is the trap Ballard has built. His teams are usually competent enough to avoid the top of the draft and flawed enough to stay away from January football. Every offseason begins with some version of the same argument: the Colts are close. A couple additions here, better health there, another year of development and maybe they finally break through. Being close for one or two years is understandable. Being close for most of a decade is just another way of saying you never got there. Andrew Luck masked plenty of issues early in Ballard’s tenure because great quarterbacks do that. The 2018 team won 10 games and a playoff game, and Luck covered up weaknesses because he was one of the best quarterbacks in football. Rivers then gave Indianapolis another legitimate season in 2020, when the Colts went 11-5 and looked like a team that might finally have some stability again. Rivers retired, the quarterback carousel restarted, and the Colts went right back to the middle. This is what Ballard has become exceptionally good at building: average football teams. Teams that are rarely hopeless, occasionally interesting and almost never good enough when the season actually matters. After ten years, there is no “bad luck”. That is the résumé. Too many early-round misses Ballard has built a reputation as a good drafter, and there is some truth to that. He has found quality players throughout the draft and deserves credit for it. Quenton Nelson became one of the best guards in football. Darius Leonard was an All-Pro and Defensive Player of the Year. Jonathan Taylor became one of the league’s best running backs. Michael Pittman Jr. developed into a legitimate starting receiver. Alec Pierce turned into a 1,000-yard player. Tyler Warren looks like another major hit. Braden Smith gave the Colts years of good starting tackle play. The problem is what surrounds those hits. Go through the first and second rounds of Ballard’s drafts and there are far too many picks that either failed completely or never came close to providing the return expected from premium draft capital. It started immediately in 2017 with Malik Hooker in the first round and Quincy Wilson in the second. Hooker had some good moments, but he never became the difference-making safety the Colts expected when they drafted him 15th overall. Wilson was gone after three seasons. A year later, Nelson and Leonard were home runs, but Kemoko Turay never became the pass rusher Indianapolis hoped it was getting in the second round. The 2019 class was worse. Rock Ya-Sin was selected early in the second round, Ben Banogu followed some picks later and neither became a long-term answer. Banogu in particular was a massive miss at a premium position, finishing his Colts career with just 2.5 sacks. The pattern continued. Kwity Paye and Dayo Odeyingbo were the first two picks in 2021. Both became NFL players, but neither became the high-end pass rusher the Colts desperately needed. Paye was useful, but a useful edge defender is not what you are hoping to get with the 21st overall pick when the position has been a problem for years. Both were gone within 5 seasons of their draft year. Then there is 2022, when the Colts did not even have a first-round pick because Ballard had traded it away for Carson Wentz. That pick became No. 16 overall. Wentz lasted one season in Indianapolis. You can call that a trade failure instead of a draft failure if you want, but the result is the same: another premium asset produced almost nothing for the Colts. Jelani Woods was taken in the third round that year and never developed into the player Indianapolis envisioned. In 2023, Ballard finally had another top-five selection and used it on Anthony Richardson. Julius Brents came next in the second round. Richardson is now the backup quarterback, while Brents never established himself as a dependable starter. The one time the Colts were bad enough to draft near the very top, they missed on the most important…
