title: Sean McVay acknowledges Rams’ Australian travel plans were ‘dumbass’
summary: After the Los Angeles Rams defeated the New York Giants in Week 2, Sean McVay was asked why his team looked so much stronger in Week 2 compared to how the team looked in Week 1? L.A.’s head coach expressed that sometimes you win, and sometimes you learn, before adding that sometimes “you have a […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Head Coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams walks the field prior to the game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the Los Angeles Rams defeated the New York Giants in Week 2 , Sean McVay was asked why his team looked so much stronger in Week 2 compared to how the team looked in Week 1? L.A.’s head coach expressed that sometimes you win, and sometimes you learn, before adding that sometimes “you have a dumbass coach” who “makes travel plans that put you in a bad spot.” It’s a revealing quote as McVay seems to make light, yet admits that the plans to travel to Australia about one day before their game against the San Francisco 49ers were a poor choice. Will the Rams ever make travel arrangements like that again? That remains to be seen. Regardless, McVay admits their plans for their Week 1 game in Australia were a mistake, he also expressed that he feels L.A. has the right players to respond from a loss the right way. The team did that on Monday night. Said McVay when asked why his team looked better against the New York Giants than the 49ers: “We got the right people. Yeah, I think, you know, sometimes you win, sometimes you learn. And, you know, sometimes you have a dumbass coach that, you know, makes travel plans that put you in a bad spot”. It’s early in the season, and the Rams may lose again, as soon as their matchup in Week 3, however McVay shows confidence that not only can this team respond to a loss, but they have the players to win. As long as their “dumbass” coach doesn’t mess things up for team, then the Rams should have a real chance to get to where they want to go. Of course, to McVay’s credit, where would this team be without him? McVay isn’t a dumbass, but he can and does make mistakes, and he owns them. We’ll see what other lessons this team can learn and apply in 2026. They say life isn’t always about winning but about learning, maybe these Rams can do both.

title: Rams remind everyone NFL is a week-to-week league
summary: The Los Angeles Rams looked awful in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers, how else can you put it? In Week 2, the Rams made some mistakes, and yet, they found a way to win 28-6 over a New York Giants team that looked darn near excellent in Week 1. The Rams and perhaps […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams scores a touchdown against the New York Giants during the first quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams looked awful in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers, how else can you put it? In Week 2, the Rams made some mistakes, and yet, they found a way to win 28-6 over a New York Giants team that looked darn near excellent in Week 1. The Rams and perhaps Week 2 in general should be a reminder to all watchers that a lot can change in a week. That rule applies to both life and the NFL. Going into Week 3, which narratives will change? Will narrative will stay true? With poor play, injuries and more factors than you can think of you never know what’s going to happen. But we do know what happened, and right now, the Rams are 1-1. They’ll go from there. Never a dull moment in the NFL. Giants-Rams on ‘Monday Night Football’: What We Learned from Los Angeles’ 28-6 win (nfl.com) “ Home sweet, home for Rams. Basking in the comfortable confines of SoFi Stadium, the Rams returned home from a wayward Australian adventure and returned to the form so many thought would be seen. Matthew Stafford looked like the MVP from a season ago, Davante Adams looked like the game-tilting wide receiver he was for years and the Los Angeles defense, with Aaron Donald at the center of it all, was sterling. As the Giants sputtered with Jaxson Dart lost to a knee injury , the Rams overcame a couple turnovers and won handily. More than a week removed from falling flat in their opener in the outback against the 49ers, the Rams handled their business and were impressive. Stafford, rebounding from a zero-touchdown Week 1, proved that was an aberration with 327 passing yards and four touchdown passes. That he did so without an injured Puka Nacua was all the more impressive. Adams was simply wonderful in the No. 1 WR role, hauling in a pair of touchdowns and nearly 200 yards, while the two-headed running game of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum also got the job done (164 combined rushing yards). In a game that felt like a blowout despite the Rams leading by only two scores throughout most of the night, L.A. racked up 481 yards. It wasn’t perfect. There were turnovers and too many missed opportunities, but the Rams got right on Monday, happy to be home, feeling, looking and playing like themselves.“ Rams get big nights from Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams as they blast Giants 28-6 in Aaron Donald’s return (sports.yahoo) “Rams roll in second half The Rams never let up after halftime. Stafford hit Adams in the third quarter on an 11-yard touchdown, which was Adams’ second score and Stafford’s third TD throw of the game. It was also Stafford’s 426th TD in his career, which moved him to sixth in NFL history ahead of Philip Rivers . Stafford would throw another touchdown to tight end Terrance Ferguson .“ Rams defeat depleted Giants 28-6 on ‘Monday Night Football’ (espn.com) “”Everybody’s freaking out, which I understand,” Adams said last week. “We didn’t put together the greatest showing out there. But you’re a fool if you think that that’s what it’s going to look like every single week.” On Monday night against the New York Giants , quarterback Matthew Stafford and Adams showed off the connection that flashed midway through last season, the wideout’s first with the Rams. Adams logged eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns during a 28-6 win in which L.A. was without wide receiver Puka Nacua . Adams’ performance sparked a return to the offense the Rams were expecting going into the season. It was Adams’ 29th career game with multiple receiving touchdowns, tied for fourth most in NFL history.“ Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams dominate Giants in Rams’ blowout win (nfl.com) “Monday marked Donald’s first game back since he retired after the 2023 season. “I was so juiced. He came running out of the tunnel and I couldn’t control myself,” Matthew Stafford said of Donald’s return. “I was freaking fired up. I’m sure y’all were in there. The fans were happy to see him back and we all were, too. Just the human being, the player, all of it combined. What he brings to our team and to our locker room is unmatched. And really to the city, which I thought was amazing. I thought it was a great reception for him tonight, well-deserved.” The juiced Stafford went out and ripped apart the banged-up Giants secondary, whipping four touchdowns on 22 of 31 passes for 327 yards. New York pressured Stafford on just 15.2% of his dropbacks, the fourth-lowest rate he has faced in a game as a Ram (since 2021), per Next Gen Stats. When kept clean, he completed 20 of 27 attempts for 302 yards, including all four touchdowns and his lone interception — which was a heat-check deep shot in the second quarter.“ PFT’s Week 3 2026 NFL power rankings (nbcsports) “1. Seahawks (last week No. 1; 2-0): No Darnold? No problem. 2. Bills (No. 2; 2-0): September wins are celebratory. January wins are mandatory. 3. Bengals (No. 7; 2-0): Joe Burrow can’t keep taking these kinds of beatings. 4. Chiefs (No. 8; 2-0): Kenneth Walker III could become one of the best free-agent signings ever. 5. 49ers (No. 10; 2-0): Brock Purdy is making a push for the list of top-10 quarterbacks. Maybe the top five.“ NFL Week 2 Sunday aftermath: Surprising Raiders, soaring Chiefs and sinking Chargers in spotlight (nfl.com “Two high-profile quarterback injuries — Jayden Daniels ( dislocated left elbow ) and Caleb Williams ( hamstring ) — will hover over the early portion of the week. As we wait to better understand the extent of those players’ potential absences, let’s look at the rest of the aftermath of Sunday’s showdowns, including: Chiefs prove they’re back with OT victory Vikings’ D dominates in gritty win at Chicago Cowboys get back on track as Dak passes Romo Concern brewing for these four offenses? One defender who stuffed the stat sheet in Week 2 But first, a look at some unexpected developments in the young season … Raiders lead surprising 2-0 teams If we were ranking the most stunning teams to begin this season at 2-0, we’d start with the Las Vegas Raiders, then there would be a wide, football-field-long gap before the next squad. Klint Kubiak and Co. took care of business in the opener against a Miami team they were supposed to beat. They were expected to be a doormat in L.A. in Week 2.“ Giants’ John Harbaugh: Jaxson Dart’s knee injury is ‘in the neighborhood’ of MCL sprain (nfl.com) “Quarterback Jaxson Dart , who was knocked out of Monday’s 28-6 loss to the Rams with a left knee injury, is believed to have suffered an MCL sprain, NFL Network Insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reported. Rapoport and Garafolo added that Dart’s X-rays were negative and he will have an MRI on Tuesday. “We’ll know more tomorrow. That’s in the neighborhood of it,” head coach John Harbaugh said when asked about the report of Dart’s sprained MCL. “We’ll get an MRI tomorrow and have a really good feel for it. Give you more information then.” Dart sustained his injury on a third-and-8 on the team’s first drive as he dropped back and tossed a deep pass under pressure. He was sandwiched between Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart upon letting the ball fly, with the force of Stewart’s body pushing Dart’s knee inward.“ Comment of the Day: “Here we go again. After just one win against the Giants. Updated SB favorites. Who’s drinking the Kool-Aid? Baltimore Ravens+1000San Francisco 49ers+1100Kansas City Chiefs+1300Feb 14, 2027, 6:35pm ET Los Angeles Rams+650Buffalo Bills+750Seattle Seahawks+850” -Jerry Woods Feedpost of the Day:

title: Rams game ball(s) from Week 2 victory
summary: Sean McVay has never been shy about handing out a game ball(s) after a victory. After all, a win is never to be taken for granted. The Los Angeles Rams defeated the New York Giants 28-6 in a great team effort win. There were still flaws and some areas of execution that need to be […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Trent McDuffie #22 of the Los Angeles Rams breaks up a pass intended for Malik Nabers #1 of the New York Giants during the third quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sean McVay has never been shy about handing out a game ball(s) after a victory. After all, a win is never to be taken for granted. Home Opener W! 💪 pic.twitter.com/8HniAbE7cm — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) September 22, 2026 The Los Angeles Rams defeated the New York Giants 28-6 in a great team effort win. There were still flaws and some areas of execution that need to be cleaned up but overall it was a solid bounce back performance by the preseason favorites. Who helped steer the team to victory and shined under the Monday Night Football lights? Here are MY game balls from the team’s Week 2 win… Game Ball #1: Davante Adams Without hesitation, Adam was the biggest performer of the night. His 8 receptions for 195 yards and 2 touchdowns paced the Rams. His 195 yards also outgained the New York Giants entire offense. Adams looked like the Green Bay Packer version of himself. Something the Rams were hoping to resurrect when they signed him last offseason. With Puka Nacua sidelined, Adams big night carried even more significance on the field and in the stat sheet. Game Ball #2: Matthew Stafford Stafford looked like the 2025 MVP Stafford. He threw for 327 yards, 4 touchdowns, and 1 interception. The interception in the 2nd quarter was reckless and overambitious but that is what you will get with Stafford sometimes. But all in all, Stafford was methodical, sharp, and in-sync throughout the majority of the night. Terrance Ferguson actually dropped two passes which hurt Stafford’s completion percentage. Game Ball #3: Kobie Turner I thought Kobie Turner was a force for the defense. I was worried about how the Rams defensive line would handle Cam Skattebo but Turner led the charge in slowing down the powerful back. There may not have been any splash plays but Turner showed up on the tape. left edge Byton Young with a mini-swim, and Kobie Turner gets his long arms extended, sheds block, stop the RB, actually middle of LOS was pushed off, Kobie and Byron winning saved some yards pic.twitter.com/aCQh9rMsTn — Jim Youngblood 53 (@53_jim70721) September 22, 2026 Game Ball #4: Sean McVay Sure the HC is not going to get the game ball typically but McVay was pretty flawless in his play calling. The only blemishes in the game were player-inflicted. Matthew Stafford’s interception. Kyren Williams fumble. Harrison Mevis’s missed field goal. Terrance Ferguson’s two drops. McVay himself called a great game. And his team responded the way they needed to after an opening Week 1 loss. Game Ball #5: Trent McDuffie The Rams traded a first round pick and paid Trent McDuffie to be the highest paid cornerback in the league. Well against Malik Nabers, the star cornerback held the talented wide receiver to 1 reception for 1 yard on 4 targets. McDuffie also got his hands on his first interception as a Ram. #22 also added a key PBU on a deep ball pass attempt to Nabers in the 2nd quarter. According to NFL Pro, Rams CB Trent McDuffie played man coverage on 17 of 21 matchups vs. Nabers, playing press man coverage on 14 of those 17 snaps. Against all Giants WRs, McDuffie did not allow a reception on five targets in coverage, including four passes defended. — Blaine Grisak (@BGMediaOnSI) September 22, 2026 It appeared the Rams shifted to more man-coverage in the game and McDuffie put his skill set on display; earning himself plenty of praise for the MNF performance.

title: Nakobe Dean was all over field in Las Vegas Raiders Week 2 win over Los Angeles Chargers
summary: It’s early, but the Las Vegas Raiders have been getting good returns on free-agent signing Nakobe Dean. Through two games, the linebacker is tied for second at his position with nine ‘defensive stops’, according to Pro Football Focus, and he was especially impressive in the Week 2 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Dean saw […]
full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s early, but the Las Vegas Raiders have been getting good returns on free-agent signing Nakobe Dean . Through two games, the linebacker is tied for second at his position with nine ‘ defensive stops ’, according to Pro Football Focus , and he was especially impressive in the Week 2 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Dean saw four of his nine stops come against the Chargers, with three of them happening as a run defender and the other coming in coverage. His figure against the run was tied for sixth among linebackers and one behind the five-way tie for first place (pre- Monday Night Football ). Additionally, he registered three pressures on five pass rushes (he has four on six rushes through two weeks), registering a sack and another quarterback hit in the process to be PFF’s highest-graded off-ball blitzer ( 88.3 ) in Week 2. The former Philadelphia Eagle was all over the field last Sunday, commanding a deeper dive into the tape. Nakobe Dean didn't necessarily stand out in coverage against LAC, but he did a few little things to contribute LAC motions to get him matched up on a WR, but Dean uses his hands well in coverage to pick up the drag route, forcing Herbert to come off it #Raiders pic.twitter.com/nqaM9ZEFD2 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 21, 2026 To be honest, Dean didn’t particularly stand out in coverage against the Chargers. However, he did a handful of little things to help make an impact in that phase of the game. Here, Los Angeles comes out in an empty formation and motions a slot receiver to get the receiver matched up against Dean. Las Vegas is playing Cover 6, a split-field coverage, meaning one side of the defense is running Cover 4 while the other is in Cover 2. A drag or crossing route is a good way for an offense to attack that because the defense is naturally going to be out of sync since they technically have two play calls going on, making it difficult to pass off and pick up routes from one side to the other. On top of that, the offense gets the matchup it wants with a speedy slot receiver on a linebacker. However, Dean does an excellent job of using his hands in coverage to get physical with the wideout in the five-yard window, slowing the wideout down. Aided by good coverage across the board, that takes quarterback Justin Herbert’s third option in the progression away. So, Herbert has to scramble and ends up gaining just a yard or two on second-and-long, setting up third-and-long for the defense. Nothing too special but good situational awareness from Dean LV is up by 2 possessions with 3 mins left and facing 1st and 15. He stays deep in his zone and rallies to the check down, making the tackle for a stop to keep LAC behind the sticks and the clock running pic.twitter.com/OfeM7HsjI8 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 21, 2026 This time, we’ll take a look at the linebacker’s lone coverage stop and, more than anything, it’s sound situational awareness. The Raiders are up by two possessions with about three minutes left on the clock, and the defense is just trying to keep everything in front of them to avoid giving up the big play, especially since it’s first-and-15. They play Cover 6 against an empty formation again, essentially putting Dean on an island in the middle of the field as the hook defender. He gets to his landmark and wisely stays deep in his zone to make sure nothing goes over his head, leaving the check down open underneath. Once Herbert dumps it off to Ladd McConkey, Herbert’s No. 1 receiver, Dean rallies to the ball and makes a nice open-field tackle to prevent any yards after the catch. That keeps the clock moving while simultaneously keeping Los Angeles’ offense behind the sticks. Nice stunt from Nakobe Dean: -1st step is upfield to disguise it -Attacks and picks the G to free up Laulu -Peels off G and takes advantage of RB picking up Laulu to get a QB hit #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/ihEMlMX6Y4 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 21, 2026 Now, let’s take a look at Dean’s best pass-rush rep from Sunday. Rob Leonard has him on the line of scrimmage for a five-man front and on the opposite side of Maxx Crosby. Since the Chargers don’t want to give Crosby a one-on-one opportunity, the running back stays in the protection scheme while the center turns right toward Crosby. That sets up a three-on-three matchup between the back, left guard and left tackle against Dean, Jonah Laulu and Malcolm Koonce. Meanwhile, Leonard calls a stunt/twist with the linebacker and defensive tackle. Dean disguises it well by taking his first step upfield before pivoting to attack the guard, catching the offensive lineman off-guard and getting him off-balance while freeing up Laulu as the looper. Then the running back and guard aren’t on the same page, with both of them picking up Laulu, freeing up Dean to speed up Herbert’s process and get a quarterback hit. Good ex of Nakobe Dean's instincts vs. the run Mirrors FB to be in a position to fill the extra gap if needed, but keeps his eyes on the RB and scrapes over the top to adjust to the play design/RB's path, making the tackle to keep LAC in 3rd and long #Raiders pic.twitter.com/i2l8K0Sd06 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 21, 2026 All of that being said, the $36 million linebacker makes his money as a run defender, and unsurprisingly, that’s where he had his biggest impact against the Chargers. The situation here is important to note. Los Angeles is backed up in its own end zone and facing a second-and-18 after Eric Stokes’ strip-sack. So, Vegas’ primary goal defensively is to limit the damage and ensure the offense is facing a third-and-long since the unit already got the negative play, meaning the backers can afford to be a little more patient against the run. The Chargers come out in 21 personnel and motion the fullback to create another potential gap between the tight end and left tackle that the Raiders have to account for. Additionally, the subtle motion makes it look like the play call is for iso, likely with the idea that Dean will see it and immediately crash downhill to take on the fullback in the hole and fill the gap. However, watch the running back’s path, as this is just a simple halfback dive. Meanwhile, Dean bumps over with the fullback’s motion to account for the extra gap in case it is iso. But he doesn’t crash downhill, recognizing the situation, and keeps his eyes on the running back. That allows him to mirror the running back and avoid the trash while scraping over the top of the formation against the halfback dive. Additionally, Dean gets his hands up to take on the left guard and defeat that block, making the tackle to keep Los Angeles behind the sticks. So, while this is a gain of six yards, the Raiders get what they want with the Chargers facing a third and 12. Tonka Hemingway and Nakobe Dean are on a twist, & Dean gets some help with a combo block that pushes him into the play, but he also does a nice job of coming to balance to make the tackle in the hole for no gain #Raiders pic.twitter.com/yebWe36c2s — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 21, 2026 This is an interesting play call from Leonard. It’s third-and-two with the Raiders up three and about nine minutes left on the clock. But he puts Dean on the line of scrimmage with Quay Walker mirroring the tight end/slot receiver across the formation, meaning no one is on the second level. Leonard also blitzes Jeremy Chinn off the edge and runs a couple of line games, almost like he was expecting a pass. However, the Chargers end up running inside split zone out of the shotgun. With Dean and defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway executing a twist, Hemingway vacates the playside A-gap while Laulu and Crosby run a T/E stunt on the other side. In other words, this play has the potential to go very poorly for the Raiders. Nonetheless, Dean gets his hands up to take on the guard while looping inside and facing a combo block from the backside guard and…

title: Hezekiah Masses, unsung heroes helping Las Vegas Raiders get love in Week 3 NFL Power Rankings
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are one of the biggest surprises in the league right now, as there aren’t many people who had the Raiders starting the season 2-0. Getting contributions from unsung heroes like quarterback Kirk Cousins and rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses is a big reason why Las Vegas is winning and starting to climb […]
full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are one of the biggest surprises in the league right now, as there aren’t many people who had the Raiders starting the season 2-0 . Getting contributions from unsung heroes like quarterback Kirk Cousins and rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses is a big reason why Las Vegas is winning and starting to climb up the charts in the Week 3 NFL Power Rankings roundup. Sports Illustrated 21. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 28 I don’t know what happens from here, but the fact that the Raiders have gotten incredible production out of a handful of players the previous regime deemed unplayable—and are getting game-changing plays from a 2026 fifth-round pick in the secondary—have me more confident in the John Spytek-Tom Brady mind meld than I’ve ever been. — Conor Orr Two weeks into the season and the difference between Klint Kubiak’s and Pete Carroll’s coaching staffs is already noticeable. It’s almost weird to see the Raiders become a well-coached team because it’s been a while, but that’s exactly what they are right now. Especially without Brock Bowers in the lineup, the Silver and Black don’t have a ton of star power on the roster, but they’re executing at a high level. That’s a testament to Kubiak, Spytek and players like Masses, who are outperforming their draft slot. What’s even crazier is the top pick of the draft hasn’t even seen the field yet… ESPN 20. Las Vegas Raiders One thing we know about the QB1: Kirk Cousins can handle pressure well. Cousins has been pressured on 36.5% of his dropbacks through two games. In those situations, he has completed 13 of 21 passes (61.9%) for 161 yards, three touchdowns, an interception and a passer rating of 105.6. Against the Chargers, Cousins was pressured on 40.6% of his dropbacks. Yet he still managed to throw for 108 yards and two scores whenever the Chargers brought the heat. — Ryan McFadden When it comes to Cousins and the offensive line, it’s been two different stories in the first two weeks of the season. The quarterback did a lot of taking what the Miami Dolphins’ defense was giving him in the season opener and only faced pressure on 22.6% of his dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus . Last Sunday, he did a much better job of pushing the ball downfield and was pressured 43.8% of the time. Now, it’s just a matter of putting it all together at once. For the record, PFF has a slightly different but still very comparable pressure percentage for the season than ESPN does, with the former coming in at 33.3%. NFL.com 22. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 29 The Raiders are 2-0! They aren’t anywhere near perfection, but they’re undefeated after two weeks and winning in new coach Klint Kubiak’s intended fashion: playing opportunistic, scrappy defense and capitalizing on opponents’ mistakes. The best part: They’re doing it with names you might have never heard before. Cody White scored two receiving touchdowns on Sunday. Hezekiah Masses picked off Justin Herbert twice . Furthermore, Kirk Cousins is out there slinging the pill with no fear! I’m not saying the Raiders are going to the playoffs, but they’re certainly fun to watch. — Nick Shook I like this take on what the Silver and Black have done so far. It’s still too early to put them in the ‘contender’ category, but the team is making plenty of strides and is already showing signs that the organization is ahead of schedule on the rebuild. It’s certainly a much more watchable product than a year ago, when opponents were taking a knee ahead of the two-minute warning. Bleacher Report 20. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 24 The Las Vegas Raiders are an unstoppable juggernaut. There’s really no point in even playing out the rest of the season. It’s a huge waste of time. Just give the Raiders their Lombardi Trophy and call it a day. Kidding aside, the Raiders haven’t played a Murderer’s Row early—the Miami Dolphins look like the NFL’s worst team, and the Los Angeles Chargers look like the league’s biggest disappointment. But 2-0 is 2-0—Kirk Cousins flat-out out-played Justin Herbert. Wide receiver Tre Tucker roasted a supposedly solid Chargers defense. The Vegas defense allowed just 14 points and forced three turnovers. It’s a great start, but we’ll find who these Raiders really are over the next five games—a wicked stretch that includes the Rams, Chiefs and Bills coming to town and a trip to New England. — Gary Davenport It’s kind of funny that the Chargers would have been considered part of the “Murderer’s Row” two weeks ago, and now they’re “the league’s biggest disappointment”. Don’t get me wrong, I agree with what Davenport is saying because the Bolts are a disorganized mess right now. Doing simple things like snapping the ball on third down is a challenge for them. But it is funny how two games can completely sway people’s opinions 180 degrees, and I’m including myself in that. Regardless, as Davenport notes, the Raiders deserve credit for getting back-to-back wins, something they didn’t do last year. When you’re the worst team in the league year ago, it’s okay to celebrate every victory in the following season, regardless of how bad the other team is or looks. The Athletic 22. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 27 Rookie spotlight: Fernando Mendoza The No. 1 overall pick doesn’t look close to getting on the field with how the Raiders are playing. Kirk Cousins is in his 15th year and is tied for the league lead with six passing touchdowns. Cousins is playing average overall (15th in EPA per dropback and 13th in yards per attempt), and that’s good enough in Las Vegas right now. Fourth-round running back Mike Washington Jr. is getting some work, but second-year man Ashton Jeanty is carrying most of the load. — Josh Kendall, Chad Graff To each their own, but choosing to spotlight a guy who hasn’t played when someone on the same team is up for Rookie of the Week is an interesting choice. On top of that, they mention how Washington isn’t getting much run behind Jeanty. I guess Masses has to get three picks in a game for Kendall and Graff to take notice! I get that offensive players/fantasy football is all most people care about these days, but this was a missed opportunity to highlight a fifth-round pick who just had an outstanding game.
author: Matt Holder

title: Revisiting Tyree Wilson trade
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders will see a former player who they once thought could be a fodunation piece Sunday when they visit the New Orleans Saints. The Raiders traded defensive end Tyree Wilson to the Saints on Day Three of the 2026 draft. The Raiders sent Wilson and a seventh-round pick to the Saints for […]
full_text: (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders will see a former player who they once thought could be a fodunation piece Sunday when they visit the New Orleans Saints. The Raiders traded defensive end Tyree Wilson to the Saints on Day Three of the 2026 draft. The Raiders sent Wilson and a seventh-round pick to the Saints for the No. 150 pick when they took Arizona safety Dalton Johnson. So, the Saints measured Wilson’s trade value essentially as a mid fifth-round pick. The Saints took Iowa cornebarck TJ Hall with the No. 219 pick frim the Raiders in the trade. Hall is on the Saints’ practice squad. Wilson was the No. 7 overall pick just three years ago. In the end, he went down as yet another recent Raiders’ failed first-round draft pick. Wilson, who will be a free agent next year because his fifth-year option wasn’t exercised, never became anything more than a rotational player and he didn’t consistently make plays in his three seasons in Las Vegas. He has played in 50 games with just 7 starts in three NFL seasons. He has 12 career sacks with 4.5 in 2024 being his career high. So far, Wilson’s time in New Orleans has been similar to his time in Las Vegas. He didn’t play on defense in Week 2 for the Saints after playing 30 percent of the snaps in Week 1. He did play 10 special teams snaps in Week 2. So, the Raiders may not see Wilson much Sunday. The Raiders aren’t getting much out of the trade either yet. Johnson has been a healthy scratch in both games. But he may have a chance to be active Sunday if fellow safety Treydan Stukes missing the game. He is currently in the concussion protocol.

title: Zeke Masses flashes big-time in starting debut
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 26-14 win at the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2 and what to look for Sunday at the New Orleans Saints: Fernando Mendoza:The No. 1 overall pick served as […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 26-14 win at the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2 and what to look for Sunday at the New Orleans Saints: Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick served as Kirk Cousins backup. He did not play. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick played 31 defensive snaps before leaving with a concussion. His availability for Sunday will be determined later this week. Stukes was good when he did play against the Chargers as he had four tackles. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick played two plays at guard and he played four plays on special teams. He did not play on offense in Week 1. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick played 18 defensive snaps and he played three snaps on special teams. He did not play at all in Week 1 despite being active. He will likley continue get get some rotational defensive snaps at New Orleans. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played 19 percent of the offensive snaps for the second straight game. He didn’t make an impact as he had seven yards on three carries. He had seven carries for 41 yards in Week 1. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was a healthy scratch for the second straight game. If Stukes is out Sunday, Johnson has a chance to be active. If not, that would not be a great sign. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick started for the injured Darien Porter and made a huge impact. He had two interceptions and played well overall. if wouldn’t be a shock tp see him become a full-time starter. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played 8 offensive snaps. He was targeted once but appeared to run the wrong route. He has one catch on three targets in two games. He had one punt return for 16 yards in Week 2 and is averaging 17 yards a punt return on three returns this season.

title: Miami Dolphins Discussion: Team To Beat Edition
summary: In the NFL, you are either one of the top teams fighting each week to stay there, be it at the top of your division or conference, or one of the “lesser” teams fighting to get through the season. The “lesser teams” generally set their sights on one team they are working to catch and […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - NOVEMBER 09: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) is helped up by teammates after a hit during the game between the Miami Dolphins and the Buffalo Bills on November 9, 2025 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In the NFL, you are either one of the top teams fighting each week to stay there, be it at the top of your division or conference, or one of the “lesser” teams fighting to get through the season. The “lesser teams” generally set their sights on one team they are working to catch and eventually compete with on a level playing field. For our Miami Dolphins, the team that we can all remember chasing the longest, or the team that the entire organization was focused on catching up to and competing directly with for the better part of two decades, was the New England Patriots. Eventually, New England’s starting quarterback, Tom Brady, left the team, and the Josh Allen-led Buffalo Bills stepped up in the AFC East to take the crown as the team everyone else was chasing. Last season shifted yet again back to the Pats for at least a season, with second-year quarterback Drake Maye leading his team to an improbable Super Bowl appearance. So this evening, Phinsider Question Of The Day is’ Which team, in your opinion, should our Miami Dolphins focus on as the team to “chase,” or at least catch up to, in roster and play quality, in the division or even the conference, as they continue their latest rebuild, and why? Please share your thougths and answers in the comment section below.

title: Dolphins bring in kickers for tryouts amidst Riley Patterson struggles
summary: Miami Dolphins kicker Riley Patterson isn’t off to the greatest start in 2026. He missed field goal tries in both week one against the Las Vegas Raiders and week two against the San Francisco 49ers. Following the loss in week two, head coach Jeff Hafley expressed his frustration with the missed opportunities for points. “Yeah, […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 12: Lucas Havrisik #35 of the Green Bay Packers kicks a field goal against the Cincinnati Bengals during the second quarter in the game at Lambeau Field on October 12, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Miami Dolphins kicker Riley Patterson isn’t off to the greatest start in 2026. He missed field goal tries in both week one against the Las Vegas Raiders and week two against the San Francisco 49ers. Following the loss in week two, head coach Jeff Hafley expressed his frustration with the missed opportunities for points. “ Yeah, we gotta hit field goals, ” said Hafley. “ That’s two misses in two games. We are counting on him to make those kicks. ” On Tuesday, Hafley backed up his words with action when the Dolphins brought in three kickers for tryouts — Chris Freeman, Tanner Brown and Lucas Havrisik. Freeman played his college ball at UConn before signing with the Houston Texans this offseason. He was cut from the squad just two days later. Brown went undrafted in the 2023 NFL Draft. He has spent time with the Los Angeles Rams, Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints in the NFL and the Louisville Kings of the United Football League. He has never attempted a kick in the National Football League, but made 25 of 28 field goal tries with a long of 60 yards with Louisville earlier this year. Havrisik has spent time with the Indianapolis Colts, Cleveland Browns, Los Angeles Rams, Buffalo Bills, and Green Bay Packers in the NFL while also spending time with the Arlington Renegades of the UFL. He is 19 of 24 on field goal tries in the NFL — with a long make of 61 yards. Miami has not signed any of these kickers as of the time of this writing, but if Patterson continues to struggle in 2026, his replacement could be inked in short order. We will continue to keep you updated on all things Miami Dolphins as the season rolls on.

title: Miami Dolphins fan confidence: Week 3 survey
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Dolphins fans and fans across the country. The Miami Dolphins are who we thought they were. And, by that, I unfortunately mean they are a team struggling to grow as a unit, play […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins looks on during the second quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Dolphins fans and fans across the country. The Miami Dolphins are who we thought they were. And, by that, I unfortunately mean they are a team struggling to grow as a unit, play together on the field, and get results that are better than an average margin of defeat of 18 points. Miami is 0-2 on the season, and there are a lot of issues that need to be addressed. But, that was the expectations for this season. Not to revel in the misery of a team struggling in just about every aspect of the game – including holding on to the ball when trying to punt – but this is a team that perfectly fits former Dolphins’ head coach Cam Cameron’s “fail forward fast” mentality. Miami is going to make mistakes. They are going to have problems in communication, execution, and understanding of the game, especially with rookies starting or being major rotational pieces all over the roster. They have to take their lumps, learn from them quickly, and improve their execution the next time they are on the field. The Las Vegas Raiders beat the Dolphins in Week 1, then the San Francisco 49ers dropped Miami in their Week 2 game. The good news is, the team comes home to Miami for the first time this year for their Week 3 game. The bad news is, they are hosting the Kansas City Chiefs, who look set to make a charge to, and through, the AFC playoffs this year. The Dolphins are who we thought they were. They probably will be all season. But, this year is more about laying the foundation for the future than it is about the play on the field each Sunday. Is that enough to keep the fans tuned into the franchise? Our SB Nation Reacts poll returns for Week 3 with our standard fan confidence survey. title: Miami Dolphins’ Most Valuable Player | Week Two | Someone has to win
summary: The Miami Dolphins were steamrolled in Northern California against the San Francisco 49ers this past Sunday. The team looked somewhat promising in the first half — moving the ball well against a stout Niners defense. They trailed by just 8 points at halftime — merely a single touchdown, plus two-point conversion away from making it […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 13: Miami Dolphins linebacker Jacob Rodriguez (10) walks off of the field after a NFL regular season game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium, Sunday September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins were steamrolled in Northern California against the San Francisco 49ers this past Sunday. The team looked somewhat promising in the first half — moving the ball well against a stout Niners defense. They trailed by just 8 points at halftime — merely a single touchdown, plus two-point conversion away from making it a nail-biter. Unfortunately, the Dolphins came out flat in the second-half — both on offense and on defense — and were ultimately trounced by a score of 35-13. Choosing a Most Valuable ‘Phin for Sunday’s game against the 49ers was not an enviable task. There wasn’t much “good” to go around against San Francisco. But… that’s just how this season is going to go, and this job must be done, so I will do it to the best of my ability. Miami Dolphins Week Two MVP – LB Jacob Rodriguez Plenty of people mentioned how Dolphins rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez should have won team MVP for his week one performance that saw the youngster notch 14 combined tackles against the Las Vegas Raiders. Well, on Sunday against San Francisco, Rodriguez followed up his stellar week one performance by adding another 8 combined tackles against the 49ers — good for second on the team behind safety Michael Taaffe. It is the second week in a row where a rookie has taken my weekly MVP award, which exemplifies what this season is all about for the Miami Dolphins. This young team needs to establish a solid foundation before it can get flashy. If Miami’s rookies become major contributors this season — and it already looks like Rodriguez is going to be one of those top contributors — the Dolphins will be better in the future for it. MVP TRACKER Week One – WR Caleb Douglas Week Two – LB Jacob Rodriguez

title: Pattern Degradations and Bad Dresses; Miami Dolphins stumble against 49ers
summary: Wow! I wrote about pattern recognition last week and boy did I see some patterns. Bad ones. My grandmother was a seamstress by trade and watching her work when I was boy was very educational. She said “Paul, cut out this pattern section for a dress or blouse and then I will sew them together […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers stiff arms Chris Johnson #3 of the Miami Dolphins in the first quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wow! I wrote about pattern recognition last week and boy did I see some patterns. Bad ones. My grandmother was a seamstress by trade and watching her work when I was boy was very educational. She said “Paul, cut out this pattern section for a dress or blouse and then I will sew them together and measure for the final fitting. Measure twice. Cut once.” Basic stuff. That was the first time I ever heard the word “pattern.” I did my best but, my grandmother always said you can undercut the pattern but never overcut the pattern because I can’t add the small sections back and the blouse will look silly. This Miami Dolphins team is a bad pattern that is overcut, undercut and not measured properly. Yes, we have terrible scissors, materials and needles. IMHO, this situation is worse than Flores’ first season. Why yes, the situation is different. But I don’t see much to build upon. We should be able to see one small but strong piece. Maybe I just don’t see it. But like back then under Flores, this is a “start from the foundation process” but I feel more scared. The question is why. Darryl Johnston made great points about the “process.” and we have to be okay with suffering under the process. And I get it but I don’t get mistakes from nearly every single position group. Sunday, against the 49ers, it is very hard to tell if it is the talent (or lack thereof) or the schemes/coaching. There were so many bad mistakes that I am not sure where to start to fix. There were simply numerous blown assignments, numerous lack of playmakings and numerous “out-classings.” Example, Michael Taafe tried to go high on Deebo Samuel or George Kittle (can’t remember) and fell off like a baby stroller trying to tackle a freight train. Welcome to the NFL, rookie! Before going any further on the defense, I will give a 15% curve upgrade score to the entire secondary because the pass rush is completely non-existent. We have zero pass-rush talent even when Chop is in there. The last two QBs have not had to worry about getting hit and the WRs know they can run all of their “ingenious routes” according to Darryl Johnston. This is simply ludicrous because ANY offensive system will work, when there is no pressure on the QB or on the RBs. Darryl Johnston probably knows this but has to build up Brock Purdy and Kyle Shanahan to prop up the NFL lore of how great the players are. Brock Purdy isn’t one-tenth the QB that Dan Marino was. He can run, yes, but his throws are all perimeter precision throws backed by a superior rushing attack. I really do like Brock Purdy but the Wing-T or Run-n-Shoot would have worked perfectly well again this defense. How do we fix the defense? What if we had very good players at every position? Could this coaching staff coach them up? You can’t blame every single defensive SNAFU on the players, many yes but not all of them. What new breakdowns will we see next week against Mahomes? Rest assured, we will see Mr. Kenneth Walker ad infinitum. My last column mentioned how special teams should be the easiest thing to fix. Boy was I wrong!!!!! This punter can’t even hold on to a ball to punt it. How does this happen? Lack of concentration, I think. Yes, I still believe they are using the “K” balls which were originally supposed to come out of the box and handed to the kicker right before it was kicked. I think the NFL has eased up on that (please correct me) so the ball is slickish( I just coined that word ). Last week we couldn’t stop the long returns; for now that seems to be fixed. For now. I should wager which special teams mistake(s) will we make next week. Why in the name of Garo Yepremian has one of our kicker/punter been needed to make a tackle the first two weeks? Who is in charge of special teams? This takes me back to the trepidation about coaching. I contend that special teams is one-third of the game. If you come out neutral on special teams, that is good enough for me. At the National Championship at the Rose Bowl, I watched Auburn lose to FSU on two game changing special teams plays: a fake punt AND a kickoff return. Other than that, Auburn was better than FSU but FSU DOMINATED special teams and deserved to beat Auburn. I don’t want that to happen to the Dolphins and I don’t want mediocrity to be accepted on special teams, offense or defense.
author: Paulie Dorsal

title: Miami Dolphins Week 2 reactions: Tuesday Miami Thoughts With The Earl
summary: That was… I mean… well… what can I say about that?  I had zero expectations about a win, but I hoped it would be somewhat competitive.  It was not.  That just plain sucked.  That is all.  Thank you for reading. Oh, you’re still here?  In that case, I’ll hit on a few things I noticed […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Jordyn Brooks #20 and head coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins talk before a game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images That was… I mean… well… what can I say about that? I had zero expectations about a win, but I hoped it would be somewhat competitive. It was not. That just plain sucked. That is all. Thank you for reading. Oh, you’re still here? In that case, I’ll hit on a few things I noticed from a quick watch of the game. As usge, I will preface by saying the best way to dissect the game if through All-22 film, which I will not get to watch today. Setting the table This loss sucked, but let’s look at it with some aqua-colored glasses for a moment. The 49ers are a Super Bowl contender. The Dolphins are not. There was plenty of discussion this week about the total number of Pro Bowls on the San Francisco 49ers roster versus the Miami Dolphins roster . There was the payroll discrepancy discussion. The broadcast highlighted how the 49ers were the oldest team in the league facing the youngest team in the league. The week prior, the 49ers went across the world to face the Los Angeles Super Rams and left with a 27-7 win. Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford went 15-of-25, 155 yards, no touchdowns, one interception, a passer rating of 61.2, and a QBR of 37.5. He had current 1st-team All-Pro Puka Nacua and three-time 1st-team All-Pro Davante Adams. They were limited to 290 yards of offense, 2-9 on 3rd down, and ran 57 total plays. The Super Rams defense allowed 379 total yards, 27 points, and generated 3 pressures with no sacks despite having the reigning DPOY and single-season sack leader Myles Garrett on their team. The Super Rams were considered THE top contender for the Super Bowl championship this season, and they were shut down by the 49ers. Enter the rebuilding Dolphins. They have a QB with limited NFL snaps, 3 rookie WRs, a ton of rookies on the defensive side of the ball, and are considered THE top contender for the 1st overall draft pick. Remember back in the day when kids would make those paper shuriken ? The Dolphins brought THAT to a nuclear war. Calling this an unfair fight is an understatement. Still, the Dolphins produced 284 yards of offense, were 7-15 on 3rd downs, and Willis had an arguably better stat line than Stafford against this same team in THEIR building. My point is that fans should not view this through the lens of how far away the Dolphins are from contention. We know that – and more on that later. The point is that the 49ers did the same thing to a far superior opponent the week before, and they’ll likely do it to others most weeks. The offense can move the ball One of the few positives from this game is that the Dolphins offense showed they can move the ball. At least in the first half. The Dolphins controlled the clock and generated 155 of their 284 yards in 3 drives. I don’t think it would have changed the outcome, but how different would it have felt if they could have scored a TD or two on those drives? Imagine if they entered halftime 17-14, 14-13, or 14-10 instead of 14-6. I don’t think the defense was stopping the 49ers at all, but let’s say the score after the 49ers’ opening 2nd-half drive is 21-14. Wouldn’t that change how the offense plays? Instead of being down 21-6 and having to force things, they could run a more balanced offense and grind down the clock. Maybe the score still ends up wild, but we would feel a little better knowing they performed well against a top tier opponent. The non-existent pass rush The elephant in the stadium for this Dolphins team isn’t the secondary or Malik Willis. It’s the pass rush that does not exist. Pro Football Focus did not have the advanced stats at the time of writing, but they now show Miami had two QB hits. That’s it. Purdy had all day to throw, and it showed. He had only two incompletions that day. The San Francisco OL is pretty good, and they limited the LA Super Rams to 3 pressures, so let’s not forget that part. But the Dolphins did not generate much pass rush against the Raiders last week. PFF has a preseason ranking of offensive lines , and Miami only plays 1 team listed outside their top 20 – Green Bay at 27th. They face 8 of the top 11 ranked OLs, including the two games against Buffalo (6th) and New England (11th). Based on a quick Google search, the lowest number of sacks ever recorded in a season was the 1956 Packers with 9. In recent history, the 2008 Chiefs only recorded 10 sacks. The 2026 Dolphins will be flirting with this record. I can’t see a game soon where the Dolphins have a good opportunity to get a sack. The Chiefs have a good OL and a QB that can avoid sacks well. The Vikings also have a good OL. This secondary needs all the help it can get and without any pressure up front, games are going to look more like this one. This and that Caleb Douglas was quiet, then got injured. That’s bad news for a team that has nothing at pass catcher. Chris Bell is still working his way back, and he should become a bigger factor. But no one else can get open. Turns out having adequate offensive skill players IS important. Willie Gay Jr. had too many mistakes in this game, and his playing time should be reduced. In fairness, I would expect a rookie like Trey Moore to make mistakes. But WGJ is a veteran and at this point, should be depth and not a starter. Malik Willis is making some inexperienced mistakes that need to be cleaned up. He ran out of bounds behind the line of scrimmage not once, but twice. Those should be throwaways. Those lose yardage and count as sacks on the stat sheet. The box score says he sacked 4 times, but only 2 of those were actual defenders getting him to the ground. These moments are coaching moments, and I kinda understand what he may be thinking. He’s likely thinking “I can make it on the run”, but that window closes quick. He is also missing some throws he should not miss. But that may be because of… The offensive line sucks again. Namely, the right tackle position. Willis and the Dolphins cannot drop back into standard passing situations without getting pressure almost immediately. Jackson is healthy but has now become a liability. For what he gives you in the running game, you lose in pass protection. At some point, the Dolphins really need to consider moving Kadyn Proctor to RT and letting DJ Campbell start at LG. I know that goes against what they said earlier this offseason, but the status quo isn’t working. Caedan Wallace may be the next guy up, but he hasn’t shown enough to feel confident he’ll be an upgrade. The Dolphins may be patient with Jackson, but they may also trade him as soon as they feel it’s necessary. Jackson will not be back in 2027. The Dolphins recently amended his contract, which makes it easier to trade him this season . Now, they won’t get much for him. Maybe a later-round pick swap or perhaps a player-for-player swap. But in a season where the Dolphins will not be competitive, getting something for a player who will be leaving anyway would be a smart move for the GM to make. I said what I said Ok… here is the “more on that later” material. I could write a couple of articles about the draft, free agency, and stuff like positional value. I will wait until the appropriate time for that. But after two weeks, some areas of need for the 2027 offseason are obvious. The Dolphins will need a new right tackle. They will need 2 new edge rushers. There are a few more needs that may become apparent. That is wide receiver, cornerback, safety, guard, tight end, and sigh… quarterback. Last week, I mentioned that Hafley could be on the hot seat quickly if the Dolphins go winless. In a glitch in the matrix, even ct1361 agrees with me . Sorta. I’m not saying he SHOULD be fired, but that is a problem for another day. Back during the draft season, I mentioned how a poorly ran…

summary: The Minnesota Vikings will once again be relegated to the late afternoon window in Week 3, and because of that the area where you’ll be able to view them live on over-the-air television is a bit more limited than it has been over the first couple of weeks of the season. The folks from 506 […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings will once again be relegated to the late afternoon window in Week 3, and because of that the area where you’ll be able to view them live on over-the-air television is a bit more limited than it has been over the first couple of weeks of the season. The folks from 506 Sports have released the coverage maps for this week’s NFL games. Here is the map for the late window games on FOX, with the Vikings’ game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers represented by the blue area. As you can see, the blue area is not terribly large. It encompasses a decent chunk of the midwest as well as most of Florida, as well as the Houston metro area, a portion of the New England states, the Pittsburgh area, and the Indianapolis/Cincinnati areas. This seems like as good a time as any to review the NFL’s doubleheader rules, since they’ll be affecting the Vikings here. Both CBS and FOX are allowed to air doubleheaders in Week 1 and Week 18, but after that they alternate weeks as to who can show a doubleheader in a single market. This week, CBS has the doubleheader. So, if you live in the blue area, there will NOT be an early game on your local FOX affiliate before the Vikings’ game kicks off at 3:05 PM Central. There will be an early and a late game on your local CBS affiliate, but not on FOX. The other FOX game in the late window is represented by the orange area on the map above, which is the Arizona Cardinals at the San Francisco 49ers. The rest of the map above is colored for the early games on FOX. Red: Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills Green: New York Jets at Detroit Lions Yellow: Seattle Seahawks at Washington Commanders Aqua: Carolina Panthers at Cleveland Browns The doubleheader rules also mean that if you live outside of the blue area, you will have to find the game on YouTube TV NFL Sunday Ticket. Or find an alternative location to watch the game from or something. So, if you want to watch the Vikings live this weekend, it might be a bit more difficult than it’s been over the first two weeks of the season. Hopefully, as many Vikings fans as possible will be able to find a way to watch this one.

title: Vikings Add Johnny Hekker, Jaret Patterson to Practice Squad
summary: On Tuesday, the Minnesota Vikings made a couple of practice squad moves, at least one of which points to a potential issue with the club’s special teams unit. The team has announced that they have added punter Johnny Hekker and running back Jaret Patterson to the practice squad. To make room, the team has waived […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Johnny Hekker #5 of the Minnesota Vikings punts the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the third quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, the Minnesota Vikings made a couple of practice squad moves, at least one of which points to a potential issue with the club’s special teams unit. The team has announced that they have added punter Johnny Hekker and running back Jaret Patterson to the practice squad. To make room, the team has waived cornerback Bryce Phillips and wide receiver Trayvon Rudolph. The Vikings have also waived defensive lineman Taki Taimani from injured reserve. Hekker, who spent the preseason with the Vikings and ultimately lost the team’s punting battle to rookie Brett Thorson, is back with the team because Thorson is now dealing with a hamstring injury that he suffered at some point during the team’s 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears on Sunday. The team is still evaluating Thorson’s condition, and it isn’t known at this time whether or not he will miss any time. If he does, the long-time veteran will be prepared to take over Thorson’s duties as both punter and holder for Will Reichard. Patterson has been in the league for a few seasons, as he signed with the Washington Football Team as an undrafted free agent in 2021. He spent his first two seasons with Washington, rushing for 266 yards and two touchdowns on 68 carries in his first season before appearing in only three games in his second season and getting just 17 carries. He spent part of the 2023 season on the Los Angeles Chargers’ practice squad and then landed back with Washington’s practice squad after being let go by the Chargers in December. Patterson has spent the last two seasons with the Chargers. He appeared in just one game in 2024 and in six games in 2025, carrying the ball 41 times for 159 yards and a touchdown. It’s possible that Patterson was brought in because DeeJay Dallas could be dealing with an injury now as well. Dallas went out of Sunday’s game in Chicago after suffering what appeared to be some sort of leg injury in the fourth quarter. The Vikings also have veteran running back Jerome Ford on the practice squad, having signed him in the week leading up to the Bears game.

title: 2026 NFL Week 3: Minnesota Vikings at Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: (Yes, the AI intro pictures are gone.) Fresh off back-to-back divisional victories to start a season for the first time since 2003, the Minnesota Vikings will start their tour of the NFC South for the 2026 season as they head to balmy central Florida to face off against a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that may […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 10: Jordan Addison #3 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a touchdown pass against Ryan Neal #23 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first half at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 10, 2023 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images (Yes, the AI intro pictures are gone.) Fresh off back-to-back divisional victories to start a season for the first time since 2003, the Minnesota Vikings will start their tour of the NFC South for the 2026 season as they head to balmy central Florida to face off against a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that may find themselves in desperation mode after their first two games of the season. The weather is going to be quite a change from what the Vikings saw last week in Chicago. After playing in wet, windy, sloppy conditions at Soldier Field last week, the forecast for the Tampa area this week is calling for temperatures in the mid-80s at kickoff and no precipitation in the forecast. After last week, both teams will be happy to see that. The Buccaneers, who fell to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1, hosted the Cleveland Browns in Week 2. Trailing late in the game, the Bucs pushed into Cleveland territory at the two-minute warning. Suddenly, the game came to a halt, and there was a delay that stretched for over two hours because of thunderstorms in the Tampa area. When the two teams got back on the field, the Bucs lost whatever momentum they may have had, and couldn’t get the ball into the end zone, turning the ball over on downs to seal a 23-19 loss to the Browns to drop their record to 0-2. The Vikings, as we’ve mentioned, have won their first two games of the season, mostly behind backup quarterback Carson Wentz. Wentz entered the season opener against the Green Bay Packers in the first quarter after Kyler Murray went out with a concussion and helped rally the team to a 39-22 victory. Last week in Chicago, the offense had its issues again, but the defense more than carried the load and ensured that three field goals from Will Reichard were enough to hold up as the Vikings got their seventh straight win in Chicago and their seventh straight win going back to last season, winning 9-3. Murray, who did not clear the league’s concussion protocol in time to play against Chicago in Week 2, has cleared protocol this week and has already been named the starter for Sunday’s game for Minnesota. After getting a noon Central Time kickoff in Week 2, the Vikings will once again be pushed to the late window in Week 3, with Sunday’s game getting underway at 3:05 PM Central Time. The game will be carried by the FOX family of networks, including KMSP-9 in the Twin Cities. We’ll be keeping all of our stories about this week’s game here in this stream for you to find more easily, so keep checking back here for all the latest. title: Vikings Autopsy: Daily Norseman Week 2 Postgame Roundtable (A 9-3 win over Bears)
summary: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 2 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off an ugly 9-3 win at Skoldier Field, and are now alone atop the NFC North at 2-0. Did the Vikings beat the Bears? Did the Bears beat themselves? Did Caleb Williams really need a […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - SEPTEMBER 2026: Minnesota Vikings linebacker Andrew van Ginkel (43) sacks Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) on the last play of the second quarter at Solider Field in Chicago, Illinois, on Sunday, September 20, 2026. (Photo by Jerry Holt/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images) Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 2 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off an ugly 9-3 win at Skoldier Field, and are now alone atop the NFC North at 2-0. Did the Vikings beat the Bears? Did the Bears beat themselves? Did Caleb Williams really need a cart to leave the field? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle for a minute — get your initial thoughts out about the Vikings beating the Bears in Week 2, 9-3. Brandon Warne : An ugly win is still a win. It’s hard to know if more credit should be given to the defense, the man running it behind the scenes, the conditions or the gawd-awful footing, but all of it came together for a nail-biter instant classic that still could have gone the other way in the closing moments. Warren Ludford : The Vikings leveraged the key elements of winning better than their opponent — turnovers, situational football, and special teams — but once again fell short in yard-based metrics. That’s fine occasionally, but it’s not sustainable without a more productive offense. Still, the Vikings could make a run in the playoffs after winning the division. Craig Williams : I wouldn’t go as far as to say it was a lucky win, but it was definitely a win by slim margins. A win in Chicago is always a good win, and starting 2-0 in the NFC North is a great place to be. I am concerned about the offense, though, and I’m hoping it looks better once Murray is back under center. ————— Question 2: Who was your Vikings MVP? BW : I think it has to be Dallas Turner, who may have already filed change-of-address forms to show he lives in the Bears backfield. I’m actually not-so-secretly enjoying roasting all the people who were so sure he was a bust before he’d even played a full year. By the way, here’s a fun fact: Turner is 23 and he’s not going to be 24 until right around the Super Bowl. Jared Verse, who went two picks after him in the draft, was nearly 24 when he played his first NFL game, and will be 26 in just over a month. WL : Aaron Jones. He was the bell cow the Vikings needed in this game despite being a bit older to still take on this role. He had over 100 yards and 4.6 ypa and no turnovers. That was key when passing yards were hard to come by. CW : How is Dallas Turner not the answer here? Jalen Redmond had a fantastic game. Aaron Jones carried the offense. Will Reichard scored all of the team’s points. That all being said, Turner is playing at a Defensive Player of the Year level right now. It’s early, but he’s been a stud for two straight weeks. ————— Question 3: Who was your Vikings LVP? BW : I’m not seeing it from Josh Metellus so far this season. I just have thought the angles for tackles and the pass coverage have been lacking so far. I’m willing to be wrong about this. WL : Caleb Banks. He showed improvement in his second game and had a few stops, but he also got schooled on the Bears’ opening drive of the second half, which allowed them to drive to the one-yard line before fumbling. CW : Theo Jackson has been a dud among the studs. He’s struggled to tackle consistently and has become the weak spot in an otherwise outstanding defense. ————— Question 4: Real talk — Caleb Williams carted off for a hamstring injury….fair or foul? BW : I have a hard time caring too much about it — but the talking heads are paid for this and Twitter (I will not call it the other name) is built for overreaction — but I will say that the memes have been absolute gold. WL : Fair. Shit happens. Just bad luck for the Bears. No sympathy or excuses for them facing a team that started their backup quarterback the whole game. CW : It’s hard for me to criticize injured players, but that wasn’t a great look. He looked like Paul Pierce in the wheelchair during the playoffs. I also just realized that half our audience is probably too young to understand that reference. That was 18 years ago, so look it up. Pierce got wheeled off the court after colliding with a teammate and then magically returned about two minutes later. ————— Question 5: The rematch in Minnesota later this season: What are you expecting? BW : It’s honestly too soon to even guess. It’ll be in better weather (read: none) conditions, you’d assume both teams have their preferred quarterbacks starting that game — whoever that might be for the Vikings at that point — and it’s a home game. KOC’s Vikings can be tough at home. I’m feeling a win, but why would I say otherwise? WL : A better game on a decent field. Beyond that, difficult to say. Hopefully the Vikings will have wrapped things up and will be playing their second string. CW : I’d expect a similar game next week. There might actually be a touchdown or two this time, but I still think it’ll be a slugfest. ( Editor’s note : Craig may have misunderstood the question)

title: Kyler Murray Clears Concussion Protocol, Will Start Against Tampa Bay
summary: As they prepare for their third game of the 206 NFL season, the quarterback carousel for the Minnesota Vikings has spun once again. At his press conference yesterday, head coach Kevin O’Connell announced that quarterback Kyler Murray had officially cleared the league’s concussion protocol and would start for the team on Sunday when they travel […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up before a game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images As they prepare for their third game of the 206 NFL season, the quarterback carousel for the Minnesota Vikings has spun once again. At his press conference yesterday, head coach Kevin O’Connell announced that quarterback Kyler Murray had officially cleared the league’s concussion protocol and would start for the team on Sunday when they travel to central Florida to take on the 0-2 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Murray played just 11 snaps in the Vikings’ Week 1 opener against the Green Bay Packers before departing after taking a shot to the head from Javon Bullard during a slide attempt following a scramble. Murray went straight to the locker room and was diagnosed with a concussion. He was relieved for the remainder of the game by Carson Wentz, and Wentz started last week’s game against Chicago when Murray did not clear protocol in enough time to play. The Vikings’ offense has had its struggles in the first two games. They put up 39 points against the Packers, but three of their touchdown drives came on possessions of less than 30 yards thanks to a Myles Price kick return and a pair of Green Bay turnovers. Against Chicago, they managed just three Will Reichard field goals, but that was enough to get the job done thanks to a stifling performance by Brian Flores’ defense. Now, they’ll likely need a much bigger offensive performance against a Tampa Bay team that figures to be in desperation mode following a pair of season-opening losses. The depth chart figures to go back to what it was in Week 1, with Wentz serving as the primary backup to Murray and J.J. McCarthy serving as the emergency quarterback in the event that both Murray and Wentz get injured. Kyler Murray will be back in the saddle on Sunday in Tampa Bay, folks. Are you excited about it? Let us know!

title: Dallas Turner, Jalen Redmond, and the Vikings’ Defensive Identity
summary: Minnesota is 2-0 after a sloppy 9-3 win at Chicago, and on The Real Forno Show Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano argued that the real story is belief: a Flores defense that can close, a run game that is finally getting volume, and enough luck to survive a backup-QB weather game. Forness opened with the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - SEPTEMBER 2026: Minnesota Vikings linebacker Andrew van Ginkel (43) sacks Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) on the last play of the second quarter at Solider Field in Chicago, Illinois, on Sunday, September 20, 2026. (Photo by Jerry Holt/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images) Minnesota is 2-0 after a sloppy 9-3 win at Chicago, and on The Real Forno Show Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano argued that the real story is belief: a Flores defense that can close, a run game that is finally getting volume, and enough luck to survive a backup-QB weather game. Forness opened with the question that framed the hour: “Have the Minnesota Vikings built themself a Super Bowl foundation? I think they have.” He was careful not to crown anyone. “I’m not saying the Vikings will win the Super Bowl, but they have started a foundation.” That foundation, in their telling, is not Kevin O’Connell’s vertical offense. It is winning when the script dies. “Two years ago, this team loses that game,” Forness said of the old Soldier Field nightmares. Chicago went 0-for-3 in the red zone. Isaiah Rodgers recovered a fumble and later blocked a kick. Dallas Turner finished Tyson Bagent when Colston Loveland was left alone. Forness called Brian Flores’ last call “a genius actual play design,” then added the Super Bowl caveat: “This play doesn’t happen if it’s Caleb Williams.” Luck is part of the pitch. “You have to have luck in order to win a Super Bowl.” The offense is the open question. “I can’t tell you if the offense is good or not because we haven’t seen the offense actually play, other than 11 plays,” Forness said of Kyler Murray. Carson Wentz “proved who he is”: high variance, a few lasers to Josh Oliver and T.J. Hockenson, and the misses that keep him a backup. O’Connell has cleared Murray for Tampa. On the ground, Aaron Jones went 23-for-105 with Jordan Mason out; Forness still called the backfield “abysmal” if Jones goes down, with Demond Claiborne “borderline unplayable,” DeeJay Dallas dinged, and Jerome Ford on the practice squad. Ben Goessling’s True Media note: Minnesota is No. 1 in first- and second-down run rate (62%+). Forness: two games is not a fix. “How do these tendencies manifest with Kyler Murray?” Key points from the episode: Winning ugly builds confidence: The Vikings leaned on a 62% run rate (number one in the NFL on first and second down, per Ben Goessling) and a defense that covered while blitzing — a combination Forness called “disgusting” in the best way. Dallas Turner’s emergence: Despite criticism for not winning enough one-on-ones, Turner has 20 pressures in two weeks and is being schemed into favorable matchups. “Brian Flores continues to be a creative mastermind,” Forness said. “I think Dallas Turner is primed to have an elite season.” Defensive line depth paying off: Jalen Redmond “might be the best player on the team not named Justin Jefferson or Christian Darrisaw.” Levi Drake Rodriguez, a seventh-round pick, has become a starter. Caleb Banks and Dominique Orange are flashing elite potential. “As much as we can criticize Kwesi Adofo-Mensah for a lot of things, that calculated bet is paying humongous dividends.” Run game concerns: Aaron Jones is banged up and sore, Jordan Mason has a broken thumb, and Demond Claiborne is “borderline unplayable.” Forness flagged the backfield depth as the biggest red flag going forward. Carson Wentz is who we thought he was: “He is who we thought he was,” Forness said of Wentz, who delivers highs and lows with no consistency. Kyler Murray has cleared concussion protocol just in time. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: If the Vikings keep finding different ways to win — and the good proves repeatable — this team has the foundation for a deep playoff run. “If it’s repeatable, then you can expect it to happen again.” Catch The Real Forno Show every Monday night on Vikings 1st & SKOL for the kind of film-level breakdown you won’t get anywhere else. Subscribe, leave a five-star review on iTunes, and join the Discord for live commentary. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . So here’s two questions, Vikings fans: Are the Vikings legitimately building a Super Bowl foundation, or is it too early to buy in? And… What part of this 2-0 start actually travels to Tampa — the front, the run rate, or Murray coming back?
