title: Jaxson Dart injury: NY Giants’ QB could miss the remainder of the 2026 season
summary: The MRI on New York Giants’ quarterback Jaxson Dart’s left knee revealed an injury more severe than was believed on Monday night, per NFL insiders Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport. Dart could miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh would not confirm the reports that Dart would miss the season. […]
full_text: The MRI on New York Giants’ quarterback Jaxson Dart’s left knee revealed an injury more severe than was believed on Monday night, per NFL insiders Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport . Dart could miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh would not confirm the reports that Dart would miss the season. “Evaluations are ongoing,” Harbaugh said. “We’ve learned a lot more. “I’m not commenting on all the different reports. In due time, at the proper time everybody’s gonna know what the outcome is. “When we know what direction we’re going to have to go or whatever it might be, we’ll announce that. But we don’t have that yet, so I don’t want to get out over our skis on that. I can’t really respond to every report that people make. We’ve got to kind of work on our own timeline here.” Dart was injured on the Giants’ first drive of the game Monday night. While throwing a pass to tight end Theo Johnson, Dart was sandwiched between Los Angeles Rams’ defenders Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart, with his left knee inverting awkwardly. Dart limped off the field under his own power, and was on the sideline in street clothes during the second half of the 28-6 loss to the Rams. The injury was initially believed to be a sprained MCL. “We can’t control things,” Harbaugh said. “We don’t have the ability to dictate as much as we’d like to any kind of outcome. So whatever transpires is what we’re going to have to respond to and react to. “We’re going to have to meet those circumstances, whatever they are. And right now, that’s a range of things and we’re just going to have to see where we’re at. But we’re going to work really hard to prepare for those things and try to focus on the task at hand, which is we have five days till we play Tennessee Titans and we’ve got to be at our best as a team. “We just got to prepare for the range of possibilities. And then once we know where we’re at, make a plan going forward, and that’s really what we’re going to do.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter is reporting that Dart could be facing surgery , and said that “Of all the QB injuries suffered in Week 2, Dart’s is turning out to easily be the most significant.” Harbaugh said Tuesday that confirming any timeline for the severity of Dart’s injury was “not the right thing to do” because evaluations and decisions are still being made. “In due time at the proper time, everybody’s going to know what the outcome is,” Harbaugh said. “But, while these conversations are being had, I don’t think that’s really fair to the person involved or the people involved tob give a running report on where it stands or what those conversations are. “It’s not the right thing to do. It’s when decisions get made and, and we know which direction we’re going to go, then heck yeah, we’ll let everybody know what they are. But until that happens I can’t breach those conversations.” The Giants were looking like a potential playoff contender after Dart completed 23 of 29 for 230 yards and 3 touchdowns while also running 11 times for 54 yards in a season-opening 28-20 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. Now, the Giants are looking at having Jameis Winston at quarterback for the remainder of the season. The Giants have quarterback Jake Haener on their practice. They could bring back Brandon Allen, who was let go when rosters were trimmed to 53 players, as a third quarterback, or look elsewhere.

title: Why did the Jets call THAT play on fourth down?
summary: Being an offensive playcaller in the NFL is one of the most thankless jobs in sports. NFL fans might occasionally get on their team’s defensive playcaller for not blitzing enough (or blitzing too much), but few focus on the way the defense is called as a determining factor in wins and losses. On the flip […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Green Bay Packers safety Evan Williams (33) makes a tackle on New York Jets running back Braelon Allen (0) during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Being an offensive playcaller in the NFL is one of the most thankless jobs in sports. NFL fans might occasionally get on their team’s defensive playcaller for not blitzing enough (or blitzing too much), but few focus on the way the defense is called as a determining factor in wins and losses. On the flip side, everybody thinks they can call offensive plays better than the guy their team has. Second guessing offensive playcalling is a weekly rite of passage for NFL fans. Unfortunately for playcallers, the analysis of their work tends to be results oriented. If a play works, it must be because the call was perfect. If it fails, it must have been foolish. Of course, results ultimately matter more than anything else. Still, I think we should try to consider the context before every play when we evaluate whether a specific call was good or bad. Back in Super Bowl XLIX, the Seattle Seahawks lost to the New England Patriots. The decisive play was an interception by Malcolm Butler at the goal line off Russell Wilson in the final minute. The Seahawks’ coaching staff was roasted for not calling a run on the one yard line. The issue for me with the call wasn’t that Seattle threw an interception. It’s that with a championship hanging in the balance, they called a passing play targeting their sixth leading receiver instead of giving the ball to the greatest short yardage back of his generation, Marshawn Lynch, needing to pick up a single yard. Conversely, there are situations where a playcall can be logical and simply not work out. In Week 2 the Jets found themselves with a fourth and one at midfield with less than a minute and a half left in the fourth quarter. If the team converted the first down, they would be close to the range necessary for a game-winning field goal attempt. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich called a run up the middle from the shotgun to Braelon Allen that was stopped. Green Bay got the ball back with a chance to win it in regulation. Since that run was stuffed, people have asked over and over why the offensive coordinator would call a shotgun run for his number two back. I can’t sit here and tell you definitively that it was the right call, but I can at least offer an explanation as to why Reich tried that play. The Jets were not terribly successful running the ball in their loss to Green Bay. In fact, their top two backs only converted three runs all game that went for first downs along with a goal line touchdown. One of them came in the first half on a third and short. The Jets ran a concept called Duo. Without getting too technical, Duo calls for the line to execute as many double teams as possible up the middle based on the defense’s alignment. The back then generally has one running back to read to find his hole. He, of course, also must see daylight from the blocks his teammates throw. Eventually if the double team is effective or if a linebacker charges to the line of scrimmage, one of the offensive linemen has to peel off the double team and hit the linebacker. Here Hall finds a hole to the outside. Holes can close quickly, though, so Hall needed to be decisive. That gap, and his willingness to lower his shoulder converted this short yardage situation. View Link In the second quarter, the Jets found themselves in a goal to go situation from the 5 yard line. This time Allen was in. Again the Jets went to Duo from the shotgun. Again, you eventually need your double teams to peel off and take a linebacker. Here there aren’t many lanes to run in the middle of the field, but Allen sees the outside is wide open. He bounces the run and takes it to the end zone. View Link Later in the game the Jets found themselves in a third and short. Again Allen is in the game. Again the call is Duo. The Jets aim to work some double teams. Here we can see Allen’s line of sight to get a pretty good sense of the linebacker he’s reading. There is a nice gap that opens for him to hit. Allen converts to move the chains. View Link Fast forward to that drive in the fourth quarter. On the play immediately preceding the fourth down stuff, the Jets had it on third and two from their own 39. Here the Packers loaded the line of scrimmage with defenders. This run might well have been Duo, but so many guys at the line make it tough to say for sure. Breece Hall is the back on this snap, and it appears he has a nice lane opening in front of him. Instead of hitting that lane, he bounces right, which takes him into traffic. The Packers stuff him for a one yard gain, setting up fourth down. Look, I don’t know how Hall was coached to execute this run. I can’t guarantee you he picks up the first down if he hits that hole in front of him with 100 percent certainty. It did look like to me like he cut into a much tougher path, though. View Link That brings us to fourth down. What has Frank Reich seen all day? His team has three rushing first downs and one rushing touchdown. Three of those four were picked up running Duo from the shotgun in either short yardage or goal to go situations. It has been the Jets’ most reliable run play of the game. Allen converted two of those three runs, and Hall just arguably made the wrong cut on a short yardage play. That’s the information Reich had to work with as he decided which play to turn to on fourth and one. Does that necessarily make giving the ball to Allen off Duo from the shotgun the best call he could make in this situation? No, of course not. Do I understand why he would make that call given the context? I do. Do I think the call is defensible? Again, yes, I do. Unfortunately we sometimes are so focused on the call that we let the players off the hook for poor execution. This play ended up being blocked so poorly that I can’t even tell you the blocking assignments with any degree of confidence. At first I thought it looked something like this. Watching it a few times I wondered if it was something like this. What I can say is the Jets missed a lot of blocks. Jeremy Ruckert was immediately beaten inside off the end of the line. Armand Membou seems to be attempting a cut block and completely misses. And Joe Tippmann also ends up on the ground as he is aiming for a double team. I can understand if you would have preferred having Breece Hall in there, but I don’t believe he or any back on the league is going to convert a first down on a play blocked like this. View Link You may say that even knowing all that, it still made more sense to run Hall from under center. No matter what happened to that point, Hall is your lead back, and under center runs tend to be more effective. I can’t really dispute that logic. Just know that there is no guarantee it would have worked. The Jets called 10 runs in this game for Hall under center which produced 23 yards. Four of the ten resulted in negative yardage. I’m not trying to absolve Frank Reich of blame here. He made some decisions during the game which were curious. If you include sacks and quarterback scrambles as passing calls, the Jets had a pass:run ratio of 2:1 in this game. The team isn’t built to play that way. You might find this to be an odd criticism given everything I just said about the Jets’ rushing woes in this game. I’ll admit that maybe more runs would not have worked. Regardless, this team’s identity is based on being a physical team that can run the ball. Geno Smith in 2026 is not the sort of quarterback who is likely to have much success when you call 50 passing plays. Sometimes running the ball effectively means taking some negatives early in the game but slowly wearing down the defense with your physicality and breaking through later. I also would question Allen getting only 5 carries. On a bad…

title: For the Eagles, first down has been the worst down
summary: The new look Eagles offense hasn’t been much fun. There are multiple reasons, but one of them is that on 1st down, they’re terrible. The offense is 28th in EPA/play and 31st in both yards per play and success rate; and have gained a 1st down on 1st down just twice, the fewest in the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Cam Jurgens #51 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on as he walks off the field against the Washington Commanders following an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The new look Eagles offense hasn’t been much fun. There are multiple reasons, but one of them is that on 1st down, they’re terrible. The offense is 28th in EPA/play and 31st in both yards per play and success rate; and have gained a 1st down on 1st down just twice, the fewest in the league. Oddly, neither were on 1st and 10, Darius Cooper’s 23 yard reception in the 4th quarter against the Titans was on 1st and 17 , and then his TD on 1st and goal was from the 3. On 1st down, the Eagles have as many negative plays as they do plays that gained 7+ yards, 9 each. On their 48 1st downs, they have failed to gain yardage on 18 of them. Their average 2nd down needs 8.7 yards to gain a first down, 26th so far this season. They’re bad at everything. Though the Eagles run 65% of the time on 1st down. They stink there. 24th in EPA/play 27th in success rate 28th in yards per carry When the Eagles do throw on 1st down, they’re woefully short. CPOE: 19th EPA per play: 26th Success rate: 31st Air yards per attempt: 31st Yards per attempt: 32nd This is not a Jalen Hurts issue. He had the 5th highest air yards per attempt on 1st down in 2025, and 14th in 2024. Nor is this a lack of AJ Brown issue, he was 48th in air yards per target last season, nor is this a Dontayvion Wicks as his replacement issue, he was 56th. And though it has only been two games, this isn’t a situation where one bad game, the team’s failure to gain a single 1st down on 1st down against the Commanders, is bogging down the numbers. The Eagles converted a 1st down on just 2 of 28 1st downs against the Titans, 7.1%. Given the same rate against the Commanders, the Eagles would still be dead last in 1st conversion rate on 1st down. The next worst team, the Steelers, have converted at 7.4%. This is an offensive line and coaching issue. The Eagles are 19th in sack rate per play, and 28th in pressures per play. Short throws to beat the pressure is a tried and true way of masking offensive line problems, but the Eagles entire first down offense is throwing short passes. They’re not trying to take a shot down the field. Even Darius Cooper’s 23 yard reception on 1st and 17 was caught 5 yards beyond the line of scrimmage, though he wasn’t the first read, that was a good progression by Jalen Hurts. Two games is a small sample size, but the NFL is built out of small sample sizes. Two games is a playoff run. Two games into the season and the Bucs, Chargers, Colts, and Texans are in trouble. Two games into the season and the Eagles offense is in trouble too. Moving Cam Jurgens, who co-leads the league in holding penalties, to guard didn’t improve things. Perhaps more time will result in improved offensive line play, but there’s not a rich history of teams making significant changes to their line in-season and getting great results.

title: Eagles News: “Dontayvion Wicks is showcasing why the Eagles thought he was an under-the-radar steal”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Dontayvion Wicks (AKA Don Wick AKA Donny Candles) has been a pretty good pickup; he’s looking like a real solid WR2 to pair with DeVonta Smith as WR1. Seems to me like Smitty and Makai Lemon missing a lot of time […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Dontayvion Wicks (AKA Don Wick AKA Donny Candles) has been a pretty good pickup; he’s looking like a real solid WR2 to pair with DeVonta Smith as WR1. Seems to me like Smitty and Makai Lemon missing a lot of time in training camp really helped Jalen Hurts foster a better connection with Wicks since that was often his top option to throw to. Good job by Howie Roseman to trade for Wicks on the cheap (two Day 3 draft picks) and sign him to an extension to keep him under team control through 2027. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Cam Jurgens’ fit, Dontayvion Wicks’ emergence, Zach Ertz’s role: Eagles thoughts – The Athletic The passing game has exceeded what I expected, and the wide receivers are quieting any external concerns. Dontayvion Wicks is validating the summer optimism. One point I made frequently this offseason was that the Eagles didn’t need to replace A.J. Brown; DeVonta Smith could handle that No. 1 role. They needed to replace Smith as the No. 2 option. Wicks is showcasing why the Eagles thought he was an under-the-radar steal when they acquired him via trade and signed him to a contract extension. Wicks has caught seven of 10 targets for 147 yards. All seven of his receptions have resulted in first downs or touchdowns. His average depth of target has been 15.7 yards. Three of his receptions have traveled over 20 yards in the air. Four of his five receptions Sunday were on third down, and two were for third-and-12 conversions. Hurts trusts him. Wicks runs precise routes. He makes difficult catches. Wicks and Smith have combined for 20 catches for 317 yards through two games. That’s more yards than in any of the first two games Brown and Smith played together. This doesn’t mean the Eagles have a duo like Brown and Smith, but it’s a formidable combination. Eagles-Titans Film Review: A very good offense is hiding in here – BGN The Eagles won 24-20, and I came away feeling much better about the passing game than I did after Week 1. The Eagles found answers against the Titans’ coverage, attacked the weaknesses I flagged in my preview (which is always great to see), and repeatedly converted third-and-long. However, the offense cannot keep making life this difficult for itself. The Eagles went 11-of-18 on third down, which is an absurd 61.1% conversion rate. That’s why they sustained drives despite averaging only 4.7 yards per play, turning the ball over twice and rushing for 89 yards on 32 attempts. Winning on third down is obviously good. Needing Hurts to repeatedly deliver elite throws on third-and-long isn’t a sustainable offensive identity. The early-down numbers are wild. I mean, come on… Chicago Bears Injury News: Tyson Bagent in concussion protocol – Windy City Gridiron If Williams and Bagent can’t go, look for 38-year-old Case Keenum to get the start. Keenum last played in a regular-season game on Christmas Eve, 2023, when he started for the Houston Texans. He was 11 of 17 for 62 yards and 2 interceptions before giving way to Davis Mills in the fourth quarter. Chicago also has undrafted free agent Miller Moss on the practice squad, who would likely be elevated to back up Keenum. Game Review – PHI 24, TEN 20 – Iggles Blitz All the WRs contributed in this game. Dontayvion Wicks went 5-74, with several catches coming on 3rd or 4th down. He did a good job of getting open and catching the ball when it came his way. He had a drop on the final drive, but it was only going to be for a couple of yards so the team was better off that he didn’t catch that. Darius Cooper was 2-26 and caught the game-winning TD. He had a chance for another good gain, but the pass was just a bit too far out front. Hollywood Brown had 2 runs for 12 yards. Makai Lemon caught 1 pass for 14 yards. He also had 1 run for -5 yards, a pass behind the LOS. Really good game from the WR corps. The Winners and Losers of the NFL Week 2 – The Ringer Every Eagles game becomes a national referendum on how much credit belongs to Hurts and how much belongs to everything surrounding him. But right now, there are real problems for Philadelphia to solve. The offensive line hasn’t played well in the first two weeks. The early-down offense has created far too many difficult third-down situations. Vic Fangio’s defense has struggled throughout both second halves and allowed Cam Ward to play one of the best games of his career on Sunday. But after an offseason spent discussing how much talent the Eagles have assembled around their quarterback, they are 2-0 because of him. He was the one who finished that shit, and he got to tell that to Simmons’s face. Evaluating surprise early-season trends for 32 NFL teams – ESPN The early surprise: The defense has generated zero takeaways. The verdict: Mirage. The Eagles ranked sixth in opponent turnovers (47) over the past two seasons under defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, and they should see their fortunes turn in the near future. They’ll get a boost in the pass-rushing department when their splash offseason acquisition, Jonathan Greenard, returns from his pec injury. “Super, super close,” Greenard said last week. Do-it-all defensive back Cooper DeJean has been dealing with calf and abdomen injuries, as well; the healthier he gets, the more dangerous that back end becomes. Does Zach Ertz still have the juice to contribute to the Eagles? Here’s what the film — and history — says – Inquirer While Ertz still can thrive as a receiver, he does not bring much as a blocker, an area where the Eagles have struggled through two weeks. Much of his time in Washington was spent as a detached slot receiver on run-pass option plays or as a lead blocker on the perimeter for zone-read runs with Jayden Daniels. He has not had an in-line blocking role for the majority of his career, and that is unlikely to change in this reunion. But with Goedert missing time, Ertz’s contributions as a pass catcher seemed to be what the Eagles are seeking in the franchise legend. 10 reasons to be optimistic about the Eagles’ defense – NBCSP Pass defense: Not everything has gone well so far, but the Eagles’ pass defense has been elite. The Eagles have only allowed 166 passing yards per game, 4th-fewest in the league, and they’ve held opposing quarterbacks to 57.4 percent completion percentage, also 4th-lowest in the league. They’ve only allowed two passing touchdowns, tied for 6th-fewest in the league. And they’ve allowed only six total plays of 20 yards or more, 10th-fewest in the league through two games. This is a passing league and the Eagles are built to stop the pass. 2026 NFL offensive line rankings: Falcons rise, Patriots tumble following injury – PFF 4) PHILADELPHIA EAGLES. The injury to Landon Dickerson forced some shuffling on the Eagles’ offensive line, with Cam Jurgens moving from center to left guard and Drew Kendall coming in to replace him in the middle of the offensive line. The results weren’t great for either player, with both earning sub-50.0 PFF grades against the Tennessee Titans. Lane Johnson was the team’s best pass-blocker, producing a 97.7% PFF pass-block win rate. There is clearly still a lot of talent on this offensive line, but how Jurgens and Kendall perform this week will be key. Spadaro: Jalen Hurts, Eagles do what it takes to win – PhiladelphiaEagles.com This has been, as all parties said from the very start, a collaborative project. Sean Mannion was hired as the Eagles’ offensive coordinator and brought with him a new scheme that required everyone to buy in, make progress on a daily basis, and understand the “why” in his…

title: Eagles rookie report card: Titans game
summary: The Eagles beat the heat and the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Despite scorching conditions down on the field, Philadelphia escaped Nashville on the back of a heroic Jalen Hurts drive. The rookie contribution on Sunday was small, but here’s what we noticed from the Eagles’ 2026 NFL Draft class. Makai Lemon: C- It’s getting kind […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles beat the heat and the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Despite scorching conditions down on the field, Philadelphia escaped Nashville on the back of a heroic Jalen Hurts drive. The rookie contribution on Sunday was small, but here’s what we noticed from the Eagles’ 2026 NFL Draft class. Makai Lemon: C- It’s getting kind of funny now. In Week 1, Makai Lemon’s peculiar usage landed him with negative five yards receiving. The screens and shuffle passes were not working for the young man. In the Tennessee game, the Eagles decided to get him on another shuffle pass that lost five yards… Luckily for his box score, it was counted as a rushing attempt. Lemon got his first quality target in this game, however, and converted on a really nice 14-yard catch. He broke nicely on a route, Jalen Hurts hit him right in the middle of the field and he caught the pass with bodies around. Those are the kinds of plays the Eagles need from Lemon, especially out of the slot. As the season goes on, I expect Lemon’s usage increases as a middle of the field target as Hurts targets that area of the field more and more. While the Titans game wasn’t a stats bonanza, we got a glimmer of hope from Lemon in this one. Extra credit: Makai Lemon HOOFED it down the field to help tackle Amani Hooker and prevent a pick six. Nice play, rook. Other thoughts on the rookies: Cam Jurgens looked really rough in this game at guard. If the Eagles want to keep Drew Kendall at center, where he played well, Philly might consider benching Jurgens at some point later this season if his bad play persists. Such a move could help Micah Morris up the depth chart behind Willie Lampkin. The Dallas Goedert injury sucks. Even with the Zach Ertz signing, the Eagles tight end situation looks really rough. Eli Stowers needs to contribute at some point this season, even a little bit. He can’t return to the active roster until Week 5 at the earliest.

summary: The New York Giants had an exciting Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys! Since then? Not great. The G-Men got blown out by the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night in Week 2 while also sustaining multiple key injuries. One of those was to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, who left the game with a […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants walks back to the locker room after being injured in a play against Byron Young #0 of the Los Angeles Rams during the first quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Giants had an exciting Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys! Since then? Not great. The G-Men got blown out by the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night in Week 2 while also sustaining multiple key injuries. One of those was to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, who left the game with a knee injury. After some initial optimism (Giants GM Joe Schoen insisted that he was “going to be OK”) that Dart avoided a major injury, the Giants are getting some bad news. Dart’s injury is “worse than anticipated” and the quarterback is “out an extended period of time, possibly the season,” according to a report from NFL insider Ian Rapoport . This news is obviously a brutal blow to the Giants’ outlook. They have an experienced backup in Jameis Winston, who struggled against the Rams but has obviously had some levels of success in the past. The Philadelphia Eagles are set to play the Giants on the road in Week 9 and at home in Week 18. It sounds like Dart will at least miss the November 8 game. And if New York is unable to stay afloat without him, they might not bother bringing him back (assuming he’s even healthy enough to play) very late in the season. Tough break for the Giants, who are now the second team in the NFC East to have a major quarterback injury with Jayden Daniels also getting hurt in Week 2. Check out more coverage of this injury over at Big Blue View . We’re also reacting to the news on the NFC East Mixtape podcast :

title: Eagles practice squad cornerback is being poached by the Falcons
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are losing practice squad cornerback Robert Longerbeam to the Atlanta Falcons, according to a report from NFL insider Mike Garafolo. With the Falcons placing starter A.J. Terrell on injured reserve, Atlanta found themselves in need of corner help and decided to poach Longerbeam. The Eagles have one of the NFL’s best corner […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Robert Longerbeam (37) looks on after the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are losing practice squad cornerback Robert Longerbeam to the Atlanta Falcons, according to a report from NFL insider Mike Garafolo . With the Falcons placing starter A.J. Terrell on injured reserve , Atlanta found themselves in need of corner help and decided to poach Longerbeam. The Eagles have one of the NFL’s best corner trios with Quinyon Mitchell, Riq Woolen, and Cooper DeJean starting for them. It’s not like Longerbeam had a great pathway to playing time in Philly. That being said, he did seem like a nice developmental option to have around on the practice squad. We wrote as much when the Eagles signed him on September 1 : He missed his entire rookie season due to a knee injury before making some noise in training camp/preseason games this summer. According to Pro Football Focus charting, Longerbeam allowed just an 84.2 passer rating while targeted in coverage. He finished the preseason as the Ravens’ third-best defender by PFF grading. In a recent roundtable article over at Baltimore Beatdown, multiple Ravens writers brought up Longerbeam as a player they were concerned about getting claimed on waivers. Bummer that the Eagles are losing Longerbeam (although I’m sure Robert Longbeam is happy about this development). But such is the nature of the practice squad.

title: Eagles reportedly sign Kenny Moore II
summary: Zach Ertz isn’t the only player joining the Philadelphia Eagles this week. The team is signing veteran defensive back Kenny Moore II, on what is reported to be a one-year deal worth up to $3 million. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that the plan is for Moore to play safety and nickel corner in Philadelphia. […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 24: Kenny Moore II #23 of the Indianapolis Colts in action against the Philadelphia Eagles during the preseason game at Lincoln Financial Field on August 24, 2023 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Colts defeated the Eagles 27-13. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Zach Ertz isn’t the only player joining the Philadelphia Eagles this week. The team is signing veteran defensive back Kenny Moore II, on what is reported to be a one-year deal worth up to $3 million. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that the plan is for Moore to play safety and nickel corner in Philadelphia. The 31-year-old defender brings nine years of experience, all with the Colts, and will add some depth to a group that has already dealt with injuries. His presence gives the Eagles more flexibility in their secondary. The Colts waived Moore shortly after the 2026 NFL Draft, and he spent the offseason looking for a new place to land. Here’s a look at Kenny Moore’s career snaps by position, per @PFF Slot corner: 4,804 snaps (62.1%) Wide corner: 1,634 snaps (21.1%) Box: 944 snaps (12.2%) D-line: 298 snaps (3.9%) Free safety: 58 snaps (0.7%) — Dave Zangaro (@DZangaroNBCS) September 22, 2026 The Pro Bowler’s career includes 649 total tackles, 68 passes defended, 21 interceptions, 20 QB hits, 11.5 sacks, and six forced fumbles. With Reed Blankenship leaving for Houston this offseason, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has played Cooper DeJean at safety in their base packages. Moore will add another option as the defense looks to tighten things up after two close games to open the season. BLG’s quick thoughts: Moore reunites with Nick Sirianni, who he overlapped with in Indy from 2018-2020. Moore also overlapped with current Eagles secondary coach Mike Pellegrino on the New England Patriots in 2017 when Moore was an undrafted rookie free agent in training camp. Interested to see how the Eagles handle their secondary configuration. With Marcus Epps struggling, could they move Cooper DeJean to safety full-time and play Kenny Moore II at nickel cornerback? Guessing that’s not the first choice. But Moore lacks safety experience, so, it’s not like it’s a no-brainer to put him on the back end. We’ll see. There are some conflicting reports about whether Moore is signing to the roster or the practice squad. Ditto for Zach Ertz. Waiting for more clarity.

title: NFL Power Rankings: Week 3 Edition
summary: Now that Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles and Saquon Barkley #26 warm up prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. (Note: Ran out of time to publish my Week 2 power rankings ahead of Thursday’s game last week. Sorry about that, my schedule was pretty hectic.) BLG’S WEEK 3 NFL POWER RANKINGS 1 – Seattle Seahawks (Last Week: 1) – The reigning Super Bowl champs have allowed the second-fewest points of any team in the NFL, just one point behind the NFL lead. Seattle’s defense is still a force to be reckoned with. And Drew Lock looked pretty good in Week 2, albeit against one of the NFL’s worst teams. 2 – Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 2) – It was a narrow overtime win for the Chiefs but it’s very clear that they’re in a much healthier spot than they were last year. The Pat Mahones and Andy Reid combo still make this team very dangerous. 3 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 3) – With nine total touchdowns and zero giveaways through two wins, Josh Allen is currently the betting favorite to win MVP. His odds are listed at +250 while the next closest player is Mahomes at +750. 4 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 6) – The Niners lead the NFL in DVOA and point differential after two games. With the Cardinals up next, a 3-0 start is certainly within reach. Seems like San Fran is back to being one of the top threats in the NFC. 5 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 7) – Aided by Jaxson Dart’s injury, the Rams bounced back from their Week 1 loss. They needed that since it seems like things were trending in a bad direction with the combination of losing to SF and Myles Garrett landing on injured reserve. Stabilized. 6 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 4) – The Ravens entered Week 2 as 8.5-point home favorites. They entered the fourth quarter on Sunday with an eight-point lead. They lost the game by seven. 7 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 10) – Jalen Hurts is the Eagles’ MVP through two games. But the offense needs to figure out their early down struggles so that they don’t have to keep relying on him to bail them out on third-and-long. Could be good if they decided to stop running into a wall on first and second downs. Let Jalen Cook! 8 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 11) – Seems like the Bengals have finally figured some things out on defense? Only seven teams have allowed fewer points through two games. If that unit holds up, they’ll be seriously competing for the AFC North crown. 9 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 16) – Brian Flores is on his way to getting a second chance as a head coach. Even with Caleb Williams getting hurt, it’s impressive to see the Vikings held Chicago to just three points … one week after the Bears dropped 59. 10 – Chicago Bears (LW: 5) – Ben Johnson described Caleb Williams as “week-to-week” with a hamstring injury, so, it seems like he’s going to miss some time. The Bears seem to be optimistic about Tyson Bagent, who hasn’t started a game since 2023. We’ll soon see if that confidence is misguided or not. Big test for the Bears with the Eagles coming to Chicago on Monday night. 11 – New England Patriots (LW: 12) – The Pats have allowed the fewest points in the NFL through two games. That’s the good news. The bad news is that only four teams have scored fewer points. And A.J. Brown still has to miss at least three more games. 12 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 13) – Dak Prescott looked pretty good against Washington. The Dallas defense did not. The Cowboys actually got outgained by 57 yards and lost the time of possession battle despite the fact that the Commanders lost their starting quarterback in this game. The Cowboys won by 17 points but the game was effectively closer than the final score looked. 13 – Houston Texans (LW: 8) – The Texans are 0-2 after getting some Super Bowl hype leading up to the season. With games against the Bills and Bengals, it’s not like they’ve had an easy schedule … but they had home field advantage in both matchups. And they only mustered six points against Cincy. 14 – Detroit Lions (LW: 9) – The Lions’ defense is atrocious. They desperately need to get healthy on that side of the ball. If they can, there’s still hope for this team since the offense can put up points. 15 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 17) – Looking like Kellen Moore might be a good head coach. Tyler Shough leads the NFL in passing yards after two games. The Saints can’t be slept on after nearly stealing a win in Detroit and then being the Ravens in Baltimore. 16 – Denver Broncos (LW: 15) – Bo Nix had 14 giveaways last year. He’s already up to 21.4% of that total through two games this season. 17 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 14) – The Jags have the makings of a middle of the pack team that holds little league-wide relevance. But they’re not in a bad spot to win the AFC South considering all of their division rivals are off to 0-2 starts. 18 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 23) – The Raiders are 2-0 for the first time since 2021! Aren’t you surprised it was that recent? Kind of fun to see them not be a total doormat. Nice to see Nakobe Dean playing well for his new team. 19 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 20) – Green Bay needed a 10-point fourth quarter comeback to force overtime and beat the Jets, a team that nearly outgained them by 100 yards. Not exactly a feel good win. 20 – New York Giants (LW: 18) – Oof. The G-Men followed up an exciting Week 1 win with a blowout loss in primetime. While Jaxson Dart’s status looms largest, New York also suffered some other key injuries on Monday night. We’ll see if they can navigate a relatively easy schedule coming up. 21 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 19) – Lol: this is incredible at first he seems like he’s taking accountability: “we need to be better, and it starts with me…” But then??? what do you need to be better at? “…at making sure the coaches know what’s not working so they call better plays” 💀💀 pic.twitter.com/nE9OSxDvIW — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) September 21, 2026 22 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 26) – Don’t look now but Bryce Young ranks sixth in passer rating (113.3) after two games. 23 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 21) – The Bucs shouldn’t have paid Baker Mayfield. Losing to the Browns is very unserious behavior. 24 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 25) – Shane Steichen opting for a field goal instead of going for the win in overtime had to be frustrating for Colts fans. You’re trusting your defense to prevent Pat Mahomes from getting a field goal? Really? With the Texans up next, either Houston or Indy will be in an 0-3 hole to start the season. Do or die. 25 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 22) – You wonder if Mike McDaniel is having second thoughts about deciding to join the Bolts. 26 – Washington Commanders (LW: 24) – The Commanders are the first team to two division losses. With Jayden Daniels injured and a game against the Seahawks up next, they’re staring an 0-3 start in the face. Dan Quinn’s seat is getting very warm very fast. 27 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 27) – Week 1 was a cute moment but Week 2 revealed who the Cardinals are truly going to be more often than not this year. 28 – New York Jets (LW: 29) – While playing at home, they blew a lead to an uninspiring Packers team. Will be interesting to see how they fare against the Lions in Week 3. 29 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 30) – The Titans had nothing to feel good about after losing to the Jets in Week 1. Week 2 offered a moral victory since they nearly beat the Eagles. Cam Ward had one of the better games of his career against Vic Fangio. Maybe there’s some hope for him? 30 – Cleveland Browns (32) – The Browns beating the Bucs only delayed Deshaun…

summary: The Eagles won 24-20, and I came away feeling much better about the passing game than I did after Week 1. The Eagles found answers against the Titans’ coverage, attacked the weaknesses I flagged in my preview (which is always great to see), and repeatedly converted third-and-long. However, the offense cannot keep making life this […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Tank Bigsby #8 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Tennessee Titans with Jalen Hurts #1 during the first quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles won 24-20, and I came away feeling much better about the passing game than I did after Week 1. The Eagles found answers against the Titans’ coverage, attacked the weaknesses I flagged in my preview (which is always great to see), and repeatedly converted third-and-long. However, the offense cannot keep making life this difficult for itself. The Eagles went 11-of-18 on third down, which is an absurd 61.1% conversion rate. That’s why they sustained drives despite averaging only 4.7 yards per play, turning the ball over twice and rushing for 89 yards on 32 attempts. Winning on third down is obviously good. Needing Hurts to repeatedly deliver elite throws on third-and-long isn’t a sustainable offensive identity. The early-down numbers are wild. I mean, come on… The Philadelphia Eagles have the largest difference in early down offensive success rate vs. late down offensive success rate to start a season since 2022, per @SumerSports Early downs: 31.5% (3rd percentile) Late downs: 60.6% (96th percentile) — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) September 20, 2026 The contrast between the pass and run games could not have been clearer. The Eagles produced +0.17 EPA per passing play but -0.20 EPA per rushing play. This was not a perfect offensive performance. But the passing game looked excellent for long stretches. Jalen Hurts and DeVonta Smith were elite. Now Sean Mannion and the rest of the offensive staff must find a way to stop wasting early downs before asking them to rescue the offense. Offense This opening play might be the most Eagles run of all time. The offense comes out in 12 personnel, condenses the formation and invites the Titans to load the box. There is no numbers advantage, no misdirection and no obvious way to manipulate the second level. The Eagles simply run straight into it. What could possibly go wrong? Pretty much everything. Johnny Mundt goes to the ground in hilarious fashion, Dallas Goedert is asked to climb to a linebacker he has little chance of reaching, and the combination between Tyler Steen and Drew Kendall is messy. Because the interior double-team never develops properly, Cam Jurgens cannot work up to the linebacker. Lane Johnson then runs into the traffic created inside and cannot generate movement on his block. It is a calamity of errors, but the design makes every error more likely because the defense can attack downhill immediately. I refuse to post 20 versions of the same failed run, because you all watched the game. The more important question is why this keeps happening. The Eagles ran 79.2% of their offensive snaps from 11 personnel and only 19.4% from 12 personnel. I think that needs to change. Long one. Eagles' Offense All22 Thread vs. Titans. 1) The Eagles start off the game, in the most Eagles way imaginable. I laughed out loud of this. 2 TE, stacked box, failed run. Who saw that coming? Mundt falls over and gets destroyed (in quite amusing fashion). They are… pic.twitter.com/c9T67bccVH — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 21, 2026 I am ready to set fire to the swing-pass section of the playbook. This is not just about one bad play. The whole operation looks slow. Hurts does not have the quickest release on these throws, and the ball often reaches the receiver when he is flat-footed or moving sideways rather than already attacking upfield. That delay gives zone defenders, who are facing the play, plenty of time to trigger and rally to the football. Most modern defenses are playing zone these days, so this look is common Perimeter blocking doesn’t save the concept either. Dallas Goedert is blown up by a cornerback here, and the play has nowhere to go. The Eagles do not currently have a group of dominant perimeter blockers who can consistently turn these throws into efficient gains. They also lost five yards on the swing to Makai Lemon immediately before Hurts’ second interception, transforming second-and-7 into another third-and-12. Screens and swings can be useful answers against pressure or aggressive fronts, but this version threatens no one. Burn it. At least until the Eagles can change the timing, blocking angles, or presentation enough to make it functional. 2) A lot of talk about why the Eagles swing/screen game sucks so much. Lots of the reasons on show here. Hurts doesn't have a particularly quick release, and it takes too long to get it out. The receiver catching the ball often isn't running upfield, which slows him down. And… pic.twitter.com/i0HvBwhw82 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 21, 2026 Now for the fun part. The Eagles loved dagger in this game, and it gave Hurts a clean answer against the Titans’ zone coverage. Marquise Brown runs the vertical clear-out with real intent, forcing the deep coverage to honor his speed, while Dontayvion Wicks pushes his intermediate route beyond the linebackers and settles in the void. That route depth is really good. The linebackers sit around the sticks on third-and-12, so a shallow in-breaker runs directly into them and leaves Wicks short of the line to gain. By getting vertical first, he creates space behind the second level. The offensive line gives Hurts time, and he hits the top of his drop and layers a perfect throw into the middle of the field. The touch is outstanding. Brown deserves credit too. He did not play in Week 1, but he ran these clear-out routes hard and looked fast. Very fast! He also carried the ball twice for 12 yards. I am not demanding he suddenly becomes a featured player, but speed changes the defense even when the ball doesn’t come his way. I would like to see more of him. Is that crazy to say? 3) One of many Jalen Hurts' dimes on 3rd and long. The Eagles loved running Dagger in this game, and shoutout to Hollywood Brown who looked fast as hell on these clear-out routes. For someone who didn't play last week, he ran these hard. The Eagles' OL does a fantastic job, and… pic.twitter.com/cq4xQq6MHm — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 21, 2026 The first interception is a mistake by Hurts, but it is also a fantastic play by Amani Hooker. Both things can be true. The Eagles are trying to isolate Smith by having Goedert pull the middle safety away, and Lemon occupy the flat defender. They create a window, but it never becomes as clean as Hurts appears to expect. Goedert does not remove the safety far enough with a pretty poor route, Smith’s route could be sharper, and Hooker recognizes the concept and drives on the throw brilliantly. Hurts is slightly late and should turn it down. In the red zone, especially, he cannot give the safety this opportunity. It was an enormously costly decision, but I can somewhat understand why he made the throw based on the pre-snap look. What I loved was the response. Hurts did not become conservative or hesitant after the interception. He continued attacking tight windows, trusted what he saw, and played aggressively. Quarterbacks will make mistakes. The good ones don’t let one mistake ruin everything that follows. 4) A rare Hurts INT in the red zone, but it's also a fantastic play by Amani Hooker. Credit where credit is due. The Eagles are trying to create space for the throw to DeVonta Smith by using Goedert to draw the middle safety away, and Lemon to draw the flat CB away. It works… pic.twitter.com/QsxJrTZNU4 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 21, 2026 Look at what happens when the Eagles spread the defense out and run away from the strength of the box. This outside zone rep is not revolutionary, but it gives the blockers a chance. The motion forces the Titans to flow in the opposite direction, and Goedert becomes eye candy rather than being asked to execute another difficult block. Steen…

title: Rookie special teamer earns praise from Steelers coach
summary: Seventh-round rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings has just one NFL defensive snap under his belt so far in the 2026 season. However, he already has seven tackles. One of the Steelers’ final selections in a 10-man draft class this spring, Spears-Jennings has made an immediate impact on special teams through the first two weeks of the […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 21: Robert Spears-Jennings #28 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action during the game against the New York Jets at Acrisure Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Seventh-round rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings has just one NFL defensive snap under his belt so far in the 2026 season. However, he already has seven tackles. One of the Steelers’ final selections in a 10-man draft class this spring, Spears-Jennings has made an immediate impact on special teams through the first two weeks of the regular season. His seven tackles in that phase of the game are the most in the NFL so far — no other player has more than five. Robert Spears-Jennings Week 2 Special Teams Supercut. Four more special tackles, now leads the league with 7. Plus a couple other impressive plays. 📈📈📈 #Steelers https://t.co/GsBICkjR5u pic.twitter.com/qq7IGX1ASa — Ross McCorkle (@Ross_McCorkle) September 22, 2026 A 6’2, 205-pound safety who ran a blazing 4.32-second 40-yard dash at the 2026 NFL Combine, Spears-Jennings’ athleticism and effort have made him a productive player when it comes to wrangling NFL returners. That hasn’t gone unnoticed by Steelers special teams coach Danny Crossman. Speaking to the media Monday, Crossman praised the Oklahoma product’s contributions. “I think obviously the scouting department and the coaches did a great job of identifying (Spears-Jennings), and more importantly, he came in with a great mindset,” Crossman said. “He came with the mindset of, whatever his role was going to be, he was going to buy in, and he was going to try to be an exceptional player at whatever we asked him to do.” Crossman highlighted how the rookie’s effort has stood out even though he hasn’t seen much time on defense. “(Spears-Jennings) is finding ways to make plays a lot of ways,” Crossman said. “He’s (at the) point of attack, making plays. He’s (redirecting), making plays. He’s getting off the ground after he gets knocked off of a tackle and still getting involved in a play. Really happy with where he is, and hopefully just keep developing him. And we think we got a good player right there.” Crossman was also asked about the special teams contributions of the Steelers’ final pick in the 2026 draft, running back Eli Heidenreich, who has also seen some work as a returner. The coach said that Heidenreich hasn’t provided the same “instant gratification and instant results” as Spears-Jennings, but has still done a good job so far. “(Heidenreich) did a good job blocking and had an opportunity with the ball in his hand and did a nice job finding the seam and getting it creased,” Crossman said. Heidenreich had a 26-yard kick return on Sunday against the Patriots. “Maybe a little bit more vertical, but both those young guys, we think they’re good players, just like a lot of these guys.”

The Steelers prepare for their most difficult task yet, facing the 2-0 Bengals with an improved defense and healthy Joe Burrow in the first divisional game of the year. title: Steelers Week 2 grades in loss to Patriots
summary: Week 2 was one of the rougher watches in recent memory for the Pittsburgh Steelers. They totaled just 235 yards, 75 of which came when the game was already out of reach late in the fourth quarter. How did they grade as a team? Let’s dive in. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers isn’t in […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - SEPTEMBER 20: Germie Bernard #17 of the Pittsburgh Steelers lines up wide during a game between the New England Patriots and the Pittsburgh Steelers on September 20, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Week 2 was one of the rougher watches in recent memory for the Pittsburgh Steelers. They totaled just 235 yards, 75 of which came when the game was already out of reach late in the fourth quarter. How did they grade as a team? Let’s dive in. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers isn’t in the most ideal of situations, as his offensive line was brutal in Week 2, and his top target has more notable drops than receptions this season. This isn’t to say that if he was behind the Broncos’ offensive line he would be perfect, but he’d likely put up better showings. That said, he is 31st in EPA per play, and his success rate when pressured sits at just 24th. He can’t do it himself, but that doesn’t mean he’s been good, either. Grade: C- Joey Bray: ​Listen, I am well aware that Rodgers has been let down by his receivers and offensive line consistently throughout these first two games. However, that doesn’t excuse how lackluster Rodgers was yesterday. The veteran quarterback’s -42.12 EPA through two weeks is the worst mark of any quarterback in the NFL . The fact is, nothing about the Pittsburgh offense is watchable right now. Rodgers is not even close to the biggest issue on the offense, but he certainly didn’t help them yesterday. Grade: D ​Offensive Line ​ Jarrett Bailey: I touched on the poor offensive line play on Monday. Spencer Anderson allowed seven pressures – no other right guard allowed more than four. Dylan Cook has been dreadful through two games, as well. Max Iheanachor and Brock Hoffman/Gennings Dunker should get starting nods in Week 3. If Dunker doesn’t start, he should at least get a helmet over Anderson. Maybe that will lead to an actual run game being developed and more time for Rodgers to get through more than one read before running for his life. Grade: F Joey Bray: Nothing about the Steelers offensive line looked good in Week 2. The right side of the offensive line needs wholesale changes at the very least. Dylan Cook has been given two starts after an abysmal preseason and has shown no signs of growth. Pittsburgh has their first-round pick in Max Iheanachor just waiting on the bench for an opportunity. Spencer Anderson allowed seven pressures against the Patriots. It was not a good showing for anyone on the line, as Zach Frazier and Troy Fautanu did not look particularly great either. The offensive line needs some new faces on the right side before we can start to feel any kind of confidence in them. Grade: F ​WR DK Metcalf ​ Jarrett Bailey: It’s just sad at this point, man. Eight catches for 67 yards through two games while making $33 million per year. Should 2026 be another disappointment as a whole, the Steelers need to eat the $36 million dead cap hit in 2027 and move on from Metcalf. Right now, he’s that bad. Grade: F Joey Bray: I would probably write something about how Metcalf needs to be benched if the options behind him weren’t just as bad. Metcalf has been targeted 19 times this season and has managed just eight receptions for 67 yards. Rodgers has a 29.9 passer rating when targeting his top receiver. Many things need to change with this offense, and one of them needs to be how many targets Metcalf is getting. Until he proves that he can hold onto the ball consistently, it is in the best interest of the Steelers to continue to involve their rookie wideout Germie Bernard, and continue to expand Michael Pittman Jr.’s role when he returns. Grade: F ​WR Germie Bernard ​ Jarrett Bailey: It was refreshing to see Bernard get targeted early and often. He caught three of his four passes on one drive, including a 19-yard pass on 3rd-and-8. He did have a pass bounce off his chest for an interception late in the fourth quarter, but the game was decided at that point. The arrow is pointing up for the rookie, and hopefully this is a sign that he’ll be a growing part of the offense. Grade: B Joey Bray: The statline of four catches for 35 yards doesn’t exactly jump off the page, but Bernard paced the Steelers’ passing attack in Week 2. The toughness and ability after the catch were apparent in the 8 targets the rookie got in the contest. It is in the best interest of the offense moving forward that Bernard is continually more involved in the passing attack. The second-round pick has all of the tools to emerge as a serious threat in the Steelers’ passing attack that they need desperately. Grade: A ​Defense ​ Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers’ defense has been terrific through two weeks, and played up to par against the Patriots. New England’s offense scored just 13 points and the Steelers forced two turnovers while sacking Drake Maye three times. Yes, there were a pair of chunk plays, but those are going to happen to just about every defense when you play a quality offense. The pass rush has been great, and the secondary has done perfectly fine without Joey Porter Jr. As it currently stands, Pittsburgh leads the NFL in defensive EPA per play. Grade: A Joey Bray: Overall, it’s hard to be too upset with the Steelers defense after Week 2. The unit held the Patriots offense to 13 points and really kept Pittsburgh within striking distance for much of the first three quarters. The edge rushers continue to dominate, as TJ Watt, Alex Highsmith, Nick Herbig, and Jack Sawyer all hand their fingerprints all over this game. I am slightly concerned with how this secondary could potentially look without Joey Porter Jr. in Week 3 after giving up several downfield chunk plays in this contest. I continue to be impressed with the play of Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen through two contests, as the two both are showing improvement through two contests. Grade: B Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Seahawks Week 3 power rankings: Seahawks stay atop the mountain thanks to Drew Lock
summary: Entering Week 2, the national media was very high on the Seattle Seahawks, even despite them losing starting quarterback Sam Darnold to a glute injury. Now, after handily defeating the Arizona Cardinals, one would expect the national media to remain high on Seattle. Or will the victories of other Super Bowl contending teams (like the […]
full_text: Entering Week 2, the national media was very high on the Seattle Seahawks , even despite them losing starting quarterback Sam Darnold to a glute injury. Now, after handily defeating the Arizona Cardinals, one would expect the national media to remain high on Seattle. Or will the victories of other Super Bowl contending teams (like the Buffalo Bills or Los Angeles Rams) potentially knock the Seahawks off a peg? Let’s take a look at five national media sites (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (BR), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where they rank Seattle. Starting with ESPN, the only site (of these five) who don’t have Seattle ranked at number one. ESPN ranks Seattle the second best team in the NFL , the same ranking as last week. In their ranking ESPN credits Drew Lock as “one of the NFL’s best backup QBs.” ESPN further notes that since stepping in for an injured Darnold, Lock has “completed almost 73% of his passes, with four touchdowns, zero turnovers, and only two sacks.” Additionally, Lock’s total QBR of 86.4 currently ranks fourth best in the league. The only team ranked above the Seahawks for ESPN? The Buffalo Bills. CBS Sports and PFT both also credit Lock’s performance as they keep the Seahawks ranked as the number one team in the NFL. CBS Sports notes that a good team is one that can “go on the road and win with a backup quarterback. ” Just as Seattle did last week in Arizona. PFT meanwhile summed up the Seahawks performance with a simple “ No Darnold? No problem .” NFL.com , who also kept Seattle ranked as first, noted that Lock’s impressive performance should allow Seahawk fans to worry less about the absence of Darnold . B/R, who also have Seattle ranked as the number one team in the NFL, also noted that Lock’s performance should allow the team to not feel rushed to get Darnold back to the field . As you have probably noticed, the power rankings – and the reasoning behind their rankings are all pretty cut and paste from all of the polled national media sites. That can be the case when your team is not only the Super Bowl defending champion, but also one of the favorites to win the next Super Bowl. In these moments, power rankings can become very static. As is the case this week. All five of the above national media sites kept the Seahawks at the same ranking as last week. Entering week two, the average power ranking between the five polled sites was 1.2. Entering Week 3, the same 1.2 average remains. However, this is still the NFL. And despite being an overwhelming top ranked team by the national media, the Seahawks are only one loss (or even one poor performance) away from slipping down these rankings once again. Their next test comes against the Washington Commanders – quarterbacked by Marcus Mariota .

title: Seahawks bring 2 wide receivers in for tryouts, host running back for a visit
summary: The Seattle Seahawks had a few undrafted players come in for visits and/or tryouts ahead of their Wednesday practice for Week 3 against the Washington Commanders. full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - JUNE 1: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Eli Pancol (83) runs through a drill during the Indianapolis Colts OTA on June 1, 2026 at the Indiana Farm Bureau Football Center in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks had a few undrafted players come in for visits and/or tryouts ahead of their Wednesday practice for Week 3 against the Washington Commanders. According to the official NFL transaction wire, the Seahawks held tryouts for wide receivers Malick Meiga and Eli Pancol. They also had running back Dontae McMillan in for a visit, which has a different distinction because it doesn’t always mean a tryout. Meiga started his college career at Penn State before transferring to Coastal Carolina, and he only had 35 career catches over five total seasons. He stayed local and signed with the Carolina Panthers during the offseason, but did not make the roster. Pancol was a former teammate of Jake Bobo at Duke, spending six seasons in Durham with the Blue Devils. His final season saw him catch 60 passes for 798 yards and 9 touchdowns. Pancol had brief stints with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Indianapolis Colts last season. McMillan barely carried the ball at Eastern Michigan his first two seasons, then broke out for over 1,000 yards on just 177 carries in 2025, to go along with 33 catches for 375 yards. His most recent team was the Baltimore Ravens. It’s hard to imagine any of these players going directly to the active roster, so keep an eye for any practice squad changes ahead of Wednesday afternoon.

title: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered ‘severe’ knee injury, likely to miss Seahawks game
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are set to face the Washington Commanders on Sunday, who will be without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels (dislocated elbow) and they may see another backup later in the season when they take on the New York Giants. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garofolo, further testing revealed the knee injury […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are set to face the Washington Commanders on Sunday, who will be without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels (dislocated elbow) and they may see another backup later in the season when they take on the New York Giants. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garofolo, further testing revealed the knee injury New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered in the teams 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night is worse than originally anticipated and he could possibly undergo season-ending surgery. Even if not, the Giants signal caller will be sidelined an extended period of time. While speaking with the media on Tuesday, head coach John Harbaugh said “evaluations are ongoing” and the team hasn’t made any final decisions yet. Dart was injured on the opening drive of the game after he took a hard hit from defensive end Byron Young and collided with linebacker Josaiah Stewart. The second-year quarterback was taken to the locker room and did not return. An MRI on #Giants QB Jaxson Dart revealed a knee injury more severe than anticipated, sources tell me and @RapSheet . He’s out an extended period of time, possibly the season. pic.twitter.com/sQO7jBAJ9W — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) September 22, 2026 It’s a brutal blow for a Giants team that appeared to be on the rise after their 28-20 upset win over the division rival Dallas Cowboys in Week 1, where Dart threw for a near perfect 230 yards and three touchdowns to go alongside 54 yards on the ground. Given Harbaugh’s comments, it’s unclear whether his injury will play a factor for their Week 13 road game against Seattle, especially considering it doesn’t come until Dec. 13. However, the Seahawks will be coming off a shortened week as they’re poised to face Dallas on Monday Night Football, meaning they’ll only have six days before taking the field against New York. On top of playing one of the league’s best at home, having their starting quarterback would certainly be a significant boost for the Giants, who are seeking their first playoff berth since 2022. Should he be unable to suit up, veteran Jameis Winston would presumably continue to handle duties under center. Although, he looked rusty while filling in on Monday, when he threw for 111 yards and an interception. New York also has Jake Haener on their practice squad. The Giants are seeking their second consecutive win against Seattle after emerging on top 29-20 the last time the two teams squared off on Nov. 6, 2024, but Dart’s health could possibly be a deciding factor.

title: Mike Macdonald reveals Sean Payton cheating accusation that led to Seahawks lawsuit threat
summary: A primetime clash between the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos next month just got a little spicier. […]
full_text: A primetime clash between the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos next month just got a little spicier. In an interview on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , widely circulated on Twitter on Tuesday morning, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald shared a story about an issue Sean Payton took with the team’s preparation ahead of a 2024 meeting. Macdonald told Bensinger that ahead of Seattle’s season-opener, and his coaching debut, against the Denver Broncos in 2024, the team took around 100 plays from Denver’s training camp that had been shared by fans on Twitter and scouted them. Mike MacDonald talking about a "behind the scenes cold war" between Sean Peyton's Broncos and Mike's Seahawks. It was over the use Twitter videos of the Broncos training camp reps by the Seahawks prior to their week 1 matchup in 2024. ( video from @GrahamBensinger ) pic.twitter.com/cRyX7WnZQt — Nikko👾 (@LegionBoomerTN) September 22, 2026 According to Macdonald, the still-yet-to-be good natured Payton took issue with this, and called general manager John Schneider to equate it to the New England Patriots’ SpyGate scandal, as well as to threaten to go public with it. In turn, Macdonald, Schneider, and the Seahawks had to respond saying they would take legal action if he made a false claim like that publicly. “He basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriot, like Spygate type of thing,” Macdonald said. “And I’m sitting there thinking, ‘Oh my God, we didn’t cheat.’ He thought it was a Michigan thing, or we had a plant and the whole thing. “So we had to counter with him to say, ‘Hey, look, if you come out with this, we’re going to sue you, because it’s not true.’ “He backed down, but he was killing John, our GM,” Macdonald added. In the end, Payton backed down and, per Macdonald, was perfectly courteous when the two ran into one another in Indianapolis the following spring at the NFL Scouting Combine. The Seahawks and Broncos meet in Week 6 on Thursday Night Football in Denver.

title: Should the 49ers be active ahead of the trade deadline?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in 49ers fans and fans across the country. The San Francisco 49ers are turning over every leaf in an effort to keep the roster competitive as they battle attrition. After a slew of injuries […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in 49ers fans and fans across the country. The San Francisco 49ers are turning over every leaf in an effort to keep the roster competitive as they battle attrition. After a slew of injuries at wide receiver, the latest move was to add veteran Brandin Cooks, who most recently played for the Buffalo Bills and New Orleans Saints in 2025. Cooks was signed to the practice squad . If Cooks is active while Demarcus Robinson is out, that is probably not a great sign for Jordan Watkins, who was inactive in the first two weeks of the season behind KhaDarel Hodge, a player the team signed in August. Kyle Shanahan is hopeful Christian Kirk can return to practice next week, but there are no guarantees. Until Robinson and Kirk return, the 49ers will likely lean on Hodge, Jacob Cowing, and Cooks. Realistically, that likely means more Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, and Mike Evans. Should the Niners be active at the deadline? Wide receiver isn’t the only position the 49ers are leaky at. Defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. also has a high-ankle sprain . Surprisingly, the 49ers didn’t work out any defensive tackles this week before they return to practice. That means they are going to roll with the bodies they have on the roster. Keion White might need to play more. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris could also lean into more 5-man fronts, where Jaden Dugger sees more snaps. Morris has his work cut out for him for at least a couple of more weeks, until Mykel Williams is eligible to return. Williams will solve quite a few of the Niners’ problems, but it’s unfair to expect him to hit the ground running after a serious season-ending knee injury. Not every athlete will return like they never left, as Nick Bosa has. That led us to our weekly survey question: Do the Niners need to make a move ahead of the deadline to stay competitive? Are you feeling confident in the Niners? Despite the injuries, the 49ers are 2-0 and look like one of the teams to beat to begin the season. What is your confidence level in the team through two weeks? title: 49ers sign veteran WR with nearly 10,000 career receiving yards
summary: After multiple injuries at the position, the San Francisco 49ers are signing veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks to their practice squad, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Cooks, who turns 33 on September 25th, is coming off a season where he played 15 games, spending time with both the New Orleans Saints and Buffalo Bills. Across […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 17: Brandin Cooks #18 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates during an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After multiple injuries at the position, the San Francisco 49ers are signing veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks to their practice squad, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Cooks, who turns 33 on September 25th, is coming off a season where he played 15 games, spending time with both the New Orleans Saints and Buffalo Bills. Across both teams, he caught 24 passes for 279 yards. Cooks ended up playing a considerable amount for the Bills in the playoffs, seeing action in both games, while catching five passes for 78 yards. Over his 12-year NFL career, Cooks has posted 734 catches for 9,811 yards and 60 touchdowns, which includes six seasons with over 1,000 receiving yards. He has spent time with the Saints, Bills, Houston Texans, Los Angeles Rams, Dallas Cowboys, and New England Patriots. Schefter reported that Cooks will get up to speed on the practice squad, but the 49ers could need him sooner than later after injuries to De’Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson at the outside receiver spot. Khadarel Hodge and Jacob Cowing ended up playing 20 and 24 snaps, respectively, against the Miami Dolphins as a result. The 49ers have been beaten up at receiver this offseason, with Ricky Pearsall out for the year. Now, Stribling and Robinson are expected to miss an extended period of time, and head coach Kyle Shanahan indicated the team would try out some players at the position ahead of Week 3. Well, the team is now signing Cooks, who will join his seventh career team as he enters his 13th year in the NFL
