title: Sean McVay admits travel mistake, takes blame for Week 1 approach
summary: There was a ton of discourse ahead of the Week 1 matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams about travel logistics, as both teams elected to take a different approach with the trip to Australia. Consulting their respective experts, the 49ers elected to fly into Australia a week early, allowing them […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was a ton of discourse ahead of the Week 1 matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams about travel logistics, as both teams elected to take a different approach with the trip to Australia. Consulting their respective experts, the 49ers elected to fly into Australia a week early, allowing them to get acclimated to the time change, while the Rams chose to go with their in-season approach from last year, flying in the day before and operating on Pacific time. There was a lot of controversy on which option was the best, and that was seemingly proven in Week 1, when the 49ers beat the Rams 27-7 for the upset. It was a game where the Rams looked flat, while San Francisco kept their foot on the gas in the second half to pull away for a key divisional victory. Los Angeles looked much better on Monday night in a 28-6 beatdown of the New York Giants, despite not having Puka Nacua. Following the game, head coach Sean McVay admitted his mistake and took the blame for the team’s travel decision in Week 1. “Sometimes you win and sometimes you learn, and sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel decisions that put you in a bad spot,” McVay chuckled as he left the podium. The Rams had done a similar approach in past international games and had seen success. But the difference was that this one was to begin the season, giving both teams ample time to adjust and return home to re-adjust. And Los Angeles’s choice backfired. Wide receiver Davante Adams acknowledged on The Up & Adams Show that the 49ers were more rested and locked in than the Rams during that Week 1 game. “The Niners went out there and played better football than us,” Adams said. “They were more ready & locked in that game. So, that’s what I attribute [the loss] to… I kind of just want to put it behind me altogether. That’s the kind of guy that Sean [McVay] is. He’s going to make some fun of a not-so-great situation with last week.” Both McVay and Kyle Shanahan have expressed their displeasure about the long travel and logistics of playing in Australia, with the Rams head coach even hoping they wouldn’t have to play in Australia again. Nonetheless, both teams have moved forward, securing wins in Week 2. It’ll be quite a while before the two sides see each other again, as the 49ers and Rams play next in Week 14, but currently: advantage, 49ers.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: The 49ers need to improve in one key area
summary: Over two weeks, the San Francisco 49ers have exceeded expectations, securing blowout wins over the Los Angeles Rams and Miami Dolphins to start the season 2-0. Their offense has looked on point, while their defense has allowed just 20 points through two games. Despite some of the injuries, the 49ers have been humming, and they […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over two weeks, the San Francisco 49ers have exceeded expectations, securing blowout wins over the Los Angeles Rams and Miami Dolphins to start the season 2-0. Their offense has looked on point, while their defense has allowed just 20 points through two games. Despite some of the injuries, the 49ers have been humming, and they get the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3 as they look to continue their strong start to the season. When you look at the numbers, San Francisco has done quite well across the board. They’re fourth in points per game (31.0), eighth in yards per game (380.5), and tenth in yards allowed per game (287.0). They’ve also maintained their excellence on third downs, converting at over a 63 percent rate so far, which ranks second in the NFL. So, they’ve done well with their new personnel on both sides of the ball. However, when you dive deeper into the numbers, there is one area that stands out for improvement. Currently, the 49ers are 17th in rushing yards allowed per game (112.0), but they’re 13th in yards allowed per attempt (3.9). Both of those numbers aren’t concerning. But when you look at the games, the 49ers did seem to struggle with the run against both the Rams and the Dolphins in the first halves. And the numbers back that up. The 49ers currently rank 13th in rush EPA allowed per play (-0.177). However, they rank 27th in success rate allowed (46.4 percent). When you specifically look at the first half, the 49ers’ rush EPA allowed per play drops dramatically to 30th in the NFL (0.165). Their rush success rate allowed? Easily the worst in the NFL at 60.6 percent, an ugly number. While the 49ers have been dealing with some injuries on the defensive line, the numbers and the tape both indicate there has been a problem with the team’s run defense, which has been masked by the fact that San Francisco’s offense has just dominated opponents. So far, it hasn’t been a problem. But we saw last year how the 49ers struggled against the run, and the defense is relying on quite a few younger players to fill the void this season. In closer games, that problem could be exemplified further. Now, the 49ers pass defense has been quite good. They rank eighth in dropback EPA allowed per play (-0.071) and third in dropback success rate (37.5 percent). Even when games have been close in the first half, the 49ers are still ninth in dropback EPA allowed per play (-0.122) and fifth in dropback success rate (33.3 percent). So there definitely have been some defensive improvements. But there is a concern that the rush defense could be exposed in closer games where opposing offenses can’t abandon the run in the second half. Reinforcements should join in the coming weeks, although it doesn’t seem like Mykel Williams will return to practice this week. But this could be the main deficiency for the 49ers this season.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers report card: The offense is exceeding expectations because of Brock Purdy
summary: Let’s hand out some San Francisco 49ers positional grades from their 22-point win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 2. It’ll serve as our weekly report card moving forward. Quarterback: A+ When your quarterback is playing well, you’ll always have a chance to win. When your quarterback has the highest EPA per play by .40 […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s hand out some San Francisco 49ers positional grades from their 22-point win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 2. It’ll serve as our weekly report card moving forward. Quarterback: A+ When your quarterback is playing well, you’ll always have a chance to win. When your quarterback has the highest EPA per play by .40 for the week, a success rate that’s 16 percentage points higher than anybody else, was on target on 91% of his throws, avoided free rushers, and managed to use his legs when he needed to to keep the offense on schedule, you have a chance to win by three touchdowns. Running backs: C+ Eh. The running backs weren’t bad, by any stretch. They didn’t have near the volume as they did in Week 1. Christian McCaffrey ran well. Kaelon Black left some yards on the table. Both continue to produce yards after contact. The passing game was so extraordinary that the running game didn’t need to do much. Still, it felt like the Dolphins got the best of the Niners’ ground game. Tight ends: A Luke Farrell didn’t get enough credit for how well he blocked in Week 1. Farrell and George Kittle played the same number of snaps in Week 2. Only one of these players was targeted. It was good to see Kittle still has enough burst to run away from safeties. He stiff-armed the poor rookie safety. Kittle benefited from a couple of coverage busts, but this group blocked well again, and when you can generate multiple explosive passing plays, you’re going to grade out well. With all the questions about how the 49ers will weather the storm with so many wide receivers banged up, the easy answer is to throw the ball to 85 more. Wide receivers: B- It looks like there’s a clear drop-off, at least in terms of responsibilities, from Demarcus Robinson to the next player. Kyle Shanahan will create space for Deebo Samuel underneath, but I don’t know if they trust Deebo as a route runner beyond 10 yards to get open. Deebo also has a case of the dropsies. Mike Evans caught all three of his targets, but two of those were a byproduct of his quarterback. In his role, Robinson has been everything you want from a “Z” receiver. He has a very good feel for the offense. The 49ers are going to miss that. KhaDarel Hodge has the size and experience to fill in for Robinson, but he’s an unknown, just like Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins. With Denver and Seattle on the horizon, somebody is going to have to step up. Offensive line: B- The run blocking was more of a stalemate. There was a mix of good and bad. Trent Williams is amazing and seems to be inventing new techniques. As always, he brings up the grade. It’s rare to see somebody get the best of Williams, but that happened in pass protection. It was somewhat mesmerizing to see Williams off balance on a play. The pressures were low, but Miami won enough times to make Purdy move or at least stand tall in the face of pressure. Overall, the offensive line was good. But probably not good enough for an opponent like the Broncos or Seahawks. Defensive line: B+ Nick Bosa didn’t make our winners list because it’s boring to put him on there every week. Bosa had more pressures than all of the other edge rushers on the roster combined. Romello Height’s sack should have an asterisk next to it since Bosa was the one who made Malik Willis run for his life. Bosa pressured Willis on 27.8% of his dropbacks. Bosa continues to impress as a run defender, though he missed a couple of tackles. Keion White keeps finding ways to be disruptive. The roughing-the-passer call on White was comically bad. He was penalized on third down for tackling. White’s getting the opportunity to play inside, and he’s flashing a couple of times a game. That’s what the 49ers need. CJ West has been this close to making plays two weeks in a row. For whatever reason, he’s missing the tackle at the point of attack. It’s hard to explain. West wins. He’s there. Then the running back slips out of his grasp. Don’t be surprised to see West start finishing those plays. But you can’t ignore the plays where West and James Thompson Jr. get blown off the ball. That’s been consistent two weeks in a row now. It’s why this group didn’t get an A. Osa Odighizuwa competes, but he also gets moved. Odighizuwa makes up for it by pressuring the quarterback, something Thompson and West have not done. The star of this group was Gracen Halton. He saved Ji’Ayir Brown’s tail on the first play of the game. Halton should’ve had a sack on the play, but Willis slipped out of his grasp. Halton had three pressures and three run stops. He was the only defensive tackle in Week 2 to finish in the top ten in both pressure and run-stop percentage. My only complaint is that Halton can’t stay on the field for more than 5 or 6 snaps at a time; it seems. The big fella needs to work on his conditioning. Linebackers: C+ I find it funny whenever a team gets over on Fred Warner. It happens once every few games. Miami caught Warner napping on the first play of the game. There was also a run play or two where I thought Warner could have played better. Honestly, I thought Dugger played the best of the linebackers, all things considered. He isn’t tasked with nearly as much as Warner, but Dugger made multiple plays. Dre Greenlaw had the most tackles of the group. His run stops were due to the scheme and the defensive line. Greenlaw missed a tackle on a screen and gave up a little too much in coverage for my liking. Secondary: B The 49ers secondary allowed 73 yards on 12 targets if you remove the garbage-time touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Upton Stout and Marques Sigle generated pressure. The cornerbacks were stingy in coverage. Ji’Ayir Brown, Sigle, and Lenoir were all good against the run. But you can’t ignore the long touchdown, or Brown on the first play in coverage, or Stout missing a tackle on third down. The short throws that went for first downs on third down, like the throw Lenoir allowed, aren’t a big deal. Special teams: C+ Corliss Waitman only punted twice, which is always a positive. His net was only 43 yards, though. Eddy Pineiro had the day off, outside of PATs. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing didn’t have a big return. Cowing had a long punt return, but it was called back due to a flag. Coaching: A+ Kyle Shanahan toyed with the Dolphins’ inexperience on defense. He drew them up early with underneath throws. As the game progressed, he got more and more aggressive. It was another masterclass of sequencing. Raheem Morris was equally as impressive. A week after only blitzing Matthew Stafford fewer than five times, Morris came after Willis early and often. We’re seeing Morris adapt to his personnel by using dime packages. But he’s also playing his best players, as evidenced by Halton’s snaps. I think for this team specifically, Morris is the perfect coordinator to get the most out of this defense.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers working with ‘good problem to have’ in unexpected area
summary: Among the list of concerns around the 49ers heading into the 2026 season, safety once again ranked highly. It is a position that has been a long-term problem for the 49ers, who have not had a settled and reliable pairing at safety since 2023, when Tashaun Gipson and Talanoa Hufanga manned the two starting spots […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Among the list of concerns around the 49ers heading into the 2026 season, safety once again ranked highly. It is a position that has been a long-term problem for the 49ers, who have not had a settled and reliable pairing at safety since 2023, when Tashaun Gipson and Talanoa Hufanga manned the two starting spots before the latter’s campaign was ended by injury and Ji’Ayir Brown came into the lineup. With Brown’s promising start to his NFL career fading and the former third-round pick experiencing inconsistencies in his performances, the 49ers have found it difficult to find a pairing that works over recent seasons. Their situation at safety has not been helped by Malik Mustapha seeing his initial progress in 2024 checked by injury issues but, two games into the 2026 campaign, it is an area of the roster where the 49ers could claim to have strength in depth. Indeed, both Brown and 2025 fifth-round pick Marques Sigle, who flashed promise as a rookie year before being benched amid struggles in coverage, have impressed as the starting safety pairing. In last Sunday’s win over the Miami Dolphins, Brown had 13 combined tackles and a tackle for loss that helped prevent Miami from cashing in on a trip to the red zone in the first half. Sigle, meanwhile, had nine tackles and the first sack of his NFL career, while the former Kansas State defender has yet to give up a reception through two games. Sigle has played 111 of 120 defensive snaps so far this season, while Brown has only missed nine, leaving Mustapha as the odd man out in the competition for playing time. After playing six defensive snaps in relief of Brown against the Los Angeles Rams, Mustapha featured on just three in the win over Miami. When on the field in previous seasons, Mustapha has displayed great playmaking instincts in coverage and enticing downhill thump against the run. However, he has been a victim of training camp misfortune to this point, with a hamstring injury seeing Mustapaha miss much of camp, allowing Sigle and Brown to make the starting jobs their own. In essence, the 49ers have a safety whom they have been very comfortable starting in recent years sat on the bench. Though that is unfortunate for Mustapha, the overall situation at safety is clearly one with which Kyle Shanahan is delighted. Asked about the play from his safeties in the early weeks of the season, Shanahan told his Monday conference call: “I think they’ve been doing great. It was just unfortunate for Malik that he missed all of training camp and he didn’t get healthy until we were down in Australia. Those guys got a lot of work together and really kind of solidified that job by how they played throughout the preseason and I think it’s shown here in these last two weeks. I think they’ve both played very well. Malik did get in there for a few plays and I thought he played really well when he got in. He’s been looking great in practice too and getting right back to where he was. We’ve got three guys right there who could all start for us, so it’s a good problem to have.” Of course, the 49ers have been here before with their safeties. Their recent history at the position is a story of promising play falling off and leaving the area as one of vulnerability. Right now, though, they have three players whom the 49ers believe are starters and a veteran insurance policy in Ashtyn Davis. It’s not out of the realms of possibility that one of Sigle or Brown struggles and Mustapha earns more playing time, but the 49ers are clearly comfortable with that as a scenario. At the spot where it looked in the offseason that there might be cause for alarm, the 49ers’ commitment to their draft picks at safety is affording them a sense of calm.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers and Seahawks now tied for first
summary: That San Francisco 49ers thumping the Miami Dolphins was fun, wasn’t it? That win means the 49ers are 2-0 with one divisional win. Unfortunately, the Seattle Seahawks are also 2-0, with one divisional win. These two teams may already be on a collision course. They won’t meet until October 11, in Seattle, but that will […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images That San Francisco 49ers thumping the Miami Dolphins was fun, wasn’t it? That win means the 49ers are 2-0 with one divisional win. Unfortunately, the Seattle Seahawks are also 2-0, with one divisional win. These two teams may already be on a collision course. They won’t meet until October 11, in Seattle, but that will be very important in the scheme of things. Both teams have shown they are more than capable in 2026, and the Seahawks are playing without their starting quarterback. Then again, the 49ers are playing without some of their wide receivers, so pick your poison. After their upcoming game against the Arizona Cardinals, the 49ers host the Denver Broncos and then face the aforementioned Seahawks. That’s two decent defenses back-to-back. If we want to know just how good this offense is, we can chat after those two games to see how things turned out. If the 49ers keep hanging 30, then a lot has been solidified. The Seahawks are a long way off, but that game, when it is on the schedule, should give us some firm answers on what the 49ers have. Speaking of Seattle… Seattle Seahawks (2-0)/Arizona Cardinals (1-1) It wasn’t until the third quarter that the Seahawks managed to open the floodgates on the Cardinals. Though that happened in the third quarter, there were still a couple of Jaxon Smith-Njigba catches to see, including his touchdown. To be honest, the Cardinals might have been in this longer than necessary thanks to a second-quarter Jadarian Price fumble. A fumble that led nowhere. The same goes for the Cardinals’ two-minute offense and the Seahawks’ equally fruitless 30-second offense. The third quarter came in, and the Seahawks scored 24 unanswered points on three touchdowns and a field goal. Smith-Njigba had two of those touchdowns to add to the one he had in the first half to finish with nine receptions for 155 yards. 31-7 Seahawks. Divisional win and now a tie with the 49ers. So how did Drew Lock do backing up that Seahawks offense? 19-26, 235 yards passing, and three touchdowns. This led to a 138.1 passer rating. If you hoped Sam Darnold’s absence would lead to a weaker Seahawks team, you’ll be disappointed. Los Angeles Rams (1-1) For a hot minute, there was hope the New York Giants could be competitive. Then Giants quarterback Jackson Dart exited the game in the first offensive series, reportedly with an MCL sprain. That means Jameis Winston was next man up. Uh-oh. What followed was the Winston experience for Giants fans to endure. That experience was 11 completions (of 27 attempts), 111 yards passing, one interception, and zero touchdowns. 28-6, Rams. Even this awful roughing the kicker (or running into the kicker) no-call wouldn’t have helped much. I’m sure the Rams will credit their defense for this amazing game. I credit them with getting Jameis Winston after the first offensive series. That can do wonders for a defense. Turnovers also help, and since the Giants defense got an interception and a fumble, they had some opportunities. It’s hard to cash those in when your starting quarterback is hurt. Speaking of defense, there wasn’t much of it from the Giants either. Injuries can hurt that part as well, especially the backfield. Matthew Stafford went 22-for-31 for 327 yards passing, four touchdowns, an interception, and a passer rating of 131.3. Running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined their powers for 163 yards rushing. The Rams offense had their way with the Giants. Great job, Rams. Now do it without the starting quarterback getting injured. Or an injury-decimated backfield. Onto Week 3 The 49ers have a chance to regain the NFC West lead as they host the Arizona Cardinals. The fact that the Cardinals beat the Chargers (which should be a better team) and stayed close to the Seahawks until the third quarter tells you all you need to know: This game is no gimme and the biggest test the 49ers have yet. The odds have the 49ers favored by over a touchdown , but the Cardinals always play the 49ers hard, so I’d expect this to be close. Should the 49ers go to 3-0 and 2-0 in the division, that gives them a lot of cushioning for later in the season. The Seahawks will be facing the Washington Commanders. The Commanders already have their backs against the wall with the dreaded 0-2 start. To make matters worse, they lost quarterback Jayden Daniels Sunday to a dislocated elbow. It’s safe to say he might not be available for Sunday’s game. How Seahawks of it for them to fly across the country and face the No. 2 quarterback. The Rams have the Philadelphia Eagles. I know it sounds dirty, but we are Eagles fans. Eagles fans, we’d love to see the dream team go to a 1-2. You know what to do. TIE – 1st: San Francisco 49ers Next vs. Arizona Cardinals TIE – 1st: Seattle Seahawks; Next: at Washington Commanders 3rd: Los Angeles Rams; Next: at Denver Broncos 4th: Arizona Cardinals; Next: at San Francisco 49ers
author: Patrick Holloway

title: 49ers have the best odds in the NFC to make the playoffs through 2 weeks
summary: It’s been only two weeks, but the San Francisco 49ers are looking like a true Super Bowl contender this year after a pair of dominant wins to start the season. After a 27-7 blowout over the Los Angeles Rams as an underdog, the 49ers cruised past the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, scoring touchdowns on each […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) It’s been only two weeks, but the San Francisco 49ers are looking like a true Super Bowl contender this year after a pair of dominant wins to start the season. After a 27-7 blowout over the Los Angeles Rams as an underdog, the 49ers cruised past the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, scoring touchdowns on each of their first five drives as they won 35-13 in a game where they never really looked in trouble. It was an amazing day for Brock Purdy, who completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns, while adding a third on the ground. San Francisco didn’t need much on the ground because their passing game was so dominant, as Purdy connected well with George Kittle and Mike Evans, who led the team in receiving. Heading into the season, the 49ers were seen as a playoff contender, but most still viewed them as the clear No. 3 team in their division behind the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and powerhouse Los Angeles Rams. Well, after two weeks, the 49ers have the best odds in the NFC to reach the playoffs at -320, according to FanDuel. Behind them are the Seahawks (-300) and Rams (-290), while the Philadelphia Eagles (-270) are the only other team above -200 odds. Now, when it comes to Super Bowl odds, the 49ers are still behind both the Rams (+650) and Seahawks (+950) at +1000 odds, while ranking behind the Buffalo Bills (+750) and alongside the Baltimore Ravens (+1000). San Francisco has a big three-week stretch coming up. They first face the Arizona Cardinals at home in Week 3, giving them a chance at a 2-0 start in the division, before facing the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks (road). If they can find a way to go 2-1 in that stretch, the 49ers will be in a great position through the first quarter of the season, looking like true Super Bowl contenders. Of course, as always with this team, the key will be health. The 49ers have dealt with a ton of injury issues ahead of the season, and they had two more receiver injuries on Sunday, as Demarcus Robinson had an ankle issue, while Mike Evans had a hip issue. Evans’s doesn’t seem to be serious, while Robinson will likely miss a couple of weeks. But the 49ers look much more complete as a team through two weeks than what they showed last season, especially on defense. In addition, Brock Purdy has looked sharp to start the season and is slowly emerging as a dark horse MVP candidate. Currently, he sits as fourth in MVP odds at +950 behind Josh Allen (+250), Joe Burrow (+850), and Patrick Mahomes (+850). This upcoming three-game stretch will tell us a lot about Purdy, as the 49ers will be in some tougher game environments, but there’s been a lot of good from the San Francisco quarterback to start the year. When the schedule initially came out during the offseason, the 49ers’ end-of-season schedule looked like a gauntlet. From Weeks 10 to 17, they face the Dallas Cowboys (road), Minnesota Vikings (Mexico City), Seattle Seahawks, New York Giants (road), Los Angeles Rams (home), Los Angeles Chargers (road), Kansas City Chiefs (road), and Philadelphia Eagles. Outside of the Chargers, each of those teams has looked good to start the year. That makes it imperative to have a strong start. So far, so good.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers’ upcoming stretch will test Trent Williams’ exciting Brock Purdy claim
summary: Even though his latest superb showing came against significantly inferior opposition in the form of the Miami Dolphins, the excitement around what 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has put together through the opening two weeks of the season is understandable. Purdy was near-perfect in the 49ers’ 35-13 rout of the rebuilding Dolphins, rewriting several pages of […]
full_text: (Photo by Santiago Mejia/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) Even though his latest superb showing came against significantly inferior opposition in the form of the Miami Dolphins, the excitement around what 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has put together through the opening two weeks of the season is understandable. Purdy was near-perfect in the 49ers’ 35-13 rout of the rebuilding Dolphins, rewriting several pages of the record books in going 20 of 22 for 287 yards and two touchdowns. Purdy also led the 49ers in rushing with 30 yards and a rushing score. Those numbers saw Purdy become the first player in NFL history to complete at least 90 percent of his passes, throw for at least 285 yards and two touchdowns and rush for a score in the same game. With a completion percentage of 90.9, Purdy now owns the top two single-game completion percentage marks in 49er franchise history. He completed 95.2% of his passes against the Arizona Cardinals in a 35-16 win in October, 2023. In addition, he joined Derek Carr as only the second player to have multiple games with a completion rate of 90%-or-higher and at least 250 passing yards. His passer rating of 149.1 gave Purdy an eighth career game with a rating of 140-or-higher and a 13th game with a rating of at least 130-or higher, both NFL records for a player in the first five seasons of his career. Unsurprisingly, the praise for Purdy after the game from his teammates was effusive, though it was the comments of Trent Williams that were the most eye-catching. Asked what impressed him most about Purdy’s showing, the left tackle said: “It’s hard for me to tell because I just see the ball coming over my head, but it was extremely accurate. He looked like he was just at practice out there, wheeling and dealing. Like I said, we’re starting to witness Brock’s prime and I think it’s going to be a sight to behold. To me, I’ve always loved Brock, but I think he’s starting to get his respect now. He doesn’t even relish in it. It’s all about next week, going 1-0, and that’s why he’s a great leader.” Williams’ remarks about Purdy hitting his prime suggest even more impressive games are to come from the 49ers’ signal-caller, but those exciting claims will be severely tested over the coming weeks. An exacting three-game stretch San Francisco’s schedule over the next three games is very tough, with the 49ers hosting the Cardinals and the Denver Broncos before making the trip up to the Pacific Northwest for a matchup with the Seattle Seahawks. While the visit of the Cardinals is not a fixture to inspire much fear, a divisional game against an opponent that has played the 49ers tough in recent years is not be taken lightly, though it is the meetings with the Broncos and Seahawks that will provide the sternest early examinations of Purdy’s progress this year. Facing a Denver defense that led the NFL in sacks (68) last season promises to be an extremely difficult challenge for Purdy, as does a reunion with a Seattle unit that overwhelmed the 49ers in Week 18 and in the divisonal round last season. And the severity of the test he will face is potentially exacerbated by the 49ers’ injury issues at wide receiver, where Demarcus Robinson is the latest player to be sidelined, having suffered a high-ankle sprain . Robinson joining De’Zhaun Stribling and Chirstian Kirk among the injured players at receiver is a huge hit to the 49ers’ depth at wideout and, while San Francisco still has high end weapons in the likes of Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans and George Kittle, a paucity of supplementary options makes Purdy’s job in overcoming two vaunted defenses that much harder. The 49ers’ 2025 season ended in ugly fashion with Purdy out of answers against the Seahawks as injuries left San Francisco with a skill-position cast ill-equipped to keep their playoff game competitive. The Niners still have enough weapons to trouble both Denver and Seattle but, with injuries impacting the depth, this upcoming slate and Purdy’s ability to find solutions amid the offense’s injury woes will provide an indicator as to the prescience of Williams’ comments about his quarterback.

summary: JC Latham has one really tough play on Sunday. It came at a terrible time, as the Tennessee Titans were set up with 1st and goal from the 8-yard line in a 17-17 game with 2:33 left to play. Latham got beat and allowed Cam Ward to get sacked. Former Titans scout Blake Beddingfield wrote […]

Former Titans scout Blake Beddingfield wrote at PaulKuharsky.com that the play design was poor there, giving Latham “no options on his block.” On the whole, Latham has been much improved this season. Check out this graphic from Pro Football Focus: JC Latham's ranks this season among OT Island Rate: Highest Island Pass Block Win Rate: 5th Highest pic.twitter.com/AJu8rIXMPI — PFF (@PFF) September 23, 2026 Latham is consistently winning in pass blocking without the Titans having to give him help. Look, those are the numbers you expect from a guy when you draft him with the 7th overall pick. It took Latham longer to get here than we had hoped, but it finally seems like the Titans have a right tackle they can count on (left tackle is another story). This gives the Titans two really good young players on the offensive line with Latham and Peter Skoronski. They are going to have to address left tackle sooner rather than later, but in case you didn’t know, it’s a whole lot easier to find one tackle than two. #math Rookie left guard Fernando Carmona improved from Week 1 to Week 2. title: Jeffery Simmons is still dominant for the Titans
summary: There was chatter going around about Tennessee Titans DT Jeffery Simmons after Week 1. The Titans endured a lifeless performance versus the New York Jets, and Simmons didn’t pop enough. Well, it’s clear after Week 2 that he’s still a dominant defender. Simmons leads the entire NFL in pass-rush wins through two weeks, according to […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jeffery Simmons #98 of the Tennessee Titans warms up prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was chatter going around about Tennessee Titans DT Jeffery Simmons after Week 1. The Titans endured a lifeless performance versus the New York Jets, and Simmons didn’t pop enough. Well, it’s clear after Week 2 that he’s still a dominant defender . Simmons leads the entire NFL in pass-rush wins through two weeks, according to ESPN Stats & Info. The Pro Bowl defender has been credited with 19 wins as a pass rusher. No contender has more than 15, with Minnesota Vikings EDGE Dallas Turner currently ranking second. Top 10 players by pass rush wins this season. -Jeffery Simmons, dear god -Dallas Turner has arrived -Boye Mafe being what Bengals need, keeping up PRWR with expanded playing time! -I thought Bradley Chubb was washed and was critical of that signing. Looking like a bad take! pic.twitter.com/jnCnlYJTlm — Seth Walder (@SethWalder) September 22, 2026 Simmons’ pass-rush-win-rate stands at 37%. Only New England Patriots DT Christian Barmore has a slightly higher win rate at 38%, because Simmons has played more reps. Not a single edge rusher in the NFL currently matches Simmons’ 37% win rate. Pro Football Focus’ metrics largely agree. They have Simmons tied for first among defensive tackles in pressures with nine. His PFF win% of 17.7 percent ranks fifth among DTs, but none of the four interior defenders ahead of him have played as many reps as he has (Aaron Donald is in first after making his Week 2 debut with just 19 pass-rushing snaps. Simmons has 66). Simmons dominated an Eagles offensive line in Week 2 that had Cam Jurgens and Drew Kendall starting in prominent roles. Kendall replaced the injured Landon Dickerson. He had absolutely no answer for Simmons. There was some concern that Simmons would take time to adjust to Robert Saleh’s new attack-style defense. Those whispers grew after Week 1 when fans believed Simmons’ impact was muted versus the Jets. This clearly isn’t the case at all. Simmons is as dominant as ever. Every advanced metric (across different outlets) proves it. The Titans still have a superstar defensive tackle in Jeffery Simmons. Hopefully the rest of the defense catches up soon.

summary: It has been a tough start for the teams in the AFC South. The Houston Texans, who were considered by most to be the heavy favorites to win the division, have started 0-2. They lost a shootout to the Buffalo Bills in Week 1. This week, despite C.J. Stroud throwing for 353 yards with no […]

(Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images It has been a tough start for the teams in the AFC South. The Houston Texans, who were considered by most to be the heavy favorites to win the division, have started 0-2. They lost a shootout to the Buffalo Bills in Week 1. This week, despite C.J. Stroud throwing for 353 yards with no interceptions, they only scored 6 points in a 20-6 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. It’s usually a tough road for a team that starts 0-2 to make the playoffs, but the Texans are still in pretty good position in the division. The Jacksonville Jaguars are leading the division at 1-1. They lost 20-13 this week to the Denver Broncos. I know the jury is still out on the Cam Ward pick for the Tennessee Titans, but it still looks better than the Travis Hunter pick the Jaguars made in the same draft at #2 overall. The Jags gave up picks number 5, 36, and 126 in the 2025 draft and pick 24 in the 2026 draft to get to pick 2. Hunter, who was supposed to be a two-way star, has just one catch for eight yards this season and has not had an interception in his NFL career. The Indianapolis Colts also find themselves at 0-2. Their schedule has been tough to start the season, facing the Baltimore Ravens at home in Week 1 and the Kansas City Chiefs on the road in Week 2. They took the Chiefs to overtime, but ultimately lost the game 33-30. There weren’t many people who expected the Tennessee Titans to have a chance at winning the AFC South, but if they can find a way to knock off the New York Giants this week, they will only be, at worst, a game back of the division leader.

title: Titans QB Cam Ward showed real progress in Week 2
summary: The Tennessee Titans endured a tough loss in Week 2, losing 24-20 to the Philadelphia Eagles. Sophomore quarterback Cam Ward showed real growth. Ward was way better than he was in Week 1 versus the Jets, and that progress is good news for the Titans. Ward finished 13-of-20 for 183 yards. The second-year No. 1 […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans drops back to pass the ball during the fourth quarter of the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans endured a tough loss in Week 2 , losing 24-20 to the Philadelphia Eagles. Sophomore quarterback Cam Ward showed real growth. Ward was way better than he was in Week 1 versus the Jets, and that progress is good news for the Titans. Ward finished 13-of-20 for 183 yards. The second-year No. 1 overall selection was better than the box score indicates. Ward was very accurate and decisive. Ward also rushed for two touchdowns. His playmaking ability on 3rd-and-goal set the offense up for 4th-and-goal from the half-yard line. A QB sneak got Ward into the end zone. Ward completed 65% of his passing attempts. He only bested that mark in four individual games last season. Ward also averaged an explosive 9.2 yards per pass. That would have been a single-game high during his 2025 rookie campaign. Ward’s only “miss” was a throw into the end zone for Ayomanor. Poor footwork led to an inaccurate ball behind Ayomanor. It was still catchable, but it should have been a straightforward completion. Ward’s footwork is still in work-in-progress mode. The former Miami standout made up for it with the aforementioned third-down scramble that led to his first rushing score on fourth down. Ward’s average depth of target (7.1) was also significantly better than his Week 1 aDOT (5.3). Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll did a good job removing some of the concepts Ward struggled with in Week 1. He played with confidence, throwing the ball with anticipation while finding the explosive plays that lacked versus the Jets. The Titans’ 2026 season is all about Ward’s progress. Week 1 was a discouraging showing, but Ward already looked significantly more comfortable in Daboll’s offense against a stout Eagles defense. Hopefully he continues taking positive steps forward versus the New York Giants in Week 3 .

(Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 23 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Room: Jayden Daniels vs Cowboys [ The play described in the excerpt below is the one in the video clip in the embedded tweet from Mark Bullock ] Jayden Daniels looked at his absolute best during the first half against the Cowboys. As a passer, he was processing reads quickly and moving well within the pocket to avoid rushers while still finding receivers down the field. But he also was more prepared to take off scrambling when there was an opportunity for him to do so. He showed signs of that combination which made him lethal at the end of the 2024 season in the fourth quarter against the Eagles last week, and it continued in the first half against Dallas. Daniels looked sharp early as a passer, processing through reads quickly to get the ball out efficiently. On third downs, Daniels stepped it up a gear and delivered some nice passes down the field. One of his best throws of the day came from a third and 18 situation. Prior to getting injured, Jayden Daniels was having a strong outing against the Cowboys. I broke down his performance: https://t.co/W5tyfhWerb pic.twitter.com/6VxjWItUtK — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) September 22, 2026 On third and 18, the Commanders call a dagger concept to the left and have Terry McLaurin running a deep curl route to the right. At the snap, a defensive tackle stunts inside right guard Sam Cosmi. Cosmi adjusts to shove the defender down the line, but he still penetrates and generates pressure. Like on the previous play, Daniels does a good job climbing the pocket but remaining a passer as he does it. He can see McLaurin spotting up on his curl route, with the underneath coverage defenders nowhere near him and the deep safety getting far too much depth. So as he climbs the pocket, Daniels pulls the trigger and throws a strike over the middle to McLaurin, who picks up a first down and more after the catch. Daniels continued to pick up third down conversions as the game went on. Fox Sports The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly From The Commanders Loss To The Dallas Cowboys The major event is the injury to Jayden Daniels, which will be discussed a length, however the even scarier injury to S Nick Cross. The Commanders hardly have time to reset as the defending super bowl champion Seattle Seahawks come to Landover. Here is what I saw from the game. Rachaad White- Running Back Rachaad White looked a but off in week one however against the Cowboys we saw the back he was planned to be. White was good running the ball, catching the ball out of the backfield, and in pass protection. Washington needed some dynamic players and White played his part. Pass Defense- For all the good stuff up front, the back end was bad. Routinely the secondary was confused, not effectively communicating, and getting beat. Add LB Leo Chenal to that equation and the Cowboys receivers had a field day. A serious decision needs to be made about CB Mikey Sainrisil because he is now the target of every offensive passing attack. Even when Sainrisil was in position Cowboys receivers still caught the ball. He needs a hard reset and needs to come off the field. It would help all parties for him to take a step back and really work his technique and understanding of Daronte Jones’ defense. Drew Stevens- With so many other issues on the team, K Drew Stevens missed another field goal on Sunday. This one would not have mattered but it shook the belief of the team that they could come back. Stevens has a monster leg but the accuracy needs to be better. If this happens a few more times then he maybe looking over his shoulder. Leo Chenal- A lot of attention has gone to the secondary and their struggles but LB Leo Chenal has looked outright confused out there. title: What Washington Commanders will get from Marcus Mariota
summary: We all know that Jayden Daniels is hurt. His dislocated elbow will keep him out for a stretch still yet to be determined as he seeks medical opinions on the best course of action.   There’s some uncertainty there. We know, however, that Marcus Mariota will start a now pivotal Week 3 home game against […]
full_text: We all know that Jayden Daniels is hurt. His dislocated elbow will keep him out for a stretch still yet to be determined as he seeks medical opinions on the best course of action. There’s some uncertainty there. We know, however, that Marcus Mariota will start a now pivotal Week 3 home game against the Seattle Seahawks. He’ll probably play more games beyond that, but we’re only dealing with absolutes right now. We know No. 8 is Sunday’s starter, and that his play will not be a revelation to Commanders fans. Mariota has been around this block before. He has been in Washington since 2024 and has appeared in burgundy & gold in 15 regular season games now. He started eight games last season and finished a few others, with a not-so-outstanding 2-6 record that wasn’t all on him. So, in sum, y’all know him well. I generally don’t like to insert my personal voice in stories, but I will in this instance because I know Mariota a little bit. I worked for the Atlanta Falcons in 2022, when he was the starting quarterback there. I had a few one-on-ones with him, including a long meeting where we went deep about his career to that point and where his confidence lay. Overall, he’s a great dude and a good locker room leader. He’s a guy who can get you a series of wins while a starter recovers, but isn’t a guy you want taking you through an entire season. Mariota has speed. He has arm talent. He is not afraid of big moments. Maybe he chooses to run too soon. That’s a thing, but he sets up protection well and keeps a team out of bad spots. If you’re expecting a film breakdown, this article isn’t that. We’ll leave that to Jamual Forrest and Mark Tyler. I’ll tell you what I know about the signal caller and the leader that will guide the Commanders through a difficult stretch. Mariota’s in his 12 th NFL season . He is what he is at this point, which is one of the best backups in the league. Everybody else probably knows that already. He’s tailor-made for Washington in that his playing style is similar enough to Daniels that offensive coordinator David Blough doesn’t have to reinvent the wheel. The same concepts apply to both guys, though JD5 obviously executes them better. Mariota is a playmaker with some arm talent who isn’t afraid to let it fly or tuck it and run. His stat line as a Commander isn’t half bad, with a 64% completion rate, 15 touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 94.3 passer rating. Again, not half bad. The Commanders can be a functional and winning football team with Mariota. As he said after the loss to Dallas, he can work with this scheme. “With as much experience as I’ve had, I feel comfortable,” Mariota told on-site reporters. “We’ve got a great crew. Those guys didn’t blink at all, and I thought we did a good job of moving the ball in the second half. But yeah, I feel confident. I feel comfortable. I really like what Coach Blough is doing. I believe in this system and we’ll get this thing right.” Washington needs to stack some victories and do it now after starting 0-2 on the season and within the division. We’ll see when Daniels can return. The Commanders must hold serve until he does. A lot of the responsibility for that falls on Mariota, someone we all know well and someone we know can be a functional quarterback and produce wins that the Commanders need. Desperately.

full_text: The Daily Slop – 22 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Review: Coverage Issues vs Cowboys [The play discussed in this excerpt is the same one shown in video clip in tweet below] There were warning signs of coverage issues early on in the game. On the Cowboys opening drive, the Commanders had a couple of coverage busts. Here, the Cowboys look to send both their outside receivers on deep curl routes down the field. The Commanders show a blitz look with a lot of defenders up at the line of scrimmage, but actually appear to be rotating back to an inverted Tampa-2 coverage scheme. Instead of both safeties sinking back to play deep halves of the field, Jeremy Reaves rotates up into one of the underneath zone coverage roles while Quan Martin works across the field to cover his half. To replace Martin on his side, cornerback Amik Robertson drops back deep to play a deep half. The Commanders defense that looked so promising against the Eagles last week was a mess against the Cowboys yesterday. I broke down the various coverage issues that led to explosive plays for Dallas: https://t.co/9oTDRwju4s pic.twitter.com/dUlm4rLQgg — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) September 21, 2026 The issue for Washington comes between linebacker Leo Chenal and safety Jeremy Reaves, and I tend to lean more towards Chenal being at fault. Reaves steps up into an underneath zone, but Chenal sinks back off the line of scrimmage into the same zone. One of them should have been covering the middle of the field, but as you can see it’s left wide open. Robertson can’t stick close to CeeDee Lamb on his curl route because Robertson is responsible for a deep half of the field, so he has to sink back deeper. One of Chenal and Reaves should have been in the middle and able to work over to close off the route. Typically in these inverted Tampa-2 schemes, you see one of the deep safeties step up into the middle hole, which would make Reaves responsible for it. However, the coverage rotation suggests Reaves is correct and Chenal is at fault. If they were going to have a safety play the middle hole, it would have been Martin with Reaves staying on his half of the field. The fact that Martin rotated across to play Reaves side of the field suggests to me that Reaves was meant to step up to the spot that he did. If that is the case, then Chenal is the one that should have been playing the middle hole. You can see after the play Reaves and Chenal both debating who was at fault, so I could be wrong, but that’s how I see it. That’s not a great start, but ultimately it’s only a 15-yard gain. You can come back from that and be fine. Unfortunately, on the very next play, the Commanders had another coverage bust. Washington Post (paywall) Jayden Daniels is injured again. Where do the Commanders go from here? After Daniels missed most of last season because of injury, the front office and coaching staff collaborated on a plan to protect him. That was launched before the end of the ill-fated 2025 campaign. Coach Dan Quinn told The Washington Post he had a film cut-up created of every play on which Daniels scrambled, then tasked him with identifying instances when he could have avoided hits. The goal was to improve his decision-making. Once the offseason arrived, Quinn parted ways with offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury and promoted David Blough to fill the vacancy. From there, Blough reconstructed the offense to include an emphasis on the traditional run game, play-action passes and snaps from under center. The goal was to create an ecosystem where Daniels didn’t have to force the issue. General Manager Adam Peters and the front office extended left tackle Laremy Tunsil and added talented pass catchers in Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Chig Okonkwo. The goal was to avoid Daniels needing to carry the offense. Despite all of that, Daniels has suffered another significant injury. At the end of the day, football is a contact sport. As unfortunate as the injury was, there’s no one to blame for what happened. It was a standard play that happened to go horribly wrong. Washington has 15 games left, and the team can’t just call it a season because Daniels is sidelined. Everyone — the front office, coaching staff and players — has work to do to keep their jobs. Nonetheless, it presents a difficult question for the Commanders (0-2): How do they move forward? Washington coach Dan Quinn reiterated Monday that Blough’s entire playbook would be available to the Commanders even as Mariota subs in. “No, like, pullback or any of that,” Quinn said. The issue: Even with all he has learned, Mariota intuitively wants to make plays for himself, for his teammates. A replacement for the dynamic Daniels might be called on to be a game manager. title: Future Hogs – Week 3: College football players who could help the Commanders
summary: It did not look like the premier matchup of Week 3 of the college football between LSU and Ole Miss would live up to the hype. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It did not look like the premier matchup of Week 3 of the college football between LSU and Ole Miss would live up to the hype. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss looked like a Heisman front-runner in the first half, converting all his third downs and leading the Rebels to a 24-7 lead at the half. Lane Kiffin motivated the Tigers at halftime as they rallied to tie the game at 24-24 in the fourth quarter. Chambliss had a little magic left as he led the Rebels to the go ahead touchdown and two-point conversion. A tipped pass in the end zone on LSU’s final drive resulted in an interception of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt that sealed the win for Ole Miss. The other ranked-on-ranked games were competitive games. Louisville and SMU was a back and forth affair with Louisville taking the lead in the fourth quarter and holding on to it for the win. A failed two-point conversion allowed Texas Tech to escape an upset by Houston. Who didn’t escape being upset this weekend? Texas A&M. Despite being tied with Kentucky at halftime, 21 unanswered points in the third quarter was enough for a Wildcats win. Virginia will fall from the AP Top 25 after a loss to West Virginia. Week 4 will feature a pivotal matchup between #10 LSU and #23 Texas A&M. A second loss for either team could end their chances for the College Football Playoff. #1 Texas will go on the road to #14 Tennessee in each team’s first SEC action. Several Big Ten teams will begin conference play. This includes #18 Michigan as they welcome #17 Iowa, a team that may finally have some offensive firepower, and #20 Oregon who will go on the road to face #12 USC who are looking to keep their playoff hopes alive. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to comment with players that stood out to you. Aidan Chiles | QB | Senior | Northwestern It was tough to see Jayden Daniels injure his elbow for a third time in the past year. While he has the talent of a top NFL QB, his health has to be a consideration with regards to his future in Washington. While I’m not at the point where the team should consider an early draft pick to replace him, it shows why it’s always important to continually look for talent at the position. Aidan Chiles has played at Oregon State, Michigan State, and now Northwestern. He’s had an up and down career. He was benched last season at Michigan State as he and the team struggled. He decided to transfer to Northwestern and, so far, it looks like a good decision. Chiles is 6’4”, 225 pounds, so plenty of size for the position. When Chiles has times, he has good mechanics and delivers accurate passes. When he has to get rid of the ball quickly, those mechanics change and his accuracy can dip. While Chiles can run, he is more of a pocket passer with a strong enough arm for NFL throws. Chiles went 17 of 22 for 241 yards and three touchdowns and two touchdowns on the ground. title: NFL Week 3 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips
summary: What now for the Giants with Jaxson Dart out? What's the buzz on Patrick Mahomes through two games? Are running back depth charts firming up in Tampa and Carolina?
full_text:
We're onto Week 3 of the  2026 NFL season , and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 There was optimism around the Giants coming into Week 2, but things went south quickly Monday night. They lost their quarterback on the first drive and lost the game in a 28-6 blowout . How are the vibes in their building and where do they go with Jaxson Dart out ? On the other end of the spectrum, the Chiefs moved to 2-0 with  Patrick Mahomes  back from last season's torn ACL . What are people saying about his play?

 Around the league, we have a sample size to draw some conclusions. What looks different through two weeks from our preseason expectations? And which previously uncertain running back hierarchies are getting clarity? It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 3.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Next steps for the Giants 
 Early thoughts on Mahomes 
 Preseason take do-overs 
 Updates on RB depth charts 
 Fantasy football advice 
 More notes and intel 

 
 

 What are you hearing out of the Giants' building? 
 Graziano: They're disappointed, obviously. They had designed a game plan for their Monday night game against the Rams around Jaxson Dart, believing his mobility would help mitigate the interior pressure they knew they were going to face from Aaron Donald and the L.A. defensive front, and they suddenly had to play a far less mobile Jameis Winston . The run game was limited once the Rams didn't have to worry about the quarterback run threat. They thought they could get more pressure on Matthew Stafford than they did. Very disappointing night all around.

 They do believe Winston will be better with a full week of practice as the starter and with a game plan built around his strengths. We are waiting to find out whether they will have Malik Nabers , Andrew Thomas or Brian Burns , all of whom also left Monday night's game due to injuries. That becomes much more important because the Dart injury has turned out to be more serious than they believed Monday night.

 

 Fowler: Your point about the game plan is an important one -- the Giants entered Monday's game with a plan tailored around Dart's skill set. But now the Giants' offense is in the hands of Winston, who signed a two-year, $13 million extension on Sept. 6. Winston is comfortable operating out of the shotgun, which offensive coordinator Matt Nagy -- with his ties to Kansas City and Andy Reid -- can accommodate.

 But man, the Giants offense looked so good in Week 1 with Dart under center, operating at a high level and making quick decisions (Dallas' defense contributed to that, to be sure). And then it looked so sloppy without him, especially in that end-of-half sequence in the red zone Monday night. This is where Nabers enters the fray. He has been slow to launch through two games, which is understandable given his recovery from a  torn ACL . But elite receivers can make backup QBs look like starters. The Giants will need Nabers to have that effect. And Winston did provide a spark last season, so perhaps he finds that groove again.

 Graziano: The problem with Winston -- or any backup, really -- is that while he can probably get you through two or three games, his deficiencies are likely to show up the longer he plays. The Giants will need to bring in someone else, even if it's just for depth. Jake Haener is on their practice squad, so he's obviously a candidate to be elevated. But there's no magic solution here.

 Jimmy Garoppolo is a free agent. Maybe they could talk the Steelers out of Mason Rudolph for a draft pick. At some point this season, maybe guys such as Jacoby Brissett (Arizona) or Kirk Cousins (Las Vegas) get replaced by younger QBs and become available in trade. But it's way too early for that now, and it looks like the Giants will have to go with Winston and work to help him play better than he did in relief Monday night.

 Fowler: Yeah, the quarterback options are scarce. Garoppolo appears to be in that half retirement phase. It might be worth a call to Minnesota, where J.J. McCarthy toils on the bench. General manager Joe Schoen did a lot of homework on the 2024 draft class of quarterbacks, so he knows the pros and cons of McCarthy's game. Rival teams believe McCarthy can be acquired at a value since Minnesota doesn't appear to have him in the long-term plans .

 Luckily for the Giants, the Thomas and Burns injuries are not believed to be serious. The Giants' strength is in the offensive and defensive lines, and the defense has enough players to maintain respectability. The Giants must find a way to run the ball effectively and keep Winston on time from the pocket. He can still throw to all levels of the field when he's decisive. Scramble plays are probably something New York wants to avoid due to the turnover threat that plagues Winston in those situations.

 

 

 
 What's the leaguewide buzz about Patrick Mahomes ' first two games back from his knee injury? 
 Fowler: That Mahomes might not be all the way back ... but he's not far off. He looked more fluid and confident in Week 2 vs. Indianapolis . "His ability to drive throws -- I thought he was ripping the ball," one NFL personnel evaluator said of Mahomes' performance against the Colts. The confidence he showed throwing the ball was something which he can build upon. It was an improvement from Week 1 vs. Denver , where Mahomes was a modest 15-of-27 for 184 yards and looked choppy as a runner. That's to be expected early as he strengthens his knee flexion.

 But overall, throwing five touchdown passes, taking four sacks and winning back-to-back games is a roaring start for Mahomes coming off reconstructive knee surgery . The Chiefs were pleased with how Mahomes looked all camp and that has spilled over. And his supporting cast looks more equipped to perform for him over 17 games.

 Graziano: And he will look even better equipped to perform once the Chiefs get left tackle Josh Simmons back from his injury. They've been leaning on the run at least in part because they've been starting undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson at left tackle. But they're earning praise around the league for the extent to which they've been willing to run it with  Kenneth Walker III . He was their big free agent signing , and they talked throughout camp about using him as their primary rusher and in the passing game. But to see Reid actually commit to it has been surprising to many.

 I believe the Chiefs will involve the downfield passing game more as the season goes along and they get more whole, but people around the league are noticing that they have embraced the run game as a means of creating explosive plays. Their offense has lacked big plays in recent years and needed to find a way to get them back. Mahomes is a marvel, and while it's objectively amazing that he looks this good so soon after that injury, I don't know if anyone is surprised by anything he does anymore.

 Fowler: You're right, Mahomes' success this season feels directly tied to Walker, who has been a revelation. Eventually, the Chiefs will want to spell him. He has 56 touches through two games (47 rushing attempts), equating to 476 over a full season. Reid game plans based on what it takes to win, and leaning on the running game early has helped Mahomes reacclimate. But that could vary depending on the week.

 The good news is rookie Emmett Johnson looks capable of being the RB2 and can aid the offense in stretches. He's not only gifted in the open field but also eager to take on tough yards. When Simmons returns, perhaps Reid can do more offensively. But Benson, to his credit, has acquitted himself well at left tackle.

 

 Graziano: He has! Benson is quite a story. He was so good in the spring that they opened camp in late July with him competing a bit with veteran Jaylon Moore for the starting…

title: Evaluating surprise early-season trends for 32 NFL teams
summary: T.J. Watt is dominant again? The Packers can't run the ball? Drew Lock is fourth in QBR? Let's figure out which early stats and trends have staying power and which are a mirage.
full_text:
We're two weeks into the 2026 NFL season , which means we know everything about all 32 teams.

 Just kidding.

 But narratives are beginning to take hold. Which early trends will stick and which will dissipate as the season goes on? The eight remaining 2-0 teams probably won't all be playoff-bound, and the eight 0-2 teams are not all doomed. And some players have had shocking performances so far -- good and bad -- and they won't all continue.

 So, what's real and what's a mirage? We tasked our 32 team reporters with identifying a trend or a stat that sticks out for every team through two weeks and sizing up whether it is likely to continue over the rest of the season.

 
 Jump to: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 

 Buffalo Bills 
 The early surprise:  Greg Rousseau is emerging as a top-tier pass rusher.

 

 The verdict:  Real. Rousseau has 4.0 sacks and nine pressures. Since 2018, the only other edge rushers to start a season with that many sacks and pressures through two games have been Aidan Hutchinson (2024), T.J. Watt (2023) and Chandler Jones (2021). That's All-Pro company, and Rousseau is doing it without fluke sacks; only one of his takedowns registers among the 20 quickest sacks from snap to tackle. His sacks appear to be products of good all-around play, not one-off big moments. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 Miami Dolphins 
 The early surprise:  The Dolphins have allowed points on 10 of their 17 defensive possessions.

 

 The verdict:  Real. Miami has yet to register a defensive stop in the first half through its first two games, and it allowed the 49ers to score touchdowns on their first five possessions in Week 2. Teams likely won't keep scoring against the Dolphins at that rate. But until first-year coach and defensive playcaller Jeff Hafley can figure out a way to manufacture a pass rush, a young Dolphins secondary will likely keep getting attacked by opposing quarterbacks. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques 

 
 

 New England Patriots 
 The early surprise:  Drake Maye has four interceptions on throws of 15-plus yards.

 

 The verdict:  Mirage. This matches Maye's total from all of 2025 on such throws and is the second-highest total through the first two games of a season since ESPN began tracking in 2006. Part of that is facing the Seahawks and the Steelers, two of the NFL's best defenses. Being without top wide receiver  A.J. Brown ( ankle ) is a factor too. Maye's accuracy and decision-making, which are his calling cards, should improve with more time on task after not playing in the preseason. -- Mike Reiss 

 

 
 

 New York Jets 
 The early surprise:  The defense is No. 1 in yards allowed (197 per game).

 The verdict:  Mirage. No doubt, the defense has improved from last season (25th), but No. 1 in the league? Let's tap the brakes. The Jets have yet to face a top-shelf offense. Ordinarily, the Packers could be in that category, but they were compromised without running back  Josh Jacobs ( commissioner exempt list ) and with a patchwork offensive line. Despite an overtime loss, the Jets held Green Bay to 199 yards. We'll know a lot more about New York's defense on Sunday against the Lions. -- Rich Cimini 

 

 

 AFC NORTH 
 

 Baltimore Ravens 
 The early surprise:   Lamar Jackson leads the NFL with 10 yards per passing attempt.

 

 The verdict:  Real. One of the buzz words for new Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is explosiveness. So, it's not a surprise that Jackson tops the league with an average of 10 yards per attempt. He has completed four passes of 40 yards or longer, connecting with Zay Flowers (twice), Chris Moore and Devontez Walker . The QB is far ahead of last season's pace, when he totaled six passes of 40 yards or longer in 10 games. -- Jamison Hensley 

 
 

 

 Cincinnati Bengals 
 The early surprise:  The Bengals' defense is putting pressure on QBs.

 

 The verdict:  Real. Cincinnati wanted its defensive line to be a true strength of the team. And all the offseason moves have made the intended impact. According to ESPN Research, the Bengals rank fifth in team pressure rate (40.2%) and are fourth in QB hit rate (20.5%). And it's not just Dexter Lawrence II creating chaos. Free agent signee Boye Mafe is tied for fourth in the NFL in pressures (nine), while Cashius Howell is tied for the most pressures by any rookie (seven). -- Ben Baby 

 
 

 Cleveland Browns 
 The early surprise:  Jared Verse has recorded zero pressures.

 

 The verdict:  Mirage. It's not the start Verse had hoped for with his new team, but opportunities have been lacking for the two-time Pro Bowler. Verse's snaps have been limited through two games; he has had only 43 pass rush snaps. Much of his team debut in Week 1 was spent facing a large deficit, but his average get-off time through two games -- 0.77 seconds, according to NFL Next Gen Stats -- would be a career-best mark. If Cleveland can play more close games, such as its Week 2 upset over the Buccaneers, Verse should get more chances, and those pass rush numbers should rise. -- Daniel Oyefusi 

 
 

 Pittsburgh Steelers 
 The early surprise:  T.J. Watt is back to his dominant ways.

 The verdict:  Real. Watt has been quick to remind the NFL that even after two down seasons, he's still otherworldly. Reinvigorated by defensive coordinator Patrick Graham's scheme, the 31-year-old Watt is playing fewer snaps (thanks to Graham's carefully monitored rotation) and varying his rush locations. A better rested and more unpredictable Watt? That's a nightmare for O-coordinators. Through two weeks, his 3.5 sacks is second only to Buffalo's Rousseau. Watt also has as many touchdowns (one) as the Steelers' offense through two weeks. -- Brooke Pryor 

 

 

 AFC SOUTH 
 

 Houston Texans 
 The early surprise:  The Texans' run game is struggling again . 

 

 The verdict:  Real. Houston's running back duo is having issues generating an efficient offense. David Montgomery is averaging 2.7 yards per carry, and Woody Marks has a 2.9 average through two weeks. That's not all on them, though. The O-line hasn't consistently provided lanes for them; that's why it feels real. Sometimes, Montgomery and Marks have to fight for every yard while getting hit in the backfield. Against the Bengals, quarterback  C.J. Stroud  led Houston in rushing yards (29); that's never a recipe for success. -- DJ Bien-Aime 

 
 

 Indianapolis Colts 
 The early surprise:  The Colts have one of the NFL's worst defenses.

 

 The verdict:  Real. Indianapolis was hardly expected to dominate on defense, but its hopes for improvement were largely built on getting dominant play from the secondary. That hasn't transpired, and it's hard to see a path toward significant improvement without it. The Colts rank last in the NFL in yards per play (7.2), yards per game (514.5) and points allowed per game (37.0) as well as 31st in defensive expected points added (minus-28.3). -- Stephen Holder 

 

 
 

 Jacksonville Jaguars 
 The early surprise:  Bhayshul Tuten is RB1.

 

 The verdict:  Real. The Jaguars signed RB Chris Rodriguez Jr.  in free agency, and the expectation was that he and Tuten would share the workload. Through the first two games, however, Tuten (28 carries) has more than doubled Rodriguez's workload (12 carries). Tuten is averaging 4.7 yards per carry and also has three catches for 19 yards, and he should be fully entrenched as the lead back. -- Michael DiRocco 

 
 

 Tennessee Titans 
 The early surprise:  The Titans have been dominated in time of possession.

 The verdict:  Real. The Titans' offense had the ball for only 21:14 against the Jets, followed by 23:35 versus the Eagles. Each game presented a different reason for the discrepancy. Tennessee coach Robert Saleh credited the Jets for running the ball well and staying ahead of the chains. The imbalance against the…

title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces seven active players making their moves among the greats.
full_text:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams  after a blockbuster trade  in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. 
 
 Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players --  Von Miller  (No. 9), Cameron Jordan  (No. 17), Calais Campbell  (No. 25), T.J. Watt  (No. 26), Danielle Hunter  (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack  (T-29th) -- in the top 30.  
 
 Joining the top 30 soon could be  Aaron Donald ,  who unretired  to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th.  
 
 As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory. 
 
 
 
 Miller, who signed with the  Dallas Cowboys  in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.   
 
 But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. 
 
 If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's.  
 
As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape 
 We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. 
 

 

 Week 2 update 

 The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the career list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

 Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded one sack apiece over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

 Donald (33rd) made his  season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack. 

 

 

 Week 1 update 

 Of all the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. 

 And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

 After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

title: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 3
summary: How do all 32 NFL teams stack up ahead of Week 3? Plus, what we know for sure about the starting QBs around the league.
full_text:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season  marked a return to defensive dominance one week after record scoring numbers . This season, NFL defenses have a 35% pressure percentage (the highest through two weeks since ESPN began tracking pressures in 2009) and a 25% pass rush win rate (highest since 2017).

 How is this impacting quarterbacks around the league? In our Power Rankings ahead of Week 3, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to name the one thing we've learned so far from each team's QB situation. Which quarterbacks are handling the pressure? How are teams such as the Giants, Bears, Commanders, Seahawks and Vikings dealing with early injuries to their QB1s?

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32. And here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The 49ers climbed into the top three, led by a near-perfect two weeks from quarterback Brock Purdy . He became the fifth QB in NFL history to record multiple games with 90% completion percentage, per ESPN Research. And San Francisco gets to stay at home for two more weeks, starting with the Cardinals this Sunday . 
 The Chargers are down to No. 22 after falling to 0-2. According to ESPN Research, they are the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to be favored by at least 6.5 points in each of their first two games and lose both. The Raiders, who most recently beat the Chargers, are at No. 20 and are 2-0 for the first time since 2021. 
 Meanwhile, the Falcons and Dolphins are squarely at the bottom of the rankings. The Dolphins are the only team to not lead at any point this season, and ESPN's Football Power Index already gives them a 43% chance at the No. 1 pick. Atlanta is hoping to rebound with quarterback  Michael Penix Jr . back in the fold from ACL surgery. 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team as last week .

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN
